The Prismfall Codex

The story bible for Pokémon Prismfall: the realm of Velmora, its seven kingdoms, eighteen Wardens and the Festival of Champions.

POKÉMON PRISMFALL — Story Bible 00: Overview

Owner: Story & World lead. Binding source: design/SPINE.md. Flags: design/FLAGS.md. Files: 00 Overview · 01 World Lore · 02 Factions · 03 Cast · 04–08 Acts I–V · 09 Mysteries & Foreshadowing. Calendar used throughout: AF = "After the Fall" (the Prismfall). The game takes place in AF 300, spring to autumn equinox.

Logline

A fifteen-year-old with no Imprint steps off the last ferry into a quarantined land where a god's broken pieces are slowly overwriting the earth. Over eighteen gyms they learn that every power in Velmora, from the eco-zealots to the energy barons to the beloved Champion, needs them at the same ceremony for opposite reasons. And the piece of god in their own chest is the reason.

One-paragraph pitch

Three hundred years ago a king tried to chain Arceus. Rather than be bound, the god broke itself apart. Its eighteen Plates fell across Velmora and its heart, the Legend Plate, shattered. The king's capital sank into the earth, and the gleaming city-state of Zenith now stands on top of it. The survivors built a civilization on the wreckage: seven kingdoms (Elowen the Evergreen Crown; Antumbra, the Kingdom Behind the Glass; Isenmar the Frozen Sea; Ashkaar the Dragonfire Dominion; Ossaria the Bone Sands; Zenith, the City Above; and Nadir, the City Below) and eighteen cities, each grown around a Plate's Imprint (endless geothermal fire, a river that runs both ways, a garden that never stops blooming). Each city is guarded by a Warden who keeps its Plate and answers to the Accord at neutral Crownhaven, not to the local king. The kings have resented that for three centuries. Now the Imprints are Bleeding past their borders, freezing towns and turning forests to glass, and the outside world has sealed Velmora's borders. You arrive on the last ferry before the quarantine closes. You're the only person anyone has met whom the Imprints won't touch. The eco-zealot Hollow want to tear the Plates out of the land. The energy conglomerate Meridian Concord wants to tap them dry. The Accord, led by Sovereign Valen Corrigan, wants everything to stay exactly as it is, and has been quietly dying to keep it that way. The Festival of Champions will bring all eighteen Plates together for the first time in a decade, and the champions of other regions are coming to watch. Everyone is waiting for you to get there. Your choice at the end decides whether Velmora keeps its miracles or finally lets its god come home.

Themes

  1. Letting go. The Plates, grief, power, a seat, a name. Every major arc ends with someone releasing something they've built their life around. Rowan can't let go of his Fixed wife. Valen can't let go of the seat. Velmora can't let go of its miracles. The good ending is literally Velmora letting go.
  2. The emergency that became permanent. The Accord's founders meant to keep the Plates for a while, until the land healed. Three hundred years later the whole economy runs on a temporary measure. Meridian industrializes the dependency (an energy-transition allegory; keep it implicit, never preachy).
  3. Inheritance. Everyone carries something handed down. Kestrel carries a disgraced name, Juno a seat she never wanted, Voss a dead king's ambition, Valen a lie three centuries old, and the protagonist a shard they never asked for. Each of them has to decide what to keep.
  4. Truth versus stability. Valen lies to keep people alive. Dorian's theater tells the truth when the throne won't. Ilsa can read every truth and chooses silence. The game never says lying is simply wrong. It shows what the lie costs.
  5. Belonging. The protagonist has no Imprint and belongs to no city. They are the only one who can carry everyone home. In the true ending they are imprinted for the first time, by the plain, ordinary land.

Tone guide

The tone curve (REVISION 2): easy to fall into, then steadily heavier.

  • Act I (Rejuvenation-warm): cozy Ferrow's Landing, a berry farm, a theater, a haunted manor romp, funny rivals. The Bleed is eerie but beautiful. The Lowlight Shatter at the end of Act I is the first real wound.
  • Act II (Reborn-grey): the cost becomes visible. Fixing wards, company towns, an act of terrorism and an unmasking that hurts someone you like.

  • Acts III–V (Desolation-leaning): kingdoms mobilize, a city sinks, a massacre in Nadir, a mentor framed, a rival curdles, betrayals, a Champion's slow death, and at least one named death the player can't prevent (Corvin's apprentice Wenlow, in the Sump Purge, Ch16). Hope survives because people keep choosing it, never because the game softens.

  • Mature but hopeful. Death, grief, political violence, corporate atrocity and complicity all happen on-screen. Cruelty is never gratuitous, and nobody is evil "for fun". Hope is earned and specific: people choose to do better.

  • Every antagonist is partially right. The Hollow are right that the Plates must leave. Meridian is right that the Accord hoards power and lies. Valen is right that ripping the Plates out unguided would kill thousands. Voss is right that gods have been absent landlords.
  • Wardens are people first. Every gym chapter turns on the Warden's personal problem, which is also their city's problem. The type theme is the costume, not the character.
  • Specific over generic. Name the street, the dish, the song, the dead. A Fixed child in the Lowlight district is more affecting than "many casualties".
  • Funny on purpose (Revision 7). The humor guide, running gags and one scripted comic scene per chapter are in 15_COMEDY.md.
  • Humor lives in the cast. Odessa's irreverence, Corvin's gallows wit, Dorian's theatrics, Bastian's folksiness and Juno's earnestness keep the dark from going grey. Rival banter should be fun.
  • No mustache-twirling. Voss is gracious, generous and devastatingly reasonable. The first person to be kind to you in Velmora is the final villain.
  • The protagonist is mostly silent, but dialogue choices matter and they speak in a few key scenes (see 03_CAST). Never write them as a blank. They are the person everyone is trying to use, and their choices are how they refuse to be used.
  • Fields are real. Characters talk about field effects as weather and geography: "Don't fight a fire-type on the ice in Rimeholt, kid, the lake'll drink it." Field transitions in story battles are plot events.

The full plot (one page)

Prologue / Act I: The Last Ferry (Gyms 1–4). In spring AF 300, the protagonist (PC) crosses the Hallow Strait on the Dovetail, the last civilian ferry before the Concert of Regions seals Velmora. Their mother Ines, a Velmoran exile, has just died. Her last letter sent them to Professor Imelda Larch in Ferrow's Landing. On board they meet Aurelian Voss, Meridian's charming CEO, who gives them a Meridian badge case "on the company". At the dock, Meridian's Imprint scanner reads the PC as NULL. Voss smooths it over and starts watching. Larch gives the PC a starter. Juno Hale, Larch's sunny assistant, and Kestrel Vane, the angry grandson of the lighthouse keeper, take theirs (K1). The PC learns they can walk into Bleed zones that make everyone else sick. The road through Elowen shows the cost of the Imprints and of Meridian's extraction Lattices. In Saltmere, the Crown's free port and the first gym, the masked Mourner of the Hollow hijacks the official Prismfall pageant and asks a whole theater to "ask your Warden". In Briarwick, the second, the young Bug Warden turns out to have an answer to hide: she secretly signed with Meridian, and the Hollow are cutting its survey lines. Across the border in Isenmar, the Water Warden of Ebbmouth is caught between the Thane's taxes, Meridian's jobs and a brother who runs a Hollow cell. The act ends at Meridian's gala in Lumen City, capital district of Zenith, whose sewers run down into Nadir. A Hollow raid on the Zap Plate goes wrong: the Plate Shatters and twelve people in the Lowlight district are turned to glass. The PC sees the Mourner holding the cracked Plate with a burning hand. Voss restores the light. Sovereign Valen arrives to grant Meridian emergency security powers.

Act II: Imprints (Gyms 5–8). Larch suspects the Plate was already cracking under Meridian's drain. In Ossaria, Duneholt's shifting sands uncover Unown ruins and murals of a golden king chaining a beast of eighteen lights. Down in Nadir, Mirefen's Poison Warden runs a ward of Fixing patients in Zenith's toxic runoff, and Juno finds her uncle Rowan's name in his ledger. In Ashkaar, a Meridian geothermal tap nearly blows Cindervault's caldera, and the Dragon-Lord threatens war on Zenith. The Hollow are fracturing: the Mourner now wants to return the Plates, while a radical called Sable wants more Shatters. At the Warden Conclave in Ironreach's pit arena, Sable tries to Shatter the Fist Plate. The Mourner shields the crowd, and his mask breaks: he is Rowan Ashby, the Grass Warden, Juno's beloved uncle. Meridian takes him into custody. Valen watches the PC stand unharmed in the Bleed burst and says: "Come to Verdance. There's a seat to fill."

Act III: Fault Lines (Gyms 9–12). Verdance, Elowen's royal seat, has no Warden and is drowning in runaway bloom. Elowen's Queen claims the Meadow Plate for her crown, Meridian offers "custody", and Valen backs Juno, who inherits the seat (J3). The Accord splits into blocs over Meridian's Mandate while the kingdoms arm. In Isenmar, Rimeholt's lake thaws under a Meridian Lattice and wakes the Kyogre frozen beneath it. Its rain floods the Dominar's legions camped on Ossaria's sands, and Isenmar and Ashkaar, who share no border, go to war on the one ground they can both reach. In Skyreach, Zenith's airship spire, Larch publishes proof that extraction feeds the Bleed and is framed for it. Kestrel, now taking Meridian's sponsorship, steals a bundle of dead letters, one of them from his mother to "I." The PC crosses the Veil into Antumbra, the mirrored Reverse Kingdom where Giratina stirs. In Lucent, the Psychic Warden Ilsa (Valen's estranged daughter) takes the PC into the Mindscape. They recover a memory: at the last Festival, ten years ago, when the PC was five, the Sovereign's Crown cracked and something went into them. At Rowan's tribunal, Sable is exposed as a Meridian operative: the Hollow's worst atrocities were Voss's false flags. Then Meridian test-fires its secret engine in Cogsworth. A continental tremor, the Fault, pulls the sea back from the south coast overnight, draining the Sump beneath Nadir and exposing the spires of drowned Aurelia under Zenith's cliffs, below Underveil.

Act IV: The Drowned Crown (Gyms 13–16). The truth comes out in layers. Bastian, the oldest Warden, saw Meridian technicians at the Crown when it cracked. In Gravenmoor's Hollow Cathedral, the Ghost Imprint replays the AF 290 Fracture (K6). Kestrel's mother, Ghost Warden Morwen Vane, shielded the five-year-old PC, smuggled them out of Velmora and took the blame. Valen let her be ruined to keep the ceremony's secret. In Cogsworth, the PC finds the blueprints of the Arbiter Engine, an artificial Judgment built into the new Festival arena. It needs eighteen Plates, a keystone and "Subject UNIMPRINTED-01". Meridian's Mandate troops "pacify" Nadir in the Sump Purge, and Zenith's topside watches it on the news. In the west of Ossaria the war digs in: Isenmar's host behind Skaldfast, Ashkaar's legions in their siege camp, and Prince-Elector Kassan renting both of them the sand. Beneath Underveil, in the drowned capital Aurelia that Zenith was built on, the murals tell the real Prismfall. Voss stands in the Gilded King's throne room as that king's heir and names what the PC carries: a splinter of the Legend Plate, Arceus's heart. Their badge case has been recording the shard's resonance for Voss with every badge.

Act V: Sovereign (Gyms 17–18 + Festival). In Gloaming, deep in Elowen's south-eastern forest, the Fairy Warden gives the PC the suppressed Hymn of Return: the founders always meant to give the Plates back. Kestrel (K7) tries to stop the PC from going to the Festival, because he finally understands that everyone wants to use them. In Ashkaar's Wyrmrest, Valen's chosen heir Sigrun, the Dragon-Lord's own daughter, makes the PC prove they are choosing this with open eyes, then flies them to the front. On the Glass Dunes, Kyogre's flood-sea meets Reshiram's fire, the sand turns to glass, and the PC walks into the beam clash. The Festival opens with all eighteen Plates and the Tuning, and the PC's shard sees Arceus. Over the week the PC beats Juno, the established rivals and Wardens the draw sets against them, and Kestrel. Kestrel tears off his Meridian gauntlet mid-battle and finally reads his mother's letter. Valen confesses everything: when the PC beats him, he will crown them and their shard will make the Crown whole. The PC will hold the Plates quiet for a century, alone. The PC beats Valen. At the coronation, Voss triggers the Arbiter Engine and the Meridian Prism Arena becomes his weapon. The PC defeats him, but the Engine drags Arceus down in golden chains. Valen holds the containment ring with his own body while the PC battles the bound, maddened god through all eighteen types. Valen burns out as Arceus is freed. Arceus offers the PC a choice: return the Plates (the Imprints fade, the Bleed heals, the Fixed who still dream wake up, and Velmora must learn to live without miracles) or keep them and wear the Crown for a hundred years.

Core mysteries and their answers

Mystery Answer Revealed
Why is the PC Unimprinted? A splinter of the Legend Plate lodged in them as a five-year-old when the Sovereign's Crown cracked at the AF 290 Festival. The Legend Plate holds every type and none, so Imprints wash through them without marking them. Hinted from the Prologue; memory in Ch13 (Lucent); named in Ch17 (Underveil)
Who is the Mourner? Rowan Ashby, Grass Warden of Verdance and Juno's uncle by marriage. His wife Elin was Fixed by the Bleed into the flowering "Bride Tree" twelve years ago. Unmasked end of Act II (Ironreach)
What is the Bleed? The Plates trying to reconverge. Each Imprint is a Plate reaching for the others. Bleed zones are where the reaching overlaps, which is why the :BLEED field borrows random effects from other fields. Theory from Larch (Act II); confirmed by the Hymn (Act V)
What does the Festival ceremony really do? The Tuning. The Sovereign wears the Crown, which holds the largest surviving Legend shard, and hushes the converged Plates for another ten years. The bearer's body pays the cost. Since the Crown cracked, it has been killing Valen: his left arm is crystal under the glove. Hinted Act I; confirmed Act IV (Brann/Bastian), confessed Act V
Why was Morwen Vane disgraced? Valen scapegoated her for the AF 290 "Glassfall" (the Bleed burst when the Crown cracked) to protect the ceremony's secret. She took the blame silently to protect the PC. Ch15 (Gravenmoor, K6)
What really happened in the Prismfall? King Theodric Aurel ("the Gilded King") tried to bind Arceus with the Gilded Chain. Arceus shed its Plates to escape, and the shockwave collapsed the capital Aurelia into a flooded abyss, the Sump. In AF 118, guild-houses founded Zenith on top of it. One of those houses, the Vosses, was secretly the Gilded King's line. His daughter Maren founded the Accord as penance. Duneholt Unown murals (Act II) → "The Gilded King" play → Underveil (Act IV)
Who cracked the Crown in AF 290? Meridian. A young Aurelian Voss's "monitoring array" drew on the converged Plates as a proof-of-concept for the Arbiter Engine. Bastian (Ch14); echo (Ch15); Voss admits it (Ch17/Festival)
What does Voss want? To finish his ancestor's work: forge an artificial Judgment and chain Arceus as a permanent power source. He sincerely believes humanity should never depend on an absent god again. Act IV
What does Valen want for the PC? To crown them as the new, nearly unbreakable bearer of the Tuning, a living lock for a century. Act V audience
Who is the Hollow's radical, Sable? Sabine Kroll, a Meridian Special Accounts operative. The Lumen Shatter and the Ironreach attack were Voss's false flags, staged to win the Mandate and to collect Shatter data for the Engine. Ch13 (Lucent tribunal)
Why are Velmorans unable to leave? Imprinted people slowly sicken far from their Imprint ("wilting"). The PC's mother wilted in exile for ten years to keep them hidden. Ch1 hint; Ch12 letters; Ch15
What do the Plates want? To go home. The founders' Hymn of Return says a "child of no color" would one day walk the eighteen roads and carry them home. Valen reads it as "a vessel"; Celestine reads it as "a walker". Act V

Endings (story concepts; triggers and the matrix are owned by story/10_CHOICES_ENDINGS.md, SPINE Rev. 3 §5)

Endings are decided by accumulated choices (Bonds, Standing, Resonance Harmony↔Ruin, the Choice log) plus the final decision in front of Arceus. The scenes are in 08_ACT_V.

  • GOOD (canon): Homecoming. The PC returns the Plates with the Wardens' consent and the shard at Harmony.
  • Arceus, made whole, takes the eighteen Plates home.
  • The Bleed recedes. The Fixed who still dream wake (Elin under Juno's first autumn; Dex finishing his sentence). The long-Fixed pass on as light.
  • The Imprints fade over years. The PC is imprinted for the first time, by the plain land, and the quarantine lifts.
  • BAD (canon): The Gilded Chain. Voss's Engine is fully calibrated (telemetry untouched, Magnus unswayed, Kestrel fallen, the Hollow broken).
  • The PC loses the final fight for Arceus, not against it: the binding holds.
  • Epilogue: Zenith glows brighter than ever, powered by a chained god. The PC is the keystone, kept asleep and adored in the Meridian Prism Arena.
  • The last image is Voss's chipped linesman's mug on a desk above the world.
  • GREY endings: 1. The Long Vigil. The PC keeps the Plates and wears the Crown. The Bleed halts and Arceus departs incomplete. The final shot is the first crystal on the PC's hand. 2. Homecoming, Unfinished. The PC returns the Plates without enough Wardens' consent. The unreleased Plates are torn free and those cities suffer a last Shatter. It's hard, but the ending is free. 3. The Hollow Spring. High Hollow Standing with Rowan radicalized (or Sable unexposed). The PC uses the shard to break the Plates rather than return them. The Imprints die in one night of fire and glass, Velmora is ruined, and nobody ever rules it through a Plate again. 4. Concord Dawn. The PC accepts Voss's offer (or Magnus's governor is kept in place). Arceus is "humanely" half-bound and the Bleed ends. Prosperity is built on a god's quiet suffering, the PC sits on the Zenith Council, and nobody looks down. 5. The Borrowed Crown. Kestrel (redeemed, high Bond) or Sigrun takes the Crown in the PC's place. The PC sails home on the first ferry after the quarantine lifts, and the person who saved them grows glass on their hand. Bittersweet.
  • RUIN: The Unmaking. Ruin Route only, unlocked by the Ledger. The Legend Plate holds "every type and none". The Ruin Route follows a PC who learns to use the none. The shard can unmake Imprints, Plates, Judgment and the Glass itself. Story premise and hooks are in 01_WORLD_LORE ("The Other Face of the Legend Plate"). The route and its ending(s) are specified by the Narrative Systems designer.

Kingdom revisits and escalation (REVISION 2)

Each kingdom is visited 2–3 times, and each return must look and feel worse (or, rarely, better because of the player). The World Design team should reuse maps with altered events, tiles and encounters.

Kingdom Visit 1 Visit 2 Visit 3
Elowen Act I: storybook forest. The Glasswood is a pretty curiosity, and Queen Maelis is a figure on coins. Act III: Verdance is choked by runaway bloom. The Queen's Thornguard occupies the Heartgarden and claims the Plate. Refugees from Isenmar camp in Briarwick. Act V: Gloaming's dusk is spreading into the whole forest. The Crown and Meridian have signed a pact, Pecharunt's Sweetrot has reached Elowen's villages, and the Thornguard checkpoint at Gloaming's edge turns the PC back until Celestine vouches for them.
Isenmar Act I: Ebbmouth's foggy docks, a strike brewing, the river confused. Act III: Rimeholt's Thaw sinks a quarter of the city and Kyogre wakes. Ebbmouth (a short detour, on strike) is flooded with refugees, and the Thane declares martial law and sends his host east over the Mast Glacier to war. — (Act V epilogue only)
Zenith Act I: neon, airships, a gala, optimism, then the Lowlight Shatter. Act III: Skyreach under Mandate curfew. The Larch Papers broadcast and the Gale Post is raided. Act IV: Cogsworth's foundries run three shifts building the Engine. Topside "Unity" rallies, Zekrom roars in the foundry stacks, and the Sump Purge plays on every screen.
Nadir Act II: Mirefen's runoff marsh and Ironreach's pits. Grim but alive, with Hollow graffiti everywhere. Act II (end): the Conclave attack. Mandate checkpoints go up at every lift to topside. Act IV: Underveil after the Fault. The Sump has drained to expose Aurelia, then comes the Purge. The PC walks through the aftermath.
Ossaria Act II: Duneholt's caravans, the collapsing aquifer, Unown ruins, the fossil lab. Act IV: Cragholm. The Prince-Elector has sold mining rights to Meridian, the deep seams shelter fugitives, and the raid comes. Two foreign armies dig in on its western dunes, on ground Kassan has leased them, and Duneholt's caravans start leaving. Act V: the Battle of the Glass Dunes, fought on Ossarian sand. Afterward the bone-carters claim the glass as a necropolis.
Ashkaar Act II: Cindervault's caldera crisis. The Dominar's legions muster and talk of war with Zenith. Act V: Wyrmrest, its riders gone to the war in the sands. Sigrun holds the gate and defies her father. —
Antumbra Act III: through the Veil into Lucent. The Mindscape and a mirrored city where up is down. Giratina is a shadow in every reflection. Act IV: Gravenmoor. The Hollow Cathedral echo, Vane Hall (the haunted house) and the Giratina boss battle in the Reverse Cathedral. (Act V: the Synod keeps the Veil Gate shut, but the Glass leaks travelers from other worlds: the cameo sidequests)

Legendary arc per kingdom (REVISION 2; species per WORLD.md §3 / POKEMON_AVAILABILITY)

Boss battles are Rejuvenation-style multi-bar fights. Note for Core: EBDX's boss module gives stat boosts and immunities only, so multi-bar HP needs custom code (SPINE_FEEDBACK). Legendaries become catchable post-game unless noted. Full beats are in the act files.

Kingdom Legendary Thematic role Arc beats
Elowen Ogerpon + the Loyal Three (Okidogi, Munkidori, Fezandipiti) A false legend. Elowen's pageants honor "the Loyal Three" who drove off "the Gossamer Ogre". The truth is the reverse: the Ogre was the forest's guardian, and the Three were thieves in thrall to poison. The official story is a lie is the whole game in miniature. The Hollow's masks are modeled on the Ogre's. Saltmere's pageant of the Three and the Mourner's "poison on their collars" (Ch2) → Briarwick's shrine, ogre masks and Celestine's rhyme (Ch3) → Ogerpon guards the Bride Grove, and the Three attack under Pecharunt's sway in a boss battle (Ch10) → Ogerpon fights beside Juno at the Festival
Nadir Pecharunt The Sump Barons' secret. "Sweetrot", the City Below's mochi-like street chem that makes users loyal and docile, is Pecharunt's poison, farmed in the Lightless Deep. It's also what enthralled the Loyal Three centuries ago. Corvin treats Sweetrot addicts (Ch7) → Meridian blames Sweetrot to justify the Sump Purge (Ch16) → boss battle in the Lightless Deep, freeing the thralls (Ch18 opener, segment 16)
Isenmar Kyogre Why the sea is frozen. When Aurelia drowned, the sea surged and Kyogre rose. The Icicle Plate fell onto it and froze it, and the sea around it, in place. Isenmar is that frozen sea. Ice-fishers' "Sleeping Whale" songs (Ch4) → the Thaw under Lake Rime wakes it. Primal rain drowns Rimeholt's lower town, and the PC's shard calms it in a boss battle (Ch11)
Ossaria Groudon The Gilders' first attempt. Theodric tried to remake the land with Groudon and Kyogre before he turned on Arceus. Groudon sleeps under the Bone Sands, and Meridian's deep drills are waking it. Unown records in the Ossuary of Dunes (Ch6) → it wakes in the Duneholt Undersands during the Act IV revisit, boss battle (Ch14→15 transit)
Zenith Zekrom (Ideals) Its Dark Stone, dredged from Aurelia, was Meridian's first power core. The Lattice was reverse-engineered from it. The black core seen at the Gala (Ch5) → a black dragon in the Stormfront (Ch12) → bound in the Cogsworth Engine core, then freed in a boss battle that cripples the Engine's first design (Ch16)
Ashkaar Reshiram (Truth) The Dominion's ancestral dragon. Its Light Stone sits in Cindervault's forge-guild vault, and the Dominar wants it on his throne. The Light Stone dispute (Ch8) → wakes to the PC's spoken truth in Sigrun's trial at Wyrmscar Rift, boss battle (Ch19)
Antumbra Giratina (the Reverse) Guardian of the Kingdom Behind the Glass, the seam that tore open in the Prismfall. The Glass touches other worlds. Reflections that move wrong (Ch13) → Reverse Depths boss battle (Ch15) → its torn Glass leaks visitors from other worlds (the optional cameo sidequests, CAMEOS.md) → Distortion Core post-game
Crownhaven / realm Zygarde (Order) Valen's partner. Its cells thread Velmora's crust and hold it together. Zygarde Cell side quest across all kingdoms → Valen's ace (Final) → chooses the PC post-game
(all) Arceus The finale. Ch21

Unown ruins The Ossuary of Dunes (Duneholt → Mirefen road), where the Aurel murals are written in Unown (Ch6)
Safari-style reserve The Royal Chase, Queen Maelis's hunting reserve outside Verdance, thrown open to the public in Ch10 as a political gesture
Post-game Battle Tower / Warden gauntlet The Concordance Spire in Crownhaven (Battle Tower) + the Warden's Gauntlet (all 18 Wardens back-to-back at level 100)

Story Bible 01: World Lore — Velmora

Geography follows design/WORLD.md §1 (World lead). Kingdom names are final per SPINE Revision 3. Calendar: AF = After the Fall.

1. Cosmology in one breath

Arceus, the Original One, shaped the world and keeps it in balance through its eighteen Plates, one for each type. At its heart sits a nineteenth, the Legend Plate, which holds every type and none. The Plates are not tools Arceus carries. They are Arceus, the way a heartbeat is part of a body. Separate them and Arceus becomes incomplete: it sleeps, wounded and unable to act, somewhere beyond the sky that Velmoran priests call the Hall of First Light.

For three hundred years Velmora has lived on pieces of a sleeping god.

2. History

Before the Fall: the Aureate Kingdom

Before AF 0, one kingdom ruled the continent: the Aureate Kingdom of House Aurel. Its capital, Aurelia, rose in gold terraces up the southern sea-cliffs. The Aurels were builders and believers. Their court artificers, the Gilders, combined clockwork, alchemy and old Pokémon pacts into something close to science.

The kingdom's last two decades were the Blight Years: crop-rot, a wasting plague and three failed harvests running. King Theodric Aurel, later called the Gilded King, tried to fix the world by force.

  • First he tried to remake the land. The Gilders woke Groudon beneath the Bone Sands and Kyogre off the western coast. The two titans nearly tore the continent in half before they were driven back to sleep. Ossaria's Unown records call this "the Year of Two Weathers". They met in Ossaria's western dunes, and the Dry Tide west of Duneholt is the seabed Kyogre's sea left there.
  • Then he went higher. The Gilders forged the Gilded Chain: eighteen golden locks, one for each Plate, around a keystone cradle shaped for the Legend Plate. They meant to summon Arceus and bind it to the throne. "If heaven will not kneel, we'll build a chain." — Theodric, as quoted in "The Gilded King".

Theodric was not a monster. His people were starving, and he loved them. That is the point, and it is why Voss can quote him without irony.

AF 0: the Prismfall

At midsummer, in the Sun Court of Aurelia, the Gilders performed the Calling. Arceus descended, and the Chain closed. For one heartbeat the god was bound.

Then Arceus did the only thing a god can do that a chain cannot hold: it broke itself.

  • The Plates. It shed all eighteen Plates in a burst of light seen from every corner of the continent. They scattered across the land and buried themselves where they struck. Every Plate began to Imprint the ground around it with its type.
  • The Legend Plate, caught in the keystone cradle, shattered.
  • Aurelia. The shockwave collapsed the city into the cliffs. The sea poured into the ruins, and Aurelia became the Drowned Crown.
  • Isenmar. The surge rolled west and north up the coast and woke Kyogre. At that moment the Icicle Plate fell into the waves and froze Kyogre and the sea around it solid. That frozen sea is Isenmar.
  • Antumbra. Behind the great forest, the world tore. A mirrored reverse side opened behind the Glass. Giratina, the guardian of reverse places, came through to hold the seam closed.
  • Arceus, incomplete, fled beyond the sky and slept.

AF 0–4: the Grey Years

Survivors gathered around the fallen Plates because the Plates kept them alive. Fire that never went out. Water that never froze. Fields that bloomed in a week. Cities grew around each Imprint. Families who kept the Plates safe from raiders became the first Wardens.

AF 4: the Concordance

Theodric's daughter Princess Maren Aurel had opposed the Calling and survived the Fall. She pulled the largest surviving shard of the Legend Plate from the wreck of the keystone cradle. She renounced her house, took the name Maren Ilse, and climbed the high caldera at the center of the continent, where all eighteen Imprints can be seen glowing on a clear night.

There she gathered the eighteen Plate-keeping families and the war-chiefs of the provinces that would become the kingdoms. Together they signed the Concordance, founding the Accord. The caldera city became Crownhaven.

Public articles (taught in every schoolroom):

  1. Every Plate is held in trust for all Velmora by its Warden. No king may own or seize a Plate.
  2. Wardens answer to the Accord, not to the crown of the land they stand on.
  3. Once each decade, the Plates are carried to Crownhaven for the Festival, and the strongest trainer in the realm holds the Sovereign Seat.
  4. Motto: "Eighteen in Concord, One in Keeping." (Everyone thinks "One" means the Sovereign. It means the Legend Plate.)

Secret articles (the Sovereign, the Hierophant, the Underveil Keepers and Gloaming's Warden alone):

  • The Tuning. Left alone, the Plates reach for each other. This is the Bleed. Maren set her Legend shard into the Sovereign's Crown. Every ten years, with all eighteen Plates gathered, the Crown-bearer hushes them for another decade.
  • The Hymn of Return. The founders swore the Plates were borrowed. "When the land is healed, one of no color shall walk the eighteen roads, and carry them home." Keeping the Plates was meant to be temporary.

3. How Imprints work

In-world science, per Larch's Field Notes (Rev. 3 adds an in-game Field Notes encyclopedia, and these are her entries' voice):

  • The Imprint. A Plate saturates the land around it with its type, typically within 5–15 km and strongest at the heart. Matter, weather and Pokémon behavior bend toward that type. This is not metaphor. Field effects are Imprints: fire really does burn hotter in Cindervault, sound really does carry on Saltmere's Grand Stage, and the ice really does drink heat in Rimeholt. Battles fought in an Imprint obey it.
  • Resources. Each Imprint is an economy: Cindervault's ever-fire, the Ebb's two-way current, Verdance's endless harvest, Briarwick's silk that never tangles, Lumen City's free current, and so on.
  • Tint. People and Pokémon raised in an Imprint carry a faint affinity for its type. Velmorans call it their tint, as in "she's Cindervault-tinted, she'll run warm." Tint shows on Meridian scanners as a color bar. Foreigners take on a tint after a few weeks. The PC never does.
  • Eevee evolves according to the Imprint it is raised in. Velmorans call it "the Plate's child", and an Eevee is a traditional gift to a newborn. (This is the lore behind the Eevee Octave.)
  • Seeds. Imprints condense into seeds in the right soil. Elemental, Magical and Telluric Seeds grow wild at Imprint borders and are harvested by seed-pickers. Synthetic Seeds are Meridian's lab-grown version, sold in every Mart since AF 294.
  • Choir glass (Z-crystals; SPINE Rev 23). After the Glassfall the Choir gathered the glass of Lower Crownhaven's broken streets, never from the Scar's forty. It sang over the glass and sent its pilgrims to leave slivers where each Imprint runs strongest, to soak it up ("tuning"). A sliver that has drunk one Imprint is a Z-crystal. Some were lost on the roads, some sold, posted to the grieving or kept as keepsakes, and a few were tuned in temples on purpose (the Crucible's brazier, Gloaming's dusk-chapels, the Octave's). A Warden's ring wakes them, because its chip is grind off the Crown's stone and the glass was made the night the Crown cracked. In dialogue it's "Glassfall glass" or "Choir glass", and "same crown, one way or another". Never say the glass is the Crown's stone or a Plate. The PC's splinter stays the only missing piece (09_MYSTERIES #1, #5, #6).
  • Terrain. Electric, Grassy, Misty and Psychic Terrain are "small, temporary Imprints a Pokémon makes itself". Where they meet a real Imprint they layer over it, are smothered by it, or transform it. Locals know which, and NPCs should say so.

4. The Bleed

  • What it is: the Plates reaching for each other. Each Imprint is slowly extending toward the others, and where two or more overlap, reality loses its grip on what type it is. In battle, that is the :BLEED field: unstable, with effects borrowed at random from other fields. It has accelerated sharply since AF 289, because Meridian's Lattices draw on Imprints like a pump draws on a well, and a drained Imprint reaches harder.
  • Bleed zones look beautiful at first: glass orchards, forests of frozen birdsong, rivers hanging in the air. They are deadly to anyone with a tint. Every zone has a Bleed Veil at its edge, a shimmer in the air that tinted people physically cannot cross ("my skin's burning, I can't"). The PC walks through.
  • Fixing: prolonged Bleed exposure Fixes a person into the substance of the overlapping Imprints. It goes in stages: 1. Glassy fingernails. 2. "Sleepwalking": staring, humming. 3. Partial Fixing: crystal, ice, bark or salt spreads from the extremities. 4. Full Fixing.

The Fixed are not dead. They dream, and with time some stop dreaming. Corvin's Quiet Ward in Mirefen holds forty patients at stages 2–3. The Accord hides whole Fixed towns: the Quiet Towns (Marrowgate, Lowmarsh, Halden's Reach East).

  • Wilting: a tinted person far from their Imprint slowly sickens with weakness, grey skin and grief. This is why Velmorans almost never emigrate, and why the outside world's quarantine is cruel twice over. The PC's mother wilted in exile for ten years to keep her child hidden.
  • The Shatter: strike a Plate hard enough and it releases its Imprint all at once. The result is a Bleed explosion and instant Fixing within a few hundred meters. The Lumen Shatter (Act I) Fixed twelve people in the Lowlight district.

5. The Tuning and the Crown

  • The Sovereign's Crown is a plain silver circlet holding a single colorless stone, the largest surviving shard of the Legend Plate.
  • The Tuning. At the Festival's opening ceremony, the Wardens set their Plates into the eighteen pylons of the Concordance Ring in the arena. The Choir sings, and the Crown-bearer hushes the Plates' reaching. To the public it is a lightshow. In truth, the bearer's body is the conduit.
  • The cost. The Crown's shard used to carry most of the load. It depletes a little every decade, and each Sovereign pays more than the last. Most Sovereigns since AF 140 have died within twenty years of their first Tuning, of what the Accord calls "the Sovereign's fatigue".
  • AF 290. When Meridian's array cracked the Crown, a splinter flew free into the PC. Brann reset the stone, but the Crown has been incomplete ever since. Valen has carried nearly the whole Tuning in his body: his left arm is crystal to the shoulder, under the grey glove.
  • The ceremony is failing, and Valen knows it. He cannot survive the AF 300 Tuning without help. With the PC's splinter rejoined, the Crown would be whole, and its bearer could hold the Plates quiet for a century, alone.

6. The Other Face of the Legend Plate (Resonance: Harmony ↔ Ruin)

The Legend Plate holds every type, and none. It has two faces, and the PC's choices tilt their shard toward one of them. This is the in-world meaning of the Resonance track (SPINE Rev. 3).

  • Harmony (every): the shard calms. Bleed-maddened Pokémon settle near the PC, Bleed zones go quiet around them, and other Plates "hum along". This face makes Return possible.
  • Ruin (none): the shard unmakes. Imprints thin to nothing where the PC stands, and a Plate touched in anger cracks. At its extreme it can unmake Judgment, the Glass, or the Plates themselves. Celestine's rhyme for it: "the color that eats colors".
  • Story rules:
  • Ruin is never "evil mode". It's the face that answers despair, the Hollow's grief in its purest form.
  • Wardens and Pokémon feel the PC's Resonance. Corvin: "You've gone cold, love." Celestine: "You're getting louder in the wrong key."
  • The Ruin Route (Narrative Systems spec) follows a PC who has seen every way the world ends (the Ledger) and decides to stop asking it to be saved.

7. Religion

  • The Prism Faith (Church of the First Light). Velmora's established faith. Arceus is "the Original One". The Benediction Doctrine holds that the Prismfall was a gift of love, which is the Accord's official myth.
  • The Prism Choir, led by Hierophant Maud Ellery, performs the Tuning liturgy without knowing what it really does.
  • Churches have eighteen colored windows around a clear nineteenth pane. Prayers end with "and keep the One".
  • The Wound Doctrine (heresy). The Plates are Arceus's wound, and Velmora is living off a god's blood. Taught by Brother Wick (defrocked) and radicalized by the Hollow into "pull the nails".
  • The Gloaming Liturgy. Gloaming's dusk-chapels still sing the complete Hymn of Return in its original form. The Choir thinks it's a quaint local variant.
  • Antumbra's Veiled Faith. Giratina is "the Warden of the Reverse", the god's own night watchman. The Veiled Synod's seers read reflections, and lantern-priests guide the dead.
  • Ashkaar's Fire-Creed. The Dragon-Lords claim descent from the white dragon of truth (Reshiram). Oaths sworn over flame are binding, so lying in a Dominion court is a capital crime.
  • Isenmar's sea-songs are about "the Sleeping Whale under the ice" (Kyogre). Fishermen pour a cup of warm broth through an ice-hole before every season.
  • Nadir's folk-saints: "the Ogre in the Mask", a protector of the forgotten borrowed from Elowen's legend, painted on sump walls beside the Hollow's ring sigil.

8. Economy

  • The Imprint economy is three centuries old. Each Warden city trades its Imprint's product, and the kingdoms tax the trade, though the Concordance forbids them from taxing the Plate itself. The kings call that "the Accord's theft".
  • Meridian Concord changed everything in a decade:
  • Lattices are extraction pylons (Larch's design) that draw energy from an Imprint. Fourteen of eighteen cities have one by Act III.
  • Prism Cells are batteries charged from Lattices. Every lamp in Zenith runs on them. Under a special quarantine exemption, Meridian exports them to the Concert of Regions, so Velmora's suffering powers other people's cities.
  • Royalties. Meridian pays cities and crowns a cut, so Wardens and kings alike depend on it. Imprint industries that compete with Meridian (Ebbmouth's tidal mills, Briarwick's looms) are bought out or starved.
  • The Mandate (from Act II on): after the Lowlight Shatter, the Accord grants Meridian Security police powers wherever Lattices stand.
  • Nadir's economy:
  • Prism slag is Lattice runoff that drains down from Zenith. Mirefen's marsh is made of it.
  • The pits are Ironreach's betting arenas.
  • Sweetrot is the street chem, and the Sump Barons control it.
  • Information is Nyx's trade.

The City Below has no seat on the Zenith Council and pays Zenith's taxes anyway.

  • Money: the Pokédollar (₽) is standard. Old-timers in Ossaria still quote prices in "bones", fossil-shell tokens.

9. Politics: the Accord versus the kingdoms

  • The tension in one line: every king rules land with a Plate in it that they're forbidden to touch.
  • The Accord Council (meets in Crownhaven): the Sovereign, the eighteen Wardens and the Chancellor (Ambrose Hollis), who runs the bureaucracy and the Wardguard budget. Votes are by Warden. Kings attend only as "honored observers", and they hate it.
  • Blocs (from Act III, "Fault Lines"):
  • Greenward (limit extraction, oppose the Mandate): Juno, Marisol, Kaito, Corvin, Tamsin, Ysolde, Celestine.
  • Concord bloc (pro-Meridian): Magnus, Rook (until Act IV), Anja (until the Thaw), and Dorian (publicly, under protest).
  • Sovereign loyalists: Brann, Sigrun, Bastian, Sahar.
  • Independents: Odessa, Nyx, Ilsa.
  • The kingdoms' agendas:
  • Elowen wants its Plates back as Crown property.
  • Isenmar wants heat and debt relief.
  • Ashkaar wants the Draco Plate and the Flame Plate under the Dominar, and Zenith humbled.
  • Ossaria sells whatever Meridian will buy.
  • Antumbra wants the Glass kept closed and Giratina undisturbed.
  • Zenith wants the Mandate everywhere.
  • Nadir wants to exist: recognition, a vote, clean air.
  • Outside:
  • The Concert of Regions (the neighboring realms across the Hallow Strait) imposed the quarantine and will decide at this Festival whether to lift it or declare Severance, permanent abandonment. Its envoy is Delphine Okoro.
  • The Veil Gate through Antumbra opens to other worlds, and it has been sealed since AF 230. Since the Bleed and the Fault thinned the Glass, it leaks: travelers from other worlds slip into Velmora uninvited, and that is the basis of the optional cameo sidequests (design/CAMEOS.md).

10. Culture notes (for NPC writing)

  • Greeting: "Light keep you." Reply: "And the One." Hollow sympathizers pointedly answer "And let it go."
  • The counting rhyme. Jump-rope chant, known everywhere, in gym order. It is also a progression mnemonic:

    One for the stage and two for the weave, three for the river that won't take its leave, four for the lantern, five for the dune, six for the fen and its poison-blue moon, seven for embers, eight for the fist, nine for the garden the frost never kissed, ten for the lake and eleven for sky, twelve for the dreamer who never asks why, thirteen for stone and fourteen for bone, fifteen for gears and sixteen unknown, seventeen dusk and eighteen for wings — and none for the cage, and none for the king.

(The Ebb "won't take its leave" because it always comes back: it runs both ways. "Sixteen unknown" because Underveil isn't on Accord maps. "None for the cage, and none for the king" refers to the Gilded Chain and the Gilded King, though no child knows that.)

  • Food: Ferrow's Landing kelp-tea and bramble tarts. Briarwick honey-silk buns. Saltmere salt-caramel. Ebbmouth smoked eel. Lumen City Fizzbolt soda. Duneholt date-bread. Mirefen "bog coffee". Cindervault ember-roasted chestnuts. Rimeholt fermented fish (a dare). Gloaming dusk-honey, which supposedly lets you dream of the dead.
  • Holidays: Fallmorn, the midsummer anniversary of the Prismfall, when families light eighteen candles and leave one holder empty. The Festival each decade.
  • Fashion tells:
  • Elowen: leaf-green and embroidery.
  • Isenmar: furs and bone toggles.
  • Ashkaar: lacquered scale armor and red.
  • Ossaria: wraps, goggles, fossil jewelry.
  • Antumbra: veils, mirror-silver, mismatched gloves (left for the living, right for the dead).
  • Zenith: brass, glass, clean white.
  • Nadir: patched leathers, rebreathers, Hollow-grey.

11. Places

Crownhaven (neutral; the Accord's capital; story-gated, Act V)

Built on the inner slopes of the Crown, the great caldera ring at the realm's center. Its eighteen gates face the eighteen Imprints. Upper Crownhaven is white stone, bell towers and the Basilica of First Light, and the Temple-Arena of the Blessing (rebuilt by Meridian as "the Meridian Prism Arena", and too new) rises above the Court of Eight Pavilions, where each kingdom's delegation and the Accord pitch their colors. Lower Crownhaven is the crowded crater-floor town that still has a scar: the Glassfall Scar, a district-sized stretch of glass where forty people were Fixed in AF 290. The Accord fenced it and planted a memorial garden around it, and nobody tends the garden. The Concordance Spire, the old Accord archive tower, becomes the post-game Battle Tower.

Elowen, the Evergreen Crown

The great forest at the heart of Velmora, from the south-west coast to the Gloamwood in the south-east, with Crownhaven at its centre. It borders every kingdom. An old monarchy under Queen Maelis Thorne. Wild types: Fairy, Grass, Bug, Normal. Character: storybook beauty with old rot underneath, a kingdom of fairy tales that are mostly lies.

  • Ferrow's Landing (start): Elowen's southern ferry dock on the Hallow Strait. A fishing village of tarred stilt-houses and drying kelp under a red-and-white lighthouse, where old Hesper Vane keeps the lamp and young Kestrel keeps out of sight. Tidewatch Station, Larch's field station and the Wayfarer Sanctuary, sits on the headland. Hale's Bramble berry farm is up the lane. The bronze Accord plaque at the dock reads "Eighteen in Concord, One in Keeping". After the last ferry, a Meridian customs gate stands beside it.
  • Saltmere (Gym 1, Normal, :GRAND_STAGE): Elowen's chartered free port on a salt lake at the forest's coastal edge. Here the Blank Plate's Imprint is ordinariness: nothing strange ever happens in Saltmere, and Bleed never touches it. So the city built its own miracles, and it is Velmora's theater capital. The Lantern Theatre on the salt-flat promenade stages the Accord's official Pageant of the Prismfall every Fallmorn; in a Festival year the run opens in spring and plays through to Fallmorn. The Pell Playhouse in the Old Town is the gym. The free-port charter means Saltmere answers to no king, and the Queen's tax-barges are turned back at the breakwater by tradition. Saltmere keeps its own oil lamps and has refused Meridian's "free light" for the promenade, which Dorian calls part of the set. It is reached from Ferrow's Landing along the chalk coast (the Strand Road). Up the Weavers' Road toward Briarwick stands Thistledown Manor, home of a dead acting family who never stopped performing (the comic haunted house).
  • Briarwick (Gym 2, Bug, :SILKWOOD): a weaving village inside the Gossamer Wood, where the Insect Plate makes Bug Pokémon spin silk that never tangles or rots. Houses are lashed between tree trunks, and the town looms clack all day. A shrine at the village edge honors the Loyal Three, who "drove the Gossamer Ogre from the wood". Children wear carved ogre masks at Fallmorn to scare it off. The road in is the Weavers' Road up the River Selvedge from Saltmere: the cloth goes down it, the salt comes up. The old forest road south to Ferrow's Landing is corded off, because the Glasswood has crossed it. The Glasswood, a crystallizing Bleed, is creeping toward the silk-moth groves from the east, along the line of Meridian's new Lattice.
  • Verdance (Gym 9, Grass, :FLOWER_GARDEN): Elowen's royal seat. A green city of terraces and glasshouses where the Meadow Plate makes everything bloom constantly. Verdance has never had an autumn. It is a true castle-city: three rings of briar-grown curtain walls with thorn gatehouses enclose the Market Terraces, the Glasshouse District, the Cathedral of the Original One and the guild halls, and a tanners' slum sprawls along the river outside the walls. Briar Keep crowns the highest terrace, and Queen Maelis holds court in its great hall from a throne of living thorn, beneath galleries hung with three centuries of tapestries. Below it lies the Warden's Heartgarden, where the Bride Tree stands in permanent blossom. Underneath, the soil is grey and starving, and nothing rots, so nothing returns to the earth. The Royal Chase, the Queen's game reserve, sprawls outside the walls.
  • Gloaming (Gym 17, Fairy, :FAIRY_TALE): the forest's oldest corner, deep in the south-east, where the Pixie Plate in the roots of the Great Tree holds the sky at permanent dusk. Lantern-moths, mushroom bridges, and a town of bargains and courtesies. Gloaming folk can't lie, age slowly, and keep the old songs. The approach is through the Gloamwood. By Act V, the dusk is spreading west across Elowen like a stain, toward Briarwick.

Antumbra, the Kingdom Behind the Glass

A mirrored realm behind Elowen's forest, entered through mirror gates such as Mirror Mere. The Reverse Kingdom is governed by the Veiled Synod under Archseer Imre Dask, and it is Giratina's domain. Wild types: Ghost, Psychic, Dark. Inverse rules (:INVERSE) hold in the borderlands: rivers run uphill, shadows fall toward the light, and type matchups flip.

  • Lucent (Gym 12, Psychic, :MINDSCAPE): a scholars' city that exists twice. The living city is reflected upside-down in the sky above it, and the Mind Plate lives in the reflection. The Lucent Athenaeum holds the Accord's archive, the sealed stacks, the Concordance original and the Secret Articles. The Accord holds its tribunals here, under Ilsa Marr's provostship. Lucent is Antumbra's seat. The Veiled Synod rules from the Palace of Glass, whose throne room floor is a still lake reflecting a second, inverted court where the Synod's reflections sit in council.
  • Gravenmoor (Gym 14, Ghost, :HOLLOW_CATHEDRAL): a moorland cathedral town of fog, barrows and lanterns, where the Spooky Plate makes the dead linger as echoes. The Hollow Cathedral replays the last moments of anyone who died near it. Vane Hall, the Vane family manor and Kestrel's childhood home, stands empty on the hill, dust-sheeted and haunted. The Lantern Hospice is where Morwen died.

Isenmar, the Frozen Sea

The west and north-west coast, a sea frozen solid since AF 0 with a hard clan-kingdom built on it, under Thane Eirik Sorrel. Wild types: Water, Ice. Character: endurance, debt, and stubborn warmth.

  • Ebbmouth (Gym 3, Water, :WATER_SURFACE): Isenmar's southern port, where the River Ebb comes down from the Crownland downs to meet the open sea. The Splash Plate makes the Ebb run both ways, inland on the morning tide and out at night, and three centuries of tidal mills grew up around it. It is fog, gulls, smoked-eel stalls and union halls. The Ebb Guild elects the Warden. Meridian's tidal Lattice at the river mouth is draining the current, and the river has started to "stutter", stopping dead for minutes at a time. Nearby: Ebb Hollow, a Bleed zone where river-water hangs in the air in still sheets.
  • Rimeholt (Gym 10, Ice, :FROZEN_LAKE): the northern ice-city built on Lake Rime, part of the frozen sea, frozen solid for three hundred years above the Ice Vault, where Kyogre sleeps. The houses are timber and whalebone, linked by sled-roads, and ice-fishers cut holes over a darkness that sometimes breathes. Meridian's Lattice heats the city and thins the ice. In Act III, a quarter of the city sinks. Rimeholt is Isenmar's seat. The Thane rules from the Holdfast, a fortress-port of black stone on the Hold-rock at the lake's heart: rime-white curtain walls, whalebone gatehouses, an ice-harbour for longships and sled-fleets, and a great hall whose hearth has burned for three hundred years.
  • Skaldfast (the war, Acts III–V): Isenmar's oldest fort, the skalds' fastness, at the foot of the Mast Glacier on the edge of the bone sands, where the first thanes stood against the desert. In the war it is Isenmar's border fortress, besieged from Ch15 (14_WAR_AND_BLESSING).

Zenith, the City Above

A gleaming city-state on the southern plateau, all brass, glass, airship masts and progress. It is governed by the Zenith Council of founding houses, chaired by Aurelian Voss. Meridian's home. Wild types: Electric, Steel, Flying. Character: optimism with the bill sent downstairs.

  • Lumen City (Gym 4, Electric, :NEON_GRID): Zenith's capital district, a neon metropolis lit by the Zap Plate's free current plus Meridian's Lattice grid. Streets of advertising holograms, Rotom delivery drones and rooftop gardens. Meridian Spire rises from the cliff edge on the foundations of the old Aurelian sun tower, with its black Dark Stone core glowing in its heart. The Lowlight is the working-class district where the Spire's shadow falls. After the Shatter, part of it is glass. As Zenith's capital district, Lumen City climbs in towering tiers: the Council Spire where the Zenith Council sits, glass skybridges, airship docks, the Gilt Market, and at the bottom the lift-shafts down into Nadir.
  • Skyreach (Gym 11, Flying, :STORMFRONT): Zenith's airship spire, a vertical city of docking masts and skybridges climbing into the Stormfront, the Sky Plate's permanent storm wall. Home of the Gale Post courier guild and of every smuggler worth hiring. Stormwatch Spire at its crown holds the relays that broadcast to the whole realm.
  • Cogsworth (Gym 15, Steel, :FACTORY): Zenith's foundry district on the plateau's eastern edge, where the Iron Plate makes metal eager to be shaped. Smokestacks and clock-towers, three shifts a day. Magnus Strade's Strade Works builds everything from airship hulls to, secretly, the Arbiter Engine. The bathysphere works that build Dive suits for the drowned coast are here too.

Nadir, the City Below

The slums, sumps and old mine shafts beneath Zenith's cliffs, built in the caverns and in drowned Aurelia's upper towers. Zenith claims it, but it has no recognized government: Sump Barons, pit-bosses and Nyx Calloway run it. Wild types: Poison, Dark, Fighting. Character: rage, solidarity and the best street food in Velmora.

  • Mirefen (Gym 6, Poison, :CORROSIVE_MIRE): a stilt-town in the runoff marsh where Zenith's Lattice slag drains into the Toxic Plate's mire. The water glows faintly blue at night, which is the "poison-blue moon" of the rhyme. Fenfolk are tinted against poison and almost nothing else. Corvin Mott's Infirmary and its Quiet Ward stand on the highest stilts.
  • Ironreach (Gym 8, Fighting, :COLOSSEUM): the pit-fighting quarter carved into the Aurel-era mine shafts. The Fist Plate makes people and Pokémon strong, so for centuries Nadir's miners have settled everything with their hands. The Iron Pit, a colosseum in a mined-out cavern, hosts the Iron Trial and the Ironreach Open. In Act II, the Accord's Conclave is held here in the shafts under Zenith's feet, to show the City Below the Accord still cares. It goes badly.
  • Underveil (Gym 16, Dark, :NEW_MOON): the heart of Nadir, a city of lanterns and smugglers in the upper towers of drowned Aurelia, half-submerged in the sea-flooded Sump beneath the south cliffs. The Dread Plate keeps it in permanent night. It's not on Accord maps ("sixteen unknown"). Nyx Calloway's Moon Market trades in secrets, and she rules from the Moon Court in the topmost drowned tower. It is a vertical undercity of stairs, lifts and lantern-bridges stacked down the old palace's flanks. In Act III, the Fault drains the Sump overnight and exposes the Sun Court, the Gilded King's throne room, for the first time in 300 years.

Ashkaar, the Dragonfire Dominion

The eastern volcanic highlands, from Cinder Cape on the north-east coast down the Wyrmspine. A feudal warrior-kingdom of dragon-lords under Dominar Hrothgar Ashfall. Wild types: Fire, Dragon. Character: honor, oaths, and a war it badly wants.

  • Cindervault (Gym 7, Fire, :VOLCANIC): a forge-city inside the caldera of the Cinderhorn, where the Flame Plate keeps the magma at the perfect working heat. Terraced smithies, lava-channels for quenching and the Hearthguild of smiths. The guild vault holds the Light Stone, which the Dominar wants for his throne. Meridian's geothermal tap is overdrawing the caldera. Quench the Imprint and it becomes :ASHEN_WASTE. Cindervault is Ashkaar's seat: Pyre Keep, the Dominar's dragon-citadel of black basalt and red lacquer, stands on the caldera rim above the forge terraces, with dragon-roosts in its towers, a war-market in the lower bailey and the Ember Throne in a great hall over a channel of living magma.
  • Wyrmrest (Gym 18, Dragon, :DRAGONS_DEN): the dragon-aerie fortress on the peaks that guard the only overland pass into the Crown. Dragon-riders patrol the Wyrmscar Rift. The Draco Plate sleeps in the Rift's heart under Sigrun Ashfall's guard, while her father's legions muster on the slopes below. By Act V they have gone to the war in Ossaria's sands.

Ossaria, the Bone Sands

The northern desert and canyon country along the north coast: fossil beds, caravan houses and deep mines. Ruled by Prince-Elector Idris Kassan, whom the caravan houses elect for life. Wild types: Ground, Rock. Character: patience, memory, and things buried for a reason. Ossarian tomb-law says the sand keeps whoever dies on it, so the bone-carters bury strangers as carefully as their own. The western dunes lie between Isenmar and Ashkaar, who share no border, and the war of Acts III–V is fought there, on neutral ground (14_WAR_AND_BLESSING).

  • Duneholt (Gym 5, Ground, :DESERT): a caravan city of sandstone terraces around a deep aquifer, which the Earth Plate keeps inside the stone so the desert above stays fertile. The dunes move, and every few years they uncover something. Sahar's Dig Lab (fossil revival) is here, and the Ossuary of Dunes (Unown ruins) is on the road out. Meridian's deep drills are collapsing the aquifer, the city's wells are sinking, and something enormous beneath the sand has started to warm. Duneholt is Ossaria's seat. The Prince-Elector's Sandglass Palace rises on the high mesa above the walled caravan districts and bazaars. Beyond the walls, the Valley of Tombs holds three centuries of caravan-princes in rock-cut halls.
  • Cragholm (Gym 13, Rock, :CRYSTAL_CAVERN): a mining town carved down a canyon wall into crystal caverns. The Stone Plate grows gems the way Verdance grows flowers. It is lamplit galleries, lift-cages and the deep seams, where Bastian hides people the Accord and Meridian would rather didn't exist. Darken the caverns and they become :DARK_CRYSTAL.

WORLD_MAP — the geography of Velmora

Owner: world cartographer. SPINE Revisions 9, 13, 14 and 18 (Geography v2: Elowen in the middle; the war on land in Ossaria). Images: art/previews/world_map.png (painted region map) and graphics/UI/Town Map/prismfall_velmora.png (the in-game Town Map, 480×320). Both are drawn by python3 -I tools/worldmap/gen_world_map.py from tools/worldmap/world_geo.py (coasts, mountains, rivers, the war front) and tools/worldmap/world_data.py (towns, roads, squares, borderlands). Roads in detail: design/ROUTES.yaml and WORLD.md §11. Names: design/PLACE_NAMES.md. Story lines that Geography v2 made wrong: design/GEOGRAPHY_V2_STORY_FIXES.md.

Coordinates below are town-map squares (x 0–29 east, y 0–19 south), the same grid as pbs/town_map.txt. One square is roughly six leagues, a long day's walk. The continent is about 27 squares across and 19 from the north coast to the Hallow Strait.

1. The shape of the land

Velmora is one broad continent. Elowen's green country fills the middle, and the Crownwall, a ring of white peaks, stands at its heart (14.5, 9.5) with Crownhaven inside it. The bone sands of Ossaria run along the whole north coast. Isenmar holds the west and north-west, where the sea itself is frozen. Ashkaar's volcanic highlands fill the east. In the south rises the Zenith Plateau, the City Above, with Nadir beneath it and drowned Aurelia under its south cliff. The narrow Hallow Strait in the south is the only way most foreigners arrive.

Sea or coast Where Character
The Northern Sea the whole north coast, y 0–1 Open, grey water off Ossaria's dunes and the Crags. West of x ≈ 9.6 it is frozen: that is Isenmar's sea. No war is fought on it.
The frozen sea the west and north-west, x 0–9 Frozen solid since AF 0 (the Icicle Plate fell into it). It is Isenmar: Rimeholt stands on Lake Rime, an inlet of it, and the Thane's sled-road runs along its shore east to the Mast Glacier.
The Western Deep the west coast below the ice, x 0–2 Deep cold water. The coast runs from Saltmere's salt flats north through the frost-flats of the Frostflat Causeway, the Rimewood's frozen shore, the sea cliffs of Gullcry and the Ebb estuary to the fjords below Rimeholt. A coast packet links Saltmere and Ebbmouth by sea.
The Ember Sea the east coast, x 27–29 Warm, dark water under Ashkaar's basalt cliffs; the Dragonback runs along the shore, and Cinder Cape is its north-east tip.
The Hallow Strait the south, y 18–19 The ferry sea. The Dovetail crosses it in the prologue (the last civilian crossing). Chalk cliffs west of Ferrow's Landing (Lacecliff Walk), dunes and a salt lagoon at Saltmere. Under Zenith's south cliff the sea covers drowned Aurelia (the Fault drains it in Act III). The Shardfall Isles (postgame) lie off the Gloamwood, x 20–24.

2. Highlands

Range Where What it is
The Zenith Plateau and the Escarpment x 15–21, y 14–18 A raised tableland, the City Above. Its edge is a cliff all round: the north face sheds the Outfall into Mirefen's marsh, Ironreach and the Long Drop sit under its north-west rim, the west face (the Escarpment) looks over the Gossamer, and the south face drops into the sea at Underveil (the Hanging Stair goes down it). Lumen City stands on its south brink, Skyreach (airship spire) on the north-east, Cogsworth (foundries) on the east rim, and the Slag Mesa spills off its east side.
The Crownwall a ring around (14.5, 9.5), about three squares across White peaks, unclimbable except at the one gap on the east side, where Sovereign's Ascent climbs in from the Pilgrim Pass. The Crown Road circles it outside.
The Frostfang Mountains x 4–8, y 3–6 Isenmar's spine between the Ebb and Rimeholt. The Frostfang Pass and the Whalebone Road (Road 10) cross them; the Mast Glacier spills off their north-east end.
The Crags of Ossaria and the Jawbone Ridge x 19–23, y 1–3 Red rock on the north coast; Cragholm's lift-galleries; a toothed ridge running south to Vigil, with the Darkglass Mine in it.
The Kneeling Stones x 18–19, y 4–5 A low ridge of fossil vertebrae where the River Leach rises.
The Cinderhorn and the Dragonback the Cinderhorn (25.7, 10.3); the Dragonback x 26–27, y 5–8 Ashkaar's volcano south-east of Cindervault, and the ridge along the east coast. Lava veins, cinder cones, dragon roosts.
The Wyrmspine x 23–25, y 13–15 The ridge Wyrmrest stands on; Road 18 climbs it from the Thornwar Marches.
The Spinners' fells x 9–10, y 12 Sheep hills north of Briarwick (Spinners' Rise, Road 3).

3. Rivers and lakes

Water Course
River Ebb Rises on the Crownland downs west of the Crownwall (11, 8), runs west over the frozen falls of the Icefall Locks, through Brassfall and the Reedholms delta to Ebbmouth. Its current runs both ways (the Splash Plate).
River Selvedge Rises in the Gossamer Wood, runs south-west past Thistledown Lea and through the Dyers' Ford (red, blue and yellow below the dye-works) to the Saltmere Lagoon. The Weavers' Road (Road 2) follows it.
The Prism From Mirror Mere south past the Crownwall's west side over Prism Falls (the rainbow that never stops) into the Gossamer, where it joins the Selvedge.
River Leach From the Kneeling Stones south through the Leach Canyons and Wormwood Lea, clean until it reaches the plateau, then over the Gutterfall into Mirefen's marsh, where Nadir's runoff turns it blue.
The Outfall Zenith's waste water, down the plateau's north face into Mirefen.
Spinefall From the Crags south over the fossil spine of Spinefall Gorge into the desert sinks near Vigil.
Gloam Water and the Thornrun South through the Gloamwood and the Thornwar Marches to the Hallow Strait.
The Blindwater Underground. It leaves the sea at Underveil through the Throat, runs east beneath the plateau's south cliff (Mothwell's lamps light it) and comes back into the light at the Gloamwood Verge. Road 17 is a boat journey along it. Drawn dotted.
Lake Rime The frozen inlet Rimeholt is built on; the Ice Vault (Kyogre) lies beneath.
Lake Sallow One great sulfur hot spring on the Elowen/Ashkaar border, north-east of Mirefen; Lantern Isle steams in the middle. Road 7 crosses it (Surf).
Mirror Mere A small silver lake in the Looking-Glass Wood, north-west of the Crownwall: gate A into Antumbra.
Saltmere Lagoon The salt lake behind Saltmere's sandbar, fed by the Selvedge; the Grey Saltings' pans line it.

4. The kingdoms

Kingdom Where Land Seat and gym towns (gym #, Revision 14)
Elowen, the Evergreen Crown the middle, from the south-west coast to the Gloamwood in the south-east; borders every kingdom Oldwood, orchards, river meadows, chalk coast and the Crownland downs round the Crownwall. The Gossamer Wood (silk) in the south-west; the Gloamwood (permanent dusk) in the south-east. Verdance (seat, 9) · Saltmere (1, free port) · Briarwick (2) · Gloaming (17) · Ferrow's Landing (start)
Isenmar, the Frozen Sea the west and north-west Snowfields, pine, fjords and sea-ice. Rimeholt (seat, 10) · Ebbmouth (3) · Skaldfast (border fortress on Ossaria's west edge, war)
Ossaria, the Bone Sands the north, along the whole north coast Sand, canyons, fossil beds, tombs, the Crags. Neutral ground: the war is fought in its western dunes. Duneholt (seat, 5) · Cragholm (13)
Ashkaar, the Dragonfire Dominion the east Basalt, ash plains, the Cinderhorn, dragon ridges, from Cinder Cape in the north-east down the Wyrmspine. Cindervault (seat, 7) · Wyrmrest (18) · Cinder Cape Warfort (war)
Zenith, the City Above the plateau in the south Brass, white stone, rail and pylons; airships. Lumen City (seat, 4) · Skyreach (11) · Cogsworth (15)
Nadir, the City Below beneath the plateau, same footprint: the marsh and mines at its foot and the undercity under its south cliff Marsh, slag, mine shafts, a sea-drowned city. Underveil (seat, 16, in drowned Aurelia's towers) · Mirefen (6) · Ironreach (8)
Antumbra, the Kingdom Behind the Glass nowhere on the real map: the inset in the south-east sea The mirror realm: inverted desert hanging in the sky, shadows falling toward the light. Lucent (seat, 12) · Gravenmoor (14)
Crownhaven inside the Crownwall at Velmora's centre, on Elowen ground The Accord's capital and the Festival grounds. Crownhaven (the Festival)

5. Borders and borderlands

Kingdoms touch only through borderlands (Revision 9), each with a town where the two peoples live together. On the map the borderlands are the mottled ground where both kingdoms' colours mix; the dashed red line marks kingdom edges. The records (biome, landmarks, wild mix, member maps) are BORDERLANDS in world_data.py, copied into maps.json and WORLD.md §10.

Code Borderland Between Where (squares) Town
A The Rimewood Elowen / Isenmar the west coast between Briarwick and Ebbmouth, x 5–8, y 10–14 (the Frostflat Causeway runs on down the coast to Saltmere) Frostwick (6, 12)
A2 The Hoarwood Elowen / Isenmar x 5–6, y 8–9 Snowbriar (5, 8)
B The Icefall Locks Isenmar / Elowen the Ebb's frozen falls, x 4–8, y 6–7 Brassfall (7, 7)
B2 The Mast Glacier Isenmar / Ossaria tundra and permafrost dunes, x 6–8, y 2–3 Anchorhold (8, 3)
C The Brass Dunes Elowen / Ossaria north of the Crownwall, x 14–15, y 4–5 Copperdune (15, 5)
D The Leach Canyons Ossaria / Elowen x 19, y 5–6 Charwell (19, 6)
E The Sulfur Reach Elowen / Ashkaar Lake Sallow and the Ironway, x 20–23, y 7–10 Scaldwater (23, 9)
F The Rootdeep Nadir / Elowen the plateau's foot: the Rootdeep (x 13–14, y 12–13), the Gutterfall (20, 12), the Long Drop (16, 12), the Blindwater (x 18–19, y 18) Lanternroot (12, 12), Mothwell (21, 18)
G The Wired Wood Zenith / Elowen the plateau's north and west foot: the Wired Wood (18, 12), the Meridian Mainline (17, 13–15), the Arc-Lamp Mile (x 14–15, y 14–15), the Slag Mesa (21, 14) Verdigris (17, 11)
H The Looking-Glass Wood Elowen / Antumbra round Mirror Mere, x 10–11, y 6–7 Glassmere (11, 6)
I The Obsidian Barrows Antumbra / Ossaria x 20, y 3–4 Vigil (20, 3)
J The Thornwar Marches Elowen / Ashkaar x 23, y 15–16 Thornwatch (23, 15)
K The Pilgrim Pass Elowen / Crownhaven from the Dominion's toll-fort west to the Crownwall's gap, x 18–22, y 10–12 Pilgrim's Rest (18, 10)
L The Hanging Stair Zenith / Nadir the plateau's south cliff, x 18–19, y 16–19 Midstair (19, 17)
M The Cinderglass Barrens Ashkaar / Ossaria volcanic ash desert, x 23–24, y 4–6 Glasswake (23, 4)

Fire and ice never border. Isenmar's land is the west; Ashkaar's is the east. Between them lie Elowen and Ossaria, and the two meet only as armies, on Ossaria's sands (§7). Zenith and Nadir border Elowen only (Nadir also touches Zenith, vertically).

Not adjacent (by design): Isenmar–Ashkaar, Isenmar–Zenith/Nadir, Ossaria–Zenith/Nadir, Ashkaar–Zenith/Nadir, Crownhaven with anything but Elowen. Antumbra touches the mainland only at its three gates.

6. Roads, sea lanes and air lanes

  • The Eighteen Roads join the gym towns in badge order; the Pilgrim Road (Road 19) goes in to the Crown. Each road is two to six named maps (WORLD.md §11). On both maps a numbered shield marks each road. The early chain (Revision 14, unchanged by v2): Ferrow's Landing → the Strand Road west along the chalk coast → Saltmere → the Weavers' Road inland up the Selvedge → Gossamer Wood → Briarwick → the Hoar Road north over the fells, through Frostwick and the Rimewood, down Gullcry Cliffs → Ebbmouth. The Frostflat Causeway along the coast closes the loop from Frostwick back to Saltmere.

  • The Crown Road circles the Crownwall on Elowen ground: Wallshadow Row (west and south), Candle Down (east), the Highwold (north), Kingsmead (north-west), with Coppice Ride linking it west to the Icefall Locks. Every road in Velmora ends on it; Roads 4, 5, 8 and 12 run along part of it, and only Road 19 goes in. It is how the gym order crosses Elowen between kingdoms that do not touch (WORLD.md §10, "Elowen in between").

  • Side roads: Windfall Row (orchards, Chapter 1), the Frostflat Causeway, the war road north from Cindervault (the Cinderglass Barrens, Glasswake, the Wyrmtongue to Cinder Cape), and the Dry Tide (Road 14's side road, open after Badge 13) from Duneholt's west gate to the bone-carters' camp and the front.

  • Sea lanes: the Last Ferry (the Dovetail, into Ferrow's Landing), the coast packet (Saltmere ↔ Ebbmouth), the Strait ferry to the Shardfall Isles (postgame). On the ice: the Thane's sled-road from Rimeholt east along the frozen coast to the Mast Glacier.

  • Air lanes (Act III, Skyreach airships): Anchorhold ↔ Skyreach (Road 11's air leg, drawn as an outlined dashed line: Isenmar and Zenith share no border), Skyreach ↔ Lumen.

  • Underground: the Blindwater (Road 17).

7. The war in the sands (Revision 18)

The Ashkaar–Isenmar war is fought on land, in Ossaria's western dunes, neutral ground that both armies march into.

  • Isenmar's host comes from the west: Rimeholt → the Thane's Sled-Road → over the Mast Glacier → Skaldfast (9, 2), Isenmar's border fortress on Ossaria's west edge → the white trench-lines of the Rimed Sands (11, 2).

  • Ashkaar's legions come from the east: Cindervault's north gate → the Cinderglass Barrens → Glasswake → west across the bone sands → the Ashkaar Siege Camp (15, 2). Cinder Cape Warfort (26, 3) is their staging fortress on Ashkaar's own north-east coast, behind the lines.

  • The Steamline (12, 1) is the steam-glass strip where the two Imprints meet: ice on one side, fire on the other.

  • The Glass Dunes (13, 2) are the battlefield. In the climax Primal Kyogre drags a flood-sea into the desert and Reshiram's fire turns the dunes to glass. Meridian's observers watch from the Observers' Mesa (13, 3) behind the lines; the Dominar holds court in his Command Pavilion in the Siege Camp.

  • Ossaria's side: the western dunes are rented to the war under Prince-Elector Kassan's Elector's Lease. The bone-carters, Ossaria's burial guild, camp at the west end of the Dry Tide (14, 3) and walk between the lines under a white bone-banner both armies let pass.

  • On the world map: blue march arrows (Isenmar) and red march arrows (Ashkaar) converge on a glowing jagged front line at x ≈ 13, crossed swords mark the Glass Dunes, and the camps are flagged. The Town Map shows the same front in pixels, and each war site has its own named point.

  • Maps 920–930 (WORLD.md §9). Duneholt (17, 3) is the nearest city, a day's ride from the front: the Dry Tide runs from its west gate to the bone-carters' camp. In Act IV the PC reaches the front from Cragholm by way of Duneholt; in Ch19 Sigrun flies the PC from Wyrmrest to the bone-carters' camp.

8. Crownhaven and the Festival grounds

Crownhaven sits in the bowl of the Crownwall at the centre of Velmora, on Elowen ground. Every kingdom's road ends on the Crown Road outside the wall, but there is one way in: the Pilgrim Pass, which runs west from Dominar's Toll at the Ashkaar border across Elowen ground (eighteen shrines, Pilgrim's Rest at its end), then Sovereign's Ascent through the wall's one gap on the east side, and the Coronation Road down into the city. The Dominar still holds the toll at the start of the only road in, which is the politics of the Festival in one fact. Inside the ring: Lower Crownhaven (the Eighteen Gates face the Imprints, the Market Ring, the Pilgrims' Quarter), Upper Crownhaven (the Basilica, the Accord Palace, the Concordance Spire) and the Festival grounds on the bowl's east side, nearest the pass: the Processional Plaza, the Temple-Arena of the Blessing (Hall of Eighteen Doors, Altar Stage) and the Court of Eight Pavilions. The Glassfall Scar lies on the inner slope of the north-west wall.

9. Antumbra

Antumbra has no place on the real map. Both images draw it as an inset framed like a mirror in the south-east sea. Its three gates are marked A, B and C on the mainland and in the inset:

  • A, Mirror Mere (Elowen, the Looking-Glass Wood, north-west of the Crownwall) → the Antumbra Threshold → Widdershins Walk → Lucent.

  • B, the Grave Glass at Vigil (Ossaria) ↔ Yesterday's Road (from Lucent) and Hindmoor → Downflame Road → Gravenmoor.

  • C, the Slagglass at the Slag Mesa (Zenith/Elowen, east of the plateau) ↔ the Noonless Road from Gravenmoor.

10. The in-game Town Map

pbs/town_map.txt (shipped as PBS/town_map_prismfall.txt) defines region 0, Velmora, with Filename = prismfall_velmora.png. Every settlement, every road square, every named dungeon and every war site has a Point; dungeons and districts show as the point of interest of their square. Every map has a MapPosition (mapgen/data/town_map_positions.json, applied by build.py; maps.json metadata.town_map_pos). Fly spots exist for the six built towns (their PC HealingSpots). Prismfall Maps/009_TownMap.rb compiles our file instead of the stock one, whose Essen region 0 it replaces, and makes Fly read the live HealingSpot from map metadata. The UI draws the 480×320 graphic over Graphics/UI/Town Map/bg.png.
