  4. Kestrel crashes the ceremony. He has been sleeping in the Sanctuary's loft because his grandmother kicked him out again. He grabs the counter-starter: "Fair fights are for people who can afford to lose." Larch lets him take it with a look that says she has history with this family. - K1 (lv 6), at the Sanctuary gate. Afterward, Kestrel: "You came in on the last ferry? Great. Velmora's sinking and they're still letting tourists on."
  5. Rowan Ashby visits. Juno's Uncle Rowan, the Grass Warden, has come down from Verdance to collect seed stock. He's gentle and funny, with soil under his nails. He came "round by Saltmere: the forest road's glass now, and they're putting the Pageant on early this year. Lot of fuss over a play." (Fair clue: the Mourner hijacks that Pageant in Ch2.) He shows Juno and the PC a sickly Phantump he rescued "from the Glasswood up past Briarwick. It was sitting in a tree that had turned to glass, crying." (Clue: the Mourner's ace is Trevenant.) - He tells Juno about larches: "Everything that grows must be allowed to die, Juno. That's not sad. That's what makes room." He touches one of the blossoms in her wreath as he says it, very lightly, the way you'd touch someone's hand. - Of his wife: "She'd have liked you." He's talking to the PC, and it lands oddly.
  6. The Ferrymen's Mile → Windfall Row → the Glassed Orchard (map 522, :BLEED, mandatory tutorial). - The Hales' neighbor's apple orchard turned to glass last winter. Glass apples chime in the wind. - Juno stops at the Bleed Veil: "My skin's burning. I can't — how are you doing that?" - The PC walks through. Inside, a Bleed-maddened Pokémon (a glassed Wurmple swarm leader) calms when the PC approaches. This is the first demonstration of Harmony. - The PC retrieves the farm's lost Skwovet for a reward. - Larch, waiting at the edge with a notebook, says very quietly: "Well. That's that, then." She records the first Field Notes entry (:BLEED). - Game over GO_ORCHARD "Two in the Orchard". Trigger: Juno asks "Can you pull me through? Just for a second?" and the PC says yes. Foreshadowing: the burning line, plus Larch's earlier warning, "Never take a tinted person past a Veil. Never." Juno's hand glasses in yours. Epitaph: "She trusted you. That was the whole problem." - On Windfall Row the Accord has corded off the old forest road north into the Gossamer Wood: the Glasswood is across it, a mile in. Briarwick, four hours away by that road, is now two days away by the coast. (This sets up why Saltmere comes first.)
  7. Evening. Hesper Vane's lighthouse. The old woman shouts at Kestrel from the gallery while the PC passes below. She sees the PC and drops her lamp-rag. Inside the lighthouse door, visible if the PC knocks, hangs a cracked mirror Hesper refuses to replace: "Leave it. It shows the truth crooked, same as everything." (A Ruin Route seed: it is the last image of END_REFLECTION.)

Cliffhanger: Larch, at night, writes in her journal (a short cutscene): "Subject reads NULL. Second such reading in my life. The first was in Crownhaven, AF 290. God help us, Ines." Fade.

CHAPTER 2 — "Curtain Call" (the Strand Road → Saltmere, Gym 1; J1)

Location: the Strand Road west along the chalk coast: the Ferrymen's Mile (520), Lacecliff Walk (527) and Marram Down (528), both :BEACH. Then Saltmere (Elowen's free port): the promenade (140), the Harbour & Breakwater (146), the Old Town (147), the Pell Playhouse (Gym 1, 150/154, :GRAND_STAGE) and the Lantern Theatre (145).

Why this chapter comes first. It is the hook. The player has just learned they're strange (Ch1). Now they learn the realm is arguing about the very thing that makes them strange, and that the argument has a masked face. The Hollow arrive as theater: a voice, a question, a mask. Ch3 turns the question into a person.

The road. The PC spends the night at the Hale Farmhouse (Wenna won't hear otherwise, and the Hale Bell guard won't let anyone onto the Strand Road before first light). In the morning Larch walks in to breakfast and sees the PC off: "Saltmere's first. The forest road's corded off, so you go round by the coast. The Warden's Dorian Pell. He'll call you 'darling' and mean it about a third of the time." Juno comes too: her mother has promised forty bramble tarts to the Pageant crowd, and Juno has wanted to see the Pageant since she was six.

  • At the Hale Bell an Accord guard waves the PC through the quarantine line. Challengers pass, which is older law than the quarantine. His partner mutters that "the null one from the dock" is to be let through "whatever happens", by order of a white seal from Crownhaven. (Valen's people are already watching.)
  • A hay-cart driver: "Used to take me four hours to Briarwick. Now the forest road's all glass and I go round by Saltmere. Two days. Glass doesn't pay my horse."
  • On Marram Down, the Pageant's travelling players are camped in their wagons, rehearsing the companion piece in the dunes. A half-buried theater barge hides the Prompter's Box (optional): the prompter's script, which hints at how the Grand Stage works, with one page the Accord cut in AF 140 (a seed for the Loyal Three lie).
  • The first view of the free port is from the Saltmere Beacon: a white town on a salt lake, every second building a theater.

Arrival. Saltmere is salt-caramel stalls, lamplit promenades and a breakwater where the Queen's tax-barges are turned back by tradition. Show it on arrival: an Elowen barge rows in, the whole breakwater stands up and boos, and the barge rows away. The man conducting the booing with a silver-topped cane is Dorian Pell, Warden of Saltmere.

  • The Blank Plate makes Saltmere ordinary: nothing strange ever happens here, and the Bleed has never touched it, so the city makes its own miracles on stage. In a Festival year the Pageant of the Prismfall (the official myth, "a gift of love from the Original One") opens in spring and plays through Fallmorn. This year's companion piece is "The Loyal Three": three faithful hounds drive the Gossamer Ogre from the wood.
  • Saltmere keeps its own oil lamps along the promenade. They're part of the set, Dorian says, and Meridian may not have them.
  • In the Lantern Theatre's prop room, the Accord's Pageant Office has sent new drawings for the Crown prop. The stone is smaller this year, and nobody says why. (Crown seed 2 of 3, between Ch1's "printing fault" and Ch3's chapel mural.)

J1. On the promenade green, before the PC's first gym, Juno challenges them to a cheerful spar (J1, on :MEADOW): "I want to know if I'm any good before you go in there. I want to know if you are." Win or lose, she promises to be the loudest person in the house.

Gym 1 (:GRAND_STAGE), a single battle: "the house loves a show". The Pell Playhouse is a simple, handsome theater: the lobby, the aisle between the velvet seats, three actors who step out of the rows to battle, and one gentle interaction at the end, the curtain rope that flies the house curtain out (GYM_PUZZLES Gym 1). Grand Stage is the PC's first gym field, and it teaches itself: the audience cheers flashy moves, and the cheer lifts the next one. Juno, in the stalls with a cone of salt-caramel, is part of the audience. Dorian in velvet: "Enter, stage left, our brave challenger! Your first Warden, your first field, your first audience." His ace is Kecleon, which changes "costume" with each type.

  • On victory he awards the Footlight Badge, and the badge case hums faintly the first time a badge goes in: one clear note. (Seed.) Juno: "Ooh, is it supposed to do that?" Dorian has lived his whole life in the one city where nothing does anything: "Darling, in Saltmere nothing is supposed to do anything. ...Do it again." It doesn't.
  • After the battle, his troupe gives the PC the gift Eevee "Understudy" ("forty auditions, never cast — you came off the ferry without a color and this one hasn't picked one either: you two are a matched set"). That afternoon at the Lantern Theatre it is cast in "The Loyal Three" as Tree Number Three and cut for pacing (comedy scene, 15_COMEDY Ch2). At the same rehearsal a costumier asks Juno which play her blossoms are from, and Juno explains, cheerfully, that they're her aunt.

The breakwater. At sunset, before opening night, the PC and Juno sit on the end of the breakwater eating salt-caramel. This is a quiet friendship scene, and it should be a breather.

  • Juno tells the PC about her blossoms: Aunt Elin, Fixed into the Bride Tree when Juno was three, in permanent bloom ever since. Juno kept wearing the flowers from the wedding, and they've never wilted. "Uncle Rowan says that's the problem. I don't know what he means." (Three hours later, the Mourner says it to a whole theater.)
  • CHOICE :ch3_juno_talk: tell Juno about the NULL scan (Juno Bond up. She promises to keep it secret, and she does) / deflect / say nothing.

The Pageant. The PC attends opening night with Juno and Dorian.

  • The companion piece plays first. Three actors in hound masks chase a sad-masked, bark-faced Ogre off a painted wood while the children in the gallery boo.
  • Mid-performance, the stage lights go grey. A child: "Is that the Ogre? He's early!" The Mourner steps out of the painted backdrop of the Plates falling. Ash-bark mask, single white lily, doubled voice:

    "Three hundred years of pageantry. Ask your Warden why nothing in Verdance ever rots. Ask your Sovereign why the old capital is underwater. Ask why the Loyal Three wore poison on their collars. Let the land grieve."

  • At "nothing in Verdance ever rots", Juno's hand goes to her wreath.
  • Bereaved grunts drop Hollow Ring banners from the flies. One of them, a grey-cowled woman with a weaver's shears, cuts the curtain ropes very neatly, and the curtain comes down on the cast without touching a soul. (Thistle; the PC meets her in Ch3.) The crowd panics, and the PC fights two grunts at once.
  • The Mourner looks straight at the PC across the theater and goes still. "...You." Then he's gone in a burst of Cotton Spore.
  • Juno, shaken: "He sounded sad. Isn't that weird? I thought he'd sound evil."
  • First meeting with the Eevee Octave. The Prism Choir's touring chorus sings the Pageant's hymns. It includes the Eevee Octave, eight Glassfall orphans each partnered with an Eevee-line Pokémon. Their leader Vesper Lindqvist (24, gentle, devout) finds the PC backstage after the panic and kneels to Understudy: "It hasn't decided which Imprint it belongs to yet. Neither have you, I think." Optional battle vs Vesper's Eevee and Lyra's Eevee (double; Lyra is the Octave's Elowen singer, going home to Briarwick). Encounter 1 of 3. Afterwards Vesper asks the PC to look in on the eight singers as their road goes through the kingdoms (SPINE Rev 19: the Eevee Octave quest line, design/EEVEE_OCTAVE.md). Carol, the eighth, never leaves Crownhaven.

Aftermath and revelation.

  • Dorian, rattled and pale, pulls the PC into his dressing room and presses a yellowed page into their hands: the prologue of "The Gilded King" (Key Item). "Ansel Crewe wrote that in AF 52. They hanged him for it. I've never staged it. I'm a coward with excellent diction." The page includes the line: "If heaven will not kneel, we'll build a chain." Why the PC? "Out of a whole theater, he looked at you. I've been looked at by audiences for forty years, darling. I know when someone's found the person they came for."
  • Kestrel is outside the theater, white-faced. He heard the Mourner's voice. "That's — the way she talks — no. No." He runs north, out of the North Gate toward the Gossamer. This sets up the "Mourner = Morwen" rumor, and his hunt (K2, Ch4).
  • Dorian, sending the PC on: "Your next Warden is Tamsin Loom, up the Weavers' Road in Briarwick. She inherited the seat in spring and hasn't slept since. Be kind. She'll apologize to you for losing. Let her." Juno decides she's coming too: Uncle Rowan wants silk-moth eggs, and she's not letting the PC walk into the Gossamer alone "after THAT".

Cliffhanger: An Elowen herald posts a royal notice on the free port's charter stone. Queen Maelis "notes with grief" the Hollow outrage in her free port, "where the Crown's protection was refused". Dorian rips it down in one long tear. "Her free port." The North Gate opens.

CHAPTER 3 — "The Weaver's Debt" (the Weavers' Road → Briarwick, Gym 2)

Location: the Weavers' Road inland from Saltmere's North Gate: the Grey Saltings (541, :BEACH, with Brinecut Mine), the Dyers' Ford (552), Thistledown Lea (540, with Thistledown Manor 546/547, the haunted house), then Gossamer Wood (524, :SILKWOOD) and Briarwick. After the gym: the Gossamer Deepwood (525) and the Glasswood's heart, Cocoonfall Hollow (548, :BLEED).

Why this chapter comes second. Ch2 asked "Ask your Warden" in front of a thousand people. Ch3 is the same question asked of one tired nineteen-year-old in a loft, with no audience at all. The Hollow stop being a voice and become a grieving weaver with a pair of shears, and Meridian shows its double edge for the first time: the free light is real, and so is the glass.

The road in. This is the road Briarwick's cloth comes down. Salt marsh first, then the dyers' river running red, blue and yellow in three bands below the dye-works, then the dead House Thistledown's unmown meadows, then silk.

  • A line of orange Meridian survey flags follows the road up into the wood: "Survey line for the new Lattice. Straight through to the wood. Trees aren't in the plan, but trees rarely are." Juno, at the first flag, quieter than she was two days ago: "These go right toward the Glasswood. That's... probably fine?"
  • The Brinecut salt miner gives the PC TM98 Rock Smash on sight of Dorian's badge. The rocks can be smashed from the second badge on.
  • In the Gossamer Wood, the Bug Catcher twins Mo and Jo fight as a pair: a preview of what Briarwick's Warden will do.

Optional set piece: Thistledown Manor (comic haunted house, on the Lea's hill). The dead Thistledown Players, a ghost acting family, are still rehearsing Hamlet-but-with-Pokémon. Two days after a pageant that was stopped mid-scene, here is a company that never let anything stop the show. The PC must "play a role" in three scenes (choose lines; wrong choices start ghost battles). Reward: Spell Tag and a Litwick. The Manor's matriarch-ghost wants the PC to stay for the second act.

  • Game over GO_CURTAIN_CALL "Curtain Call". Trigger: accept her offer to "join the company forever". Foreshadowing: the butler-ghost mouths don't behind her. Epitaph: "Your notices were excellent. The run has not closed. It never will."

Arrival. Briarwick is a weaving village lashed between trees, with looms clacking and silk drying like flags. There is a shrine to the Loyal Three, the same story the Pageant told, carved in stone, and someone has left a honey bun in front of the Ogre, not the hounds. Children wear carved ogre masks at Fallmorn, and every mask has the same sad face the PC saw step out of a painted backdrop in Saltmere. (Seed for Elowen's legendary arc: the Hollow's masks are the Ogre's.) There is also a Meridian survey line of orange flags marching east, toward a half-built Lattice pylon.

  • A youngster: a boy in a too-big black coat came through yesterday asking about masks, bought a honey-silk bun and was rude about it. (Kestrel, a day ahead and hunting.)

Conflict.

  • The silk-moths are dying. The Glasswood, a crystallizing Bleed, is creeping toward the groves, and it is creeping fastest along the Lattice line.
  • Warden Tamsin Loom (19, anxious, a measuring tape around her neck) is overwhelmed. She is polite, apologetic and lying about something.
  • The first Hollow sabotage. Somebody is cutting the survey flags at night, and the cuts are very clean: a weaver's shears. The PC catches the saboteurs at the pylon base. This is the first admin battle: Pallbearer Thistle (HOLLOW_THISTLE), a grieving ex-weaver, and she is the woman who cut the Lantern Theatre's curtain ropes. In Saltmere the Mourner told a theater to ask its Warden. Thistle tells the PC which question: "Lowmarsh had looms too. Ask your Warden what she signed."
  • On the way out, a wandering old woman at the Loyal Three shrine (actually Celestine, in disguise, unnamed) sings: "Three loyal hounds and an ogre so bold — but who was the thief, when the story was told?" After the Mourner's "poison on their collars", this is the second voice saying the pageant has it backwards. (A seed for Elowen's legendary arc and for Celestine's Act V reveal.)

Gym 2 (:SILKWOOD), a double battle: "a thread holds because it's twisted with others." The Loomhouse is the first real puzzle, and still a friendly one (GYM_PUZZLES Gym 2, SPINE Revision 19): above Granny Loom's looms, the gym is the hollow of Briarwick's elder, strung by Tamsin's Bugs with web trampolines. Taut webs throw you, sticky webs hold you, and two Joltik flip whole strands. Tamsin fights two at a time, because a thread on its own is just string. She battles with nervous fury: "We spun this whole hollow together, the Bugs and me. Don't you dare tear it." Her ace is the Leavanny line.

  • On victory she awards the Weft Badge, and the badge case answers with a second note, in tune with the first. Juno: "It's doing a chord." Tamsin: "I don't think they do that. ...Do they do that?" (Each badge adds a tone. Rook films the fourth.)

Aftermath and revelation. Thistle's accusation sticks. Tamsin confesses to the PC in the loom-loft: Briarwick is bankrupt, and she signed the Lattice contract alone. The free light works, and the looms ran till midnight for a week. The Lattice is also feeding the Glasswood.

  • CHOICE :ch2_tamsin:
  • Expose her publicly at the village meeting. Village trust is shaken and the contract is torn up. The Hollow and Accord gain Standing, and Meridian loses some.
  • Help her confess herself. The slow route: she renegotiates the contract, and Meridian keeps a smaller pylon. She never forgets who stood next to her.
  • Keep her secret. Meridian Standing goes up. The pylon keeps draining Briarwick, Thistle's cell comes back angrier in Ch10 ("You knew"), and in Act V Tamsin can't afford to release her Plate (her Consent condition).
  • Every branch leads to the same next beat.
  • Boss battle, "The Glass Matriarch" (multi-bar, Rejuvenation-style). The Briarwick Cutter will now give the PC Cut ("Saltmere's badge is a theater ticket. Ours is a badge."). Past a Cut tree in the Gossamer Wood, through the Deepwood, lies Cocoonfall Hollow, where a giant glassed Galvantula has woven a nest of crystal silk at the Bleed's heart. Tamsin can't cross the Veil, so she gives the PC her grandmother's shuttle "for luck". Defeating the Matriarch slows the Glasswood's spread (map state change: the Hollow's edge recedes on return in Ch10, and the corded forest road back to Windfall Row opens as a shortcut home). The PC's presence calms the nest's Pokémon afterward.
  • CHOICE :ch2_matriarch: the beaten Matriarch thrashes in the silk-moth grove, shedding crystal.
  • Soothe: stay with it all night. It calms at dawn, but half the grove crystallizes (Harmony).
  • Silence: press your hand to it, and the Imprint drains out of it like water down a drain. The grove is saved, and the Matriarch is left hollow and dull-eyed (Ruin −2). Tamsin, seeing it: "Oh. Oh, that's — thank you. I think."
  • This is the player's first lesson: the efficient choice is the Ruin one.

Optional thread: cameo sidequest "Lost in the Gossamer" (Shelly). See design/CAMEOS.md. After Gym 2, a pink-haired stranger is stuck in the Gossamer Deepwood, apologizing to the Bug Pokémon. It's the first cameo, and it teaches players that the Glass leaks.

Cliffhanger: A Festival poster in Briarwick's square shows the Crown. Its stone is drawn with a tiny chip missing, and someone has circled it in charcoal. The old mural in the chapel shows it whole: "It's painted before," says the chaplain. A child: "Mum says the Crown got hurt once. How do you hurt a crown?" The PC's hand moves, unprompted, to their chest. (Crown seed 3 of 3. The Landing's poster called it a printing fault and Saltmere's prop-maker shrank it. Here it's a wound.) Juno heads home to Verdance with forty silk-moth eggs in a hatbox, and the road goes north out of the Gossamer, where the silk on the last trees is already white with frost.

CHAPTER 4 — "Both Ways" (the Hoar Road → Ebbmouth, Gym 3; K2)

Location: the Hoar Road north out of Briarwick: Spinners' Rise (566), Frostwick Pass (577), the borderland village Frostwick (570), Rimewood Path (578) and the Rimewood (562), then Gullcry Cliffs (561, K2), Gullcry Caves, and Ebbmouth (Isenmar's southern port). Side road: the Frostflat Causeway (560), the salt road back down the coast to Saltmere, chained at the Border Stones until the PC reaches Frostwick. Off it lies The Rehearsal (568, :BLEED), an optional zone where a stretch of road replays the same five seconds of a wagon crash forever.

Borderland. The PC climbs out of the Gossamer and crosses from Elowen into Isenmar through the Rimewood, where the same silk forest froze when the sea did. Mixed wild types, the first fur-coated NPCs, bone toggles. At the Handfast Arch on Frostwick Pass, half whale-jaw and half living briar, someone has bolted a Meridian sunburst over both halves. (Frostwick's Border House stamps the same sunburst over both kingdoms' seals.)

K2 (Gullcry Cliffs, before Gym 3). Kestrel has been hunting a Hollow cell since Saltmere: Thistle's people, running north out of the Gossamer to join the cell in Ebbmouth. He wants the PC out of his way. He is more raw than in K1. He has his new Honedge from his grandmother ("It was your mother's blade's child. Don't you dare lose it."). After the battle:

  • CHOICE :ch4_kestrel_mourner: ask whether he thinks the Mourner is his mother.
  • Kind: Kestrel Bond up a little. He snaps, but later sends a curt note.
  • Blunt: Kestrel Bond down. He shoves past.
  • Silence: neutral. He fills the silence himself: "...She'd never wear a mask. She hated masks."

Arrival. Ebbmouth: fog, gulls, smoked-eel stalls and union halls. The Ebb runs both ways, but lately it stutters, stopping dead for minutes. Mill-wheels freeze mid-turn and dockworkers hold their breath. Meridian's tidal Lattice squats at the river mouth. A strike is brewing: the Ebb Guild is squeezed between Thane Eirik's harbor taxes and Meridian's layoffs.

  • Ice-fishers in the tavern sing about "the Sleeping Whale under the ice". This is a Kyogre seed. ("When the whale wakes, the sea remembers it's a sea.")
  • Get the Good Rod at the Anglers' Guild.

Conflict. Warden Marisol Reyes, elected and brash, is caught in the middle. At midnight Meridian's tidal Lattice runs its night export draw and the river stops entirely for an hour (the cause). A Hollow cell blows the intake to stop the draw, and the river comes back all at once: recklessly, because nobody looked at the water, where a child has taken a punt out on the dead-still river. The punt is dragged at the Guild Mill's race, the race that killed the Reyes siblings' father in AF 297, and the PC, Marisol and the masked cell leader haul the race gate down together in a battle-and-chase (script: story/23_SCRIPT_CH4.md, "The Night the Ebb Stopped"). The cell leader is Teo Reyes (HOLLOW_TEO admin battle), 19 and furious, and he is Marisol's brother. Marisol lets him run. The PC sees it, and a Meridian guard asks the PC, with Marisol standing there, who it was.

  • CHOICE :ch4_teo:
  • Report Teo to the Meridian guard: Meridian Standing up, Marisol's Bond down hard, and Teo is hunted (his Act II arc gets harder).
  • Keep Marisol's secret: Marisol's Bond up, Hollow Standing up a little.
  • Confront Marisol privately: Marisol's Bond up. She admits it, crying and swearing.

Gym 3 (:WATER_SURFACE). Thematic note: a current that changes direction mid-fight. Marisol: "The Ebb runs both ways. Always has. Lately it can't decide." Her ace is Gyarados (from her first Magikarp on the docks). She awards the Tideturn Badge. Afterward she buys the PC smoked eel and says the thing Act I needs said: "Meridian pays my people. Meridian's killing my river. Pick one, kid, I dare you." (Tamsin couldn't pick, and signed. Marisol won't, and swears.)

Revelation. Larch arrives by Gale Post with tide data. The stutters line up exactly with Meridian's Lattice draw peaks, and the full stop with the night export. The Hollow didn't stop the river; they started it, recklessly. "It's not the Hollow stopping the river. It's us. It's my design." She tells the PC she was Meridian's Chief Engineer (not yet why she left). This is the first crack in Larch's guilt, and the start of the red herring that she still works for Meridian.

Cliffhanger: Hesper Vane's letter reaches the PC via the post: "Whoever you are — stay away from my grandson. Everyone who gets close to that boy's mother's ghost gets hurt." Unsigned, but on lighthouse paper.

CHAPTER 5 — "Ten Years of Light" (the Lock Road: The Icefall Locks → Wallshadow Row → Lumen City, Gym 4; the Lowlight Shatter)

Location: the Lock Road up the Ebb and round the Crownwall: the Reedholms (580), the Icecutters' Haul (592), the lock-town Brassfall (590) and the Icefall Locks (581, borderland B), then Elowen's Crownlands on Coppice Ride (595) and Wallshadow Row (594, the Crown Road's south-west arc), then the Arc-Lamp Mile (593, borderland G) into Lumen West Gate (582). Off the road: Voltaic Sluiceworks (:SCRAPYARD, Rotom) and Ebb Hollow (588, :BLEED). Then Lumen City (Zenith's capital district), the Lowlight district (181, replaced by 608 after the Shatter), Meridian Spire.

The road. Isenmar never touches Zenith, so the Lock Road crosses Elowen to get there. The PC climbs the frozen falls of the Icefall Locks, past Meridian's Extraction Lattice No. 4, onto the Crownland downs. At the ride-side shrine on Coppice Ride they see the Crownwall for the first time: a ring of white peaks with Crownhaven inside, where nobody goes without eighteen badges. The star-shaped scar on their chest aches, and they don't know why. Wallshadow Row's tithe barns and the Southgate shrine take the Crown Road round the wall's south side, and then the hundred numbered lamps of the Arc-Lamp Mile run out of the orchards to Lumen's West Gate.

Arrival. The first big-city wow moment: airships, holograms, Rotom delivery drones and a skyline of brass and glass. Everything is free-lit and humming. "Light for Everyone" banners celebrate Lumen's Tenth Year of Light, ten years since the first Lattice switched on.

  • The PC meets Dex (11), a Fizzbolt soda seller outside the Spire. He's talkative and lovely, and he tells you which roof has the best airship view. He's halfway through a story about his sister when he waves the PC off: "Tell you the rest tomorrow!"
  • Topside versus below. Down every alley there are grilles and lift-shafts into Nadir, with grimy air coming up and Hollow Ring graffiti. A Zenith officer moves a Nadir kid along: "Back downstairs."

Rook's gym is closed because he's filming. The PC helps Rook Calder with a blackout in the Sluiceworks (wild Rotom swarm) and earns his attention. He's hyper, a little lonely, and constantly on camera: "Chat says you're cute. Chat also says you're gonna lose."

Gym 4 (:NEON_GRID). Thematic note: circuits you complete with your own body. Rook's ace is Rotom (his camera drone, in battle form). He awards the Arclight Badge and gives the PC Flash. He's also the first person to notice the badge case pulse brighter on the fourth badge, the fourth note of a chord that started in Saltmere. He films it: "Ooh, special edition?"

The Gala (main set piece). Voss invites the PC, Juno, Rook and Larch (Larch refuses at first, then comes to keep an eye on things) to Meridian Spire's Tenth Year Gala.

  • Champagne, airships outside the windows and the Dark Stone core glowing black in the atrium shaft. (Zekrom seed: guests swear it "breathes".)
  • Voss's speech: "They'll tell you light is a gift. Light is work. Every lamp in this city was lit by someone who was told to be grateful for the dark." It's genuinely stirring.
  • Valen Corrigan is present. White robes, grey glove, grave and courteous. He speaks briefly with Voss and with nobody else.
  • Larch, murmuring to the PC: "The Zap Plate's not in Rook's gym, you know. It's here. In their vault." Rook, overhearing, goes very quiet.

The raid.

  • Lights flicker. The Hollow breach the Spire through Nadir's service lifts. Partner battle: PC + Juno vs two Bereaved Pallbearers' squads, the first tag battle.
  • The PC pursues them down to the Plate Vault and arrives in time to see it go wrong. The Mourner reaches the Zap Plate's cradle, but Sable (masked, Hollow-grey, cheerful) slaps a Splitter charge on the Plate. The Mourner lunges for it.
  • The Shatter. A white-violet blast. The Plate cracks. The Mourner catches it barehanded and his glove smokes: "No — no — what did you do?" (To Sable. The player will read it as aimed at the PC or at himself.) Sable is gone. The Mourner sees the PC, drops the cracked Plate into its cradle, and flees.
  • Boss battle, "Overcharged" (multi-bar): a Bleed-maddened Electivire, swollen with the Shatter's discharge, blocks the vault door. The field flips mid-battle from :NEON_GRID to :BLEED, the first scripted any→BLEED transition.
  • Game over GO_LIVE_WIRE "Live Wire". Trigger: during the Electivire fight's interlude prompt, choose "Grab the cracked Plate and run". Foreshadowing: the Mourner's smoking glove a moment earlier, and Rook's shout, "Don't touch it with your hands!" Epitaph: "Even you weren't made to hold lightning bare."

Aftermath: the Lowlight.

  • The Spire's shadow-district has been hit by the Shatter wave. Twelve people are Fixed in glass mid-motion: a woman hanging laundry, a man mid-laugh, and Dex, mid-wave, soda crate on his hip.
  • The PC can walk through the Lowlight's Veil (map 608, :BLEED) when no one else can. They are the only one who can stand among the glass. NPCs watch them do it.
  • Rook, off-camera, shaking: "...Turn it off. Rotom. Turn it off."
  • Voss restores the light. Meridian crews reroute the grid in under an hour, and Lumen sees Voss on every screen, in shirtsleeves, carrying a glassed child's soda crate out of the Lowlight himself. He's a hero. (He means it, and he did it. Both are true.)
  • Valen walks into the Lowlight's edge, removes his glove for a moment to touch the Veil, and the player glimpses crystal. Then he sees the PC standing inside. "You were in the Lowlight when it went? And you're... standing." He looks a beat too long, then turns away.
  • Valen's broadcast that night grants Meridian the Mandate: security powers wherever Lattices stand. "Velmora endures."

CHOICE :ch5_lowlight_testimony: a Directorate officer asks what the PC saw.

  • "The Mourner broke the Plate" (what it looked like): Meridian Standing up, Hollow Standing down, and the Mandate passes with a bigger majority (flavor).
  • "Someone else was there" (the masked second figure): Hollow Standing up, Meridian Standing down a little. Marchetti makes a note of the PC's name. Larch quietly says "good".
  • "I don't know": neutral.
  • If the PC said "The Mourner broke the Plate", Dorian reads it in the papers in Saltmere: "So you told them the pageant version. I know that one by heart." This seeds his Act V refusal: he keeps the lie he knows, and won't release the Blank Plate. (He was the first Warden who trusted the PC, which is why it stings.)

Revelation. Larch, in the ruined vault at 3 a.m. with a borrowed scanner: "That wasn't the Hollow's hammer. Look at the stress lines. The Plate was already cracking. Something's been drinking from it for ten years." She looks up at the Lattice conduits. "Something I built."

INTERLUDE I — "Lamplight" (playable as Kestrel).

  • Ferrow's Landing lighthouse, the same night. The player controls Kestrel on the gallery while Hesper sleeps.
  • He finds his mother's old Ghost Warden's veil in a trunk.
  • A short memory plays: Kestrel, age 6, in a crowd, his mother in a veil running toward "a kid made of light". He wakes before he sees the rest.
  • Mini-battle: Kestrel vs a wild Bleed-touched Haunter on the lighthouse stairs. He talks to his Honedge like a person.
  • It ends with him packing a bag. "If you're alive, I'll find you."

END OF ACT I. Title card: II — Imprints.

Story Bible 05: Act II — Imprints (Ch6–9, Gyms 5–8)

Tone: Reborn-grey. The cost of Velmora's miracles becomes visible: company towns, Fixing wards, a street drug, an act of terror, and an unmasking that hurts someone you like. Humor stays, but it's gallows humor now. Conventions as in 04 (CHOICE / GO / map names per WORLD.md). Revision 6: this act carries beats of the Ashkaar–Isenmar War and the Blessing. See 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING.md (timeline table) for the inserts per chapter; that file wins on conflicts.

Act-opening beat (start of segment 4): the PC leaves Lumen City through the Lowlight (Shattered) (608, :BLEED). A shrine of soda cans and candles has grown around Dex's glass figure. If the PC stands with him, the shard hums and the glass warms slightly under their hand. (Harmony seed for the Good ending's waking.) Mandate checkpoints with Directorate officers in white-and-gold now stand at every lift down to Nadir.

Revision 7 (comedy): each chapter here has a scripted funny scene in 15_COMEDY.md §4 (Ch6–9), plus running gags (§3) and optional kingdom bits (§5). Place each scene where its heading says, and never inside the beats §1 lists as joke-free.

CHAPTER 6 — "What the Sand Keeps" (the Brass Road: Candle Down → The Highwold → The Brass Dunes → Static Tunnels → Duneholt, Gym 5; Ossuary of Dunes; K3)

Location: the Brass Road north out of Lumen: the Meridian Mainline (612, borderland G) off the plateau, then Elowen's Crown Road round the Crownwall's east and north, Candle Down (602) and the Highwold (603), then the Brass Dunes (600, borderland C) with Copperdune (610) and Static Tunnels (604/605, Flash), the Rib Road (601, :DESERT) and Sunbleach Flats (613) to Duneholt (Ossaria). Past the city: the Marrow Road (620) with the Ossuary of Dunes (Unown ruins, Strength), and Sinkfield (628).

Borderland: Zenith and Ossaria don't touch, so the road crosses Elowen. The Mainline's cutting drops off the plateau into the Crownlands, and the Crown Road takes the PC round the Crownwall: Candle Down's pilgrim cairns, with a view into the wall's one gap, then the Highwold's chalk and skylarks north of the wall. The downs give way to the Brass Dunes, where the railway ran into the sand, and then to Ossaria, the Bone Sands. Fossil ribs as big as houses poke from the dunes. Caravan-houses pitch tents in the lee of them. NPCs quote prices in "bones".

Arrival. Duneholt is sandstone terraces around a great sinking well. The aquifer the Earth Plate holds in the stone is collapsing under Meridian's deep drills, and every week the waterline drops another rung. The Prince-Elector's men post notices: "By license of His Excellency Idris Kassan, the Concord deep-works are a protected enterprise." Caravan-mothers curse at them.

  • Sahar's Dig Lab: fossil revival opens here. Ossaria is fossil country, so a wide selection is available, and Sahar is delighted by anyone who brings her bones.
  • Under the town, the ground is warm. Children say "the sleeping red giant" is turning over in its bed. (A Groudon seed.)

Conflict.

  • A drill-site explodes. The Hollow freed Pokémon that Meridian had been using as living drill-cores (Excadrill and Drilbur fitted with Lattice collars). The Directorate arrives with the Mandate's new powers and starts arresting caravan kids.
  • CHOICE :ch6_drillsite:
  • Help the Hollow get the freed Pokémon into the dunes: Hollow Standing up, Meridian Standing down. Directorate ambushes follow in Ch7.
  • Help the Directorate secure the site: Meridian Standing up, and you earn a "commendation" (a lightly sinister Key Item: a Mandate Pass that later opens checkpoints).
  • Get Sahar to invoke the Warden's right of sanctuary over the children: Accord Standing goes up and the Directorate backs off, furious. (Choosing the Directorate here is Sahar's Consent refusal in Act V.)

Gym 5 (:DESERT). Thematic note: dig down, because what you need is buried. Sahar is patient, dry and coughing: "The desert keeps everything. It just doesn't keep it where you left it." Her ace is Claydol. She awards the Sandglass Badge and gives Strength via her excavators.

Aftermath and revelation: the Ossuary of Dunes (Unown ruins set piece).

  • The latest dune-shift has uncovered a doorway in a giant fossil skull on the Marrow Road.
  • Sahar goes pale. She has seen this before. She confesses: in AF 281 she excavated these ruins, reported them to Valen, and resealed them on his order.
  • Inside, Unown drift in the walls. The PC solves Unown-script puzzles (World/puzzle team) and reveals murals: 1. A golden king, the Gilded King. 2. Two titans, one red and one blue, tearing the land ("the Year of Two Weathers"). 3. A chain of eighteen golden locks around a radiant beast of eighteen lights. 4. The beast breaking apart, with lights falling like rain and a city crumbling into the sea.
  • Sahar takes a rubbing: the Duneholt Rubbing (Key Item). "I buried the truth once because I was told to. The sand dug it up. I'd rather not argue with sand twice."
  • A boss-grade guardian (a giant Unown-swarm "glyph" formation) defends the deepest chamber. It's an optional multi-bar fight that rewards an Unown and the Unown Report.

K3 (after Gym 5, at the Ossuary exit). Kestrel has been following the Hollow's trail from Ebbmouth and arrived in time to see the murals over the PC's shoulder.

  • After the battle he finally says it aloud: "Everyone keeps telling me to let it go. My mother had a seat, and a Plate, and a city that loved her. Then one night she had nothing. Let what go?" He lays out the rumor running all over Velmora: the Mourner is Morwen Vane, alive. "She wasn't killed by the Bleed. She was made to disappear."
  • CHOICE :ch6_kestrel_rumor:
  • Encourage him to find out (Kestrel Bond up, and his obsession grows).
  • Warn him it might not be her (Bond down a little now, but it pays off at Ironreach, where he remembers you warned him).
  • Silence.

Game over GO_SINKFIELD "Sinkfield". Sinkfield (628) is a Bleed zone where the collapsing aquifer and the Earth Imprint have made the sand behave like water. Trigger: ignore Sahar's three warnings ("walk the bones, never the sand") and step off the fossil path to grab a glinting item. Foreshadowing: the Field Notes entry and a caravan-boy's lost sandal sinking slowly. Epitaph: "The desert kept you. Somewhere else."

Cliffhanger: A Gale Post courier finds the PC with a letter from Juno: "Uncle Rowan's been 'away on Warden business' every time something happens. I'm being silly. Come to Mirefen? I'm helping Dr. Mott with his seed-medicine. Bring snacks."

CHAPTER 7 — "The Quiet Ward" (the Leach Road: The Leach Canyons → Wormwood Lea → The Gutterfall → Mirefen, Gym 6; J2)

Location: the Leach Road down the River Leach: the Marrow Road (620), the Kneeling Stones (632, Ossaria's crossroads), the Leach Canyons (621, borderland D) with Charwell (630), then Elowen's Wormwood Lea (634) east of the Crown, and the Gutterfall (633, borderland F) down into Nadir. Mirefen (Nadir, :CORROSIVE_MIRE), the Quiet Ward, the Sump Barons' Sweet Market, Leechman's Walk, Miasma Caverns, Weeping Fen (648), Lake Sallow (Surf after the badge).

Arrival: first descent into Nadir.

  • The PC rides a rattling lift-cage down the Gutterfall, beside the blue waterfall where the Leach drops off the Crownland edge and Zenith's outfall pours in from the plateau's north cliff. Under the overhang the sky disappears, and Zenith's underside is a ceiling of pipes dripping slag. The air tastes of pennies. Rebreathers are for sale on every corner.
  • Hollow Ring graffiti is everywhere, often beside a painted Ogre in the Mask (Nadir's folk-saint).
  • Mirefen is stilt-houses over a marsh that glows blue at night: Zenith's Lattice runoff mixing with the Toxic Plate's mire, the "poison-blue moon" of the rhyme.
  • This is the best street food in Velmora (bog coffee, slag-fried noodles), and people are kinder here than topside.

Conflict: Corvin and the Ward.

  • Warden Corvin Mott is gaunt, in a plague-doctor half-mask, and wickedly funny. He runs the Infirmary and its Quiet Ward: forty patients at Fixing stages 2–3, some humming, some half-glass, one a child whose hair has turned to salt.
  • His apprentice Wenlow (17) is cheerful and clumsy, and introduces the PC to every patient by name. (Players should love Wenlow. Wenlow dies in Ch16.)
  • Sweetrot. Pastel mochi-like sweets sold in the Sweet Market by smiling vendors of the Sump Barons (Mother Gutter's people). Users go docile, loyal and blissful, and they keep coming back. Corvin's other ward is full of Sweetrot addicts. "It's not a drug. It's a leash." This is the Pecharunt seed: the sweets have a faint peach-and-poison smell, and a child's rhyme mentions "the peach that keeps you".
  • Game over GO_SWEET_TOOTH "Sweet Tooth". Trigger: accept Sweetrot from a vendor three times across the chapter (each offer gets more insistent; Wenlow's warning comes after the first). Epitaph: "You were so happy. You never wondered why again."

J2.

  • Juno is in the Infirmary helping Corvin brew seed-medicine from Verdance stock. She is luminous with purpose.
  • Alphabetizing his ledgers, she finds an entry from the night of the Lumen Shatter: "R.A. — 2nd-degree Bleed-burn, right palm and fingers. Lightning pattern. Discretion." Corvin snatches it back too quickly.
  • Juno laughs it off ("R.A., there's loads of R.A.s") and challenges the PC to a spar on the stilt-walk to shake off the feeling (J2). Mid-battle line: "He wouldn't. He wouldn't."
  • CHOICE :ch7_ledger:
  • Say "Rowan Ashby" out loud: Juno's Bond drops sharply and she storms off. At Ironreach she is less shattered, because she already knew. This becomes a branch flavor in J3.
  • Reassure her: Juno's Bond goes up. The unmasking hits her full-force.
  • Ask Corvin directly, privately. He says only, "I'm a doctor. I treat hands. I don't ask whose."

Hollow admin: Brother Wick (HOLLOW_WICK).

  • The PC tracks a Hollow medicine-runner to a drowned chapel on the edge of the Weeping Fen, a Bleed zone where rain falls upward and every puddle weeps.
  • Brother Wick is old, half-blind and gentle, and he's here to bless dying Bereaved. He fights only because the PC forces it, or the PC can talk him down if Hollow Standing is high enough or they chose kindly in Ch5 (no battle).
  • After the battle (or the talk) he explains the Wound Doctrine: "The Choir teaches that the Plates were a gift. Child, nobody bleeds for three hundred years from a gift." Then, more quietly, something new: "The Mourner doesn't want to break them anymore. He wants to carry them home. But you can't carry what you can't hold." He looks at the PC's chest and doesn't say why.

Gym 6 (:CORROSIVE_MIRE), a double battle. Thematic note: poison is a dose; the right amount heals. Corvin: "Don't worry. I'm a doctor. I know exactly how much this hurts." His ace is Toxapex. He awards the Remedy Badge, and the Mirefen ferrymen give the PC Surf.

The Ward Night (key event; creator-approved 2026-11-21, design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md proposal B). After the gym, Corvin and the PC drink bog coffee on the Infirmary roof. Every screen in Nadir flickers: Sable, unmasked mouth, cheerful: "The Mourner's gone soft. The Hammer hasn't. Cindervault's next. Light for everyone, right?" As she speaks, the Infirmary's lamps die: the Hammer has cut the Gutterfall junction that runs the Quiet Ward's dampers. The ward's Bleed rises into a Veil across its door; Corvin and Wenlow can't go in. The PC can. They carry out Ama, the nine-year-old with salt hair Wenlow introduced by name, and under the clear salt her eyes are moving. Juno gets the peat-fired seed-medicine stills onto the damper coils and the Veil sinks back. On the roof afterwards, Corvin: "Do you know why nobody in my Ward is dead? They're not dying. They're dreaming. You saw it too. Two's a study." (This seeds the Good ending's waking and Venam's testimony; the Hammer is now the Hollow's enemy on screen. Script: story/26_SCRIPT_CH7.md.)

Optional thread: cameo sidequest "Sewer Royalty" (Venam). See design/CAMEOS.md. A loud punk girl with a Seviper has fallen through a sewer mirror into Mirefen's runoff tunnels, and she is helping Wenlow drag Sweetrot addicts to the Infirmary. Completing it earns Venam's Testimony, a recording of her account of being turned to stone and coming back ("I could hear everything"). It counts as one of the Envoy's proofs in Ch20 and can be played for Juno in Ch10.

Cliffhanger: Morning. On every wall in Mirefen the Hollow Ring has been painted over with a hammer, and under one of them somebody has chalked: "NOT OURS. — the Hollow". Sable's "Cindervault's next" is Chapter 8's hook.

CHAPTER 8 — "The Light Stone" (Leechman's Walk → Lake Sallow → Cindervault, Gym 7; the Caldera Crisis)

Location: the Sulfur Road: Leechman's Walk (640), Lake Sallow (641, Surf, borderland E) with Scaldwater (650) and Lantern Isle (optional, :BEACH), then the Pyre Road (652) up into Ashkaar. Cindervault (:VOLCANIC), the Cinderhorn (664–666), Emberfall (668), the Ashmarch (:ASHEN_WASTE after the crisis).

Borderland: past Lake Sallow's sulfur shallows, still Elowen ground, the land climbs into Ashkaar, the Dragonfire Dominion: black basalt, red lacquer banners and dragon-riders overhead. Oaths are sworn over braziers at every gate. Lying to a Dominion guard is a crime, and an early NPC teaches this ("Say true or say nothing, stranger").

Arrival. Cindervault is a forge-city inside the Cinderhorn's caldera. Lava-channels for quenching, smithies stacked up the crater walls, the Hearthguild's bells.

  • Warden Brann Holloway is a giant, booming and sentimental. He drops his hammer to bear-hug Larch, an old friend, and then the PC for good measure.
  • Two crises: 1. Meridian's geothermal tap at the caldera floor is overdrawing the Flame Plate's Imprint. The magma is rising, and the forges run too hot to work. 2. The Dominar's envoys are in town demanding the Light Stone, the Hearthguild's ancestral relic (Reshiram), "for the throne of Ashkaar, as is right." Brann refuses on Concordance grounds.
  • First appearance of Sigrun Ashfall, the Dragon Warden. She arrives on a Salamence to mediate between Brann and her father's envoys. She is fierce and curt, and she treats the PC with frank appraisal: "So you're the ferry child everyone's whispering about. Hm. Smaller than I expected." She calls the Dominar "my father" exactly once, in a tone that ends conversations.

Gym 7 (:VOLCANIC). Thematic note: a forge you can stoke or quench, changing the field's heat level as you go. Brann: "Some things you forge to last. Some things you forge to break right — that's the harder craft." His ace is Coalossal.

The Caldera Crisis (set piece). The tap's pressure spikes, and the caldera will erupt within the hour. Three groups converge on the caldera floor:

  • Wick's Hollow faithful, with a plan to vent the pressure by quenching the Imprint with Lake Sallow water piped through the old lava-channels. It's safe but drastic: it turns the caldera to ash for a season.
  • Dr. Percival Quent's Meridian team, who want to install "dampers" and keep the tap running. Meridian admin battle: Quent (MERIDIAN_QUENT), giggling: "Oh, it's you. The null reading! Hold still, I've only got one probe."
  • The Hammer: a Bereaved squad planting a Splitter on the tap to cause an eruption "Meridian can't cover up".
  • CHOICE :ch8_caldera:
  • Help Wick vent. The battle field transitions :VOLCANIC → :ASHEN_WASTE. The eruption is averted and the forges go cold for months, and Brann grumbles about it for a season. Hollow Standing goes up, Meridian Standing down. The Ashmarch becomes ash.
  • Help Quent's dampers. The eruption is averted, Meridian Standing goes up and the tap keeps running. The Bleed at Emberfall grows (map state), and Brann's Bond goes up ("You kept my forges lit").
  • Shut the tap down by force (a harder fight vs Quent plus Directorate). The eruption is averted, Accord Standing goes up and the Dominar is impressed (DOMINAR respect +1). Meridian Standing drops hard.
  • Game over GO_LET_THEM_LISTEN "Let Them Listen". Trigger: a Hammer bomber hands the PC the detonator and says "Do it. They'll finally listen." The PC accepts. Foreshadowing: the Field Notes entry on Shatters, and the Lowlight's glass. Epitaph: "They listened. There was no one left to tell."

Aftermath: the Light Stone.

  • After the crisis, the Dominar's envoys try to seize the Light Stone in the confusion, and Sigrun stops them herself.
  • CHOICE :ch8_lightstone:
  • Back Brann in keeping it under the Hearthguild. The Dominar's grudge grows.
  • Suggest it go to Sigrun at Wyrmrest, neutral ground under a Warden: Sigrun's Bond up, Accord Standing up. This seeds DOMINAR_SWAYED, because the Dominar respects his daughter's claim more than Brann's.
  • Say it should go to the Dominar ("it's his people's"): Ashkaar's favor goes up and Accord Standing drops. Brann is hurt, and in Act V he won't release the Flame Plate "for a man who gave the Light Stone away" (his Consent refusal). Late payoff: Reshiram's trial at Wyrmrest is harder.

Revelation. Brann, drunk and maudlin over chestnuts, lets slip one sentence: "I reset the Crown's stone myself, y'know. After the accident. Ten years back. It was smaller than it should've been." Then he catches himself: "Ach, I'm an old fool. Forget it." The PC's shard throbs once. (Larch notices the PC wince.)

The Ring-Day (withdrawn from Ch8 by SPINE Revision 21; it is now in Ch14, Bastian's lamp-room in Cragholm, 07_ACT_IV. What stays in Ch8 is the chestnut slip above, the clue it pays off. The old text below is a record only.) (next morning, Hearthguild Hall; SPINE Revision 20). Sober, Brann gives the PC a Warden's ring (the Mega Ring) and an Aggronite: Mega Evolution opens. The ring's colourless chip is grind off the Crown's own stone, and this ring is the odd one out: he cut it "ten years back" and it has "sulked on every hand" he's tried it on. In the PC's palm it sings, and something under their ribs answers. "They don't sing. Thirty years at this anvil." Larch lowers her book. He lies about it out loud and admits it's a lie. The opening line follows :ch8_caldera. Script: 22_SCRIPT_CH8.md; lore: design/MEGA_EVOLUTION.md §1. (Brann names neither the Legend Plate nor the reset: 09_MYSTERIES #5/#6 stay for Ch15–17.)

Cliffhanger: The Dominar's herald reads a proclamation in the caldera square: Ashkaar holds Zenith responsible for the "assault on the Flame" and closes the eastern passes to Meridian. War-drums. Sigrun, watching her father's banner, says nothing at all.

CHAPTER 9 — "The Iron Conclave" (the Iron Road: The Ashmarch → The Ironway → Candle Down → The Long Drop → Ironreach, Gym 8; K4; the Conclave; the Mourner unmasked)

Location: the Iron Road west out of the Dominion: the Ashmarch (660), the Ironway (661, :MOUNTAIN, borderland E), Candle Down (602) on the Crown Road, then the Long Drop (672, borderland F), the shaft road down under Zenith's west rim. Optional: the war road north from Cindervault's north gate (the Cinderglass Barrens 662, Glasswake 670, the Wyrmtongue 673 to Cinder Cape Warfort; 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING). Ironreach (Nadir, :COLOSSEUM), the Iron Pit, the Conclave galleries, the old Aurel mine shafts.

Arrival. Ironreach is Nadir's pit-fighting quarter, carved into Aurel-era mine shafts. The Fist Plate makes everyone strong, and arguments are settled in chalk circles. It's loud, sweaty and honest. Warden Kaito Ren (ex-Wardguard captain, laconic, wrapped hands) is the only former Accord soldier Nadir trusts.

  • The Conclave. Sovereign Valen has called a rare Accord Conclave here, the first held in Nadir in a century, to vote on extending the Mandate realm-wide. Every available Warden is present.
  • Introductions/reunions: Dorian, Tamsin, Marisol, Rook, Sahar, Corvin, Brann, Sigrun, Rowan (who embraces Juno; his right hand is bandaged, "Kettle", and his ring finger is bare, "Being sized"), and Odessa Gale herself, who delivers Fly in person from a skiff she lands on the Pit's rim ("Courier's privilege").
  • First sightings (Revision 5: these Wardens must be met before the Festival):
    • Ysolde Ashgrave, veiled, watches Kestrel across the Pit and leaves before he sees her.
    • Nyx Calloway is "slumming it" in the observers' gallery and buys the PC a drink they're too young for.
    • Celestine Aubade, barefoot and openly herself this time, smiles at the PC: "We've met. You didn't know it yet."
    • Anja Sorrel arrives with her brother's envoy and complains about the heat.
    • Bastian Ore pretends to be deaf to Hollis for the whole session.
  • Each Warden gets one line. Their full chapters come later.
  • Chancellor Hollis presides.
  • Kings' envoys sit in the "observers' gallery", and the Elowen and Ashkaar envoys refuse to sit next to each other.

The Ironreach Open, K4. The Iron Pit's open tournament runs during the Conclave as entertainment. Nadir loves it. The PC fights through brackets of pit-fighters (trainer gauntlet) to the final vs Kestrel (K4).

  • Kestrel is here because rumor says the Mourner will strike the Conclave. He wants to be closest when it happens.
  • The crowd chants for "the null kid".

Gym 8 (:COLOSSEUM). Thematic note: the crowd's roar is a stat; earn it. Kaito: "Stand up. Again." His ace is Lucario. After the battle, quietly: "A fist is a promise. Don't make one you won't keep."

The attack.

  1. During the Mandate vote, the galleries go dark. The Hammer has rigged the Fist Plate's reliquary, which was brought up for the Conclave's oath, with Splitters. Sable's voice on the pit speakers: "Vote yes on the Mandate. Go on. Give them the leash. We'll give you a reason."
  2. Partner battle: PC + Kestrel vs Sable + Hammer Captain Brisk. Sable escapes into the shafts.
  3. The PC pushes up to the Pit's upper ring and finds the Mourner standing over the reliquary. He's not planting the charge; he's trying to disarm it. But the player doesn't know that yet.
  4. The Mourner battle (HOLLOW_MOURNER). Boss: Trevenant (multi-bar), with a Shiftry and Cacturne escort. The Mourner fights defensively. He keeps saying "Not now — you don't understand — get BACK."
  5. The partial Shatter. The charge goes off anyway, and half the Fist Plate's Imprint bursts. The field in the reliquary chamber flips to :BLEED. Glass races across the stone toward the gallery, where Juno is shielding a child (Nell, the Open's chalk-girl, met at the bracket).
  6. The Mourner throws himself in the way. His Trevenant's roots tear up through the floor to wall off the glass, and his mask takes the burst and cracks in half.
  7. Juno, three meters away: "...Uncle Rowan?"
  8. Rowan, bleeding and half-glassed at the shoulder: "Juno. Don't look at me like that. Look at the flowers. Look at what they're standing on."
  9. The PC is the only one who can walk into the Bleed to pull Rowan out. Everyone, Valen included, watches them do it.

CHOICE :ch9_teo_sable (the act's big choice). Through the smoke the PC sees two things at once:

  • Teo Reyes is pinned under fallen scaffolding at the Bleed's edge. He came with Rowan to stop the Hammer, and he is Fixing fast.
  • Sable is running for a Meridian service lift with a comm-device in her hand.

The PC has time for one:

  • Save Teo (TEO_SAVED). Teo lives, glassed fingers and all, and Marisol's Bond goes way up. Sable escapes clean, and her Meridian link has to be proven later and at higher cost (Ch13 via Ilsa/Nyx).
  • Chase Sable (IRONREACH_EVIDENCE). A short chase battle through the shafts. The PC tears the comm-device from her belt: Meridian Special Accounts encryption, and a voice on it saying "Kroll, report." Teo dies in the Bleed, half-glass, reaching for his sister. Marisol's line in Ch13: "He was nineteen. Nineteen. Tell me again how the Hollow are the monsters."

Aftermath.

  • Meridian Directorate officers take Rowan into Meridian custody, not the Accord's, under the Mandate, which just passed in the chaos. Marchetti: "Mandate jurisdiction, Sovereign." Valen allows it.
  • Kestrel stares at Rowan's face for a long time. "...It's not her." He doesn't know whether he's relieved. He walks away into the shafts.
  • If the PC warned him in Ch6: "You said it might not be. I hate that you were right."
  • Juno sits on the Pit's floor in the glass dust. She won't speak to anyone except, if :ch3_juno_talk was kind, the PC.
  • CHOICE :ch9_rowan_words: as Rowan is led away, he looks to the PC. Answer:
  • "Why?": he says, "Ask the Drowned Crown."
  • "I'll look after her": he says, "I know. That's why I'm not afraid."
  • Silence: he says, "You saw what I saw. In the Lowlight. Didn't you?"

Each sets a small Rowan Bond and colors his tribunal in Ch13.

Optional thread: cameo sidequest "Two Lucarios" (Garret). See design/CAMEOS.md. In the Ironreach Open's undercard, a gruff stranger with a Lucario asks every pit-fighter about a missing girl named Eden. It's available after the Conclave, in the shafts below the Pit.

Revelation. Valen crosses the ruined Pit to the PC, whose shoulder is dusted with glass that isn't hurting them. He looks at the glass, then at the PC.

"Come to Verdance. There's a seat to fill — and I think you should see what it costs."

He leaves. Brann, at his elbow, looks back at the PC with an expression of pure grief.

Game over GO_PULL_THE_NAIL "Pull the Nail". Available only if Hollow Standing is high. Before the attack, Sable approaches the PC in the shafts: "You can walk in the Bleed. You could plant it where no one else can reach." Accepting leads to the Shatter in full, and Juno is Fixed. Foreshadowing: Wick's Ch7 line ("he wants to carry them home") and Sable's broadcast. Epitaph: "You pulled the nail. The whole house came down."

INTERLUDE II — "The Bride Tree" (playable as Rowan, as a flashback that plays after the unmasking).

  • Five days before the Conclave (the Root Road takes that long). Verdance's Heartgarden. The player controls Rowan as he waters the Bride Tree.
  • Gentle walk-and-talk with the tree, which is Elin: "The roses are coming in again. They don't stop, love. They never stop."
  • Mini-scene: he shows the healed Phantump from Ch1, now a Trevenant, the bark mask, and the lily he picks from her branches every time.
  • Before the mask, he twists off his Warden's ring and seals it into an envelope with his Warden's testament, addressed to the Sovereign, and leaves it for the Gale Post. ("A mask can't hide a Warden's ring.") This is how the ring and the seat reach Juno in Ch10, and why the Mourner never Mega Evolves.
  • It ends with him folding the mask into his coat, lily-side in: "One more. Then I'll find the other way. I promise." (He walks into the Conclave unmasked, as the Grass Warden, and puts the mask on at Ironreach. Script: story/27_SCRIPT_CH9.md.)

END OF ACT II. Title card: III — Fault Lines.

Spoilers ahead: this chapter covers late-game twists.

Story Bible 06: Act III — Fault Lines (Ch10–13, Gyms 9–12)

Tone: Desolation begins. Political fracture, kingdoms arming, a city sinking, a mentor framed, a rival curdling. The PC is now known, and everyone wants something. Each chapter ends worse than it began. Conventions as in 04. Map names per WORLD.md (segments 8–11). Revision 6: this act carries beats of the Ashkaar–Isenmar War and the Blessing. See 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING.md (timeline table) for the inserts per chapter; that file wins on conflicts.

Act-opening state: the Mandate is realm-wide. Directorate checkpoints stand at every kingdom border, and Meridian scanners at every Pokémon Center door now flag the PC's NULL reading with a polite "Fellowship Priority Guest" banner. Even being watched is courteous.

Revision 7 (comedy): each chapter here has a scripted funny scene in 15_COMEDY.md §4 (Ch10–13), plus running gags (§3) and optional kingdom bits (§5). Place each scene where its heading says, and never inside the beats §1 lists as joke-free.

CHAPTER 10 — "The Seat That Blooms" (the Root Road: The Rootdeep Lift Road → Prism Falls → The Briarway → Verdance, Gym 9; J3)

Location:

  • The Root Road: the Tailings (692) outside Ironreach, then the Rootdeep (680, borderland F), whose great freight-lift, the Rootdeep Lift Road, hauls ore from Nadir's mines up to Elowen's downs west of the plateau, past Lanternroot (690). Then across the Crown Road to Prism Falls (681, :RAINBOW) and the Briarway (693), the royal road to Verdance.
  • Grudgestone Quarry, Echo Coliseum (688, :BLEED: Ironreach's attack replaying as ghost-sound).
  • Verdance (Elowen's royal seat, :FLOWER_GARDEN), Briar Keep (the Queen's castle on the highest terrace), the Heartgarden, the Bride Grove (708), the Royal Chase (Safari-style reserve).
  • Branch maps by Standing: 698 Hollow Sanctuary (high Hollow) or 699 Meridian Black Site (high Meridian).

Branch scene on the Lift Road:

  • High Hollow Standing: Brother Wick's runner leads the PC to the Hollow Sanctuary in Grudgestone Quarry. The leaderless faithful are in hiding. Wick teaches the missing verse of the Hymn early (Key Item fragment), and gives the PC a letter for Rowan's jailers (WICK'S LETTER, delivered in Ch13). Thistle is in custody since Lumen (Ch5); her people speak for her.
  • High Meridian Standing: Calla Wren invites the PC to tour the Meridian Black Site, "a Fellowship privilege". It holds Project NULL: a Type: Null in a containment cradle that reacts to the PC exactly the way the badge case does. Quent: "It's modeled on something. We're not allowed to say what." The PC can leave with the Type: Null (Bond event). It's an unsettling gift.
  • Neither: a short scene of refugees climbing the Lift Road from Nadir with everything they own.

Arrival: Elowen, second visit (escalation).

  • Verdance is drowning in flowers. The Meadow Plate has no Warden, and its Imprint has burst its banks. Roses grow through cobbles, vines pull down gutters, and pollen hangs so thick the Pokémon Center hands out masks. It is beautiful and horrifying.
  • Under the bloom, the soil is grey. Nothing rots.
  • Three claimants for the Meadow Plate: 1. Queen Maelis has sent her Thornguard to occupy the Heartgarden: "the Plate lies on Crown soil." 2. Meridian offers "temporary custody for public safety". Prince Caedmon smiles beside the Meridian delegate. 3. Rowan's sealed Warden's testament, opened by Valen, names Juno Hale heir. His Warden's ring is sealed in with it (Interlude II); Valen puts it in her hand.
  • Valen presides from the Heartgarden steps. Juno is terrified. "I didn't want this seat. I wanted him in it."
  • Tamsin has come up from Briarwick to stand with Juno, the first small-town Warden to join what the press is calling the Greenward.
  • If :ch2_tamsin was "keep secret", Thistle's people (Lowmarsh weavers; Thistle herself is in custody since Ch5) heckle Tamsin ("You knew"), and the PC must defuse it.

The Bride Tree.

  • In the Heartgarden stands the Bride Tree, a flowering tree in a woman's shape, arms raised, in permanent blossom. Juno tells the PC the truth: it's her Aunt Elin, Fixed in AF 288. Rowan watered her every dawn.
  • Juno: "Sometimes I think she's listening. Isn't that stupid?"
  • If the PC carries Venam's Testimony (cameo sidequest, Ch7), they can play it for her under the tree: "I could hear everything. Everyone who sat with me." Juno sits down in the petals and talks to her aunt for the first time in years. (This sets up the Good ending's waking. Without it, Corvin's Ch7 line carries the same idea, more quietly.)

Juno's Warden trial (set piece). A Warden is confirmed when the Plate accepts them. Juno must walk to the Meadow Plate at the Bride Tree's roots, in the Bride Grove (708), the sunken grove at the foot of the stone stair under the Bride Tree, where the Plate lies in the roots in plain sight. Since Rowan fell it is choked with bloom and Bleed-adjacent, so the PC must clear the way inside the Veil, then guide Juno along the one safe path.

  • Ogerpon: in the Grove the PC meets the "Gossamer Ogre", Ogerpon in its mask. It has been guarding the Bride Tree since AF 288, which is why nothing ever got close enough to harm Elin.
  • Boss battle, "The Loyal Three" (multi-bar, a triple-boss sequence). Okidogi, Munkidori and Fezandipiti come for the Plate. Their collars glow with poison (Sweetrot-pink), and they're thralls of something in the Lightless Deep. (Pecharunt seed. Their eyes are the same blissful blank as Corvin's addicts.)
  • CHOICE :ch10_ogre: the Three present themselves as the heroes of the shrine story, and the Ogre roars at the PC.
  • Stand with the Ogre (OGERPON_TRUSTED): Ogerpon fights alongside the PC in the boss sequence as a partner-battle ally. It later joins Juno, and it appears at the Festival.
  • Stand with the Three: the "official story" choice. See GO_LOYAL.
  • Hesitate: the Ogre fights alone, the battle is harder, and Ogerpon leaves the Grove afterward, distrustful.
  • Game over GO_LOYAL "Loyal". Trigger: side with the Loyal Three. Foreshadowing: the Mourner's Ch2 line at the Saltmere pageant ("ask why the Loyal Three wore poison on their collars"), Celestine's Ch3 rhyme at Briarwick's shrine ("who was the thief"), and the poison collars themselves. The Three seize the Meadow Plate and their poison runs into the Bride Tree's roots. Epitaph: "You believed the story everyone told. So did the people who wrote it."

Gym 9: J3 (:FLOWER_GARDEN, 5 growth stages). Thematic note: a garden you grow during the fight; the stages rise with Juno's confidence. Juno, newly confirmed, with pollen in her hair:

"I didn't want this seat. I wanted him in it. But the city's drowning in flowers and nobody else is coming, so. Hi. I'm the Warden of Verdance. Please don't go easy on me — I'll cry either way."

Her ace is Tsareena. If :ch7_ledger was "said his name", her mid-battle line is "You knew before me. You knew." Otherwise it's "He lied to me. Every summer."

Aftermath and revelation.

  • Juno's first act as Warden: she refuses Meridian's Lattice and orders the Thornguard out of the Heartgarden in front of the Queen. The Queen is coldly amused: "Little gardener. We'll see how long you bloom."
  • Queen Maelis throws open the Royal Chase (Safari-style reserve) to the public "as a gift to the people in troubled times" (PR, but it's a fun area). Here, in her private garden, she speaks to the PC and is shrewder than she looks: "Every Sovereign since Maren has died tired. Did you know? I've buried four. Ask yourself why the Accord needs a new champion so badly this year."
  • CHOICE :ch10_succession_stance (asked by the press on the Heartgarden steps): "Should the Plates belong to the kingdoms, the Accord or Meridian?" Answer Wardens/Accord, the kingdoms or nobody. This is the first explicit "nobody" option, and it sets a key the Return path checks.

Optional thread: cameo sidequest "What Are You For?" (Melia). See design/CAMEOS.md. In the newly opened Royal Chase, a blonde girl with a Togekiss is looking for a friend who "fell through a sewer". The quest pays off extra if the Venam quest is done.

Cliffhanger: Juno, alone that night, writes a letter: "Dear Uncle Rowan." She can't finish it. The pages she throws away bloom where they land.

CHAPTER 11 — "The Thaw" (the Hart Road: The Hart's Run → The Hoarwood → Frostfang Pass → Rimeholt, Gym 10; Kyogre; war)

Location: the Hart Road: the Hart's Run (700), the Hoarwood (701, :SNOWY_MOUNTAIN, borderland A2) with the lodge-town Snowbriar (710), Gossamer Heartwood (Silkwood revisit), Frostfang Pass (704/705), the Whalebone Road (712) down to Rimeholt (Isenmar, :FROZEN_LAKE) and Lake Rime. After the Thaw: Ebbmouth (detour), then the Mast Road out (below).

Travel: Juno travels with the PC. She is lobbying the northern Wardens for the Greenward and is nervous about it. She practices speeches on the PC's Pokémon.

War 1 on Frostfang Pass (:war_warning, before the Thaw). From the top of the pass on a hard, clear morning, the PC can see north-east across the Mast Glacier to the bone sands: cookfire smoke along the horizon and a dragon-column circling over it. The Dominar's legions are already camped on Ossaria's western dunes, on sand Kassan has leased them, and nobody in Isenmar knows. Juno: "Those aren't caravans, are they." (Staging and options: 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING Part B.)

Arrival: Isenmar, second visit (escalation). Rimeholt is timber and whalebone on the ice of Lake Rime, part of the frozen sea. Sled-roads, fishing huts and breath-smoke. Meridian heat-towers keep the city alive, and the ice under them is grey and thin. Fishers' holes near the towers don't refreeze. Old men sing the Sleeping Whale song more often than usual.

  • Warden Anja Sorrel is blunt, pragmatic and loyal to her brother, the Thane, who signed the kingdom's heat contract. She tells Juno to her face that southern idealists can keep their principles: "You want me to choose between my principles and my grandchildren's toes? Easy choice. Toes."

Gym 10 (:FROZEN_LAKE). Thematic note: ice that remembers every weight; crack the wrong tile and the field changes. Her ace is Mamoswine. After the battle, the Rimeholt ice-climbers give Rock Climb and the ice-fisher gives the Super Rod.

The Thaw (set piece).

  1. At night, the heat-towers overdraw. The PC and Juno see the readings on a technician's console: red and climbing.
  2. The ice breaks. A quarter of Rimeholt's lower town starts to sink. The field transitions :FROZEN_LAKE → :WATER_SURFACE mid-battle.
  3. Partner battle: PC + Juno vs Directorate officers trying to "secure the Lattice" while people drown.
  4. Then the lake breathes. Under the broken ice, something vast and blue opens an eye. - Prompt: Fight it now / Get to the towers. Anja has told the PC all chapter: "When the lake breathes, you run." - Fight it now triggers Game over GO_WEATHER "Weather": the sea doesn't notice you. - Get to the towers is a sprint across breaking ice to the heat-tower platform, where the fight becomes winnable.
  5. Boss battle: Kyogre (multi-bar). It wakes in Primal rain that floods the lower town further. - The PC fights it on breaking ice. Mid-fight, the shard resonates, and on a Harmony lean the boss's final bar "calms" instead of being knocked out. - Kyogre recognizes the PC: the Field Notes entry later says "it looked at me as if I were very small and very familiar". - It sinks back to sleep, but the sea is no longer fully frozen.
  6. Game over GO_THIN_ICE "Thin Ice". Trigger: mid-Thaw, a Meridian technician begs the PC to retrieve the Lattice's data core ("It's proof! It'll prove who's to blame!"). The PC goes back for it. Foreshadowing: Anja's "Ice remembers every weight", and the cracking-tile tutorial in her gym. Epitaph: "You went back for the proof. The lake kept it, and you."

Aftermath and revelation.

  • Anja stands on a fishing hut's roof in the rain, watching her city sink: "I read the numbers. I read them. And I signed anyway, because the heaters were warm."
  • CHOICE :ch11_anja:
  • Expose her to the Thane's court in the Holdfast's great hall with the console readings (ANJA_EXPOSED). Anja is stripped of her honors, though Wardens can't be removed by kings. Accord Standing goes up and Meridian is blamed loudly. In Act V she refuses to release the Icicle Plate: "Rimeholt drowns without it."
  • Let her confess herself before the court. She becomes a key Act V swing vote, and at the end she lets go.
  • Either way, Anja breaks with Meridian publicly.
  • Thane Eirik declares martial law and evacuates the lower town south into Elowen, which causes a border crisis with Queen Maelis's Thornguard.
  • Juno, wet through and shaking: "That's what Uncle Rowan meant. Isn't it. The flowers. The heaters. It's all the same thing."
  • War. Kyogre's Primal rain rolls east for three days, over the Mast Glacier and across the bone sands, and flash-floods the Dominar's forward camps in the dunes. The Thane blames the embargo, and the Dominar blames "Isenmar's sea-beast". On the third day war is declared on every screen, and the Thane's host starts east along the Sled-Road for Skaldfast (14_WAR_AND_BLESSING).

Detour (segment 10): Ebbmouth, Isenmar second visit. The Thane's evacuation takes Rimeholt's lower town south, back over Frostfang Pass and down the Icecutters' Haul toward Elowen, and Juno goes with it to face the Thornguard at the border. The PC walks the column as far as Ebbmouth (or Flies; the Ebbmouth Sea Grotto, 723, is open to revisit with Surf), where Isenmar's refugees reach a city on strike:

  • The Ebbmouth Strike. Marisol leads the Ebb Guild in cutting Meridian's tidal Lattice with dockworkers' saws, and in refusing the Thane's war levy: the Guild's sleds were requisitioned for the front that morning. "The Guild'll run food to Skaldfast. On our sleds, on our say. Not on Eirik's." The Ebb runs both ways again for the first time in a year, and the whole city cheers on the quay.
  • If TEO_SAVED: Teo is there with glassed fingers, organizing.
  • If not: Teo's photograph is nailed to the strike's banner pole, and Marisol delivers the "He was nineteen" line here instead.
  • CHOICE :ch11_strike: when the strikebreakers arrive at the picket:
  • Stand: a tag battle with Marisol. Her Bond rises a lot, and more if Teo died. This is the only Act III way back to her after Teo's death.
  • Mediate: talk the Directorate foreman down. It's peaceful and polite, and Marisol notes that you didn't pick a side.

Then the Mast Road (Road 11). Isenmar and Zenith share no border, so the road to Skyreach has an air leg. Back north through Rimeholt and east along the Thane's Sled-Road (720), past ice-fishing camps and war-sleds going east, up the Mast Glacier (721, borderland B2: tundra and permafrost dunes) to Anchorhold (730), where Skyreach's airships are anchored in the ice. Stillwater (728), just outside Rimeholt, is an optional Bleed zone where a waterfall hangs frozen in mid-fall without being ice.

Optional thread: cameo sidequest "Crystal Sleep" (Alexandra). See design/CAMEOS.md. In the Thaw's aftermath, a tall woman with a Latias is sitting among Rimeholt's half-Fixed fishers, asking whether they can hear her. Her mother sleeps in crystal in another world.

Cliffhanger: At Anchorhold's moorings a Gale Post mail-ship is loading in a hurry, trailing a banner from Skyreach: "LARCH SPEAKS TONIGHT." The PC goes aboard. As it climbs off the glacier they can see Isenmar's host strung east across the sands toward Skaldfast, and the smoke of the Dominar's camps beyond it. Then the ship turns south over Ossaria's dunes and Elowen's forest, and the Crownwall passes under the keel: a white ring with a city inside.

CHAPTER 12 — "Dead Letters" (the Mast Road's air leg: Anchorhold → The Tetherline → Cloudstair → Skyreach, Gym 11; K5; the Larch Papers)

Location: the Tetherline (732), the walkway under Skyreach's mooring cables, and the Cloudstair (724–726, Rock Climb) up into Skyreach (Zenith's airship spire, :STORMFRONT), the Gale Post sorting halls, the dead-letter archive, Stormwatch Spire (the relay crown).

Arrival: Zenith, second visit (escalation).

  • The mail-ship moors low, on the Tetherline, because the Directorate searches everything at the upper docks. The PC climbs the Cloudstair (Rock Climb) the back way into the city.
  • Skyreach is a vertical city of docking masts and skybridges climbing into the Stormfront, the Sky Plate's permanent storm wall. It now has a Mandate curfew: searchlights from 9pm, and Directorate airships patrolling the masts.
  • Larch is here, hiding in plain sight in the Gale Post sorting halls as a guest of Warden Odessa Gale (goggles, scarf, irreverence). Odessa: "Skyreach's got one law: the wind doesn't care. Everything else is negotiable."
  • Meridian's keystones (SPINE Rev 21; before the raid, where Marchetti's Mega Manectric is the first Meridian Mega). Larch, watching Directorate officers walk the mooring cables past a sorting-hall window: "See the steel bands on their wrists? Lattice-glass. Meridian can't buy a Warden's ring off the Hearthguild, so it grows its own keystones. A Warden's ring asks a heartstone to open. Theirs pry it open. If they come for me tonight and Marchetti's dog changes shape on you, don't stand there gawping." (Meridian's bands never sing, and Meridian doesn't lend them out: design/MEGA_EVOLUTION.md §1.2.)
  • A black dragon is glimpsed in the Stormfront's lightning by airship crews: "the Stormfront Wyrm." (Zekrom seed. Larch, softly: "That's impossible. That's the shape of the Spire's core.")

Gym 11 (:STORMFRONT), a double battle. Thematic note: wind lanes that redirect moves and Pokémon between rounds. Odessa: "Hold onto something. No, really." Her ace is Corviknight. The sky-river guides give Waterfall.

The Larch Papers.

  • At midnight, Larch broadcasts from Stormwatch Spire through the Gale Post's relays to every screen in Velmora. Her original AF 292 report shows Lattice extraction accelerating the Bleed: tide data, Rimeholt's ice, Cindervault's caldera, Lumen's cracked Plate.
  • "I designed the Lattice. I was wrong. I'm telling you now because nobody else will."
  • It's electric, and the realm hears it.

The raid.

  1. Within the hour, Director Marchetti's Directorate storms the Gale Post.
  2. A bomb tears through Stormwatch's relay mast, and the broadcast dies mid-sentence. Meridian's news cycle has the story by dawn: "Hollow sympathizer Larch bombs Skyreach relay."
  3. The bomb was Kroll's (Special Accounts). The PC finds a Splitter casing in the wreckage identical to Lumen's (Key Item Splitter Casing, useful in Ch13).
  4. Meridian admin battle: Marchetti (MERIDIAN_MARCHETTI) on the sorting-hall catwalks. She's cold and professional: "You're not under arrest. You're under protection. Learn the difference before it's taught to you."
  5. Odessa gets Larch out on a Gale Post skiff through the Stormfront, to Cragholm ("I've got friends who live underground").
  6. The PC's Meridian Fellowship is cancelled that night, which they learn from a Mart clerk's apologetic terminal ping: "Fellowship status: SUSPENDED."

K5: the dead letters.

  • In the chaos, Kestrel breaks into Odessa's dead-letter archive, the undeliverable mail of a decade. He now wears Meridian's sponsor jacket and a Resonance Gauntlet on his left hand. Voss has promised him "the full AF 290 file" in exchange for one bundle of letters.
  • The PC catches him among the shelves (K5). The Gauntlet makes his Pokémon hit unnaturally hard: field effects surge whenever he attacks (visual tell only).
  • After the battle he flees with the bundle. One letter falls. The PC reads it:

    "I. — You must not let the child come back. Not for my sake, not for anything. If Valen learns what lodged in that little chest, he will put a crown on it. Keep wilting, love. Keep them small and safe and far. I'll carry the name. — M."

  • CHOICE :ch12_letter:
  • Keep the letter: the PC holds it, and it becomes leverage or a gift in Ch15.
  • Send it to Kestrel via the Gale Post: Kestrel Bond up, and K6's opening line changes ("You sent me a letter. Hers.").
