  • Burn it: Resonance shifts toward Ruin (−2). Ysolde later says, "So you chose not to know. That's a choice too." Odessa finds the ashes in her archive: "Dead letters are the last thing some people ever said." In Act V she won't release the Sky Plate.

INTERLUDE III — "Dead Letters" (playable as Kestrel).

  • Meridian Spire, Voss's office in the small hours. Kestrel hands over the bundle.
  • Voss is kind, attentive and paternal. He makes Kestrel tea in a chipped mug. He gives Kestrel a folder marked AF 290, and it's real, mostly: it proves Valen scapegoated Morwen. It omits Meridian's array entirely.
  • The player can walk the office: a photo of young linesman Voss, a model of the new Prism Arena, and a gold sunburst pin on the desk shaped exactly like a lock.
  • Voss's line: "Your mother was destroyed by a man who thinks he's holding up the sky. I'd like to help you take the sky off him." Kestrel signs the Festival sponsorship contract.
  • Game over GO_FINE_PRINT "Read the Fine Print". Interlude-only, Kestrel's game over. Trigger: Kestrel opens Voss's private desk drawer when Voss steps out (he's warned once by Calla's glance). Inside is a file on the PC titled UNIMPRINTED-01: KEYSTONE. Voss returns: "Ah." Epitaph: "Kestrel Vane was reported missing the next morning. Meridian offered a reward."

Cliffhanger: On Conductors' Causeway, leaving Skyreach, the PC sees their reflection in a puddle move a half-second late.

CHAPTER 13 — "Behind the Glass" (the Glass Road: Conductors' Causeway → The Wired Wood → The Crown Road → Mirror Mere → Antumbra Threshold → Lucent, Gym 12; the tribunal; the Fault)

Location:

  • The Glass Road north off the plateau: Conductors' Causeway (740, :STORMFRONT), the Wired Wood (741, borderland G) with Verdigris (750), then the Crown Road round the Crownwall's east and north: Candle Down (602), the Highwold (603) and Kingsmead (756). Then the Looking-Glass Wood (752, borderland H) with Glassmere (753), and Mirror Mere (742).
  • Antumbra Threshold (743, :INVERSE), Widdershins Walk (755), Lucent (Antumbra, :MINDSCAPE), the Lucent Athenaeum.
  • Stormwatch Spire (optional revisit), Shattered Sky (748).

The road. From Kingsmead's old paddocks under the Crownwall's north-west face, the PC can see the Glassfall Scar glittering high on the wall, where forty people were Fixed in AF 290. The scar on their chest aches the whole way past it. (It sets up the Mindscape.)

Crossing the Glass: Antumbra, first visit.

  • At Mirror Mere, Archseer Imre Dask of the Veiled Synod meets the PC. He has two different-colored eyes and speaks in mirrored sentences: "Welcome, behind. Behind, welcome." He grants passage because Ilsa sent for the PC.
  • His one rule: never look back through the Glass once you've crossed.
  • Game over GO_LOOKING_BACK "Looking Back". Trigger: on the Threshold, the Mere shows Juno calling the PC's name from the other side, and the PC turns. (A prompt: "Look back? Yes/No.") Foreshadowing: Dask's rule, stated twice and written on a Threshold signpost in mirror-writing. Epitaph: "You looked back. Now you're the reflection, and something else is wearing your face to the Festival."
  • The Antumbra Threshold is :INVERSE. Rivers run uphill, shadows fall toward lamps, type matchups flip, and wild Ghost, Psychic and Dark Pokémon are everywhere.
  • Every reflection the PC passes contains a shadow with six black wings, watching (Giratina seed).

Arrival. Lucent exists twice: the living city of white colonnades, and its upside-down reflection in the sky where the Mind Plate lives. The Athenaeum is the Accord's archive and court.

  • Provost Ilsa Marr wears earmuffs against other people's thoughts. "You're thinking very loudly. Please stop."
  • She hosts Rowan's tribunal here. The Accord insisted on its own court, and the transfer from Meridian custody is a political fight Valen won narrowly.

Gym 12 (:MINDSCAPE). Thematic note: the arena reshapes itself to the challenger's memories. Her ace is Hatterene.

The Mindscape (set piece; the PC speaks). After the badge, Ilsa offers what she's been dreading: "Someone sealed a memory in you. Not you. A Ghost-type did, a long time ago. I can open it. I won't enjoy it."

  • The PC enters the Mindscape: a dream-version of Lower Crownhaven, AF 290, all bells and Festival banners.
  • The PC's five-year-old self stands holding a Choir ribbon. This is the first authored PC dialogue.

    Child: "Mum's singing. Do you want to see the light? It's going to hurt." PC (CHOICE :ch13_remember): "Show me." / "I'm scared too." / "...Not yet."

  • "Show me" or "I'm scared too": the fragmented memory plays.
  • Ines singing in the Choir.
  • The Crown blazing on a white-robed man (Valen).
  • Strange brass machines behind the Choir loft, with Meridian sunburst plates.
  • A crack. Light. Pain in the child's chest.
  • A woman in a black Ghost Warden's veil (Morwen) throwing herself over the child.
  • A man's voice: "Find the child."
  • Then darkness, and the shape of a Mismagius closing the memory like a curtain.
  • "Not yet": Ilsa respects it. The memory plays in Ch15 instead, in the Cathedral echo, harder.
  • Ilsa, afterward, white-faced: "The man in white was my father." She has known for eleven years. "The truth is a weapon. I've kept it sheathed. Don't mistake that for mercy." (This seeds her "Little Owl" sidequest.)

Juno and the Ralts (the Athenaeum's cloister garden, the night before the tribunal; a warm scene; SPINE Rev 21 sets up her Festival Mega). Juno has come to Lucent as Grass Warden to sit in the Wardens' row at her uncle's trial. A wild Ralts (Lucent is Psychic country, and Ralts are wild from 11 badges) has been riding in her blossom veil since the Antumbra Threshold, drawn by how frightened she is. She keeps it, and it becomes her Gardevoir "Veil" (it replaces Comfey on her team). By the Festival, Rowan's ring answers her through it (J4, 08_ACT_V).

(The cloister garden at night. Juno sits on the rim of a reflecting pool with a speech in her lap she isn't reading. Her blossom veil trails in the water. Something in the veil is trembling.)
Juno · sad Don't. I know. I look like a wedding that got lost.
Juno He's in a cell under this building. Tomorrow I sit in the Wardens' row and listen to them decide what he is. I've written this speech eleven times. It says "uncle" in all of them.
(The veil moves. A small white Pokémon with a green bowl of hair peers out of the blossoms: a Ralts, its red horn glowing faintly.)
Juno · shocked ...Oh. Hello. How long have you been in there?
Juno · happy Since the Threshold, I think. Ilsa says Ralts can feel what you feel. So it's had a horrible week.
Juno Everyone stares at the veil. Nobody looks inside it. That's actually very clever of you.
Juno · neutral They feel it when you're frightened, and they come closer instead of running away. That's backwards. I like it.
> It's picked you.
  Juno · happy Has it? ...Then you're Veil. I name things after where they hide. It's a system.
> (Say nothing.)
  Juno · happy You're right, it's not my decision. ...Veil? Do you want to be Veil? It's nodding. Or shivering. I'm counting it.
Juno · sad Uncle Rowan's ring still won't talk to me. Maybe it's waiting for me to stop being scared. Maybe Veil can teach me how.

The tribunal (set piece). In the Athenaeum's Glass Court, Valen presides. Wardens attend, and the kings' observers sit in their gallery. Rowan is gaunt from Meridian custody, with his right hand still Bleed-burned in a lightning pattern.

  1. In attendance: Hierophant Ellery, with the Eevee Octave as her honor guard. Vesper's second encounter is an optional sparring double battle in the Athenaeum cloister; afterwards she says how the singers' letters about the PC are going, and that Lento, at the frozen Mirror Mere past Glassmere, hasn't written (her quest, The Still Water, is this chapter's Antumbra Trial). She is shaken by the Fault later in the chapter: "The Choir says we were born lucky. I don't feel lucky." Celestine refuses to swear the witness oath ("I can't lie anyway; it'd be rude to pretend").
  2. Rowan's statement: "I wanted to pull the nails. I was wrong about how. I was not wrong about why."
  3. Kaito's testimony. - CHOICE :ch13_kaito: before the session, Kaito asks the PC whether he should speak about Marrowgate. Encourage him (KAITO_TESTIFIED) or tell him it isn't his burden. - If he testifies: > "Marrowgate. Fifteen years ago. My orders. My unit. I sealed the gate. They were still knocking." - The Glass Court goes silent. Valen doesn't deny it. The Accord's moral authority cracks, and the kings' gallery erupts.
  4. The PC's testimony. - CHOICE :ch13_rowan_testimony: Condemn (Rowan is sentenced to the Pale Gaol, Juno's Bond drops, Accord Standing rises) / Plead for mercy (Rowan's Bond and Hollow Standing rise; he gets a lesser sentence, house arrest in Verdance under Juno, which he never serves because of the Fault) / Refuse to testify (neutral; Juno never asks why).
  5. Sable exposed. - With IRONREACH_EVIDENCE (the comm-device is required; the Skyreach Splitter Casing alone is only circumstantial, though it still lets the PC turn Marchetti in Ch14): the PC presents the comm-device. Ilsa reads the court's minds, confirms it, and speaks it aloud: "Sable is Sabine Kroll. Meridian Special Accounts." Uproar. Kroll, in disguise in the gallery, attacks. Admin battle: Kroll (MERIDIAN_KROLL), now fighting openly as Meridian. - Without the evidence: Ilsa reads it privately and tells only the PC. Kroll stays hidden. The public learns in Act IV, through Rook's leak, and believes it less.
  6. Voss's response on every screen within the hour: "If any Meridian contractor acted outside the law, they acted alone. I've ordered a full inquiry." His approval ratings rise.

The Fault.

  1. That night, across the realm, the ground moves.
  2. Under Cogsworth, Meridian test-fires the Arbiter Engine's first core. It is built around the Dark Stone and draws on all eighteen Plates at once.
  3. A tremor runs through every Imprint. The Bleed leaps forward everywhere, and from Act IV on all early maps use encounter version 1 (Bleed-spread).
  4. On the south coast, the sea pulls back from Zenith's cliffs overnight. The Sump drains, and the spires of drowned Aurelia stand naked under Underveil for the first time in three hundred years.
  5. In the Athenaeum, the Glass Court's windows shatter.
  6. The undercroft floods. The Glass Court's floor gives way into the flooded undercroft. Rowan is chained in the dock and the water is rising around him. The orrery's great brass ring has come down on Director Marchetti, pinning her. Wick's people are on the far side of the water. The PC can reach one. - CHOICE :ch13_fault (MAJOR, who lives):
    • Rowan: the PC breaks his chain. He escapes with Wick, and the Accord guard look the other way. Marchetti is dragged out by her own troops, maimed and unturned. Before he goes, Rowan finds the PC in the broken court: "Ask the Drowned Crown. It's awake now. So are you."
    • Marchetti: the PC heaves the ring off her. Rowan drowns in the dark under the court, still chained. Juno arrives in time to see Wick's people bring the body up, and her Bond drops sharply. Marchetti, bleeding, says only: "I owe you a life." She stands the Directorate down at the hijack.
    • Knock-ons if Rowan drowns (all later files): Teo leads the Lantern Hollow if he was saved, otherwise Thistle and Wick, and Rowan's Act IV–V lines go to whoever leads. "The Gardener" can't be drawn in the Festival R16. In Homecoming, Juno holds Elin alone under the first autumn. In the Hollow Spring, Thistle plants the first seed.

Shattered Sky (748, :BLEED, optional): the reflected Lucent in the sky has cracked. Pieces of the upside-down city hang between earth and sky. The PC can walk among them and find the first Zygarde Core (Zygarde Cell quest hook).

Cliffhanger: Ilsa finds the PC at dawn on the Athenaeum steps, among the shattered glass. She hands over a sealed envelope. "Father's Secret Articles. The parts the Accord doesn't teach. Don't read them yet. Go and find Bastian Ore first. He was there." Behind her, in every broken pane of glass, six black wings fold and unfold.

END OF ACT III. Title card: IV — The Drowned Crown.

Spoilers ahead: this chapter covers late-game twists.

Story Bible 07: Act IV — The Drowned Crown (Ch14–17, Gyms 13–16)

Tone: Desolation. Truth arrives in layers, and every layer costs something. A massacre the player can't stop, a rival's world shattering, a beloved mentor's complicity, a villain who is reasonable. Keep one warm scene per chapter (a meal, a joke, a Pokémon moment) so the dark has contrast. Conventions as in 04. Map names per WORLD.md (segments 12–15). From the start of Act IV, revisited early maps use encounter version 1 (Bleed-spread). If Rowan drowned at the Fault (:ch13_fault = marchetti): every Rowan line in Acts IV–V goes to the Lantern Hollow's leader instead: Teo if TEO_SAVED, otherwise Thistle with Wick. Juno's scenes reference her uncle's death. Revision 6: this act carries beats of the Ashkaar–Isenmar War and the Blessing. See 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING.md (timeline table) for the inserts per chapter; that file wins on conflicts.

Act-opening state (after the Fault):

  • The Bleed has leapt forward everywhere. Briarwick's Glasswood has reached the looms. The Lowlight's glass has spread a block. Saltmere, never once touched by Bleed, has a glass puddle on the promenade, and Dorian has roped it off as "our first miracle, darlings".
  • News screens show the south coast: the sea pulled back from Zenith's cliffs, and drowned Aurelia's golden spires standing in the mud below Underveil.
  • The Concert of Regions announces it will decide on Severance at the Festival.

Revision 7 (comedy): each chapter here has a scripted funny scene in 15_COMEDY.md §4 (Ch14–17), plus running gags (§3) and optional kingdom bits (§5). Place each scene where its heading says, and never inside the beats §1 lists as joke-free.

CHAPTER 14 — "The Deep Seams" (The Obsidian Barrows → Spinefall Gorge → Geode Hollow → Cragholm, Gym 13)

Location: The Obsidian Barrows (:INVERSE, Antumbra exit), Spinefall Gorge (Waterfall, a mirror exit into Ossaria), Geode Hollow (:CRYSTAL_CAVERN), Dreaming Quarter (768, :BLEED: a mining street where the sleeping Fixed's dreams play as mirages), Cragholm (Ossaria), the deep seams.

Arrival: Ossaria, second visit (escalation).

  • Cragholm is a canyon wall of lamplit galleries and lift-cages. Prince-Elector Kassan has sold its seams to Meridian. Linesmen and Directorate guards stand at the main lifts, and Meridian's new Lattice-drill chews into the Stone Plate's crystal halls.
  • The miners are sullen and terrified. Many of them are refugees: Isenmar families from the Thaw, Ossarian well-folk driven off the western dunes by two foreign armies, and Nadir families fleeing Mandate raids.
  • Warden Bastian Ore (74, a miner's lamp on his hat, pretending to be deaf to Directorate questions) greets the PC like a grandson: "Ilsa sent you? Sit down, I'm telling you about the crown."
  • Pip Ore (14), his granddaughter, runs lamp-errands and is the fastest talker in Ossaria. She's the PC's guide through the deep seams.

The deep seams (hidden-refuge sequence). Below Meridian's level, Bastian shelters everyone the Accord and Meridian would rather didn't exist:

  • Professor Larch, smuggled in by Odessa.
  • Rimeholt refugees.
  • Lantern Hollow faithful: Rowan, gaunt (or their new leader, if he drowned), with Wick and Thistle.
  • Corvin's field hospital, if CORVIN_FREED. That flag comes from the Act III side quest "The Doctor's Cell", available Ch11–13: Corvin was arrested under the Mandate for treating Hollow wounded, and the PC can free him from a Directorate holding barge on Lake Sallow. If he wasn't freed, the hospital is run by a frightened Wenlow alone, and Corvin's absence is felt.

Anja arrives on the second day with a column of Rimeholt refugees, frostbitten and furious at herself. Ossarian bone-carters walked them east across the lines under their white banner, the one flag both armies let pass. If she was exposed in Ch11 she won't meet the PC's eyes, and if she confessed she shakes their hand. This is her second encounter before the Festival. When she leaves, she goes west to the front, to Skaldfast (:war_prisoner, Ch15–16).

Warm scene: a communal meal of date-bread and miners' stew. If Rowan lives, he and Juno (if she's visited) don't speak, but they sit at the same table. If he drowned, Juno sits with Thistle, who was with him at the end.

Bastian's account.

"I've seen three Festivals, two Sovereigns and one crown break. AF 290. I was carrying the Stone Plate in the procession. I was nearest the Choir loft. There was brass behind the loft that had no business in a church, and men in white coats with little gold suns on their pockets, watching dials. When the Crown cracked, the dials jumped. They weren't surprised. They were pleased. Then Valen said 'find the child', and Morwen Vane threw herself over a little thing in a Choir ribbon, and the next week Morwen was ruined and nobody ever asked me what I saw. I never told. I was afraid. I'm still afraid. I'm telling you anyway."

Gym 13 (:CRYSTAL_CAVERN). Thematic note: light through crystal; darken it and the whole field turns. (:CRYSTAL_CAVERN → :DARK_CRYSTAL.) Bastian: "Rock's patient. Rock'll wait a thousand years. I'm only seventy-four, so I'll wait about ten minutes." His ace is Gigalith. His old Aerodactyl "Amber" Mega Evolves ("Rock's patient. So's this."): it's the last Mega the PC faces without a ring of their own.

The Ring-Day (after Gym 13; SPINE Revision 21). The Mega Ring comes here, at 13 badges, as in Reborn and Rejuvenation. By now the PC has faced a Mega in every gym since Rimeholt, and Marchetti's at Skyreach. Bastian sends Pip up the lifts for the PC and gives them a Warden's ring (the Mega Ring) and an Aggronite in his lamp-room. The one ring opens both Mega Evolution and Z-moves (SPINE Rev 23; one of each per side). It comes before Larch opens the badge case and before the raid, so the PC goes into the raid wearing it. The ring is the odd one out. Brann cut it in Cindervault "ten years back", and it "sulked" on every hand, so he posted it to Bastian "in a sock". It sings in the PC's palm. Bastian is half-deaf and can't hear it, but he feels it in the table. A player who remembers Brann's chestnut slip ("After the accident. Ten years back.") and Bastian's crown story an hour earlier can put the three together. Nobody says it until Ch17. Must not say: "reset" or "Legend Plate" (09_MYSTERIES #5/#6). Plays as the hidden Trials quest OS_RING_DAY on map 363 (pf_trial_talk(:BASTIAN_LAMPROOM)), which gives MEGARING and AGGRONITE, with no Trial gong. The plugin's strings match the lines below. Lore: design/MEGA_EVOLUTION.md §1 and §4.

(Map 363, the lowest of the Lift Galleries. Bastian's lamp-room: a cot, a kettle and forty years of lamps. Pip is perched on a crate; Larch sits by the door with a book she isn't reading.)
Bastian · happy Sit, sit. Flawless cut, that was. Don't tell the cavern I said so. It sulks.
Bastian · neutral You'll have seen a few of those by now. Anja's Glalie. Odessa's bird. That Directorate woman's dog. My old Amber, just now. Nobody's told you properly what it is, I'd wager. Every Warden's seat has a ring. 'Mega Ring', the Accord calls it. The Hearthguild's cut one for every seat since the Concordance.
Bastian A gold band, and a chip of the Crown's own stone. No colour of its own, so it takes any colour you put to it. That's how it opens a heartstone.
Bastian Heartstones. 'Mega Stones', if you're Accord. Leave an Imprint in one kind of Pokémon long enough and it pearls. Your partner holds the stone, you wear the ring, and for one fight it carries its whole Imprint.
Bastian · deadpan One heart at a time, mind. Two rings on the same side ring against each other. One Mega to a side, always. Remember it in a double.
Bastian · neutral And if you come by a Choir crystal, a sliver of Glassfall glass, it'll answer that too. The chip's grind off the Crown's stone, and the glass came out of the night it cracked. Same crown, one way or another. One Z-move a fight, and one to a side, same as the hearts.
He unwraps an oilcloth: a plain gold band, and set in it a chip of stone with no colour at all.
Bastian · neutral Holloway cut this one. The forge-man in Cindervault. Ten years back. He sent it to me in a sock, with a note: 'It sulks. Keep it where nobody asks questions.' So it's been under my mountain.
Bastian · deadpan Two old men who don't ask each other things. That's how you get to seventy-four.
Bastian · neutral Rock's patient. I reckon this has waited long enough. Hold out your hand.
He drops the ring into your palm. The colourless chip catches the lamplight... and sings: one clear note, like a wet finger round the rim of a glass.
Somewhere under your ribs, something answers it.
(Cutscene RD-1, 13_CUTSCENES.md.)
Pip · shocked Grandad. Grandad, it's SINGING.
Bastian Is it? Can't hear a thing. Half-deaf, me.
Bastian · sad ...I can feel it in the table, though. Holloway swore they don't sing. Thirty years at his anvil, and not one of them ever sang.
(Larch has lowered her book.)
Bastian · worried Well. It isn't sulking, anyway. Here: an iron heart to start you off. The Aron down the east seam wear these like warts.
(Received: MEGA RING. Received: AGGRONITE.)
[if the Bag already held a Mega Stone] The other stones in your Bag are warm now, and quiet, as if they had stopped waiting.
Bastian · happy Wear it. If the Directorate comes down my lifts tonight, I'd like them to meet a ferry child with a Warden's ring.

Idle, after: Bastian is cleaning a lamp he can't possibly need. He hums, flat, a note behind the tune. (Brann sees the ring on the PC's hand at 15 badges: "Brann's forge", Ch16 below. Morwen's Ring comes in Ch15, at the grave.)

Larch and the badge case (revelation). Larch takes the PC's Meridian badge case apart on a miner's bench. Inside the lining is a sliver of Lattice-glass and a transmitter.

  • "Every badge you've won, it's recorded your — whatever it is in you — resonating with that Plate. And it's been sending it to Meridian. Voss isn't watching you. He's tuning you."
  • CHOICE :ch14_telemetry (major; it feeds the endings):
  • Destroy it. Voss loses the stream. In the finale the Engine is under-calibrated, but Voss knows immediately and moves faster (Directorate pressure in Ch16–17).
  • Feed it false data (Larch's plan, TELEMETRY_SABOTAGED). The PC keeps the case and Larch rigs it to send corrupted resonance. Voss's Engine is miscalibrated in the finale, which is the strongest single weakening. It's risky: every remaining badge triggers a tense "did he notice?" beat.
  • Leave it. It keeps working. This is the road to the Bad ending if other weak points also fail.
  • Game over GO_WILLING "Willing". Trigger: Dr. Quent arrives with the raid and offers to "remove the faulty device painlessly, and give you a full Fellowship medical". The PC agrees. Foreshadowing: Larch's flat instruction a scene earlier, "Never, ever let them examine you." Epitaph: "The exam was painless, as promised. You've been asleep since. Meridian sends flowers."

The raid.

  1. Marchetti's Directorate raids the seams, hunting Larch and Rowan.
  2. Admin battle: Marchetti in the Darkglass gallery (:DARK_CRYSTAL after the lamps are shot out). Her Mega Houndoom makes it the first fight in which both sides can Mega Evolve, hours after the Ring-Day.
  3. Thistle defects openly to the PC's side, earlier and warmer at high Hollow Standing. Her Pokémon hold the lift-shaft while refugees escape.
  4. CHOICE :ch14_marchetti: after her defeat, the PC can show Marchetti the Splitter Casing or the Ironreach comm-device: "Your own Special Accounts bombed Skyreach." With either item, MARCHETTI_TURNED becomes possible. She doesn't turn now. She just goes very still, and in the Festival hijack she stands down. Without the evidence, she remains loyal.

Transit (segment 13), Ossaria: Duneholt at the war's edge, the Undersands and Groudon.

  • On the road to Gravenmoor, the PC passes back through Duneholt. The aquifer has gone, the great well is a dry shaft, and Meridian's deep drill has punched through into something hot.
  • The war is a day's ride west. Ashkaar's supply columns go round the city on the Lease's roads, and Kassan's notices of neutrality hang on the Sandgate over older ones about the drilling. The caravans are leaving by the east gate, one house at a time. (14_WAR_AND_BLESSING Part B, "Ossaria".)
  • Prince-Elector Kassan receives the PC in the Hall of Audience (206), between a Meridian paymaster and two foreign quartermasters, Isenmar's and Ashkaar's, who are not speaking to each other. He is delightful. He shows the PC the Elector's Lease as if it were a wedding present: "The Bone Sands have buried every army that ever marched into them. I only charge for the plot."
  • The bone-carters load their carts at the west gate under the white bone-banner. Their elder asks the one who can walk in the glass to bring out the dead their carts can't reach (optional, from their camp on the Dry Tide).
  • War 2, :war_convoy: Marisol's sledges are waiting in the bazaar. The caravan-mothers will lead them west to the Steamline's edge, and the PC walks them through.
  • Duneholt Undersands (783, :DESERT) opens.
  • Boss battle: Groudon (multi-bar), woken by the drills, in a chamber of Unown glyphs that record Theodric's "Year of Two Weathers".
  • Sahar is with the PC, and she reads the glyphs mid-fight (story text between bars): "The King woke the red one and the blue one to remake the land. When they would not obey, he turned his eyes to heaven."
  • After the battle, Groudon sinks back into the earth. The aquifer starts, very slowly, to refill. This is the first good news in an act.
  • Sahar sits down in the dust and looks west: "The King woke the red one and the blue one. Someone's going to bring the blue one here again, you know. The sand remembers the sea. It doesn't want it back."
  • Stonesleep (788): the fossil beds exposed by the collapse. Rare fossils go to the Dig Lab.

Cliffhanger: At the Antumbra border on Hindmoor, Kestrel's Meridian airship passes overhead toward Gravenmoor. Pip: "That's a sponsor ship. Who'd sponsor a graveyard?"

CHAPTER 15 — "The Hollow Cathedral" (The Jawbone Ridge → Hindmoor → Gravenmoor, Gym 14; K6; Vane Hall; Giratina)

Location: The Jawbone Ridge (:MOUNTAIN), Hindmoor (Antumbra moors, fog), Gravenmoor (Antumbra, :HOLLOW_CATHEDRAL), Vane Hall (haunted house), the Lantern Hospice, the barrows, then on the way out Barrow of the Wardens and Giratina's Reverse Depths (806, :INVERSE), The Hush (808).

The road. On the Jawbone Ridge the war's smoke stands on the western sky. A Gale Post courier catches the PC at Vigil with the news, the Siege of Skaldfast, and with Anja's name on the list of the taken (:war_prisoner, 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING).

Arrival: Antumbra, second visit. Gravenmoor is fog, barrows and lanterns. The Spooky Plate makes the dead linger as echoes: a woman sweeping a step that isn't there, two children playing a game that ended in AF 211.

  • Archseer Dask has come to Gravenmoor himself (his second encounter, needed for the Ruin Route): "The echoes are louder. Louder, the echoes. Something behind the Glass is listening back."
  • The Veiled Synod's lantern-priests are frightened. Since the Fault, the echoes have been getting louder, and some have started to notice the living.
  • Warden Ysolde Ashgrave, lace and veil, lantern always lit, greets the PC softly: "The dead aren't gone here. They're just very bad at conversation." She knows who the PC is. She has been waiting for them, and for Kestrel.

Vane Hall (haunted house set piece, the sad one).

  • Kestrel has arrived on Meridian's ship and gone straight up the hill to his childhood home. The PC follows.
  • Vane Hall is dust-sheeted and haunted. The echoes are of his family: his grandmother younger and laughing, Morwen reading to a six-year-old Kestrel, Morwen at a desk writing a letter and crying.
  • A puzzle path (World/puzzle team) through rooms that replay the night of AF 290 from the household's side: a servant's echo saying "the Warden's not back yet", a clock stopped at 11:40.
  • Kestrel walks through it like a ghost himself. Short lines only. "That's my room. That's — don't touch that."

Gym 14 (:HOLLOW_CATHEDRAL). Thematic note: echoes of earlier turns replay; the dead fight beside the living. Ysolde: "Mind the candles. Some of them are people." Her ace is Chandelure.

The Cathedral echo (the central revelation of the game).

  1. Kestrel's Resonance Gauntlet (Meridian-built) can amplify the Spooky Plate's echoes. Voss told him the full truth of AF 290 is "recorded in the Cathedral". He means to force the Plate to replay it.
  2. Ysolde begs him not to: "Not like this. She made me swear — when you were ready—"
  3. He does it anyway. The Hollow Cathedral replays AF 290 in full, through Morwen's eyes. The PC sees it whether or not they chose "Not yet" in Ch13. If they did, this is their first time, and it's harder. - The Crownhaven arena, bells, the Choir. Ines singing. - Behind the loft: brass machines, sunburst plates, and a young, eager Aurelian Voss in a white coat, watching the dials. - The Tuning begins. The Crown flares on Valen. A sound like a bell breaking. - A splinter of colorless light flies from the Crown, straight into the chest of a five-year-old in a Choir ribbon. - Morwen runs. She throws herself over the child as the Glassfall sweeps the lower stands, and forty people turn to glass around them. - Valen, through the light: "Find the child. Whatever it costs. Find the child." - Morwen, hiding the child in a vestry, to Ines: "Take them. Edda's boat is at the Landing at midnight. I'll carry the name. Go." - Morwen's Mismagius gently closes the child's memory like a curtain. - The echo ends with Morwen alone in the vestry, kneeling, saying to no one: "Kestrel. I'm sorry."
  4. Silence. Then Morwen's echo turns, impossibly, and looks at the PC across ten years:

    "Little one. You came back. I told her not to let you." It fades.

K6 (raw, furious).

  • Kestrel turns on the PC:

    "My whole life for you. Do you know what they called me in school? The Glassfall boy. My grandmother spat on her grave. And she was saving YOU."

  • If :ch12_letter was "sent to Kestrel": he opens with "You sent me her letter, and you still came here."
  • The battle is K6. His Gauntlet surges with the Cathedral's grief. Mid-battle the field flickers to :BLEED for a turn, the Gauntlet overloading.
  • After K6: the PC speaks (authored line, CHOICE :ch15_kestrel). 1. "I'm sorry. I didn't know. I'd give it back if I could." Kind: Kestrel's Bond goes up a lot, delayed. He can't accept it now. 2. "I was five. She chose. Don't you dare make her choice my crime." Blunt: his Bond drops now, but it unlocks his Redeemed path in K8, because he respects being fought back. 3. "...Your mother saved my life. I'm going to make it worth it." The Resolve option: his Bond goes up, and Resonance leans Harmony.
  • Kestrel leaves without a word. Ysolde follows him to the moor's edge and gives him Morwen's Mismagius and Morwen's sealed letter. He takes the Mismagius and refuses the letter. Ysolde keeps it for him (it returns in the Festival SF).

Edda Morrow at Morwen's grave. In the barrows below the Lantern Hospice, the PC finds Captain Edda Morrow laying kelp-flowers on a plain stone marked M.V.

"I took you out on the night ferry. Brought you back on the last one. Tide's got a sense of humour." A beat. "She paid me in her Warden's ring. I never sold it."

She gives the PC the ring (Key Item Morwen's Ring; plot-relevant in Act V for Kestrel).

Game over GO_ECHO "Echo". In the Cathedral, after the replay, an echo of Ines keeps singing in the Choir loft. A prompt: "Stay and listen?" Choosing to stay three times triggers it. Ysolde warns that "echoes are a door that only opens one way", and the PC's own hand turns translucent on the second "stay". Epitaph: "You stayed for the song. Gravenmoor has one more echo now. It sings harmony."

Transit (segment 14), Giratina's Reverse Depths.

  • Leaving Gravenmoor through the Barrow of the Wardens, where generations of Wardens are buried with replica Plates, the PC finds a barrow-door that opens downward into the sky: the Reverse Depths (806, :INVERSE).
  • Giratina waits there. The Fault and the Gauntlet's abuse of the Spooky Plate have torn the Glass, and Giratina is furious and wounded.
  • Boss battle: Giratina (multi-bar; Altered, then Origin on the last bar).
  • After the fight it doesn't flee. It looks at the PC the way Kyogre did. Story text: it knows what you carry. It has been guarding the hole your god left for three hundred years. It lets the PC pass and closes the tear behind them.
  • The Glass has been leaking since the Fault, and Giratina's wound is why visitors from other worlds keep slipping into Velmora (the cameo sidequests, design/CAMEOS.md). Post-game: the Distortion Core.
  • Ruin Route trigger (only with a full Ledger, ruin_unlocked). A pane of black glass in the Depths shows Juno on the other side, calling the PC's name: the exact image of GO_LOOKING_BACK. The prompt appears again: Look back? (:ch15_look_back).
  • Yes: it no longer kills you. The reflection steps aside, and the PC walks through into story/12_RUIN_ROUTE.md (The Ferrymen's Mile).
  • No: the main story continues, and the door never reopens on that save.
  • The Hush (808): a Bleed zone where sound doesn't exist. The PC can see their own footsteps as ripples. Atmospheric breather.

CHAPTER 16 — "Clear Air" (The Noonless Road → The Slag Mesa → Cogsworth, Gym 15; the Arbiter blueprints; Zekrom; the Sump Purge begins)

Location: The Noonless Road, the Slag Mesa (:WASTELAND, Zenith's eastern waste), Cogsworth (Zenith's foundry district, :FACTORY), Strade Works, the Engine core chamber.

Arrival: Zenith, third visit (escalation).

  • Cogsworth runs three shifts. Smokestacks never stop, and clock-towers chime every quarter-hour.
  • Topside "Unity Rallies" fill the plazas. Voss on giant screens: "Order. Light. Unity." Directorate banners hang from every gantry.
  • Workers are tired and proud. Many are from Nadir, commuting up the lifts. They know something huge is being built and don't know what.
  • Rook Calder is here, off-camera and unshaven. Since the Lowlight he has been quietly collecting Meridian Spire security footage. He finds the PC in a workers' canteen: "I've got Sable on tape. With a Meridian keycard. I've had it for months. I was scared."
  • CHOICE :ch16_rook:
    • Leak it now: it's public, and Kroll's identity is confirmed realm-wide even without Ch13 evidence. Meridian fires Rook within the hour and blacklists him from the Spire, so he can't cut the grid in Ch21 and can't reach the Zap Plate to release it (unless Marchetti turns).
    • Hold it for the Festival: Rook stays inside, smiling for cameras. He leaks it at the worst possible moment for Voss (Ch20 opening ceremony), and he's still in position to cut Lumen's grid in the hijack (ROOK_CUTS_GRID).

Gym 15 (:FACTORY). Thematic note: conveyor-belt arena; machines you can jam or overdrive. Magnus Strade is immaculate, prosthetic hand, pocket watch. "Faith gave us three hundred years of the Bleed. Engineering will give us the next three hundred without it." His ace is Metagross. He gives Dive suits via the bathysphere works.

Infiltration: Strade Works (set piece).

  1. With Rook's keycards, the PC and Rook infiltrate the deep foundry after the gym.
  2. Partner battle: PC + Rook vs Marchetti + Quent on the casting floor. The field goes :FACTORY → :SCRAPYARD as the floor is wrecked mid-battle.
  3. In the drafting vault the PC finds the Arbiter Engine blueprints (Key Item Arbiter Blueprints): - A ring of eighteen locks to be built into the new Festival arena. - A keystone cradle "to be recovered from site AURELIA". - The notation: "Calibration subject: UNIMPRINTED-01. Retention: indefinite."
  4. The core chamber: the Dark Stone at the center of a cage of Lattice-glass. It has cracked open, and Zekrom is half-emerged and bound in golden cable. This was the Fault's test-fire.
  5. Boss battle: Zekrom (multi-bar). Each bar breaks a containment cable, and the PC is freeing it, not beating it. On victory, Zekrom tears free through the foundry roof into the Stormfront. Story consequence: the Engine's original core is lost (ZEKROM_FREED), and Voss must reroute through Lumen's grid.
  6. Game over GO_OVERTIME "Overtime". Trigger: during the core-chamber sequence, a prompt to "finish copying the blueprints" while the containment klaxon counts down from 3 (warned twice by Rook: "We go when the whistle goes, no heroics"). Epitaph: "You stayed past the whistle. Strade Works issued a statement about an industrial accident."

Magnus (choice). Magnus finds the PC in the ruined vault with the blueprints. He doesn't call security.

"I don't build weapons. I build tolerances. I was told it was a Plate stabilizer. I learned the truth two years ago and kept building, because the math was beautiful and the alternative was the Bleed."

  • CHOICE :ch16_magnus:
  • Expose him (MAGNUS_EXPOSED): the PC takes the blueprints to the Zenith Council via Councillor Sallow. Magnus is arrested, Meridian loses a board vote and some public trust, and the Engine's design leaks publicly. But nobody is inside to sabotage it later.
  • Appeal to his conscience (MAGNUS_KEPT_FAITH): "Will you let it take a child?" He says nothing. He winds his watch. In the finale, he disables the Engine's safety governor, which weakens Voss's binding: "No machine I have built will kill a child."

The Sump Purge begins. That night, every screen in Zenith shows "Operation Clear Air."

  • Since the Fault drained the Sump and exposed Aurelia, Meridian claims Nadir's lower districts are "lawless": Sweetrot gangs and Hollow terror cells. The Directorate descends into Nadir.
  • Topside watches it like weather. A Cogsworth worker beside the PC, quietly: "My mum lives down there."

INTERLUDE IV — "Clear Air" (playable as Wenlow, Corvin's apprentice).

  • Mirefen, the same night. The player controls Wenlow in the Infirmary as the Directorate comes up the stilt-walks.
  • Wenlow moves patients, hides Sweetrot addicts in the Quiet Ward ("They won't search the glass ones. Nobody ever looks at the glass ones."), and fights two officers with Corvin's spare Pokémon.
  • The last scene: Wenlow standing in the Ward's doorway between a Directorate squad and forty dreaming patients. "This is a hospital. You have to—"
  • Cut to black. A single gunshot sound-effect, and nothing else.
  • If CORVIN_FREED, Corvin is in Cragholm and learns by radio. If not, he's in a Directorate cell and learns from a guard.
  • This death cannot be prevented. It is the act's moral floor.

Cliffhanger: Dawn. The PC, Rook and the blueprints on a supply-lift heading down into Nadir. Through the grille below, smoke rises from Underveil.

Optional thread: Brann's forge (any time from 15 badges until the Festival). Brann is at the Hearthguild anvil (map 244) whenever he isn't at Valen's side (he comes to Underveil from Crownhaven in Ch17). Most players find him on the road through Ashkaar to Wyrmrest in Ch19. He knows his ring on the PC's hand. If the PC told him the Light Stone was the Dominar's (:ch8_lightstone = dominar), it still hurts, and he says so and then won't talk about it. He gives the Cameruptite, the twin of Kiln's. Plays as the hidden Trials quest AS_FORGE_REMEMBERS on pf_trial_talk(:BRANN_HEARTHGUILD); the strings match.

Brann · happy There you are! War on the doorstep and you still come by. Sit. No, not there, that's hot.
Brann · shocked ...That's my ring. The odd one. So old Ore finally gave it away. Ten years it sulked in his lamp-room.
[if :ch8_lightstone = :dominar]
  Brann · sad I haven't forgotten the Light Stone, mind. 'It's his people's,' you said. ...No. I'm not going to talk about it. The ring doesn't hold it against you, so I won't. Not today.
Brann · neutral Kiln, my Camerupt. If you've met her, you remember her. She likes to erupt on people.
Brann Every heartstone's got a twin somewhere. Hers turned up in the slag this spring, still warm. The caldera makes them like other mountains make gravel.
Brann · smug I'd give it to a Warden. You'll do better than most Wardens.
(Received: CAMERUPTITE.)
Brann · deadpan Your ring still singing? ...No. Don't tell me. I sleep badly enough.

(Kiln is on Brann's Standard and Hard teams only, so the line doesn't assume the PC fought her. If the confession has already happened (Ch17), "Don't tell me" lands harder: he still won't ask where the rest of the stone went.)

CHAPTER 17 — "The Drowned Crown" (The Hanging Stair → The Drownings → Seabed → Underveil, Gym 16; Aurelia; Voss)

Location:

  • The Hanging Stair (:SCRAPYARD), the Drownings (:WATER_SURFACE, the drained south coast), Under the Drownings (:UNDERWATER, Dive).
  • Underveil (Nadir's heart, :NEW_MOON), the Moon Market.
  • Aurelia (824 :UNDERWATER / 825–826 :CAVE), the Sun Court.
  • Ironbloom (828, :BLEED: rust that flowers).
  • Branch map 838 Accord Archive (high Accord Standing).

Arrival: Nadir, third visit (aftermath of the Purge).

  • Underveil is a city of lanterns in the upper towers of drowned Aurelia, in permanent night under the Dread Plate. This morning it is smoke, broken lanterns and Directorate barricades.
  • Dozens are dead. Nadir's fighters have pushed the Directorate back to the lifts. Mother Gutter's Muk holds one barricade, and Lantern Hollow volunteers hold another.
  • Game over GO_INTO_THE_LINE "Into the Line". Trigger: at a barricade, a Directorate line advances on unarmed Nadir protestors. The PC is offered "Step between them?" Nyx's courier warns the PC twice, "Not you. You're the one thing they want alive. Don't make them choose." Epitaph: "They didn't choose. The bullet did. Meridian called it a tragic accident, and meant it."

Nyx Calloway.

  • Silk, smoke, a crescent-moon earring. She receives the PC in the Moon Market among sellers of secrets.
  • Today she isn't amused. She has been carrying bodies. "Underveil isn't on the Accord's maps, sweetheart. That's the point of Underveil. Apparently it's also why nobody comes when they shoot us."
  • Nadir declares independence from Zenith that afternoon, by Nyx's proclamation read from the Moon Market steps with every Sump Baron present. It's symbolic, defiant and legally meaningless, and everyone cheers.

Gym 16 (:NEW_MOON), an illusion double battle. Thematic note: nothing on the field is what it looks like; illusions mask both sides. Nyx: "Everything has a price. Yours just went up." Her ace is Zoroark.

Nyx's bargain.

  • CHOICE :ch17_nyx: Nyx has the Engine's arena schematics, Meridian's install plans for the Prism Arena.
  • Trade the PC's own secret (NYX_BARGAIN_TAKEN). Nyx gets to know exactly what the PC is, and she will use it. The PC gets the schematics, and in Ch21 Nyx cuts Meridian's comms precisely.
  • Refuse: Nyx shrugs and helps anyway in Ch21, sloppily, at a cost to herself (she's injured).
  • Nyx confesses, unprompted, after the gym: "Two years ago I sold Voss the way into the Sun Court. I told myself it was just a door. My family's kept that door shut for three hundred years. I'm the one who opened it."

Accord Archive branch (838, high Accord Standing only). Brann meets the PC in a sealed Coastwatch vault on the Drownings. It holds the Concordance's Secret Articles in Maren's handwriting: the Tuning, and the Hymn of Return. Brann confesses everything here, gently and early (see below), and gives the PC Maren's original Hymn page.

Aurelia (dive set piece).

  1. With Dive suits from Cogsworth, the PC descends from the Drownings's drained shallows to the Seabed and into drowned Aurelia. - Sahar Ostrand leads the expedition. She's the expert, terrified and thrilled: "Three hundred years. I've waited my whole life." - Edda Morrow pilots the support boat.
  2. Golden terraces lie under green water. Gilder machines are rusted into coral. The Gilded King's statues have had their faces chiseled off by his daughter's people.
  3. The murals of the Sun Court tell the real Prismfall in full: the Blight, the Two Weathers, the Chain, the Calling, the god breaking itself, the city falling, and Princess Maren pulling a colorless shard from the wreck of the keystone cradle.
  4. The keystone cradle itself sits in the throne room's center: a golden hand, open, the size of a door. The PC's shard resonates violently. The PC's chest glows through their shirt, and the drowned room lights up with eighteen faint colors.
  5. Nyx, who came down after all: "Oh. Oh, darling. You're the missing piece."
  6. The truth, named. Sahar reads the cradle's inscription: "Here rests the One that is every color and none." The PC carries a splinter of the Legend Plate, Arceus's heart.
  7. Game over GO_THE_THRONE "The Throne". Trigger: an exploration prompt, "Sit on the Gilded King's throne?" Foreshadowing: Sahar ("Don't touch anything gold. Anything."), and the throne's armrests shaped like open hands. The cradle closes. Epitaph: "You fit perfectly. That was the problem the Gilders were trying to solve."

Aurelian Voss in the Sun Court.

  1. A Meridian salvage team cuts in through the throne room's far wall, and Voss walks in among them in a pressure suit with his helmet off in an air-pocket. He's here to collect the cradle. He is delighted to see the PC.
  2. The reveal, his way:

    "House Aurel. My family. We changed the name and kept the grudge. I was eight when my grandfather showed me Theodric's notebooks. I was twenty-two when I realized he was right about everything except the chain. Metal was the wrong material."

  3. He admits AF 290 plainly: "My array. My dials. I was trying to measure the convergence. I didn't know it would break the Crown. I was very sorry about the forty people. I was even sorrier when I understood what I'd learned."
  4. On the Lowlight: "Twelve people. I've lost more to the Bleed in a quiet week. I made those twelve mean something."
  5. His philosophy: "Gods are absentee landlords. Arceus dropped its furniture on our heads three hundred years ago and never came back. I'm not trying to become a god. I'm trying to make sure we never need one again."
  6. His offer (CHOICE :ch17_voss_offer):

    "Stand with me at the Festival. When it's done, no child in Velmora will ever be Fixed again. Your mother wilted in exile because of a broken god. I can fix the god." - Refuse (always available). - Feign agreement (VOSS_FEIGNED): Voss lets the PC close in the finale, and the hijack has a different opening beat. It's risky, because if Meridian Standing is high and telemetry is intact, it tips toward Concord Dawn or the Bad ending. - Accept (VOSS_ACCEPTED): this opens the Concord Dawn ending path. Narrative Systems owns the consequences.

  7. Meridian admin battle: Kroll (MERIDIAN_KROLL), or Quent if Kroll was beaten publicly in Ch13. They hold the PC off while Voss's team lifts the keystone cradle out through the wall. Voss leaves on a Meridian submarine. His last words: "Win your badges. I'll see you at the coronation."

Ysolde in Underveil. The Ghost Warden has come down the lifts with a cart of Gravenmoor lanterns, one for each of the Purge's dead, and she lights them along the Moon Market stairs with Nyx's people. She asks the PC one thing: "Is he eating? Kestrel. You'd know better than I would." (Her third scene before the Festival.)

Brann's confession (if not already given in the Archive branch). Above water, at Underveil's docks, Brann Holloway is waiting. He has come from Crownhaven on Valen's behalf. Confronted with everything, he tells the truth at last:

  • The Tuning is real.
  • The Crown kills Sovereigns.
  • He reset the Crown's stone after the Fracture and knew it was short, and never asked where the rest went.
  • Valen's arm is crystal to the shoulder.
  • "He has weeks. Maybe the Festival."

He delivers Valen's message:

"He says: 'Win your last two badges. Then come to me, and I'll tell you everything.'"

Optional thread: cameo sidequest "Deliverer" (Amaria and Titania). See design/CAMEOS.md. Edda's divers report a woman swimming without a suit in drowned Aurelia's lower galleries, singing to a Lapras, and an armored knight pacing the drained shallows above, refusing to leave. After Gym 16, before the PC leaves Underveil.

Cliffhanger: Night on the Underveil docks. The PC, Nyx, Sahar, Edda and Rook (and Rowan, if he came down) sit on crates in the lantern-light. Nyx counts on her fingers:

"Meridian wants you in that arena. The Accord wants you in that arena. The Hollow wants you in that arena. Two kings want you as their champion in that arena. Thirty days, sweetheart. Every power in Velmora is waiting for you to walk into one room."

Edda: "Then we'd best make sure you walk in on your own feet."

END OF ACT IV. Title card: V — Sovereign.

Spoilers ahead: this chapter covers late-game twists.

Story Bible 08: Act V — Sovereign (Ch18–21, Gyms 17–18, the Festival of Champions)

Tone: Desolation-dark, then a hard-won dawn. Everything planted pays off. The Festival week should feel like the whole game is in one city: every Warden, every faction, every Bond. Mechanics ownership: the Festival draw, game-over IDs and ending triggers belong to story/10_CHOICES_ENDINGS.md and design/NARRATIVE_KEYS.md. This file gives the story content of every branch they select from. "Default" means the SPINE Rev. 2 path, the fallback. Map names per WORLD.md (segments 16–18, Crownhaven 480–519). Caps: R16 90 · QF 92 · SF 94 · Final 96 · Hijack 100 · True Finale 100. Revision 6: this act carries beats of the Ashkaar–Isenmar War and the Blessing. See 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING.md (timeline table) for the inserts per chapter; that file wins on conflicts.

Revision 7 (comedy): each chapter here has a scripted funny scene in 15_COMEDY.md §4 (Ch18–21), plus running gags (§3) and optional kingdom bits (§5). Place each scene where its heading says, and never inside the beats §1 lists as joke-free.

CHAPTER 18 — "Once Upon a Time" (The Blindwater → Lightless Deep → The Gloamwood Verge → Gloaming, Gym 17; Pecharunt; K7; the Hymn)

Location:

  • The Blindwater (:CAVE).
  • Lightless Deep (844 :DARK_CRYSTAL / 845 :NEW_MOON).
  • Inverted Ward (848, :INVERSE: an abandoned Choir hospital turned upside-down by the thinning Glass).
  • Gloamwood Verge, Gloaming (Elowen's oldest corner, in the deep south-east, :FAIRY_TALE), the Great Tree.

The Lightless Deep: Pecharunt (Nadir's legendary arc)

The road out of Underveil runs down, not up: below the drained Sump into the Lightless Deep, the oldest dark under the City Below.

  1. Corvin (or Wenlow's notes, if Corvin was never freed) has traced Sweetrot to its source.
  2. The Deep is a sweet-smelling cavern of pink crystal and docile, smiling thralls tending peach-shaped growths. Mother Gutter, the oldest Sump Baron, is here, blissed and centuries-old. She isn't the master. She's the first thrall.
  3. Boss battle: Pecharunt (multi-bar). Its "mochi" poison spreads Sweetrot status-flavor across the field.
  4. Defeating it frees the thralls across Nadir, and the Sweet Market's vendors blink awake in the street.
  5. Lore payoff: Pecharunt enthralled the Loyal Three centuries ago and sent them to steal Elowen's Plates. The "Gossamer Ogre" drove them off. The pageants have had it backwards for 250 years.
  6. If OGERPON_TRUSTED, Ogerpon appears at the Deep's mouth, waits for the PC and walks with them to Gloaming.

Gloaming: Elowen, third visit (escalation)

  • Thornguard checkpoints. Prince Caedmon (now effectively ruling Elowen, since his mother is "resting") has signed the Forest Compact. Meridian survey-flags line the Gloamwood. The Thornguard turns the PC back at the Verge "by royal order".
  • The dusk is spreading: Gloaming's twilight has crept west across half the forest, and Briarwick's looms now work by lamplight at noon.
  • Optional scene, Queen Maelis: in a dusk-garden she's "resting" in under polite guard. Shrewd and finally honest: "My son thinks the forest is a resource. I've been queen for sixty years. The forest is the sovereign. I'm just the gardener it tolerates." She gives the PC a Royal Writ (key item). It opens the Wardguard escort to Crownhaven even at low Accord Standing, and it seeds Elowen's epilogue: Maelis disowns the Compact.
  • Celestine (in her true form; the PC met her disguised in Ch3, at Briarwick's shrine) dissolves the checkpoint with one sentence the Thornguard captain can't argue with, because she can't lie and everyone knows it: "If you stop this child, the forest will remember your name, and it will say it wrong forever."

Gym 17 (:FAIRY_TALE), a double battle: "the knight and the dragon"

Thematic note: the arena is a storybook. Choose your role (knight, dragon or thief), and the story's rules change who's strong. Celestine: "Once upon a time — which is the only time there ever is, here —" Her ace is Sylveon. Her one power play is a Z-move, not a Mega (SPINE Rev 23): her Mimikyu holds the Mimikium Z (Let's Snuggle Forever). The reason is Gloaming's dusk-chapels, which still sing the whole Hymn and tuned the crystal for her storybook's ghost. Before the battle, in her voice (she cannot lie, only phrase):

"My dusk-chapels still sing the whole song: every verse the rest of Velmora stopped singing. They sang over a sliver of glass for me, a year of dusks, until it knew my little ghost by heart." "Every story needs one true thing in a borrowed costume. Mine is wearing yellow." When the Z-move fires: "This is the part where it hugs you. Hold still. It's worse if you don't." (The Hymn itself comes after the badge, in the same chapels.)

The Hymn of Return

In the dusk-chapel at the Great Tree's roots, Celestine gives the PC the complete Hymn of Return, sung for them by the Gloaming choir. If the PC received Wick's verse (Ch10) or Maren's page (Archive branch), the last verse visibly completes in the Key Item.

Eighteen we borrowed, eighteen we keep till the wounded land has learned to sleep; then one of no color, the eighteen roads walked, shall carry them home, as the old ones talked — not chained, not broken, not bought, not crowned: given back, as a gift is found.

Celestine: "I've been waiting for you for forty years, little colorless thing. Valen reads 'one of no color' as vessel. The Hollow read it as hammer. Meridian reads it as key. It says walker. I cannot lie. I can, however, sing. These are the verses I sing." (Her phrasing is exact and deliberate. On the Ruin Route she admits there's a verse she stopped singing.)

K7 (the Great Tree's roots)

  1. Kestrel, Meridian's sponsored Festival entrant with 18 badges, arrives on a Directorate skiff. He's here to stop the PC going to Crownhaven, not for Meridian.

    "They all want to use you. Valen wants a lock. Voss wants a key. Your Hollow friends want a crowbar. Stay out of Crownhaven and let me end it. I'll beat Valen in front of the whole world and make him say her name."

  2. K7 on the Fairy Tale field. Kestrel insists he's the knight and the PC is the dragon. If the PC's Bond with him is high, he flinches mid-battle.
  3. After the battle: - CHOICE :ch18_kestrel_ring: if the PC has Morwen's Ring (Ch15), give it to him now or keep it for later.
    • Give it now: Kestrel's Bond goes up, and his Redeemed path becomes more likely. He doesn't say thank you. He puts it on. (It answers him at the SF: his Scizor's first Mega, K8.)
    • Keep it: the ring can be given at the SF instead, for a bigger moment if he's Redeemed.
  4. Prompt: Stay out of Crownhaven? (Yes / No.) Yes triggers Game over GO_STAY_OUT "Somebody Else's Story": the PC does what everyone has told them since the ferry, and the Engine takes Kestrel instead.
  5. On No, Kestrel leaves for Crownhaven: "Don't come. I mean it. ...You're going to come. Fine. Then don't lose before you reach me."

Optional thread: cameo sidequest "Dreamwalker" (Shiv). See design/CAMEOS.md. In Gloaming's dusk-chapels, a grinning stranger keeps appearing in the townsfolk's dreams. He says he's met the PC before, on a ferry.

Game over GO_FAIR_BARGAIN "Fair Bargain"

Gloaming's lantern-moth market offers bargains. One stall promises "the answer to your mother's last question". Accepting without asking the price triggers it. Celestine has warned the PC on arrival: "In Gloaming, always ask what it costs before you say yes." Epitaph: "The price was your name. You are very happy now, as a lantern-moth, and you will glow at every dusk."

CHAPTER 19 — "The Last Gate" (The Gloamwood → The Thornwar Marches → Wyrmscar Rift → Wyrmrest, Gym 18; Reshiram; Sigrun's trial)

Location: Gloamwood (:FAIRY_TALE), the Thornwar Marches (:MOUNTAIN), Wyrmscar Rift (864 :CAVE / 865 :DRAGONS_DEN), Wyrmrest (Ashkaar), Rainbow Scar (868, :RAINBOW).

Arrival: Ashkaar, second visit (escalation)

  • Dominar Hrothgar is at the front with his legions, in the Ashkaar Siege Camp on Ossaria's western dunes, the length of Ashkaar and half of Ossaria away (14_WAR_AND_BLESSING). Wyrmrest is held by Sigrun's own riders. The Dominar means to march on Zenith "the hour the Festival ends", and he has ordered his daughter to close the pass to everyone Zenith-tainted. That includes the PC: Meridian's Fellowship, Meridian's badge case.
  • Sigrun Ashfall keeps the pass open anyway, in open defiance, standing on the gate in dragonhide with her Salamence. "Wyrmrest is the last gate. Dragons don't let anything through they haven't weighed. I do the weighing, Father. Not you."

The Dominar (optional political scene, DOMINAR_SWAYED)

  • The PC petitions the Dominar in his command pavilion at the Siege Camp, after the Battle of the Glass Dunes (Sigrun has flown them there; below). Lies are a capital crime in an Ashkaar court, and the oath-brazier is lit.
  • Persuading him to fly for Crownhaven instead of against Zenith requires:
  • the Light Stone sent to Wyrmrest (:ch8_lightstone = wyrmrest) plus proof (the Arbiter Blueprints or the Larch Papers), or
  • Sigrun's Bond ≥ 4, so that she speaks for the PC (:ch19_dominar).
  • Success: "If the god is in chains, then dragons will break them. Not for the Accord. For the god." His legions are present in the hijack.
  • Failure: his riders go home after the truce and take no part in defending Crownhaven. (DOMINAR_SWAYED can't be set if Isenmar won the war without mercy terms.)

Sigrun's trial (Wyrmscar Rift)

  1. Sigrun won't let the PC challenge her until they walk the Wyrmscar Rift to the Draco Plate with her and speak aloud what they intend to do at the Festival.
  2. Sigrun's confession on the walk:

    "He trained me to be his successor. Then he told me I'd never survive the Crown, and I was relieved. Do you understand? Relieved. And then he went looking for you. I knew. For two years I knew, and I let it happen, because it meant it wasn't me."

  3. At the Rift's heart, at the brazier over the Draco Plate, the PC speaks. This is an authored line and also a soft commitment that the ending checks (Narrative Systems owns how much weight it carries). CHOICE :ch19_oath: - "I'm going to give them back." (Return) - "I'm going to keep them safe. Whatever it costs me." (Keep) - "I don't know yet. I'm going to find out with my eyes open." (Open) - (Only if Resonance ≤ −2:) "I'm going to end it. All of it." Sigrun draws her blade but lets them pass, horrified.
  4. Game over GO_LIARS_PYRE "Liar's Pyre". A fifth option is always offered: "Whatever you want to hear." Foreshadowing: the Ashkaar gate-guard's "say true or say nothing", and the brazier oath. The fire answers. Epitaph: "Ashkaar burns liars. It is the oldest law, and the dragons remember it even when men forget."

The Battle of the Glass Dunes (between the oath and Gym 18)

After the oath, word comes that Kyogre has risen and is dragging a flood-sea across the desert, and that the Dominar has carried the Light Stone to the front. Sigrun flies the PC to Ossaria's western dunes overnight. The battle, its choices (:war_climax, :war_terms), WAR-1 and the legendary fight are in 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING Part B; the Dominar's petition follows it. Then Sigrun flies the PC back to Wyrmrest for Gym 18.

Reshiram (Ashkaar's legendary arc)

(Unless :war_legend is :neither, the Light Stone wakes in the Dominar's hand on the Glass Dunes and the fight below happens there, on the dunes' field; see 14. With :neither the stone stays dark at the front, and the fight happens here, as written, after the truce, when the stone comes home.)

  1. Any true answer wakes the Light Stone, which has hung in Wyrmrest's Rift-shrine since Ch8 if it was sent there, or which arrives carried by a Hearthguild runner if it wasn't.
  2. Boss battle: Reshiram (multi-bar) on :DRAGONS_DEN. Its fire is the truth of the PC's oath: Return and Open lean Harmony, Keep is neutral, and Ruin makes the fight savage.
  3. After the battle, Reshiram bows to Sigrun, not to the PC: "the truth is hers to carry now." It flies to Crownhaven ahead of them.
  4. Sigrun, stunned: "...It chose the one who finally said it out loud."

Gym 18 (:DRAGONS_DEN)

Thematic note: the den's heat rises each turn, and the dragons grow stronger the longer you hesitate. Sigrun fights at her absolute best. "If you can't beat me, you can't survive him." Her ace is Salamence. On victory she gives the 18th badge, and the badge case sings: all eighteen tones together.

  • If the telemetry was left intact, a Meridian airship on the horizon turns toward Crownhaven within the minute.
  • If it was sabotaged, Larch's voice on the radio: "He bought it. God help us, he bought it."

Rainbow Scar and the road to Crownhaven

Rainbow Scar (868) is a Bleed zone where all eighteen Imprints bleed together into light. It foreshadows the Prism Arena. Then The Pilgrim Pass and the Sovereign's Ascent:

  • At high Accord Standing or with the Royal Writ, the Wardguard escort takes the PC up the processional stair.
  • Otherwise, Edda's smugglers take them through the Glassfall Scar (888), the forty Fixed of AF 290, still in Lower Crownhaven where they fell. The PC walks among them. One of them is a Choir cantor with her mouth open mid-note who is not Ines; Ines got out. The PC finds the place where they stood at five.

CHAPTER 20 — "The Festival of Champions" (Crownhaven, Festival week)

Revision 4: no sister-game cameos appear anywhere in Festival week. They are optional sidequests elsewhere (design/CAMEOS.md). The bracket, draw pools and exhibitions use original characters only, following story/10_CHOICES_ENDINGS.md §3 and NARRATIVE_KEYS §6. Revision 5: every possible opponent is someone the PC has met at least twice by Act IV. Revision 6: the Festival is the ceremony of Arceus's Blessing. Entrants are kingdom delegations (two per kingdom, Valen, and the PC), chosen by player choices: see 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING.md Part A, which replaces the seed list here. The PC picks their colors on Day 0 (:ch20_colors). Companion-vs-companion matches can be watched as highlight cutscenes (13_CUTSCENES.md). The Coronation in Ch21 is "the Blessing", and Ch19's Dominar scenes play inside the Battle of the Glass Dunes.

Day 0: Arrival

  1. Crownhaven is white stone and bells in the caldera. Upper Crownhaven is festooned with Tamsin's eighteen banners, woven since Ch10. The Meridian Prism Arena gleams where the old grounds were, too new.
  2. The Consent display. By Day 1 each Warden's banner hangs white (they would let go) or grey (they won't). It is Tamsin's private reading of her colleagues, and the player can read it. These are the Consent conditions made visible (NS §6.2).
  3. Every faction is here: - Meridian runs security under a Council vote that Anja's swing vote couldn't stop. - The Lantern Hollow are disguised as Choir porters. - The kings are in the observers' gallery: Caedmon for Elowen, Eirik, the Dominar's herald, Kassan, Dask. - Envoy Delphine Okoro of the Concert, deciding on Severance.
  4. The Veil Gate stays shut. The Festival used to host champions of other worlds, until the Synod sealed the Gate in AF 230 (01_WORLD_LORE). Archseer Dask refuses Hollis's request to reopen it "for prestige": "The Glass is leaking already. I won't open a door in a wall that's falling down." No foreign champions come this year. Every entrant is someone the PC has met on the road (Revision 5).
  5. The Draw. The Hierophant draws lots from a crystal bowl at the Basilica steps. - Sixteen stand in the arena: the PC and fifteen kingdom delegates (10_CHOICES_ENDINGS §3.1; staging in 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING Part A). The war decides how many seats Isenmar and Ashkaar hold. - The PC's colors (:ch20_colors). Before the bowl, Queen Maelis, the Zenith Council and Nyx each offer the PC their colors, and Larch offers none: the old clause for "the Unsworn". Values elowen / zenith / nadir / unsworn (NARRATIVE_KEYS §4.3). - The lots are honest; the bowl isn't. The Accord's old customs (the Right of Grievance, yielded invitations, a Warden asking for a challenger's quarter, and Dorian, who has never once let the bowl ruin a good story) bend it on screen (NS §3.1).

Day 1: The Opening Ceremony (the 18 Plates)

  1. The procession. At dusk, eighteen Wardens descend the Sovereign's Stair into the Prism Arena, each carrying their Plate in a reliquary, in gym order to the counting rhyme sung by the Choir: - Dorian (Blank) - Tamsin (Insect) - Marisol (Splash) - Rook (Zap, still cracked, in a cradle; if Rook was fired in Ch16, a Meridian officer carries it, and Rook watches from the crowd) - Sahar (Earth) - Corvin (Toxic; carried by a Choir porter in his mask unless CORVIN_FREED) - Brann (Flame) - Kaito (Fist) - Juno (Meadow) - Anja (Icicle) - Odessa (Sky) - Ilsa (Mind) - Bastian (Stone, leaning on Pip) - Ysolde (Spooky) - Magnus (Iron; under guard if MAGNUS_EXPOSED) - Nyx (Dread) - Celestine (Pixie) - Sigrun (Draco)

Each sets their Plate into a pylon of the Concordance Ring.

  1. The Tuning. Valen in white, the Crown on his brow, the grey glove off. The arena sees his crystal arm for the first time, and a murmur runs through forty thousand people. The Choir sings the half-Hymn. The Ring lights in eighteen colors, and the sky over Crownhaven ripples.
  2. The PC's vision. The shard resonates violently. The world goes white. In the white, a vast shape of light with eighteen empty places in its wheel opens one eye:

    "...Little light. You have carried me far."

The PC collapses in the stands. Valen sees. Ilsa, in the Warden ranks, takes her earmuffs off and flinches at her father's pain.

  1. Rook's leak (if :ch16_rook = hold): the Spire footage of Kroll with a Meridian keycard plays on the arena's own screens, hijacked by Rook's Rotom. The crowd turns. Voss, in his box, doesn't blink: "Rogue contractor. The inquiry continues." Meridian's polling drops, and the Envoy takes notes.

Day 2: Round of 16 ("someone from your past")

Story staging for each R16 candidate (draw rules: NS §3.2):

  • Marisol, by Right of Grievance (she holds an Isenmar seat, Teo died, and her Bond ≤ 2). The old Accord custom lets a Warden claim a first-round match against a challenger who wronged their city, and the Hierophant reads it out. Marisol and Juno swap seeds: "Let's see you run past me."
  • Anja (she holds an Isenmar seat, and was exposed in Ch11). She invokes the same right, and she and Juno swap seeds: "You threw me to the court. Fine. Ice remembers."
  • Rowan, "the Gardener" (Rowan alive, mercy pleaded at the tribunal, Hollow Standing ≥ 4). Rowan enters masked under a false name. Juno gave him her own invitation: "One last garden, child. Then I'm done with masks." If Rowan drowned at the Fault, this candidate doesn't exist.
  • Juno (J4, fallback). Joyful and nervous under the arena's lights: "We started on the same dock. Let's see who's grown more." The fields cycle on :PRISM_ARENA. Her ace is Tsareena, with Ogerpon in her party if OGERPON_TRUSTED. Rowan's ring answers her at last. The first time she fights at the Festival (J4, or her match in another seed), her Gardevoir Veil, the Ralts from Lucent (Ch13), Mega Evolves. "...Oh. There you are." As the Ch21 partner (J7) she doesn't Mega, because the side's one Mega is the player's. If she's displaced by Marisol or Anja, she plays on in their seed (Isenmar's: against Nadir's second delegate, or against Ashkaar's), and her Garden Match exhibition opens when she's out. If she gave her invitation to Rowan, she watches from the Wardens' box.

After the match: the garden court.

  • If Rowan lives, the PC finds Juno and Rowan in the arena's garden court, sitting apart on the same bench. If Teo lived, he says it himself, holding up his glassed fingers: "I could hear everything while it had me. Everyone who sat with me." (If the PC carries Venam's Testimony from her optional sidequest, it can be played here instead.) Rowan sits down on the grass and cries, and Juno takes his good hand. It's the first time they've touched since Ironreach.
  • Without the testimony, Juno does it herself, more slowly: "Corvin says they dream. I'm going to believe him."
  • If Rowan drowned, Juno sits alone with Elin's pressed lily from the Bride Tree.

Other R16 results follow the companion match rules (NARRATIVE_KEYS §6), and each can be watched as a highlight (13_CUTSCENES.md). Story requirements:

  • Kestrel advances with the Gauntlet, over Zenith's first delegate (Rook or Odessa).
  • Valen and Sigrun advance.

Day 3: Exhibitions and the Festival Grounds

  • The Eevee Octave (SPINE Rev 19; design/EEVEE_OCTAVE.md). On arrival (Day 0) the PC meets Carol, the Octave's Crownhaven singer, in the Glassfall Memorial Garden (489); her quest The Ninth Verse opens once the PC has helped the other seven singers on the road (Lyra, Aria, Cadence, Sona, Noct, Forte, Lento). Once all eight are helped, Vesper waits in the garden with the others: they want to thank the PC and test whether they can carry the power of Eevee. The gauntlet: the eight singers in the order the PC helped them, back to back with no healing, each with one Eeveelution on its home field using its type's Z-move; then Vesper's Eevee Amen with Extreme Evoboost on the Grand Stage. Open from then on, through Festival week and after.
  • Vesper, gentle: "We all lost everything the year the Crown broke. The Choir calls us the lucky ones. I think we're just... what was left." (The singers were children in the AF 290 Glassfall; Vesper was 14.)
  • Reward: an Eevee and the Eevium Z. There's no ring (SPINE Rev 23): the PC's Warden's ring from Cragholm wakes it. Vesper: "Its chip is off the Crown's stone, and our glass came out of the night the Crown broke. They know each other." If Understudy is still an Eevee, Vesper says the crystal works for it too; if it has evolved, she notes which Imprint "claimed" it.
  • Other exhibitions (NS §3.6, original characters only):
  • The Pageant Bout: Dorian and Rook in a double battle staged as "a duet for the cameras", with Rook's Rotom filming it.
  • Juno's Garden Match, if she wasn't the PC's R16.
  • The Ebb Guild match with Marisol while Teo heckles from the stands, if Teo was saved and Marisol is close.
  • Festival grounds side content: the Concordance Spire (Battle Tower) under construction, a teaser; street food from every kingdom; Dorian rehearsing in secret with Celestine.
  • Diplomacy with Envoy Okoro (:ch20_envoy).
  • Proof needs two of three: the Larch Papers, the Arbiter Blueprints, and testimony that the Fixed still dream (any one of: Teo's, if he lived; Corvin's Quiet Ward records, if he's free; Venam's Testimony from her optional sidequest). Together they show the Bleed is caused and so curable, not contagious. Okoro recommends against Severance (ENVOY_PERSUADED).
  • Plea: she listens and drafts Severance anyway, "with regret".

Day 4: Quarterfinal ("the honest view")

The story job is an honest view of the PC's choice from someone who isn't trying to use them, delivered in a hard fight at cap 92. Conditional candidates swap seeds with the fallback (NS §3.5).

  • Celestine (fallback, the headline). She confirms the Return, and it counts as an oath because she cannot lie: "I cannot lie, so listen while we fight." After the match:

    "Give them back. I've waited forty years to say that to someone who could."

  • Sigrun (Resonance ≤ −3, or the PC helped Isenmar break her father's legions): "Dragons weigh things. You've gotten heavier."
  • Kaito (the oath was Keep): "You'd keep them? Marrowgate's still knocking."
  • Ysolde (Kestrel has fallen): "If I can't reach him, I'll find out what reached you."
  • Odessa (she holds a seat; five close Bonds; Harmony-leaning): "Everyone keeps telling you what you're for. The wind doesn't care. What do you want?"
  • (Ruin Route: Archseer Dask. See 12_RUIN_ROUTE.)

Other QF (default): Kestrel beats Kaito, whose Lucario felt it: "That isn't him fighting." Valen advances. Sigrun advances, unless she was drawn into the PC's quarter (then Celestine plays on in Ashkaar's seed).

Day 5: The Night of Masques, the audience, Little Owl

  • Corvin, privately, after treating Valen in the Sanctum: "He has weeks. Maybe. He's holding the Plates quiet right now, with his body, every hour since the ceremony. He'll fight you tomorrow on what's left."

The Night of Masques: "The Gilded King."

  1. In the Basilica square, Dorian stages Ansel Crewe's banned play for the first time in 248 years. Celestine, who cannot lie, voices Princess Maren's lament, and the Saltmere Players wear the Hollow's ogre masks as the chorus.
  2. The square watches the true Prismfall: the Blight, the chain, the god breaking itself, the city drowning, the daughter's penance.
  3. Chancellor Hollis sends the Wardguard to stop it. Kaito (and, if alive, Teo's strikers) stand in the way, and the guard doesn't push.
  4. When the actor playing the Gilded King says "If heaven will not kneel, we'll build a chain", every head in the square turns to the Meridian box.
  5. Voss stands and applauds. Alone. Warmly.

    "Bravo. They finally cast the king correctly."

Calla's defection (:ch20_calla, who lives). Only offered if someone inside is already moving (:ch16_rook = hold, or MAGNUS_KEPT_FAITH).

  • In the crowd after the play, Calla Wren finds the PC, shaking, still in her Meridian lanyard. She can get the arena's power schematics to Larch.

    "I scanned you on the dock. I photographed the screen. I've been sending him your life for six months. Let me do one thing that isn't that."

  • Shelter her with Edda's boat. She brings the partial schematics she already has: one crack in the Engine. She lives.
  • Send her back for the full set: two cracks. Kroll finds her in the Spire stairwell, and she doesn't come back. The schematics arrive by Gale Post at dawn, with a smear of blood on the envelope.
  • Turn her away: "Then I'll just — go home, I suppose." She leaves, and nobody sees her again.

Valen's audience (the PC speaks). Valen summons the PC to the Sovereign's Sanctum: candlelight, a camp bed, his crystal arm resting on a cushion like something borrowed. He doesn't defend himself. He explains.

"Every ten years I bring the Plates home to Crownhaven, and every ten years Velmora endures. You noticed I never said 'thrives'. Nobody ever notices."

"Morwen didn't cause the Glassfall. I let them say she did, because if the world knew the ceremony could fail, the kings would tear the Plates out of the ground and we'd all drown. I chose a country over a woman's name. I'd do it again. I hate that I'd do it again."

"When you beat me tomorrow — and you will — I'll put the Crown on you. The splinter in your heart will make it whole. You'll hold the Plates quiet for a hundred years, and you won't age as fast as I did. You'll be... very lonely. I'm sorry. I have no other door."

The PC answers (authored line, CHOICE :ch20_audience):

  1. "There's another door. The Hymn. We give them back." (Return) - Valen: "And let eighteen cities go dark? Rimeholt drowns, Cindervault freezes, Verdance's fields fail in a year..." - The PC can answer with the Hymn ("given back, as a gift is found") if they hold the complete version. - Valen, very quietly: "...Maren wrote that. I thought it was a poem."
  2. "Then I'll wear it. Somebody has to." (Keep) Valen weeps, once.
  3. "You don't get to decide that for me. Nobody does." (Refuse) Valen: "Good. Then decide it yourself, tomorrow. That's all I ever wanted, and I never had the courage to want it out loud." - If the PC refuses with a cold Bond, Ilsa never came, and the telemetry still runs, this sets VALEN_COLLAPSED. Voss's pre-ignition drains him overnight, and he can't stand for the Final.

Game over GO_EARLY_CROWN "Early Crown". Valen offers, desperate, to crown the PC tonight and skip the Final, "so I don't have to hurt you first." Accepting triggers it. Foreshadowing: Ilsa's earlier warning, "Don't let him hand you anything tonight. He's not thinking, he's drowning." The Crown is incomplete without the Engine's cradle, which Voss has. The half-Tuning Fixes the PC in the Sanctum, and Voss's men collect the keystone from the Sanctum floor. Epitaph: "The Crown was whole for one second. Then it was Meridian's."

"Little Owl" (Ilsa's side quest culmination, :sq_little_owl). If the PC completed her quest steps, carrying her messages to her father through Acts III–V, Ilsa comes to the Sanctum after the audience.

"You chose a country over a daughter. Fine. Then save the country, Father. Don't make a child pay for it."

Valen: "...Little owl." It's the name from her childhood, which the player heard in the Mindscape in Ch13. She stays the night. If not completed, she watches the Sanctum door from the colonnade and doesn't go in.

Morwen's Echo (conditional exhibition, NS §3.6: Kestrel and Ysolde reconciled, and the K6 line was Resolve). After midnight, Ysolde lights the Hollow Cathedral's lantern in a Crownhaven chapel. Morwen's echo fights the PC once, gently, "to see what I bought."

INTERLUDE V — "The Last Night" (playable as Valen).

  1. Short and quiet. The player controls Valen in the Sanctum before dawn.
  2. He writes three letters: - To Ilsa: if reconciled, he tears it up, because he doesn't need it. - To Morwen's son: "I'm not asking you to forgive me." - To "whoever wears it next".
  3. He walks to the window and talks to Zygarde (a single Cell glowing on the sill): "Order, not justice. I chose order. Was I wrong?" The Cell pulses once. The player decides what that means.

Day 6: Semifinal — Kestrel (K8)

Kestrel's state (KESTREL_FALLEN or not; NS rules):

  • Kestrel (Redeemed) (fallback). He fights with the Gauntlet at first. Mid-battle, at the first field-cycle, he looks at the Gauntlet's light and tears it off, then throws it across the arena floor:

    "No. Not like this. If I beat you, I beat you."

He finishes with Morwen's Mismagius and his Aegislash, honest and ferocious. - If he wears Morwen's Ring (:ch18_kestrel_ring = give_now): the ring answers him the first time he wears it into a fight. When his Scizor comes out, it Mega Evolves (PrismfallMega::MORWEN_RING, automatic at battle start). It's his first Mega, and the only Mega he ever uses. His line as it changes: "Mum. Just this once. Answer me." Then, quieter, when it does: "...She'd have hated the Gauntlet."
