Giving the ring early keeps him from falling, and it also makes the SF the harder fight. - If the PC kept the ring: no Mega. He has no ring of his own, and the story never lends him one (SPINE Rev 21: no borrowed rings, no one-off contrivances). If the PC gives the ring after the match (below), it first answers him in the hijack tag battle, on the player's side. The side has one Mega, though, and the player's comes first. - Kestrel (Fallen). He never got Morwen's Ring (a Fallen Kestrel can't have it), so he has no Mega: the Gauntlet is all he has. He keeps the Gauntlet on. His Pokémon glow with stolen Imprint, the field cycles under his command, and he fights like someone drowning. After the loss, the Gauntlet overloads and burns his hand, and Voss's men carry him off "for medical attention". He reappears in the hijack harnessed into the Engine (Ch21).

After the match, Morwen's letter. Ysolde walks onto the arena floor and gives Kestrel the sealed letter at last. He reads it there, in front of forty thousand people, and the arena screens tactfully cut away. The text (Key Item, readable later):

"Kestrel. If you're reading this, you're ready, or Ysolde's given up waiting. Both are fine. I didn't fail. I chose. There was a child in the light and I was nearest, and I'd have wanted someone to choose you. They'll call me a disgrace. Let them. Be a Vane anyway — be the kind that's nearest when it matters. I love you more than my seat, more than my name, more than my Plate. That's the whole letter. — Mum."

  • Redeemed: Kestrel sits down on the arena floor. If the PC still has Morwen's Ring, they can give it now. Then:

    "...Then you take him. Take him for both of us."

If both Ysolde's and Kestrel's Bonds are high (KESTREL_YSOLDE_RECONCILED), he lets her sit beside him.

  • Fallen: he doesn't read it. Ysolde keeps it. If the PC kept :ch12_letter, they can quote Morwen to him in the Engine instead.

Other SF (default; if Sigrun was the PC's QF, Valen's semifinal is a one-line result instead): Valen beats Sigrun. Sigrun entered to win the Crown herself and spare the PC, and Valen beat her to protect her. She leaves the arena without a word. The PC finds her on the Basilica roof: "He beat me with an arm made of glass. I've never been so angry in my life."

Day 7: The Final, the Coronation, the Hijack

See Chapter 21.

CHAPTER 21 — "Sovereign" (the Final, the Hijack, Arceus, the endings)

The Final: Valen Corrigan (CHAMPION_VALEN, cap 96)

  1. Dawn. The whole cast fills the arena.
  2. Valen, with no glove at all now: "Come on, then. Show me there's another door."
  3. The battle on :PRISM_ARENA, with fields cycling. His ace is Zygarde (Complete Forme on its last bar: "Order, not justice. I chose order.").
  4. Mid-battle, every time the field cycles, his crystal visibly spreads, from shoulder to throat.
  5. Draw variant, "Valen or his successor": if Valen has collapsed before the Final, the PC fights the Sovereign-designate instead. - This happens if VALEN_COLLAPSED is set (Ch20 audience). - Sigrun (Bond ≥ 5): "He beat me with an arm made of glass. Now he can't stand. So it's me." - Otherwise Brann, who fights in tears: "He asked me to. Last thing he asked." - Valen watches from a stretcher, which puts him in position for the Ring later.
  6. After the PC wins: Valen yields, smiling. "Velmora has a new champion."

The Coronation

  1. Valen lifts the Crown from his head and walks to the PC at the arena's heart, inside the Concordance Ring.
  2. The Choir sings, and the crowd is on its feet.
  3. CHOICE :ch21_crown: kneel to receive it / stand / step back. Each is flavor that the Narrative Systems endings may read.
  4. The moment the Crown is raised over the PC's head, the eighteen Plates in the Ring scream.

The Hijack (default hijacker: Voss)

  1. The Meridian Prism Arena wakes. Its rings (the Arbiter Engine, built into the venue) ignite in gold.
  2. The keystone cradle, installed beneath the arena floor, rises in a golden hand.
  3. The Concordance Ring's pylons sprout golden locks, the new Gilded Chain.
  4. The Crown is torn from Valen's hand into the cradle. The PC is pinned by their own shard's pull, half-kneeling at the cradle's palm.
  5. Voss descends from his box onto the arena floor in a Meridian Engine-harness. He's calm, almost apologetic, wearing his gold sunburst pin.

    "You carried my key through eighteen doors. Let me show you what it opens."

Hijacker variants (NS §3.2):

  • Dr. Quent (Voss discredited: MAGNUS_EXPOSED plus Rook's leak plus the Night of Masques). The board removed Voss in disgrace before Day 7. Quent giggles in the harness, with Voss's Silvally team. Voss watches from the gallery, appalled at his own machine in someone else's hands.
  • Ruin Route: Theodric, the Gilded Reflection (story/12_RUIN_ROUTE.md, R7).

His hand. Larch has warned the PC that morning: "Don't let him make you a part. He's very good at parts." Voss offers his hand: "Stand up. Stand with me. It doesn't have to hurt."

  • With VOSS_ACCEPTED (:ch21_hand):
  • Take it: Concord Dawn begins here, and Arceus is never fought.
  • Refuse: Voss, genuinely hurt: "You promised."
  • Without it, taking his hand is Game over GO_HIS_HAND "His Hand". Foreshadowing: Kestrel's K7 speech, and Celestine's "not chained, not bought". Epitaph: "It didn't hurt. That was the cruelest part."

The allies move. Each beat fires only if its condition holds. Show as a fast montage, one line each. These are Larch's eleven lamps (NS §6.2).

  • Rook (ROOK_CUTS_GRID, which needs :ch16_rook = hold) cuts Lumen's grid from the arena feed: "First time Lumen's been dark in ten years. Kinda pretty." The Engine flickers.
  • Nyx blacks out Meridian comms. With the bargain (NYX_PRECISE) it's surgical. Without it, it's bloody, and it doesn't count as an Engine break.
  • Magnus (MAGNUS_KEPT_FAITH) in the arena's machine-gallery disables the safety governor: "No machine I have built will kill a child. Governor's off. Go."
  • Marchetti (MARCHETTI_TURNED: Ch14 evidence, or saved at the Fault) orders the Directorate to stand down: "Not for this. Never for this."
  • Larch reads the Engine's live output off her board of eleven lamps. With TELEMETRY_SABOTAGED: "It's miscalibrated! It's reaching for a shard that isn't where it thinks!"
  • Calla's schematics (:ch20_calla) light one lamp, or two if she went back. If she went back, Larch touches the second lamp and says nothing.
  • Sigrun and her dragons hold the sky against Meridian's Gilded Hours airships, with Reshiram beside her. With DOMINAR_SWAYED, the Ashkaar legions fly with her.
  • Marisol's fishing fleet evacuates Lower Crownhaven across the caldera lake. Edda pilots the lead boat.
  • Tamsin's silk nets catch falling arena debris over the stands.
  • The Lantern Hollow (LANTERN_HOLDS), led by Rowan, Teo, or Thistle and Wick, guard the Ring's pylons against Directorate techs.
  • Kaito holds the arena gate.

Tag battle (story). It's a short, desperate double battle on the cracking arena floor that clears the way to the hijacker.

  • Partner: Kestrel if Redeemed, otherwise Juno.
  • Foes: two of Marchetti / Quent / Kroll, whichever aren't turned, dead or hijacking (NS: "Ch21 tag foes v21").

Voss (MERIDIAN_VOSS, cap 100) on :PRISM_ARENA

  • Boss battle (multi-bar for his ace): Silvally (Project NULL), whose type follows the active field as the Prism Arena cycles through the eighteen gym fields. The rest of his team is "things men made" (see 03_CAST).
  • Mid-battle lines:
  • "Your mother wilted for ten years because a god dropped its furniture on her."
  • "I'm not your enemy. I'm the only adult in this arena who'll say the true thing out loud: we don't need it."
  • Between bars 2 and 3, if KESTREL_FALLEN: Kestrel is revealed harnessed into the Engine as Voss's conduit, Gauntlet fused to the cradle and burning. CHOICE :ch21_reach_kestrel:
  • Reach (needs Morwen's Ring or Morwen's words from a kept letter): the PC says her line, "Be the kind that's nearest when it matters." He comes back. The Gauntlet goes dark, and Kestrel tears himself loose.
  • Burn: the PC's shard tears the Gauntlet off by force. He lives, scarred across the arm (Ruin −3).
  • Let go: he burns out as the Engine fires (KESTREL_LOST). This is the road to The Empty Lighthouse.
  • On defeat: the Engine doesn't stop. Voss drives his harness-spike into the cradle and becomes the conduit himself. "Then I'll hold it."

Arceus Descends

  1. The sky over Crownhaven opens, white.
  2. Arceus is dragged down through it into the Engine's golden chains, eighteen locks closing on eighteen empty places in its wheel. It is enormous, half-bound and in agony. The Prism Arena turns to :BLEED across the whole caldera.
  3. The hijacker, at the cradle, ecstatic and horrified: "It's — it's beautiful —"
  4. Arceus's Judgment strikes the harness. CHOICE :ch21_spare_voss: - Shield him with the shard (PC_SPARED_VOSS): he lives, crippled. - Let it judge: he becomes light at the arena's heart.
  5. The Bleed surge rolls out toward forty thousand people in the stands.

Valen holds the Ring.

  1. Valen puts the cracked Crown back on, from the cradle's palm where the PC tore it loose, and walks into the Concordance Ring.
  2. He grips two pylons and holds the surge. His crystal blazes white.
  3. If ILSA_RECONCILED, Ilsa is at his back with her hands on his shoulders, pouring her mind into his: "I've got you. Little owl's got you."

    "Go. Free it. I'll hold the door — I've had thirty years of practice."

(If Valen collapsed before the Final, he is carried to the Ring on his stretcher and stands up anyway.)

The True Finale: Arceus (cap 100)

Boss battle: Arceus, multi-bar, type- and field-shifting. Variant by state (NS §6.6): Bound (default), Miscalibrated (telemetry sabotaged), War (Resonance ≤ −6), Gilded (Engine calibrated: the Bad ending), Judgment (Ruin Route only).

  • Six bars, three locks each, in gym order. Bar 1 is Dorian, Tamsin and Marisol, and so on through bar 6: Nyx, Celestine and Sigrun. The Prism Arena shifts to the matching gym field for each lock.
  • Between bars, those three Wardens kneel at their pylons and release their Plate, letting go of the bond they've carried their whole life, or refuse. Every refusal makes the next lock forced: Arceus gains +1 to every stat stage for that bar.
  • All 36 lines (18 releases, 18 refusals, each refusal tied to the player's choice that caused it) are in story/11_FINALE_LINES.md.
  • Celestine sings the Hymn's last verse as her lock breaks. The Gloaming choir in the stands picks it up, then the Prism Choir, then the crowd.
  • Harmony vs Ruin. At high Harmony, the PC's Pokémon are steadied by the shard (systems: minor buffs). In the War variant, the shard eats Arceus's types instead of freeing them, and the battle is a war, not a liberation.
  • Gilded variant: the PC fights for Arceus against the chains and loses the struggle anyway. The last bar can't be broken. This is The Gilded Chain.

Valen's death (all main-route paths except Gilded). As the final lock breaks, Valen's crystal burns through, not to glass but to light. He says the PC's name. If reconciled, he says "Little owl." Then he's gone, and the Crown falls empty to the arena floor.

Arceus speaks

  1. Freed, Arceus stands over the arena, whole except for its heart.
  2. The PC's shard is pulled gently out of their chest, painless and luminous, and hangs between them and the god beside the Crown's shard.
  3. The Legend Plate is whole for the first time since AF 0.
  4. Ilsa (if reconciled) gives Arceus's voice to everyone in the arena:

    "Little light. You have carried me far. You may give my heart back, and the rest of me with it. Or you may keep what was borrowed, and wear it, and hold this land quiet in your two hands for a hundred years. I will not take what is not given. I learned that here."

(The last sentence is a Ruin Route hint: Arceus is talking about Judgment.)

The final decision. The PC speaks (authored), CHOICE :ch21_final. Availability per NS §6.1:

  • Return (always): "Go home. Take them with you."
  • Keep (always): "I'll keep them. I'll keep everyone safe."
  • Borrowed (Kestrel Redeemed and devoted, or Sigrun Bond ≥ 6): the PC hesitates, and Kestrel (or Sigrun) steps forward and takes the Crown: "Not you. Let me be nearest."
  • Concord (VOSS_ACCEPTED, or Magnus's governor never switched off): "Stay. Stay and power the world."
  • Unmake (Resonance ≤ −6, or Hollow Standing ≥ 4 with Rowan radicalized or Kroll never publicly exposed): "No. No more gods."

THE ENDINGS (scenes; the conditions matrix is NS §6.3)

GOOD: "Homecoming"

  1. Arceus takes the eighteen Plates and its heart, and ascends. Light rains on Crownhaven.
  2. The Bleed recedes across the realm in one long exhale.
  3. The Fixed who still dream wake: - In Verdance, the Bride Tree's blossom falls all at once, and Elin opens her eyes in Rowan's arms with Juno beside them, under the first falling leaves Verdance has ever seen. If Rowan drowned at the Fault, Juno holds her aunt alone and has to tell her. - In the Lowlight, Dex blinks, finishes his wave, and says, "—and that's why my sister says I talk too much." Rook, standing there in the dark city, laughs until he cries. - In Mirefen, Corvin's Quiet Ward sits up. - In Lower Crownhaven, the Glassfall Scar's forty breathe again.
  4. The Fixed who stopped dreaming (Marrowgate's oldest, the long-Fixed of the Quiet Towns) dissolve into soft light. Kaito is there to watch it, at Marrowgate's sealed gate, with his Lucario. He opens the gate.
  5. The PC, alone in the arena center, feels something they've never felt: the ground. The plain land, with no Imprint at all, imprints them. A Meridian scanner left on the floor reads a faint, ordinary color at last.
  6. Voss: if shielded, he's alive, crippled, and asks to see the sunrise. Otherwise he is light at the arena's center, a man who reached for a god.

Epilogue ("One Year Later": Fallmorn, AF 301, the first Festival of Seasons). Slides:

  • Juno in Verdance's first autumn, raking leaves with Elin, and with Rowan if he lived.
  • Kestrel, Ghost Warden of Gravenmoor (KESTREL_ACCEPTED_SEAT), or a Gale Post wanderer.
  • Teo on the Ebbmouth quay, or his photograph on the Guild wall.
  • Calla's name on the new Spire memorial, if she went back.
  • Rimeholt rebuilding on the southern shore, with Anja and Eirik and a thaw-fishery.
  • Cindervault's forges on coal again. Brann has forged Valen's memorial from the empty Crown's setting.
  • Ossaria: the caravans walk the western road again, round the Glass Dunes, where the bone-carters keep the newest necropolis in the Bone Sands. Kassan is arrested on the Sandgate steps, and the Elector's Lease is read out among the charges.
  • Lumen with fewer lights and more stars, and the Zenith Council reformed with Nadir's first elected seat. Nyx is in it and hates it.
  • The quarantine: it lifts now (ENVOY_PERSUADED) or a year late, grudgingly. Edda's ferry runs again.
  • Bastian dies peacefully at home: "the first Warden in three hundred years with nothing in his keeping".
  • Celestine sees her first full night sky in sixty years and starts to age, gladly.
  • The PC stands at the Ferrow's Landing rail where they arrived, as the first ferry comes in. Edda: "Don't lean on my rail like that, sprog."

BAD: "The Gilded Chain"

  1. The Engine holds. Arceus is bound in gold above Crownhaven, a second sun.
  2. The PC, the keystone, sleeps in the cradle, adored as "the Sovereign Who Sleeps", visited by schoolchildren.
  3. Zenith blazes. Nadir is cleared. The Bleed stops.
  4. The kingdoms kneel, because Meridian owns the light.
  5. The final image is the chipped linesman's mug on a desk above the world, steaming. Quent variant: the mug is Quent's novelty mug, and Voss stands among the visiting schoolchildren's parents, looking up at the PC in the cradle.
  6. Credits, then the title screen. There is no post-game.

GREY: "The Long Vigil" (Keep)

The PC wears the Crown. The Plates sleep quiet. Arceus departs incomplete, sorrowing. The Bleed halts, the Fixed stay Fixed, and the miracles remain. The epilogue is the PC at the next Tuning, ten years later, with the first crystal on their hand. Juno and Kestrel are beside them, swearing to find another door. Post-game: the Warden's Gauntlet is framed as Sovereign's audiences.

GREY: "Homecoming, Unfinished" (Return, Consent < 12 or Resonance < 2)

The Return happens without enough consent. The unreleased Plates are torn away, and those cities suffer a Last Shatter. The rest is Homecoming, but with funerals. The slides show one image per refusing Warden's city, in gym order, using the lines in 11_FINALE_LINES.md §3. If Resonance was below Harmony, the PC's scar never takes the land's color. It's hard, it's free, and it's ash-grey and hopeful.

GREY: "The Empty Lighthouse" (Return with Consent and Harmony, but KESTREL_LOST)

Everything in Homecoming happens, but Kestrel burned out as the Engine's conduit.

  • Hesper climbs the lighthouse every night and lights a lamp nobody needs.
  • Ysolde keeps the Ghost seat.
  • The PC reads Morwen's letter aloud at Kestrel's grave in Gravenmoor, beside his mother's, for the boy who never opened it.
  • Last slide: Kestrel's Aegislash, sheathed, on the PC's belt.

GREY: "The Hollow Spring" (Unmake, main route)

The PC uses the shard to break the Plates. The Imprints die in one night of fire and glass. Arceus, with no Plates to receive, departs wounded forever. Velmora is ruined, and free: nobody will ever rule through a Plate again. Rowan plants the first seed in plain soil, or Thistle does if Rowan drowned. Juno doesn't speak to him, or to her. If Teo lived, he's the one who won't. Post-game: partial (Spire and Gauntlet only).

GREY: "Concord Dawn"

  • Arceus is "humanely" half-bound by Magnus's governor and powers the realm.
  • The Bleed ends and prosperity booms. The PC sits on the Zenith Council.
  • Over the last slide, Celestine speaks in fairy-tale cadence: "Once upon a time a god was kept in a box. It was quiet. For a while."
  • If reached through :ch21_hand, the PC never fought Arceus. The last slide is the PC reading the arena's power output on a Council screen.
  • Post-game: partial (Spire only; the Wardens are pensioned off; Quent's Concord Zero arc starts).

GREY: "The Borrowed Crown"

Kestrel (KESTREL_BEARS) or Sigrun takes the Crown in the PC's place. The Plates sleep, and the bearer starts to crystallize. The PC sails home on the first ferry after the quarantine lifts, then comes back every Festival.

  • With Kestrel, the last slide is his hand on the rail, beginning to turn to glass, and he's smiling.
  • With Sigrun: "Ten years. Maybe twelve. I was relieved once. Never again."

RUIN: "The Unmaking" / "The One Who Came Back"

Ruin Route only. See story/12_RUIN_ROUTE.md (R7) and NS §5.4.

POST-GAME HOOKS

Scope by ending (NS §6.5): full after Homecoming, Unfinished (refusers are absent from the Gauntlet), Empty Lighthouse, Long Vigil, Borrowed Crown and both Ruin endings. Partial after the Hollow Spring and Concord Dawn. None after the Gilded Chain.

  • The Concordance Spire (Battle Tower) in Crownhaven, and the Warden's Gauntlet: all eighteen Wardens back-to-back at level 100. In Homecoming their teams no longer use fields, because the Imprints are fading, so it's a "pure" gauntlet.
  • Zygarde chooses the PC at Valen's memorial (ZYGARDE_CHOOSES: Valen Bond ≥ 3 or Ilsa reconciled), completing the Zygarde Cell quest.
  • The Distortion Core (Antumbra, 910): Giratina's rematch and capture, and the leak in the Glass.
  • Legendary rematches and captures: Kyogre (Lake Rime), Groudon (Undersands), Zekrom (Stormfront), Reshiram (Wyrmscar, if not with Sigrun), Pecharunt (Lightless Deep), Ogerpon and the Loyal Three (Bride Grove).
  • Shardfall Isles (905) and the Hallow Strait (900/901): the outer islands, where the quarantine began. Bleed remnants are fading.
  • Concord Zero: Dr. Quent escapes with an Engine fragment, the seed of a post-game villain arc.
  • Cameo superbosses (design/CAMEOS.md), all optional: Lin (with her lines changed by ending), Garret's Eden rumor near Marrowgate (a deliberate dead end, and a kindness), and level-100 rematches with the earlier cameos.
  • The Ferrow's Landing lighthouse: Hesper Vane, finally, asks the PC to tell her about her daughter's last night.

Red herrings (keep them fair)

  • "The Mourner is Morwen." Seeded by Kestrel. Disproved at Ch9. Morwen's real fate is in Ch15.
  • "Dorian is the Mourner." A theatrical voice, he owns the stage the Mourner walked out of, and he's oddly calm afterward. Disproved on the night itself: he is in his box above the PC, shouting for the house lights, while the Mourner is on the stage.
  • "Larch is working for Meridian." Her past, her Lattice. She's guilty but loyal. It resolves at Ch12, when she burns her career on air.
  • "Valen is the villain." He's the most suspicious figure in Acts III–IV. He's the liar, not the villain. Ch20 recontextualizes.

Wording rules for rings and crystals (#1, #5, #6; SPINE Revs 21 and 23)

  • Before Ch17, a Warden's ring is "a chip of the Crown's own stone" and a Z-crystal is "Glassfall glass" or "Choir glass". The link between them is "the glass came out of the night it cracked" or "same crown, one way or another". Nobody names the Legend Plate (#5) or says the stone was "reset" (#6).

  • Never write that a crystal, or the glass, is the Crown's stone or a piece of a Plate. The PC's splinter must stay the only missing piece (Ch17: "You're the missing piece").

  • Glassfall glass is ten years old (AF 290). A crystal can't be older than that, and it can't be buried in old rock unless someone put it there (a Choir pilgrim leaving it to soak, 01_WORLD_LORE §3).

Story Bible 14: The Ashkaar–Isenmar War and Arceus's Blessing (SPINE Revision 6)

Authoritative for the war arc, the Blessing, and the kingdom delegations. Where 01, 02, 05–08 disagree with this file, this file wins (the act files carry short pointers). Storyboards are in 13_CUTSCENES.md. Keys marked (proposed) are for the Narrative Systems agent to adopt in NARRATIVE_KEYS.

PART A — ARCEUS'S BLESSING (the Festival reframed)

What everyone believes

The Festival of Champions is the one sacred ceremony all seven kingdoms share. Every ten years each kingdom carries its Plates to Crownhaven and sends two delegates to fight before the Plates. The last one standing receives Arceus's Blessing:

  1. The Light. The Crown is set on the victor inside the Concordance Ring, and the light of all eighteen Plates passes through them. The Choir teaches that this is Arceus touching one mortal.
  2. The Seat. The Blessed holds the Sovereign Seat for the decade.
  3. The Boon. The Blessed may speak one decree that every crown must honor until the next Festival: a border, a peace, a tax, a pardon. This is why kings care, and why they send their best. Maren's first Boon founded the Wardguard. Valen's three Boons: the Plate-tax ban (AF 270), the Marrowgate silence (AF 280, sealed), the Morwen verdict (AF 290, sealed).

What is true

  • The Light is the Tuning. "The Plates' light passing through the Blessed" is the bearer's body hushing the Plates. The Blessing shortens every life it touches. Nothing in 01 §5 changes except the name the public uses.
  • The Boon is real law and was Maren's own invention: a reward large enough that the strongest person in the realm would always volunteer for a thing that kills them.
  • Valen has been Blessed three times. He intends the PC to be the fourth name on the list and the last.
  • Voss needs the Blessing moment itself: eighteen Plates converged, the Crown raised, a bearer in the Ring. The Arbiter Engine fires during the Light. He also wants Zenith's delegates to win the Boon as a fallback ("Mandate in perpetuity").
  • The Hymn of Return read correctly: the last Blessed gives the Light back.

Retcons (small)

  • "Sovereign" = "the Blessed". The Coronation in Ch21 is "the Blessing". Arceus's speech gains one line: "They call this my blessing. I have never once been asked."
  • The Good ending adds a Boon beat: with the Plates gone, the PC still gets one decree. CHOICE :ch21_boon (proposed): end the war's reparations / seat Nadir on every council / dissolve the Seat itself.
  • Entrants are delegations, not a free draw (below). The bowl still decides pairings.

Delegations (fifteen delegates plus the PC)

The seat rules are owned by Narrative Systems: 10_CHOICES_ENDINGS.md §3.1 and NARRATIVE_KEYS §6.1 are authoritative. In short:

  • Two seats per kingdom, plus Valen for the Accord. Every delegate has been met at least twice by Act IV.
  • Elowen: Juno and Celestine (Juno may give her seat to Rowan, "the Gardener").
  • Antumbra: Ysolde, and Kestrel if Gravenmoor restores the name Vane, else Ilsa.
  • Zenith: Rook or Odessa, and Kestrel under Meridian's sunburst, else Magnus.
  • Nadir: Kaito, and Nyx or Corvin.
  • Ossaria: Sahar and Bastian. Ossaria fought nobody, so the war never costs it a seat.
  • Isenmar: Marisol and Anja. Ashkaar: Sigrun and Brann.
  • The war decides seats. A kingdom that lost the war, or both if the clash broke both armies, forfeits its second seat, and the Accord lends it to a seatless Warden.
  • Story staging: the delegations camp in the Court of Eight Pavilions. Each ruler presents their delegates to the Hierophant on Day 0, and a forfeited seat is shown as an empty pavilion pole with the banner cut down. Ossaria's pavilion is pitched between Isenmar's and Ashkaar's, because nobody else would stand there, which is how it was on the sands.

The PC's colors — CHOICE :ch20_colors (proposed to NS; flavor and one Standing only). The PC enters as the Unimprinted challenger, but may wear a kingdom's colors. Three crowns offer the PC theirs on Day 0: Queen Maelis (the PC landed on her soil), the Zenith Council (Voss's Fellowship), and Nyx ("Nadir could use a null"). Larch offers a fourth: no colors at all, entered under the old Accord clause for "the Unsworn". Each choice changes crowd reactions, one R16 line and one Standing; Unsworn is the Harmony option and Celestine's Hymn names it ("one of no color").

Pairings. The bowl avoids same-kingdom pairs in R16. Stage pools from 10_CHOICES_ENDINGS §3 stand, re-read as delegations. War pairings (Ashkaar vs Isenmar) are staged as grudge matches under truce.

PART B — THE ASHKAAR–ISENMAR WAR

Why they fight (and why it isn't a detour)

  • Isenmar's heat is Ashkaar's fire. Meridian's heat-towers in Rimeholt are fed by Prism Cells charged at the Cindervault geothermal tap. Ashkaar's Flame Imprint is being drained to keep Isenmar's children warm. Meridian sold it to both crowns as two unrelated contracts.
  • Old grievance: the bone sands between them. Fire and ice share no border (WORLD.md §10). Isenmar holds the west, Ashkaar the east, and Elowen and Ossaria lie between. The one ground both can reach is Ossaria's western dunes: Isenmar comes down the Mast Glacier, Ashkaar comes west through the Cinderglass Barrens. Isenmar's sled-caravans and Ashkaar's riders both cross those dunes to the salt and glass markets, both claim the old caravan road and its wells under treaties with long-dead Electors, and they have skirmished there for a century. Ossaria signed neither treaty and honors neither.
  • Voss wants the war. Two opposed Imprints colliding at scale is the best calibration data the Engine can get short of the Festival. Meridian arms both sides with Prism weapons and logs every clash. The war also keeps two crowns too busy to vote against the Mandate.
  • The Bleed: wherever the Fire and Ice Imprints meet, the sand between them turns to steam-glass, a Bleed zone. The front line is a Bleed line, the Steamline, and only the PC can cross it.
  • The legendaries: Kyogre (woken by the Thaw) and Reshiram (the Light Stone) become the kingdoms' banners, and the climax is their clash: a sea dragged into a desert against a fire that turns it to glass. Ossaria has seen this once before. Its Unown records call it the Year of Two Weathers (01 §2), and the Dry Tide west of Duneholt is the seabed it left behind.

Ossaria: the ground the war is fought on

Two foreign armies fight on Ossarian sand, and Ossaria pays for it. This is how the Bone Sands answer.

  • Prince-Elector Kassan sells the battlefield. When the Dominar closes the eastern passes (Ch8), Kassan declares Ossaria neutral, then rents the war a place to happen. Under the Elector's Lease the Thane gets the western edge (Skaldfast's "forward works" on the Rimed Sands), the Dominar gets the eastern dunes for his camp, and Meridian gets the road between them for its "neutral logistics". Three treasuries pay him rent. The one clause he enforces is that no army comes within a day's ride of Duneholt's Sandgate. It is Meridian's trick with the heat, done with sand: sell the same thing to both sides. Kassan, in Duneholt's Hall of Audience (07, Ch14 transit): "The Bone Sands have buried every army that ever marched into them. I only charge for the plot."
  • The caravan houses turn their backs on him. The western dunes are the caravan road: its wells, its salt pans, the glass market. The war closes all of it. The caravan-mothers elected Kassan for life and can't unseat him, so they ignore him. They guide refugees east to Cragholm, sell bread to both armies at war prices, and lead Marisol's relief sledges to the edge of the Steamline (:war_convoy). Through Acts IV–V Duneholt's caravans leave by the east gate, one house at a time.
  • The bone-carters bury everyone. Ossarian tomb-law says the sand keeps whoever dies on it, so no army takes its dead home. At dusk the bone-carters of Duneholt and Vigil walk out between the lines under a white bone-banner, and both armies hold fire, because both want their dead buried properly. It's the one thing the war agrees on, and the only flag both sides let pass: Anja's refugee column comes east under it (07, Ch14). The carters can't go into the Steamline's glass, so they ask the PC to bring out the ones inside it (optional, from their camp on the Dry Tide, the old seabed west of Duneholt). They witness the :war_prisoner exchange at a caravan well, where Ossarian guest-law forbids blood, and after the climax they are the first people onto the glass.
  • The Wardens. Sahar has read the war before anyone else. The Ossuary's mural of the red titan and the blue one tearing the land (Ch6) shows the western dunes' coastline, and after Groudon's fight in the Undersands she says it aloud (Ch14): "The sand remembers the sea. It doesn't want it back." Bastian shelters both kingdoms' refugees in his seams, and the Ossarian well-folk the armies drove off their wells.
  • What it changes (no new keys; this is how the war keys below read on Ossarian ground): an occupation leaves a foreign army on Ossarian sand, so the land with a boot on its neck is the one kingdom that never fought. Reparations make Kassan bill both crowns "for the sand". With mercy, or with the war stopped, the caravans are back on the western road within the month. In the epilogue Kassan is arrested (Good), with the Lease read out among the charges, or knighted by Meridian (Bad), with the Lease renewed in Meridian's name.

Timeline and inserts per chapter

When Beat (insert into the named chapter)
Ch4 Ebbmouth (seed) Dock gossip: an Ashkaar rider burned an Isenmar sled-caravan on the dune road west of Duneholt. The Ebb Guild's strike is partly about war-levy taxes the Thane is raising "just in case". A Meridian recruiter sells heat contracts under a poster of Cindervault's forges.
Ch6 Duneholt (seed) A caravan-mother at the Sandgate: the western wells have changed hands twice this year, "and both times the new owners had an accent." In the Ossuary, Sahar traces the coastline behind the two titans with one finger: "That's our western dunes. Before the Dry Tide was dry."
Ch8 Cindervault (seed) The Dominar's envoy says it aloud: "Our fire warms our enemies' beds." Brann shows the PC the tap's manifest: destination Rimeholt. The closing of the eastern passes is aimed at Isenmar's heat, with Zenith second. (Retcon: the Dominar's threat is to Isenmar first.) Optional, after the badge: the war road north from Cindervault's north gate (the Cinderglass Barrens, Glasswake, the Wyrmtongue) shows legions drilling on black sand under Cinder Cape Warfort, and Glasswake's furnace-masters losing their apprentices to the levy.
Ch9 Conclave Anja and the Dominar's envoy nearly come to blows in the observers' gallery. Valen separates them. Kassan's envoy, sitting between them, leaves with both their seals: the first copies of the Elector's Lease.
Ch11 Rimeholt: war breaks out :war_warning comes first, on Frostfang Pass: the Dominar's legions are already camped on the western dunes, on leased sand. With the passes closed, Rimeholt's towers overdraw the local Lattice to compensate, which causes the Thaw. Kyogre's Primal rain rolls east for three days, over the Mast Glacier and across the bone sands, and flash-floods the Dominar's forward camps in the dunes (and two Ossarian well-villages nobody mentions). The Thane blames the embargo for his drowned town; the Dominar blames "Isenmar's sea-beast". On the third day war is declared, before the PC leaves Isenmar, on every screen, with Voss offering Meridian's "neutral logistics" to both. The Thane's host goes east along the Sled-Road to Skaldfast.
Ch12 Skyreach Gale Post flies war mail for both sides. Odessa refuses Directorate orders to carry Prism munitions. The Larch Papers include the two heat contracts side by side. Nobody reads that page.
Ch13 Lucent Rowan's tribunal is interrupted twice by couriers from the front. The kings' gallery has two empty chairs. Kassan's is not one of them.
Ch14 Cragholm / Undersands The Steamline is on every screen: steam-glass across Ossaria's western dunes, west of Duneholt, where Isenmar's trench-lines on the Rimed Sands face Ashkaar's Siege Camp. Refugees in Bastian's seams fight over bread: Isenmar's Thaw families, and Ossarian well-folk who don't see why Isenmar's children eat in Ossaria while Isenmar's army drinks from Ossarian wells. A Meridian convoy passes through carrying identical Prism lances for both armies (the PC can see the manifests; this is evidence for Okoro, not a choice). In the transit through Duneholt the PC meets Kassan and the bone-carters (07). War 2, :war_convoy is offered here by Gale Post from Marisol, and it leaves from Duneholt.
Ch15 interlude beat News: the Siege of Skaldfast. Ashkaar's dragons ring the border fortress and burn the sled-road behind it on the Mast Glacier. Marisol's Ebb Guild runs sled-convoys over the glacier from Anchorhold by night. If Teo lived, he's organizing the sleds. From the Jawbone Ridge, on the road to Vigil, the war's smoke stands on the western sky.
Ch16–17 The Purge happens while both crowns are looking at each other. That is why nobody stops it. Nyx says so.
Ch18 Gloaming shelters deserters from both armies, who walked the length of Velmora to reach the one town where nobody can lie to them. They can't lie there either, so they tell the truth about why they ran.
Ch19 Wyrmrest: the climax See below. This replaces "the Dominar marches on Zenith": his legions are dug in on Ossaria's western dunes against Isenmar's host, which has come east over the Mast Glacier and out of Skaldfast onto the Rimed Sands, with Kyogre's flood-sea before it.
Ch20 The Peace of Plates: a truce for the Festival. Both kingdoms send delegates to win the Boon and end the war on their terms.

The Battle of the Glass Dunes (Ch19)

Setup. The front is in Ossaria's western dunes (WORLD.md §9, WORLD_MAP.md §7). Isenmar holds Skaldfast, its border fortress on Ossaria's west edge at the foot of the Mast Glacier, and has dug white trench-lines across the Rimed Sands east of it, sand its host has frozen hard. Ashkaar's legions hold the Ashkaar Siege Camp in the bone sands further east, supplied from Cinder Cape Warfort on Ashkaar's north-east coast through the Cinderglass Barrens and Glasswake. The Bleed strip of steam-glass where the two Imprints meet is the Steamline, and south of it, between the hosts, lie the dunes both sides want: the caravan road and its wells, no-man's-land since Ch14. Sigrun's trial and oath (08, Ch19) happen first, at Wyrmrest. Then word comes that Kyogre has risen from the Ice Vault and is dragging a flood-sea across the desert, and that her father has carried the Light Stone to the front (if it hung in Wyrmrest's Rift-shrine, his riders took it while Sigrun was in the Rift with the PC). Sigrun flies the PC there overnight and sets them down at dawn on the Dry Tide, by the bone-carters' camp a mile behind the lines. The climax is fought on the Glass Dunes between the two hosts, where the flood meets Reshiram's fire and the sand turns to glass.

The flood-sea. Primal Kyogre leaves the Ice Vault under the frozen sea, swims east into the open water off Ossaria's coast, and comes ashore at the western dunes, dragging the Northern Sea in behind it over the Rimed Sands and down into the dunes. For one morning the Dry Tide's old seabed is full again. Reshiram answers it, and its Blue Flare turns wet sand to glass wherever it passes, so the beam clash happens over glassing dunes. If :war_legend is neither, neither legend comes and there is no flood-sea (see the battle, below).

The six war choices (keys and effects: NARRATIVE_KEYS §4.3; this is their staging):

  1. :war_warning (Ch11, before the Thaw). From the top of Frostfang Pass on a hard, clear morning, the PC can see north-east across the Mast Glacier to the bone sands: cookfire smoke along the horizon and a dragon-column circling over it. The Dominar's legions are already on Ossarian sand, and nobody in Isenmar knows. Warn Isenmar, warn Ashkaar that they've been seen, warn both through Valen, or stay silent.
  2. :war_convoy (Ch14). Marisol's siege-runners have bought food in Duneholt's bazaar (the caravan-mothers sell to anyone) and need the Unimprinted to walk the convoy the last mile. The caravan-mothers lead the sledges west across the sands from Duneholt to the edge of the Steamline. From there the PC walks point through the steam-glass, the Bleed quieting around them, and the sledges follow in their footsteps into Isenmar's lines and on to Skaldfast as the siege closes: relief (food), arms (harpoon-guns), or refuse (the caravan-mothers take the food back to Duneholt's refugees).
  3. :war_prisoner (Ch15–16). Anja went west from Cragholm to Skaldfast after Ch14 and was taken in a sortie on the Rimed Sands. Ashkaar holds her in the Siege Camp; the Thane holds the Dominar's nephew in Rime Keep. Odessa flies the PC over the lines by Gale Post, and from there it's a short walk across the sands. Free Anja by walking her out through the Steamline, broker an exchange at a caravan well between the lines under the bone-carters' banner (no blood at a well), or leave it. This is Anja's extra pre-Festival scene: in the cage she says, "Tell my brother I'd have signed for the heaters again."
  4. :war_legend (Ch17–18). Each side begs the PC to bring its legend to the front: calm Kyogre in the Ice Vault (Isenmar's ask: quiet it enough to follow the skalds' horns east), wake Reshiram early with the oath (Ashkaar's ask), or neither. A legend on the sands calls its opposite, as in the Year of Two Weathers, so calm or wake puts both legends at the climax (a calmed Kyogre fires only when Reshiram does). Neither leaves both asleep and the dunes dry. It is the only value that keeps them away (the cutscene plugin's legends: false).
  5. :war_climax (Ch19, MAJOR). On the Glass Dunes, with the flood coming in: stand between, back Ashkaar or back Isenmar.
  6. :war_terms (Ch19 aftermath, only if one side won). At the armistice table in Skaldfast's great hall, with Kassan seated at the end of it uninvited ("Nobody signs anything about my sand without me"), the PC argues for mercy (both armies off the sands), reparations (the loser pays the winner, and Kassan bills them both) or occupation (the winner garrisons the western dunes and the loser's road into them: Skaldfast and the Mast Glacier road if Ashkaar won, Glasswake and the Cinderglass Barrens if Isenmar won, and Kassan extends the Lease for ever).

The four outcomes:

  • WAR_STOPPED (stood between, and both armies have seen enough of the PC to trust them: War Trust ≥ 4). Both lines hold fire. The beams meet over the PC and part. The flood goes back to the sea with Kyogre, and the glass stops where it is.
  • WAR_BOTH_BROKEN (stood between without that trust). Nobody listens. The clash detonates over the dunes and glasses both front lines where they stand. Both kingdoms forfeit a Festival seat.
  • WAR_ASHKAAR_WON / WAR_ISENMAR_WON. The loser's host breaks, Isenmar back behind Skaldfast's walls or Ashkaar back over the Siege Camp's earthwork, and the winner's banners go up over it. The loser forfeits a seat. Occupation terms poison the Good ending: Arceus won't bless a land with a boot on its neck, and this boot stands on two, the loser's and Ossaria's.

The battle. Playable set pieces around the cutscene: from the Dry Tide, a gauntlet through the lines of the side you didn't choose (Isenmar's trench-lines on the Rimed Sands, or the Siege Camp's earthworks; both, by way of the Steamline, if you stand between), a partner battle with Sigrun or Marisol, then the boss fight as written for Reshiram in 08, reframed: the PC fights whichever legendary is about to fire on the other army (Reshiram by default; Kyogre if backing Ashkaar). It is fought on the Glass Dunes' own field, :DESERT until the flood comes in and then changed by the flood and the fire (the fields team owns those transitions). The PC's oath (at Wyrmrest, or spoken early with :wake_reshiram) is what the Light Stone was waiting for: it wakes in the Dominar's hand here (WAR-1 shot 3). If :war_legend kept both legends away, the clash is between the Wardens' aces instead, Sigrun's Salamence against Anja's Mamoswine or Marisol's Gyarados, and the Light Stone stays dark in the Dominar's hand: Reshiram's fight happens at Wyrmrest as 08 wrote it, after the truce, when the stone comes home.

The climax is the pixel-animated cutscene WAR-1 "The Beam Clash on the Glass Dunes" (13_CUTSCENES.md): Kyogre's Origin Pulse, fired out of the flood-sea it dragged into the desert, meets Reshiram's Blue Flare over the flooded dunes. Where they meet, sand and flood-water turn to steam-glass and a Bleed dome swells over both armies. The PC's shard (and the two Wardens who love each side) ends it.

Aftermath.

  • Meridian observers on a sandstone mesa behind the lines pack up their instruments before the steam clears. Larch, by radio: "That wasn't a battle to them. That was a reading." Field Notes logs the Engine's calibration jumping.
  • Sigrun and Anja (or Marisol) stand on the glass between the armies and call the truce: the war will be settled by the Boon. The rulers agree because their legendaries have both left: Reshiram to Sigrun, Kyogre back to the sea, its flood draining out over the dunes behind it.
  • The bone-carters walk out onto the glass under a new white banner. The Glass Dunes stay glass: a steam-glass plain across the caravan road, with both armies' glassed dead standing in it. Ossaria claims it under tomb-law, the newest necropolis in the Bone Sands and the only one with no Ossarians in it.
  • Then come the Dominar's petition in his command pavilion (08, :ch19_dominar) and, if one side won, the armistice in Skaldfast (:war_terms). Sigrun flies the PC back to Wyrmrest for Gym 18.

What the war changes later

  • Consent: side-taking adds refusals (Brann or Anja/Marisol). Standing between adds none.
  • Hijack montage: if the truce held without a victor, Ashkaar's riders hold the sky and Isenmar's ice-riders hold the lake shore, together.
  • Endings: Homecoming's Boon can end reparations, and with them an occupation of Ossaria's sand. The Gilded Chain: Meridian annexes both exhausted kingdoms and buys the Lease from Kassan. Hollow Spring: the war restarts with no Plates and no fire, on the same sand.

Spoilers ahead: this chapter covers late-game twists.

Story Bible 10: Choices, the Festival Draw, Game Overs, the Ruin Route and the Endings

Owner: Narrative Systems. Binding: design/SPINE.md Revision 3. Implementation contract (every key, value, condition and ID): design/NARRATIVE_KEYS.md — if this file and that one disagree, NARRATIVE_KEYS wins and this file is the bug. Built on the story lead's act files 04–08 and the FLAGS.md crosswalk; their key names are kept (lowercased). Kingdom names are Revision 3: Elowen, Antumbra, Isenmar, Ashkaar, Ossaria, Zenith, Nadir, and Crownhaven.

0. Design pillars

  1. No good/evil buttons. Every prompt trades something real: a life now against proof later (Teo or Sable's comm-device), the truth against the person who'd tell it (expose Magnus, or trust him), honesty against a friend's dignity (expose Anja, or let her confess).

  2. Delayed and visible. Most choices pay off two or three chapters later, and the game shows the debt coming due (§1.4), never the numbers.

  3. The world keeps score, not a meter. The big outcomes are counts of people: how many Wardens let go of their Plate (Consent), how many cracks the PC and their friends put in Voss's machine (Engine breaks). Both are shown on screen before the finale.

  4. Easy in, dark later. Act I's choices are small and kind-hearted (who to trust, what to say). Act II asks who to save. Acts III–V ask who you'll let die, and who you'll become.

1. Choice architecture

1.1 Bonds (10)

Range −10..+10. Tiers: hostile ≤ −5 · wary −4..−2 · neutral −1..1 · friendly 2..4 · close 5..7 · devoted 8+.

Bond Start Why it's tracked What it changes
Juno +2 the friend you start with Consent (≥ 0); estranged Juno (≤ −5) travels apart in Ch11; Garden Match exhibition; Homecoming slide with the PC
Kestrel −1 the rival who can fall Fallen at ≤ −4 (or ≤ 1 with the pity line, or ≤ 1 while you're Meridian's ally), unless you gave him the ring or answered K6 bluntly; devoted (8+) lets him take the Borrowed Crown; Ghost seat with Ysolde
Rowan 0 the Mourner radicalized (≤ −2 after being condemned) opens the Hollow Spring; his R16 appearance needs mercy, not affection
Voss +1 the first person who was kind to you how warmly he offers, how bitterly he takes refusal; Ruin R4
Valen 0 the father-figure who planned your life his collapse (≤ −2 with a refusal at the audience); his last words; Zygarde chooses the PC post-game at ≥ 3
Ilsa 0 the daughter who reads minds Little Owl (≥ 3 to start, ≥ 4 to reconcile); Consent (≥ 5 or reconciled)
Sigrun 0 the heir who was relieved war trust (≥ 4); she draws into your QF if you've gone Ruin-leaning or broke Ashkaar; Borrowed Crown bearer (≥ 6)
Nyx 0 the broker Consent (≥ 4 or the bargain)
Marisol 0 the sister of the boy you may not save if Teo died: Consent at ≥ 3, otherwise she claims her Right of Grievance in R16
Ysolde 0 Morwen's partner Kestrel–Ysolde reconciliation (≥ 4), Kestrel's Ghost seat, Morwen's Echo exhibition

Other Wardens are not Bond tracks. When an act file says "Tamsin's Bond goes up", the choice key itself carries it, and it surfaces in that Warden's Consent condition (§6.2). That keeps ten relationships deep instead of thirty shallow.

1.2 Standing (Hollow / Meridian / Accord)

Range −10..+10 (Meridian and Accord start at +1, the Hollow at 0). "High" = ≥ 4 (the Ch10 Sanctuary / Black Site branches, the Ch17 Archive branch); "Low" = ≤ −2; "broken" Hollow = below 0. Standing gates content (branch maps, who ambushes you, Voss's warmth, Lantern Hollow at the hijack) far more than endings; the endings read Standing only through the Hollow Spring and Concord options.

1.3 Resonance (Harmony ↔ Ruin)

One integer from −10 (Ruin, none) to +10 (Harmony, every). It moves only when the PC uses the shard or chooses how to carry grief: soothing or silencing the Glass Matriarch (Ch3), venting or forcing the caldera (Ch8), the Ogre (Ch10), "nobody" (Ch10), burning Morwen's letter (Ch12), the Mindscape line (Ch13), the K6 line (Ch15), the oath (Ch19), Calla (Ch20), burning Kestrel's gauntlet off (Ch21). Bands: ruin ≤ −6 · ruin-leaning −5..−2 · balanced · harmony-leaning 2..5 · harmony ≥ 6.

1.4 How the player sees consequences (no numbers)

  • "X will remember that." Only when a Bond changes tier, or on a MAJOR choice. Rare on purpose, so it lands.

  • The Ties page (Trainer Card, page 3): ten portraits with a lantern that is cracked / guttering / lit / bright / blazing / starred, plus three faction sigils with one word each (Enemy … Ally). The openbook password adds numbers.

  • The scar. The PC's star-shaped scar in the Bag portrait shifts from pearl-white through colorless to a black-violet that eats the edges of the icon. Bleed motes drift toward the PC at Harmony and away at Ruin. Wardens comment ("You've gone cold, love.").

  • The Velmora Gazette in every Pokémon Center: two headlines per chapter picked by rule (e.g. "IRONREACH BOMBER STILL AT LARGE" vs "MERIDIAN CONTRACTOR LINKED TO IRONREACH" after Ch13).

  • Tamsin's eighteen banners (Ch20, the opening ceremony): she weaves one per Warden, in white thread if that Warden will let go and grey if not. "Twelve white. I don't know what it means, but it feels like it means something." That is the Consent count, shown.

  • Larch's Engine board (Ch20, Day 5): a hand-built panel of eleven lamps wired to her readings of the arena. Each lit lamp is a crack in the Engine (§6.2). "If that case is still singing to him and Magnus never flinched, three lamps won't be enough. I can't make that sound kinder."

  • The Journal records every named decision in one line of prose ("You told the Glass Court what you saw in the Lowlight.").

2. Choice catalog (48 keys)

Format: key — situation. Options → immediate effect. Long-term. Exact deltas: NARRATIVE_KEYS §4.2. ★ = MAJOR (10).

Prologue and Act I — "The Last Ferry" (warm; nothing here can ruin you, but everything is remembered)

  • :pro_fellowship — Voss offers a Fellowship card on the Dovetail. accept (money, Meridian trust) / decline (Voss likes you more: "Independent. Good.") / silent (he leaves it on the rail). Sets how warmly Meridian treats you in Acts I–II.

  • Key names keep their pre-Revision-14 chapter prefixes (IDs never renumber): :ch3_juno_talk is in Chapter 2 (Saltmere), and :ch2_tamsin and :ch2_matriarch are in Chapter 3 (Briarwick).

  • :ch3_juno_talk (Ch2) — on Saltmere's breakwater: tell Juno about the NULL scan? told (she keeps it) / deflect / silent.

  • :ch2_tamsin (Ch3) — Tamsin's secret Lattice contract. expose / help_confess / keep_secret. Keeping it means the pylon keeps draining Briarwick, and in Act V she can't afford to let go of her Plate (Consent).

  • :ch2_matriarch (Ch3) (new) — The beaten Glass Matriarch thrashes in the silk-moth grove. soothe (stay with it all night; half the grove crystallizes; Harmony) / silence (press your hand to it and the Imprint leaves it like water down a drain; the grove is saved, the Matriarch is left hollow; Ruin −2). The player's first lesson: the efficient choice is the Ruin one.

  • :ch4_kestrel_mourner — is the Mourner his mother? kind / blunt (−2) / silent.

  • :ch4_teo — Marisol is tipping off her brother's cell. report (Meridian trust; Marisol −4; Teo is hunted) / keep_secret / confront (she breaks down; the strongest Marisol bond). Seeds who Marisol is if Teo dies.

  • :ch5_lowlight_testimony — a Directorate officer asks what you saw. "The Mourner broke the Plate" (it's what it looked like) / "Someone else was there" / "I don't know." Telling the official story on record costs Dorian's Consent: "I keep the lie I know until someone shows me a better one."

Act II — "Imprints" (who do you save?)

  • :ch6_drillsite — the freed Pokémon and the drill-site children. hollow / directorate (a Mandate Pass that opens checkpoints later) / sanctuary (Sahar invokes Warden's right). Directorate costs Sahar's Consent.

  • :ch6_kestrel_rumor — K3. encourage (+2 now, −3 at Ironreach when it isn't her) / warn (−1 now, +2 at Ironreach: "I hate that you were right") / silent. The kind answer now is the cruel one later.

  • :ch7_ledger — J2. name_him (Juno −3, then +2 at Ironreach: she already knew) / reassure (+2, then −2) / ask_corvin.

  • :ch8_caldera — the Caldera Crisis. vent with Wick (forges cold; Harmony) / dampers with Quent (the tap keeps running; Ruin −1) / shutdown by force (a harder fight; Accord trust; the Dominar's respect).

  • :ch8_lightstone — hearthguild / wyrmrest (Sigrun +2; the only route to swaying the Dominar) / dominar (Brann won't let go of his Plate for a man who'd give away his guild's relic).

  • ★ :ch9_teo_sable — the Conclave Shatter. Teo is Fixing under the scaffolding; Sable is running for the service lift with the comm-device. Save Teo (he lives with glassed fingers; Marisol +4; Sable escapes clean) / chase Sable (you tear the device from her belt; Teo dies reaching for his sister). Long-term: Teo leads the Lantern Hollow strikers, or his photo is nailed to the strike banner; only the device exposes Kroll publicly at the Ch13 tribunal; Marisol's Consent or her Right of Grievance in R16.

  • :ch9_rowan_words — Rowan, led away. why / look_after (+2) / silent (+1).

Act III — "Fault Lines" (who do you let fall?)

  • :ch10_null — Black Site branch only: take the Type: Null. Voss +2. An unsettling gift: it reacts to you like the badge case.
  • :ch10_ogre — the Loyal Three or the Ogre (three is GO_LOYAL). ogre (Ogerpon fights with you, later joins Juno) / hesitate.
  • :ch10_succession_stance — "Who should own the Plates?" accord (Valen +2) / kingdoms / nobody (the first "nobody"; Harmony).

  • :ch11_anja — her suppressed readings. expose (ANJA_EXPOSED; Meridian blamed loudly) / let_confess (she becomes the Act V swing vote). Exposing her costs her Consent and makes her claim R16: "You threw me to the court. Fine. Ice remembers."

  • :ch11_strike (new) — the Ebbmouth Strike picket when the strikebreakers arrive. stand (the optional tag battle with Marisol; +2, +3 if Teo died) / mediate. The only Act III way back to Marisol after Teo's death.

  • :ch12_letter — Morwen's dead letter to "I.". keep (you can quote her in the hijack) / send (Kestrel +3: "You sent me a letter. Hers.") / burn (Ruin −2; Odessa finds out: "Dead letters are the last thing some people ever said." She won't let go of her Plate.)

  • :ch13_remember — the five-year-old in the Mindscape. "Show me." / "I'm scared too." (Ilsa +2, Harmony +2) / "...Not yet."

  • ★ :ch13_kaito — Kaito asks whether to speak about Marrowgate. Encourage (the Accord's moral authority cracks; Valen −2; Ilsa +2; Kaito's Consent) / spare him the burden (Accord trust; Kaito never lets go). A man who never confessed can't release anything.

  • ★ :ch13_rowan_testimony — your testimony at the Glass Court. Condemn (Pale Gaol; Juno −3; Rowan −4: if he survives, he radicalizes, which opens the Hollow Spring) / Mercy (Rowan +3, Juno +3, Hollow +2; with Hollow trust ≥ 4 he comes to the Festival as "the Gardener" with Juno's blessing) / Refuse (Ilsa, privately: "Coward. Kind of a coward. I understand.").

  • ★ :ch13_fault (new, who lives) — the Fault. The Glass Court's undercroft floods with Rowan chained in the dock, and the orrery's brass ring comes down on Director Marchetti. Wick's people are on the far side of the water. You can reach one. Rowan (he escapes with Wick, as written; Marchetti is dragged out by her troops, maimed and unturned) / Marchetti (Rowan drowns in the dark under the court, still chained; Marchetti owes you her life and stands the Directorate down at the hijack). Long-term: who leads the Lantern Hollow (Rowan, else Teo, else Thistle and Wick); whether Elin wakes into her husband's arms; Juno −4.

  • :sq_doctors_cell — "The Doctor's Cell" (Ch11–13): free Corvin from the holding barge, or fail. Corvin's Consent; the Cragholm hospital.

The Ashkaar–Isenmar War (Revision 6; chapters placed by the story lead, Act III–IV) — six proposed choices

  • :war_warning — from Frostfang Pass you see the Dominar's legions massing on Ossaria's sands before anyone. Warn Isenmar / warn Ashkaar they've been seen / warn both (the Accord's way; both sides note it) / say nothing.

  • :war_convoy — Marisol asks the one person who can walk the Bleed-front to take a convoy through the Steamline into besieged Skaldfast: relief (food) / arms (harpoon-guns; Marisol +3, Sigrun −2) / refuse.

  • :war_prisoner — Ashkaar holds Anja; the Thane holds the Dominar's nephew. free one in secret / broker an exchange / leave them.

  • :war_legend — both sides beg you to bring their legend: calm Kyogre / wake Reshiram / neither. It decides whose beams meet in the climax.

  • ★ :war_climax — the Glass Dunes, both lines charging and Kyogre's flood coming in. Stand between them / back Ashkaar / back Isenmar. Standing between only stops the war if both armies have seen you act in good faith four times (war trust: warned both, relief, a prisoner helped, no legend used as a weapon, Sigrun ≥ 4, Marisol ≥ 3). Otherwise the beam clash goes off over your head and breaks both armies.

  • :war_terms — if one side won: argue for mercy, reparations or occupation at the armistice table in Skaldfast.

  • :ch20_colors (the story lead's key) — whose colors the challenger wears on Day 0: Elowen's, Zenith's, Nadir's, or none ("the Unsworn", a whisper of Harmony). Crowd reactions, one R16 line, one small delta.

  • :ch21_boon (the story lead's key) — the Blessed's one binding decree: end the war's reparations / seat Nadir on every council / dissolve the Seat. It is asked before the ending is fixed, so ending reparations can undo an occupation you argued for and reopen Homecoming.

Long-term: a beaten kingdom forfeits a Festival seat (§3.1); beaten and unforgiven, its Wardens won't release their Plates (Marisol and Anja, or Brann and Sigrun; both pairs if the clash broke both armies), which can sink Consent below 12 on its own; occupation makes Homecoming impossible (Unfinished at best); the winner's host or legions (both, if you stopped it) defend Crownhaven in the hijack; Anja vs Brann in the bracket is decided by it.

Act IV — "The Drowned Crown" (who are you willing to become?)

  • ★ :ch14_telemetry — Larch opens the badge case. Destroy (Voss knows at once; Directorate pressure in Ch16–17; an Engine crack) / Sabotage (keep it and feed it lies: two cracks, a tense "did he notice?" beat at every later badge) / Leave it (the road to the Bad ending, and Bastian's Consent is gone: "You walked a Meridian beacon into my seams.").

  • ★ :ch16_magnus — the Arbiter blueprints. The honest public act removes the man who could have saved you from inside.

Act V — "Sovereign" (who carries it?)

The safest choice and the most dramatic choice are different. Then the prompt that is GO_STAY_OUT.

Marrowgate's still knocking."; Sigrun won't let go of the Draco Plate) / Open ("I don't know yet") / Ruin (only at Ruin-leaning or lower; Sigrun draws her blade and lets you pass). The hidden "Whatever you want to hear." is GO_LIARS_PYRE.

3. The Festival draw (Revisions 5–6: kingdom delegations, story-met characters only)

3.1 What the Festival is now

The Festival of Champions is the rite by which all Velmora chooses the one person who receives Arceus's Blessing. Sixteen stand in the Prism Arena: the Unimprinted challenger and fifteen delegates, two from each of the seven kingdoms and the Accord's Sovereign. Nobody in the bracket is a stranger: every possible opponent has been met at least twice by Act IV. The four Rev-4 outsiders are gone.

Who each kingdom sends (exact rules: NARRATIVE_KEYS §6.1):

Kingdom Seat A Seat B What decides it
Elowen Juno Celestine fixed, but Juno gives her seat to "the Gardener" (Rowan) if you earned it (R16 draw)
Antumbra Ysolde Kestrel if Gravenmoor names him (redeemed, and the ring given or Ysolde ≥ 4), else Ilsa whether the name Vane is restored or he's disowned
Zenith Rook if he held the footage and is still Meridian's face, else Odessa Kestrel under Meridian's sunburst if Gravenmoor didn't claim him; else Magnus unless exposed; else Odessa/Rook Rook's and Magnus's Ch16 choices; Kestrel's state
Nadir Kaito Nyx, or Corvin if you freed him and refused Nyx's bargain who the City Below trusts
Ossaria Sahar Bastian, unless the raid came in on your beacon (telemetry left); then the seat is lent out Ch14
Isenmar Marisol (or Anja, if only one seat is left and she's the one with the open account with you) Anja, or forfeit the war
Ashkaar Sigrun Brann, or forfeit the war
The Accord Valen — —

The war decides seats. A kingdom that lost the war (or both, if the clash broke both armies) forfeits its second seat; the Accord lends it to a Warden with no seat (Dorian first, then Tamsin, Rook, Odessa, Ilsa, Nyx, Corvin). A victor gets terms, never a third delegate.

I've waited forty years to say that to someone who could."). The warning before His Hand is Larch's ("Don't let him make you a part. He's very good at parts."). "That isn't him fighting" is Kaito's, because his Lucario felt it. The Ruin hint is Ilsa's: "You're thinking very loudly. Twenty-three times."

3.3 Proof: exactly one opponent per stage, never the same person twice

  1. At least one / at most one. Every list ends in an unconditional fallback who is always seated (Juno, Celestine, Kestrel, Valen; Voss), and the resolver stops at the first match.

  2. No duplicates. Persons per stage are disjoint: R16 {Marisol, Anja, Rowan, Juno}; QF {Dask, Sigrun, Kaito, Ysolde, Odessa, Celestine}; SF {Kestrel}; Final {Valen, Brann}; Hijack {Theodric, Quent, Voss}. Core's validator enforces it.

  3. Only seated people are drawn. Candidates whose seat depends on choices (Marisol, Anja, Odessa) carry seated() in their condition; Kaito, Ysolde and Sigrun are always seated; Rowan and Dask enter by replacing the default; Brann's stand-in is live and needs no seat.

  4. Fifteen seats always fill. Each seat ends in an unconditional candidate or a forfeit drawn from a pool of seven for at most three forfeits.

  5. Alive and present. Rowan needs ROWAN_ALIVE; Quent precedes Voss when Voss was removed; Brann only when Valen collapsed.

3.4 Companion matches and highlights

NPC matches resolve by rule, and the player can watch any notable one as a pixel-animated highlight (MATCH_RULES, NARRATIVE_KEYS §6.5: winner rule plus 2–4 key moments each). Order: a drawn path opponent wins until they meet the player; then the pair's rule; then rating. Examples:

  • Anja vs Brann, the war in miniature: Anja wins if Isenmar won or the war was stopped with the prisoners freed, else Brann. Its centre is a Blizzard–Flamethrower beam clash where, this time, nobody dies.

  • Kestrel vs Kaito (Kestrel wins): Lucario flinches from something that isn't the blade.

  • Juno, when a Grievance displaces her: she beats Ysolde at Bond ≥ 5 ("Your aunt is listening"), and loses to Sigrun with her garden at stage five.
  • Valen vs Sigrun (Valen): "He beat me with an arm made of glass." Valen vs Kaito: Kaito's first Aura Sphere goes a hand's width wide, on purpose.

4. Game overs: the Ledger

23 canonical game overs (the story lead's 22 minus the cut "Encore", plus two new ones) and 2 Ruin-only extras. Titles, epitaphs, hints, triggers, the foreshadowing that must be on screen first, and checkpoint placement are in NARRATIVE_KEYS §9–10, verbatim. Rules every one of them follows:

  • Fair. Each is a deliberate player choice, warned at least once on screen in the same chapter, and most need a confirm or a repeated prompt. None fires from a cumulative stat on its own (Pull the Nail is offered only at high Hollow trust, but you still have to say yes).

  • Cheap to retry. Prismfall.checkpoint sits directly before each trigger, so a curious player loses seconds, not an hour.

  • Recorded. Each death writes its epitaph to the cross-save Ledger, where it stays across new games.

The two new ones.

  • Weather (Ch11). At step 4 of the Thaw, "the lake breathes". Anja, already running: "That's not a Pokémon, that's weather. Towers!" Prompt: Fight it now / Get to the towers. Fighting starts an unwinnable lv 80 Kyogre (one Primal-rain Origin Pulse). "You tried to fight the sea. The sea didn't notice. In spring, Rimeholt carved your name on the ice wall, and the thaw took that too." Choosing the towers continues to the partner battle and the real boss, as written. This is the game's one "battle you were told to flee", and it teaches the Ch21 lesson early.

  • Somebody Else's Story (Ch18). After K7, Kestrel: "Don't come. I mean it." Prompt: Stay out of Crownhaven? → He's already walking away. Let him go? Everyone who matters has told the PC it must be them (Celestine's "walker", Sigrun's summons, Larch's letter). "You did what everyone had told you since the ferry. The Engine took Kestrel instead. He lasted eleven minutes. Velmora lasted a week."

Cut: "Encore" (Ch20). It needed four conditions to fire and duplicated Into the Line's lesson ("don't make them choose"). Dorian's ad-lib stays as flavor; the PC simply doesn't go up.

Hints. After the first ending is seen (or with the ledgerhints password), unfound Ledger slots show a one-line riddle instead of "???". Hesper Vane's lighthouse mirror has one crack per game over found; at 23 the cracks make a door shape (the only diegetic hint that the Ledger means something).

5. The Ruin Route: "Every Type and None"

5.1 Unlock and branch

  • Unlock: all 23 canonical game overs in the Ledger (ruin_unlocked).

  • In-story trigger: Ch15, right after the Giratina boss in the Reverse Depths. A pane of black glass shows Juno on the other side, calling the PC's name: the exact image of Looking Back (GO 13). On a save with a full Ledger, the prompt appears again: Look back? Saying yes no longer kills you. The reflection steps aside, and the PC walks through. (:ch15_look_back; no keeps the main story and the door never reopens on that save.) The branch comes after K6, so Kestrel's state is already set.

  • Why it needs every death: inside the Glass, the PC finds out that every game over happened. Antumbra is the reverse side of the world, where things that almost were are kept, and Giratina kept every one of them. You can't walk into the Reverse until it knows your face, and it learns your face from your graves.

5.2 What the Ruin Route reveals (never stated on the main route)

  1. The Ledger is real. The Reverse Depths' floor is a field of twenty-three graves, each carved with its epitaph. "You have no Imprint in Velmora. In here, you have twenty-three." The PC's Reflection stands up from the last grave: the one who remembers dying every time.

  2. Antumbra is an unfinished Judgment. At AF 0, when the Chain closed, Arceus began to judge Aurelia: to unmake it. The Prismfall was the god choosing to break itself rather than finish. The half-done unmaking is Antumbra. Rivers run uphill there because that's what a world looks like halfway to nothing. Giratina, guardian of reverse places, has held the seam shut for three hundred years so the sentence can't finish.

  3. The verse of none. Maren carved a third verse of the Hymn of Return on the Reverse side of the Concordance, where only the Glass could read it: "And if the walker comes with no color in their heart, the god will come home to finish what it began." A whole Arceus, returned to a land that chained it, could complete the Judgment of AF 0. Celestine knew: "I cannot lie, so I stopped singing it."

  4. What "I learned that here" means. In every main-route ending Arceus says "I will not take what is not given. I learned that here." It's talking about Judgment. It came within one heartbeat of unmaking a kingdom, and chose to break instead. Homecoming works because the Wardens give, and the PC carries the shard in Harmony. The Ruin Route is the PC deciding nobody, god or Crown or company, should hold that power again.

  5. The Gilded King is still alive, behind the glass. Antumbra froze the Sun Court at the instant of the Calling. Theodric's reflection stands in it mid-command, the reflected Chain in his hands. Voss has dreamed of him all his life.

5.3 Chapter outline (replaces the rest of Ch15 through Ch21)

  • R1 "Twenty-Three Graves" (Reverse Depths). The graves; the Reflection, who speaks in the PC's own authored lines, reversed. Mirror battle: the Reflection (your own party, generated at your levels, on :INVERSE). Then Giratina (Origin) tests the Renegade (multi-bar trial on :INVERSE). Giratina gives the PC the none: Resonance locks at ruin (≤ −6), and the Ledger becomes a Key Item, the Black Case. New traversal, Mirrorwalk: marked mirrors in Zenith, Nadir, Elowen and Ashkaar open onto their Reverse maps.

  • R2 "Built to Break" (Cogsworth, Gym 15). The PC now wants the Engine finished: it's the only machine that can hold all eighteen Plates still long enough to unmake them. Zekrom still has to be freed (the core must fail so Voss reroutes everything to Crownhaven). :ch16_magnus reads differently: expose means you ruin him so nobody stops the build; conscience means you persuade him to build it "to break right". Gym 15 (Ruin): Magnus on :FACTORY, which becomes :SCRAPYARD on turn one: "You came here to break it. So did I, once."

  • R3 "The Sun Court Below" (Underveil, Gym 16; Aurelia). Nyx sides with the Renegade; her house kept the drowned truth for three hundred years and she's tired of it. Gym 16 (Ruin): an illusion double battle where :NEW_MOON runs with Inverse matchups. In the Sun Court, Theodric's reflection fills the mirror-wall. Voss walks in, sees him, and falls to his knees: "He's alive. Behind the glass he's still alive." He leaves with the cradle, serving a dead king now.

  • R4 "Midnight in Gloaming" (Gym 17; Pecharunt; K7). Celestine tells the PC the verse of none, and refuses the badge. Gym 17 (Ruin): :FAIRY_TALE turns :INVERSE for her last Pokémon ("Once upon a time, which was the only time"). Xerneas does not wake; the dusk stays. K7 plays as written, but Kestrel knows: "You're going to erase her? Everything she paid for?" :ch18_kestrel_ring is still offered.

  • R5 "The Last Gate" (Wyrmrest, Gym 18). The oath can only be true one way: "I'm going to end it. All of it." Reshiram accepts the truth and flies away without a fight. Gym 18 (Ruin): Sigrun on :DRAGONS_DEN, no Reshiram, every Pokémon a step faster ("Dragons don't let anything through they haven't weighed. I've weighed you."). The Dominar can't be swayed; his legions march from the sands across Elowen on Zenith during the Festival.

  • R6 "The Unfestival" (Festival week). The Accord bars "the Renegade". Archseer Dask claims the PC for the Veiled Synod and walks them in through the Glass; Dorian, who has never once let the bowl ruin a story, seeds them anyway. R16 Juno ("You'll make sure Verdance never gets an autumn."), QF Archseer Dask (his offer to stay behind the Glass is GO_R_WELCOME_BEHIND), SF Kestrel (he tears the Gauntlet off to fight you as himself), Final Valen, the Last Tuning ("I'll hold them quiet one more time. I'll die doing it. That's still better than you."). No exhibitions. Ilsa, earmuffs off: "You're thinking very loudly. Twenty-three times." At the Night of Masques, the actor playing the Gilded King freezes mid-line, because the mirror behind the stage is showing the real one.

  • R7 "Every Type and None" (the finale). At the Coronation the Engine wakes, but the hand that reaches up through the arena's crystal walls isn't only Voss's: Theodric's reflection steps through wearing the Chain. Voss kneels (kneel with him: GO_R_KNEEL). When Theodric casts him aside, :ruin_voss: spare him or abandon him to the Chain. Hijack: Theodric. Then Arceus descends, not dragged but coming, to finish what it began. True Finale: Arceus (Judgment), seven bars, Giratina at the PC's side (player side of two), the last bar on :INVERSE as Giratina turns the arena inside out. Valen holds the Ring one last time, to keep the crowd alive while god and Renegade fight. Then the Unmaking.

5.4 Final boss, endings and cost

  • Final boss: Arceus (Judgment), ARCEUS_JUDGMENT (NARRATIVE_KEYS §6.6).
  • The Unmaking needs a vessel. The none unmakes the Chain, the Plates, Judgment and finally the Glass, and whoever carries it goes with the Glass. The Reflection offers to go in the PC's place: "I've done this twenty-three times. Let me do it once on purpose." Then :ruin_walk: who walks out of the Glass?
  • :me → END_UNMAKING "The Unmaking". The Reflection is unmade with the Glass. Antumbra and Velmora fold into each other. Every Imprint ends at once: no fields, no Bleed, no miracles; Rimeholt thaws, Cindervault cools, Verdance gets its first autumn (Juno won't look at the PC while it falls). The Fixed wake, all of them, even the long-Fixed who had stopped dreaming, and some of them wake as strangers. Arceus, with nothing left to judge or be chained by, leaves as a light with no color and never comes back. Giratina, the final witness, closes its eyes. Mirrors are just mirrors. The PC is the only person alive who remembers the old world, and twenty-three ways it ended. The scar is still colorless, by choice.

  • :reflection → END_REFLECTION "The One Who Came Back" (secret). The PC is unmade with the Glass, and the Reflection walks out wearing their face, which is GO 13's epitaph come true. The epilogue is the same world as the Unmaking, seen slightly wrong: the Reflection signs its name mirrored once and corrects it; Juno, raking the first leaves: "You never used to hum." Last image: Hesper's lighthouse mirror, with nothing behind it.

  • Post-game: Antumbra's mirrors stay open as ordinary places (the Reverse maps), Giratina is catchable at the Distortion Core, there is no Arceus, and the Festival never runs again. On END_REFLECTION the post-game is played as the Reflection (nobody else notices).

5.5 Why it's worth playing

It answers the three questions the main route leaves open (what Antumbra is, why the Ledger remembers, what Arceus meant by "I learned that here"), and once you know them, Homecoming reads differently: it was one consenting Warden away from the end of the world. It adds four re-fought gyms, a new Festival bracket (Dask, Valen of the Last Tuning, Theodric), the only scenes where the Gilded King speaks, Giratina as an ally, Mirrorwalk maps, two endings, and two more graves for completionists.

6. Endings

6.1 The final decisions

  1. Ch17, the Sun Court (:ch17_voss_offer). Accepting is a promise you keep or break later.

  2. Ch21, the hijack (:ch21_hand, only if you accepted). Taking Voss's hand ends the game in Concord Dawn before Arceus is ever fought. Without the promise, the same gesture is GO_HIS_HAND.

  3. Ch21, the True Finale. If the Engine is fully calibrated, the PC fights for Arceus and loses the struggle anyway: The Gilded Chain.

  4. Ch21, Arceus speaks (:ch21_final). The PC says it aloud: - Return — "Go home. Take them with you." (always) - Keep — "I'll keep them. I'll keep everyone safe." (always) - Borrowed — the PC hesitates, and Kestrel (redeemed and devoted) or Sigrun (Bond ≥ 6) steps forward: "Not you. Let me be nearest." - Concord — "Stay. Stay and power the world." (if you accepted Voss's offer, or Magnus's governor was never switched off) - Unmake — "No. No more gods." (main route: Resonance ≤ −6, or Hollow trust ≥ 4 with Rowan radicalized or Kroll never publicly exposed)
  5. Ruin Route, R7 (:ruin_walk). Who walks out of the Glass.

6.2 What decides the outcome

  • Wardens' Consent = how many of the 18 Wardens release their Plate (NARRATIVE_KEYS §5 WARDEN_CONSENT, one condition each, in gym order). It's on screen twice: Tamsin's white and grey banners (Ch20), and the Arceus fight itself, which is six bars of three locks each. Between bars those three Wardens kneel and let go, or refuse. Every refusal makes the next lock forced (Arceus gains +1 to every stat stage for that bar). Each refusal has a reason the player caused: Tamsin can't afford it (her secret kept), Dorian keeps the lie he knows (you told the official story), Rook can't reach his Plate, Corvin is in a cell, Brann won't for a man who gave the Light Stone away, Kaito never confessed, Anja "drowns without it", Odessa remembers the burned letter, Bastian remembers the beacon, Ysolde lost Kestrel, Magnus "won't hand my city's future to a god", Celestine hears the wrong key, Sigrun meant to wear the Crown.

  • Engine breaks = eleven lamps on Larch's board: telemetry destroyed or sabotaged (sabotage counts twice), Zekrom freed, Magnus's conscience, Rook still inside, Nyx's precise blackout, Calla's schematics (twice if she went back), Marchetti turned, the Lantern Hollow at the pylons, Kestrel not lost. The Engine is calibrated (Bad ending live) only if the telemetry was left running, Magnus wasn't reached, and three or fewer lamps are lit.

6.3 Conditions matrix (first row that matches wins; exact strings: NARRATIVE_KEYS §12)

# Ending Kind Condition
