6.4 Epilogue beats

The story lead's scenes in 08_ACT_V stand for Homecoming, the Gilded Chain, the Long Vigil, Unfinished, the Hollow Spring, Concord Dawn and the Borrowed Crown. This spec adds the conditions that vary them, and three new endings.

  • Homecoming (Good). As written. The variable slides: Elin wakes in Rowan's arms or, if Rowan drowned at the Fault, Juno alone holds her aunt and tells her; Teo on the Ebbmouth quay or his photo on the guild wall; Kestrel as Ghost Warden (KESTREL_ACCEPTED_SEAT) or a Gale Post wanderer; Calla's name on the Spire memorial if she went back; the quarantine lifts now (ENVOY_PERSUADED) or a year late; Voss watches the sunrise (spared) or is light at the arena's heart; Nadir's first elected seat with Nyx in it.

  • Homecoming, Unfinished (Grey). One slide per refusing Warden's city, in gym order, each a single image of what the Last Shatter took ("Briarwick: the looms went still in one night. Tamsin weaves by hand now."). If Resonance was below Harmony, the PC's scar never takes the land's color.

  • The Empty Lighthouse (Grey, new). Everything in Homecoming happens, but Kestrel burned out as the Engine's conduit. Hesper climbs the lighthouse every night and lights a lamp nobody needs. Ysolde keeps the Ghost seat. The PC reads Morwen's letter aloud at the grave he never visited, the letter he never opened. Last slide: Kestrel's Aegislash, sheathed, on the PC's belt.

  • The Long Vigil / The Borrowed Crown (Grey). As written; the bearer is Kestrel if KESTREL_BEARS, else Sigrun. With Sigrun: "Ten years. Maybe twelve. I was relieved once. Never again." Juno and the PC swear to find another door either way.

  • The Hollow Spring (Grey). As written. If Rowan drowned, Thistle plants the first seed in plain soil; if Teo lived, he's the one who won't speak to her.

  • Concord Dawn (Grey). As written, plus: if reached through :ch21_hand, the PC never fights Arceus at all, and the last slide is the PC reading the arena's power output on a Council screen with Celestine's line over it: "Once upon a time a god was kept in a box. It was quiet. For a while."

  • The Gilded Chain (Bad). As written. The PC as "the Sovereign Who Sleeps". If Quent hijacked, the mug on the desk is Quent's, not Voss's, and Voss is in the crowd of schoolchildren's parents, visiting.

  • The Unmaking / The One Who Came Back (Ruin). §5.4.

6.5 Post-game state

Per NARRATIVE_KEYS §12. In short: full post-game (Concordance Spire, Warden's Gauntlet, Distortion Core, legendary rematches) after Homecoming, Unfinished (refusers are absent from the Gauntlet and their cities keep Bleed scars), Empty Lighthouse, the Long Vigil (the PC is Sovereign; the Gauntlet is framed as Sovereign's audiences), the Borrowed Crown (the bearer is absent) and both Ruin endings (Mirrorwalk maps stay open). Partial after the Hollow Spring (Spire and Gauntlet only; most legendaries are gone with their Plates) and Concord Dawn (Spire only; the Wardens are pensioned off; Quent's Concord Zero arc starts). None after the Gilded Chain: credits, then the title screen. Zygarde chooses the PC at Valen's memorial in any ending with a memorial if Valen's Bond is 3 or more, or Ilsa reconciled with him (ZYGARDE_CHOOSES).

7. Other systems

  1. Quiet Hours (relationship scenes). A bench icon at Pokémon Centers when a Bond first reaches friendly and again at close: 20 short scenes (Juno's seed catalogue, Kestrel teaching the PC to throw stones at the lighthouse, Ysolde lighting a lantern for Ines). Each grants +1 and a keepsake at close (Juno's seed packet = a Grassy Seed; Marisol's union pin; Nyx's crescent earring, which sells for one Poké Dollar and is priceless). Impl.: one common event per scene; condition bond_tier(:X) == :friendly && !made(:qh_x1), register :qh_<bond><n> choice keys with value [:seen].

  2. Interludes. The act files already define five (Rowan, Kestrel, Wenlow, Valen…). Add Interlude VI "The Night Ferry" as Morwen in AF 290, unlocked after any ending: a stealth walk carrying the five-year-old PC to Edda's boat. Its last line is Morwen's echo's line from Ch15. Impl.: pbChangePlayer to the interlude character, stash $player.party in Core state, give a preset party, restore on exit; interlude choices never touch the PC's Bonds (except where the act file says so).

  3. Field Notes. Each field gets an entry on first battle; individual effects fill in only once observed ("Fire moves hit harder here."). :BLEED keeps a log of which fields it has borrowed. Impl.: listen to :prismfall_field_changed; Field Effects marks effect lines as seen when they trigger; Core stores a set per field.

  4. The Ledger viewer and Hall of Reflections. The Ledger also records every Festival opponent variant the player has met. Post-game, the Distortion Core's Hall of Reflections lets them re-fight any variant they've met in any playthrough (Kestrel Fallen, the Gardener, Brann for Valen, Quent…) at lv 100. It reuses every team the balance team built. Impl.: Ledger lines MET:<ENTRANT>; the hall's menu reads them.

  5. The Second Ferry (New Game+). After any ending, the secondferry password starts a new game that keeps the Ledger (always), Field Notes, Pokédex seen flags and one Pokémon of choice from the Hall of Fame as "a passenger". Ines's letter gains a postscript that matches the last ending seen. The Journal shows faint "echo" lines under choices made in the previous run. Impl.: a carryover file written at the ending, read by the password handler.

  6. The Velmora Gazette. Two headlines per chapter per Pokémon Center, chosen by condition strings from a table (§1.4). Impl.: GAZETTE[chapter] = [[condition, headline], …], first match per slot, shown by a newspaper event.

  7. Promises. A Quest Log category for things the PC says they'll do ("I'll come back for a Fizzbolt," to Dex; "I'll look after her," to Rowan). Kept promises pay off in epilogue slides; broken ones get one quiet line. Impl.: choice keys :promise_<name> with [:made, :kept, :broken]; the Quest Log lists :made ones.

  8. Passwords. Core's table plus ledgerhints, nomercy (no checkpoints before game overs), openbook (numbers on the Ties page), colorless (halved Resonance swings) and secondferry (NARRATIVE_KEYS §14).

Spoilers ahead: this chapter covers late-game twists.

Story Bible 12: The Ruin Route — "Every Type and None" (R1–R7)

Mechanics, unlock and endings are specified in 10_CHOICES_ENDINGS.md §5 and NARRATIVE_KEYS §11. This file is the chapter outline at the same depth as the main acts. It replaces the rest of Ch15 through Ch21 on a save with a full Ledger where the PC answers yes to Look back? (:ch15_look_back) after the Giratina boss. Tone: quiet, cold and lucid. The PC isn't a villain. They have seen every way this world ends and have stopped asking it to be saved. Everyone who loved them on the main route still does, which is the horror of it. Revisions 4–6 applied: no sister-game cameos in the Festival (Nova is an R5 sidequest); every opponent is met earlier on this route or the main one; the Festival is the ceremony of the Blessing; the war still happens.

What this route reveals (never stated on the main route): the Ledger is real; Antumbra is an unfinished Judgment; the Hymn has a third verse, "the verse of none"; "I learned that here" means Arceus stopped one heartbeat short of unmaking Aurelia; and the Gilded King is still alive behind the Glass.

R1 — "Twenty-Three Graves" (the Reverse Depths)

  • Location: Giratina's Reverse Depths (806, :INVERSE), then a new floor beneath it.
  • Beats: 1. The PC steps through the black glass. Juno's reflection steps aside, and it isn't Juno. 2. The floor is a field of twenty-three graves, each carved with one of the PC's epitaphs from the Ledger. "You have no Imprint in Velmora. In here, you have twenty-three." 3. The Reflection stands up from the last grave: the PC's own sprite, mirrored, the one who remembers dying every time. It speaks in the PC's authored lines, reversed ("Yet not... too scared I'm... me show"). 4. Mirror battle: the Reflection. The PC's own party at their levels, on :INVERSE. 5. Giratina (Origin) tests the Renegade: a multi-bar trial, not a hunt. It ends when the PC stops attacking for one turn. 6. Giratina gives the PC the none. Resonance locks at Ruin (≤ −6). The Ledger becomes a Key Item, the Black Case, and the PC's badge case turns black to match.
  • New traversal: Mirrorwalk. Marked mirrors in Zenith, Nadir, Elowen and Ashkaar open onto Reverse versions of those maps.
  • Archseer Dask is waiting at the Depths' mouth (third meeting): "Welcome, behind. You looked. I told you never to look. I'm glad one of us disobeys."
  • Cliffhanger: the Reflection falls into step behind the PC like a second shadow. Only Pokémon and Celestine can see it.

R2 — "Built to Break" (Cogsworth, Gym 15)

  • Premise: the PC now wants the Engine finished. It is the only machine that can hold all eighteen Plates still long enough to unmake them.
  • Beats: 1. Cogsworth as in Ch16, seen colder: the PC walks past Rook's canteen table. If the player sits anyway, Rook: "You look like me after the Lowlight." 2. Zekrom must still be freed, so the core fails and Voss reroutes everything to the Temple-Arena. The boss plays as written, but when it's free it doesn't flee. It looks at the PC and recoils. 3. :ch16_magnus reads differently. Expose ruins him so nobody can stop the build. Conscience persuades him to build it "to break right", and he understands exactly what he's being asked.
  • Gym 15 (Ruin): Magnus on :FACTORY, which becomes :SCRAPYARD on turn one. "You came here to break it. So did I, once."
  • War beat: the foundry is casting Prism lances for both armies. The PC can stop it or not, and the game no longer tells them which is kinder.
  • Cliffhanger: the Sump Purge on the screens. The Reflection says its first forward sentence: "We died there once. It didn't help."

R3 — "The Sun Court Below" (Underveil, Gym 16; Aurelia)

  • Beats: 1. Underveil after the Purge. Nyx sides with the Renegade without being asked: her house kept the drowned truth for three hundred years and she's tired of it. "You're going to end the secret-keeping business. I should be upset." 2. Gym 16 (Ruin): the illusion double battle, with :NEW_MOON running Inverse matchups. 3. Aurelia by Mirrorwalk: the Sun Court's mirror-wall is a window. Behind the glass the court stands frozen at the instant of the Calling, and Theodric's reflection is in it mid-command, the reflected Chain in his hands. His eyes move. (First meeting with the route's hijacker.) 4. Voss walks in, sees him, and falls to his knees: "He's alive. Behind the glass he's still alive." He leaves with the cradle, serving a dead king now. The PC watches the most reasonable man in Velmora become a zealot in ten seconds.
  • Game over hook: GO_THE_THRONE is already in the Ledger, so the throne's armrests are closed fists now. Sitting does nothing. The Reflection: "We've done that one."
  • Cliffhanger: Theodric's reflection mouths one word at the PC through the glass: "Finish."

R4 — "Midnight in Gloaming" (Gym 17; Pecharunt; K7)

  • Beats: 1. Pecharunt in the Lightless Deep, as written. The thralls wake and thank the PC, and it lands wrong. 2. Celestine tells the PC the verse of none, which Maren carved on the Reverse side of the Concordance: "And if the walker comes with no color in their heart, the god will come home to finish what it began." "I cannot lie, so I stopped singing it." 3. She refuses the badge, and fights for it anyway. Gym 17 (Ruin): :FAIRY_TALE turns :INVERSE for her last Pokémon ("Once upon a time, which was the only time"). 4. The dusk does not lift. Ogerpon, if it walked with the PC, leaves at the Verge and goes back to the Bride Tree. 5. K7 plays as written, but Kestrel knows: "You're going to erase her? Everything she paid for?" :ch18_kestrel_ring is still offered. Giving it is the last warm thing on the route.
  • Cliffhanger: GO_STAY_OUT's prompt appears and can't be answered yes. The cursor won't move there.

R5 — "The Last Gate" (Wyrmrest, Gym 18; the Glass Dunes; Nova)

  • Beats: 1. The oath can only be true one way: "I'm going to end it. All of it." Reshiram accepts the truth and flies to the front without a fight. 2. Gym 18 (Ruin): Sigrun on :DRAGONS_DEN, no Reshiram, every Pokémon a step faster. "Dragons don't let anything through they haven't weighed. I've weighed you." 3. The Battle of the Glass Dunes (14_WAR_AND_BLESSING). The PC can't stand between: the option reads "End it." The shard doesn't calm the beam clash. It eats it, and both legendaries' beams go out like candles. WAR-1 plays with shots 10–12 replaced: the clash-ball turns black and vanishes, the flood stops dead and sinks into the sand, Kyogre and Reshiram both flee the PC, and both armies stop fighting out of fear. The truce is called anyway. Nobody thanks the PC. 4. The Dominar can't be swayed, and neither ruler will ride with the Renegade.
  • Sidequest: Nova (CAMEOS.md §9), on the Mirrorwalk dream-road out of Gloaming. She offers a gentler unmaking: everyone asleep and happy forever. Accepting is GO_R_SWEET_DREAMS. Refusing is a fight, and the Crescent Charm.
  • Cliffhanger: on the Sovereign's Ascent the Wardguard bars the road. Dask's Synod opens a mirror in the cliff instead.

R6 — "The Unfestival" (Festival week)

  • Beats: 1. The Accord bars "the Renegade" from the Blessing. No kingdom offers its colors. Dask enters the PC as Antumbra's second delegate, "Unsworn, behind", and Dorian, who has never once let the bowl ruin a story, seeds them himself. 2. Opening ceremony: the Plates dim as the PC passes each pylon. The vision of Arceus is the same eye, but it speaks differently: "Little light. You have carried me far. Why are you so cold?" 3. R16: Juno. "You'll make sure Verdance never gets an autumn." She fights to stop the PC, and cries the whole match. 4. QF: Archseer Dask (met Ch13, Ch15, R1). He fights to measure the PC, on :INVERSE: "Behind, welcome. Welcome, behind. The Synod must know what it is letting through." 5. SF: Kestrel. He tears the Gauntlet off to fight the PC as himself. If he has the ring: "She was nearest. I'm nearest now. Stop." 6. Night of Masques: the actor playing the Gilded King freezes mid-line, because the mirror behind the stage is showing the real one. 7. Valen's audience is three lines long. Valen: "I know what you are now. I'll hold them quiet one more time. I'll die doing it. That's still better than you." 8. Final: Valen, the Last Tuning. He fights with the Crown on and the Plates lit behind him.
  • No exhibitions except the Eevee Octave (its gauntlet still needs all eight singers helped). Vesper hosts it without once looking at the PC, but Understudy's siblings do.
  • Cliffhanger: the Blessing. Nobody will raise the Crown. The PC picks it up off the arena floor.

R7 — "Every Type and None" (the finale)

  • Beats: 1. The Engine wakes, but the hand that reaches up through the arena's crystal walls isn't only Voss's. Theodric's reflection steps through wearing the Chain, and the Aureate court is visible behind him in every reflective surface in Crownhaven. 2. Voss kneels. Theodric invites the PC to kneel with him: GO_R_KNEEL. 3. Theodric casts Voss aside into the Chain. CHOICE :ruin_voss: spare him (the PC pulls him out; he lives, hollow) or abandon him. 4. Hijack: Theodric, the Gilded Reflection. His team is the Gilders' court: Golurk, Aegislash, Gholdengo-gold reflections of Wardens' aces, on :PRISM_ARENA running Inverse. 5. Arceus descends, not dragged but coming, to finish what it began in AF 0. Valen holds the Ring one last time, to keep the crowd alive while god and Renegade fight. No Warden releases anything; all eighteen locks hold. 6. True Finale: Arceus (Judgment), seven bars, with Giratina at the PC's side. The last bar is on :INVERSE as Giratina turns the arena inside out. 7. The Unmaking needs a vessel. The none unmakes the Chain, the Plates, Judgment and finally the Glass, and whoever carries it goes with the Glass. The Reflection offers: "I've done this twenty-three times. Let me do it once on purpose." 8. CHOICE :ruin_walk: who walks out of the Glass.
  • Endings (10_CHOICES_ENDINGS §5.4):
  • :me → "The Unmaking". The Reflection is unmade with the Glass. Every Imprint ends at once. All the Fixed wake, even the long-Fixed, some of them as strangers. Verdance gets its autumn, and Juno won't look at the PC while it falls. Arceus leaves as a light with no color and never returns. The PC is the only person who remembers the old world and twenty-three ways it ended.
  • :reflection → "The One Who Came Back" (secret). The PC is unmade, and the Reflection walks out wearing their face. The epilogue is the same world seen slightly wrong: a signature mirrored once and corrected, and Juno saying "You never used to hum." Last image: Hesper's cracked mirror, with nothing behind it.
  • Post-game: Mirrorwalk maps stay open as ordinary places, Giratina is catchable, there is no Arceus, and the Blessing is never held again.

Requests to other teams

  • World: four Mirrorwalk Reverse maps (Zenith, Nadir, Elowen, Ashkaar) and the graves floor under 806.
  • Balance: the Reflection (mirror party), four Ruin gym teams, Dask (QF), Valen (Last Tuning), Theodric, Arceus (Judgment), Nova.
  • Cutscenes: the WAR-1 Ruin variant (shots 10–12).

Story Bible 13: Cutscene Storyboards (SPINE Revision 6)

Shot-by-shot storyboards for the Prismfall Cutscenes plugin (DSL spec: design/CUTSCENES.md when it lands). Each shot lists camera, sprites/action, FX, text. Durations are suggestions at 60 FPS feel. Sprites are battle/overworld Pokémon and trainer sprites; no new painted art is assumed except the listed backdrops. Variants are selected by narrative keys (NARRATIVE_KEYS). Proposed keys are marked (proposed).

Portrait use (every script; SPINE Revision 22)

The user: "i dont think we need a portrait for every conversation", "the speech bubble thing only needs to exist for like special scenes for like dramatic effect (usually comic relief)" and "portrait for main cast (like desolation) doesnt sound like a bad idea". Engine: plugins/Prismfall Cutscenes/014_Portraits.rb. A line can look three ways:

  • Face (the default for the story cast): a framed 96×96 face beside the message box, Desolation-style. Script tag Name · expression, map events \pf[NAME,expr]. Tag a speaker's first line in a conversation and any line where their expression changes. Their later lines in the same conversation are Name, and the engine keeps their face with the last expression. Until a character has portrait art, the face falls back to a name box on its own.

  • Bubble (rare, opt-in): the round portrait with a tail pointing at the speaker on the map, plus emotes. Use it only for a special dramatic or (usually) comic beat, marked per line: Name · expression · emote / \pfb[...]. Allow about a handful per chapter. Emote names: sweat, shock, anger, sparkle, gloom, question, exclaim, tears, blush, dots. Older scripts' (shock lines)-style notes are staging only, and they show nothing in face mode.

  • Plain (everyone else): the message box with a name label, X. That means generic NPCs, townsfolk, shopkeepers, quest-givers, route and gym trainers, guards, signs and objects. Only characters in Prismfall::Portrait::CAST get a face or a bubble. Anyone else stays plain even if tagged, so don't tag them (Coll and the sister-game cameos, for example, are plain).

  • A new conversation starts fresh: a new event, an [after X] variant, or a choice branch.

How the engine reads these (014_Portraits.rb; shots: docs/playtest/portraits_*.png):

  • Face: the frame is cut from the message box's own windowskin and sits on the box's left edge, above it, or below it when the box is at the top (Desolation's face window). It rises and fades in (0.16 s) for a new speaker and gives a 2 px nudge for a new expression. A same-speaker, same-face line does not move at all.

  • The expression only picks the file: Graphics/Portraits/NAME_expression.png, else NAME.png (any expression name works, e.g. Juno's surprised). With neither file, the line is plain. PLAYER uses PLAYER_A or PLAYER_B, by the look picked on the Dovetail.

  • Carry-over: a cast member's untagged Name: ... line keeps the face from their last tagged line, until a new event starts. A choice branch inside the same event inherits it, so tag a branch's first line when the face should change. A bubble line counts too: the next X line goes back to that character's face.

  • In face mode, the emote and event fields of a tag are ignored. In bubble mode, the tail points at the event named in the 4th field (\pfb[LARCH,angry,anger,Professor Larch]), else at an event named like the character, else at the event running the text.

  • Script calls: pf_say(:JUNO, :happy, "text") (face), pf_say(:LARCH, :angry, "text", bubble: true, emote: :anger). Trials talk rows: [:JUNO, :happy, "text"] (face), [:LARCH, :angry, "text", :bubble], or [:LARCH, :angry, "text", { :bubble => true, :emote => [:anger], :event => "Professor Larch" }]. A choice prompt [:SPK, :expr, "prompt", :bubble] works the same way.

  • The map builders' mapgen/layouts/scriptpour.py turns Name · expr · emote into \pfb[NAME,expr,emote]Name: ....

WAR-1 — "The Beam Clash on the Glass Dunes" (Ch19 climax; ~95 s)

Staging: on map 926, the Glass Dunes, with on_map: true (the way 013_Scenes_War_OnMap.rb stages it), or on a stage picture exported from that map until it is built. The legendaries are overworld-scale acting sheets in the map's 3/4 view (design/CUTSCENES.md §4), never battle sprites: Primal Kyogre is as long as a rank of soldiers, and Reshiram's wings cover the Siege Camp's earthwork. The armies are charset blocks under banners. Isenmar and Kyogre are on the left (west), Ashkaar and Reshiram on the right (east).

Backdrop: the Glass Dunes at dawn. Bone-white dunes under a low sky; the grey line of the Northern Sea along the far (top) edge; the Steamline's wall of steam between the hosts at the top. Far left (west), Skaldfast's rime-white walls at the foot of the Mast Glacier, with the white trench-lines of the Rimed Sands in front of them. Right (east), the Siege Camp's palisade, red banners and dragon pickets. Between the hosts, on a dune crest, the bone-carters' small white banner. Cinder Cape is out of sight, behind the Ashkaar lines.

Variants (NARRATIVE_KEYS §4.3): A = WAR_STOPPED, A′ = WAR_BOTH_BROKEN (shots 1–10 as A; then shot 11 is a white-out, shot 12 is cut, and shot 13 shows both lines gone and the two rulers alone on the glass), B = WAR_ASHKAAR_WON, C = WAR_ISENMAR_WON. No-legend variant: if :war_legend = :neither (the only value that keeps the legendaries away; the plugin's legends: false is right), there is no flood-sea. Shots 2–5 use Sigrun's Salamence (Draco Meteor, then Flamethrower) against Anja's Mamoswine, which bursts up out of the Rimed Sands' frozen trench-line, or Marisol's Gyarados, which rises out of the trench-lines' meltwater (Blizzard / Hydro Pump). The clash in shot 6 is unchanged, and in shot 7 the glass comes from frost meeting fire.

Story Bible 15: Comedy (SPINE Revision 7 — "we need funny moments!")

The game gets darker every act. That is exactly why it needs people being ridiculous at each other. This file is the humor guide, the recurring dynamics, the running gags, one scripted funny scene per chapter (Ch0–Ch21), optional bits per kingdom, and the portrait-art list. Script format: Name · expression then the line. Expressions: neutral, happy, smug, angry, crying, shocked, deadpan, panic, sad, blush. Emotes in (italics): sweat drop, shock lines, anger vein, "..." bubble, music note, heart, question mark. The PC's replies are choice prompts shown as > option. The PC has no portrait.

1. Humor guide

  • Where the comedy comes from: people who care about each other, losing patience. The PC is a fifteen-year-old who walks into Bleed zones, vaults and wars as a habit. Every adult who loves them reacts the way that Rejuvenation portrait does: crying and yelling.
  • Character-based, never quippy. A line is funny because of who says it. If the line could be handed to anyone, cut it.
  • The silent PC is a comedy engine. Characters argue with the PC's silence, answer questions nobody asked, and read whole speeches into a "...". The three choice options are often two sensible replies and one that is clearly a bad idea, and the bad idea gets the best reaction.
  • Absurdity lives in optional content: signs, NPCs, sidequests, shop names. The main path stays grounded.
  • Never undercut the big beats. No jokes inside: the Lowlight Shatter aftermath, Rowan's unmasking, the Thaw, the Fault choice, the Cathedral echo, Interlude IV, Valen's audience, the finale from the hijack onward. A joke may come before a blow (it makes the blow land) or a full scene after (it lets the player breathe). Never during.
  • Comedy tracks the tone curve. Act I: broad and warm. Act III onward: drier, shorter, gallows. By Act V a single dry line from Corvin is the whole joke.
  • Jokes can carry plot. Several running gags below are foreshadowing wearing a silly hat.

2. Comic dynamics

A. "The Lecture" — Larch (exasperated) and the PC (chaos, silently)

Larch has kept this child alive by post for six months and is discovering they treat every Bleed Veil like a doorway. She starts each scolding as a scientist and ends it as a parent. She cries when she's angriest and denies it ("It's the tea. The tea is very strong."). Brann and Corvin inherit the role when she's absent, in their own registers: Brann booms and then hugs; Corvin lectures in the form of a medical bill.

B. "The Committee" — Juno (earnest chaos), Kestrel (furious straight man), the PC (tie-breaker)

Juno narrates plant facts at dramatic moments and adopts things. Kestrel has rehearsed being cool and is ambushed by Juno's kindness every time. Their bickering is the party banter. Kestrel insists he isn't part of any group; the group has a name (Juno named it; see the gag).

C. "The Wardens' Group Chat" — Odessa (chaos), Ilsa (deadpan), Dorian (ham), Bastian (selectively deaf)

From Act III the Wardens share Gale Post relay messages the PC can read at any Pokémon Center ("Warden Circular"). Odessa posts nonsense. Dorian replies in stage directions. Ilsa answers thoughts nobody typed. Bastian replies to the wrong message a week late. Anja's only contribution, every time: "Toes."

3. Running gags (with payoffs)

# Gag How it runs Payoff
1 Larch's kelp tea Everyone who is handed a cup finds a new way to not drink it: Juno waters a plant with it (the plant dies), Kestrel "saves it for later" for nineteen chapters, Brann quenches a blade in it (the blade improves). Festival, Day 5: Valen, dying, drinks a whole cup and says, "That's rather good." Larch has to sit down. In Homecoming's epilogue the PC finally drinks one. > It's disgusting. Larch: "I know."
2 The Lecture count Each scolding is numbered by the scolder ("This is lecture nine."). Different adults keep separate, incompatible counts. Festival hijack aftermath / epilogue: Larch: "Lecture forty. You fought God. I had it written down as a thing not to do."
3 "Team Compost" Juno names the trio in Ch1. Kestrel refuses it in every act. It ends up on a Gale Post parcel, a pit-fight bracket, and a Directorate arrest warrant. Festival, SF (Redeemed): after he tears off the Gauntlet, the arena board lists his affiliation as he requested that morning: "TEAM COMPOST". He says nothing about it, ever.
4 Rook's chat Rook relays what his stream chat says. Chat is always wrong about battles and always right about feelings. Hijack: Rook cuts the grid; his stream dies. First line offline: "Chat? ...Oh. It's just me." Then, quieter: "Okay. Still charged."
5 Bastian's deafness He can't hear questions about fugitives, taxes or bedtime. He can hear a biscuit tin open through forty meters of rock. Arceus fight, his release line is followed by Pip: "Granddad, did you hear what it said?" Bastian: "Every word. I've heard every word for thirty years. Don't tell Hollis."
6 Understudy never gets the part The gift Eevee is cast in every Saltmere play and cut before curtain (as Tree #3, as "a bush", as the understudy to a prop). Dorian sends apology notes. Night of Masques: Understudy walks on as the infant Princess Maren and gets a standing ovation. If it has evolved, the program credits it as "a much older Princess Maren".
7 Corvin's bills After every reckless thing the PC does in his sight, he hands them an itemized invoice ("Item: one (1) heart attack, mine. Item: gauze."). The total is always ₽0. Epilogue: the last invoice arrives by post. "Item: one (1) world, saved. Paid in full."
8 The mirror that waves late (dark) From Ch12 the PC's reflection lags. Optional mirror interactions are jokes: it's caught yawning, it fixes its hair, it mimes "behind you" when nothing is there. Juno finds it hilarious. Ruin Route, R1: the Reflection: "You laughed at me in Skyreach. I was trying to warn you." No joke after that is safe in a mirror.

5. Optional funny bits per kingdom

  • Elowen:
  • A Briarwick weaver has knitted a jumper for a Caterpie. It has sixteen sleeves. She's on the fourth.
  • Sidequest "Gerald" (Royal Chase): the Queen's named Scatterbug keep escaping. Each has a personality file.
  • Saltmere's rival theater stages "The Pageant of the Pageant", a play about Dorian. Dorian has seen it nine times "to gather evidence".
  • Isenmar:
  • A Rimeholt ice-fisher has been waiting at one hole for eleven years. His Bergmite is now an Avalugg and he hasn't noticed he's sitting on it.
  • Ebbmouth's eel-stall owner keeps a ledger titled "THE BOY (4 EELS, DAILY)".
  • Zenith:
  • A Lumen City vending machine has gained sentience from the free current and only sells Fizzbolt to people who compliment it.
  • Sidequest "Customer Support": a Meridian helpdesk Rotom needs the PC to walk a form through nine offices. The form is to cancel the form.
  • Nadir:
  • Mirefen's noodle cart rates customers out of ten. Nobody has scored above a four. Corvin has a two and comes daily.
  • An Ironreach pit announcer narrates everything the PC does in town ("AND THEY'RE OPENING THE DOOR, FOLKS").
  • Ashkaar:
  • Because lying is a crime, Cindervault shop signs are painfully honest: "ADEQUATE SWORDS", "BREAD (YESTERDAY'S)".
  • A dragon-rider recruit is afraid of heights and has been assigned a Trapinch "until he's ready".
  • Ossaria:
  • Sahar's Dig Lab interns revived a fossil they can't identify and have been calling it "Kevin". Kevin is a rock. Kevin is in the staff photo.
  • A caravan trader will only barter in riddles and doesn't know the answers either.
  • Antumbra:
  • In the Inverse borderlands, an NPC complains his umbrella keeps the rain in.
  • A Lucent student's reflection attends lectures for her. It gets better marks. She's furious.
  • Mirror gag set (running gag 8): three optional mirrors where the PC's reflection misbehaves.
  • Crownhaven:
  • The Court of Eight Pavilions has a lost-property tent. Its only item, every day, is Kestrel's eel receipt.

Story Bible 11: Finale Lines — the Eighteen Locks

For the True Finale (08_ACT_V, Ch21): six bars of three locks, in gym order. Between bars, the three Wardens of that bar release or refuse. Conditions are WARDEN_CONSENT in NARRATIVE_KEYS §5. Every refusal has a reason the player caused. A refusal forces the next lock (Arceus +1 all stats for that bar). Staging: the Warden kneels at their pylon; one line; on release the golden lock opens and the Plate rises into Arceus's wheel; on refusal they grip the pylon and the lock stays shut. §3 gives the Homecoming, Unfinished slide for each refusing Warden's city.

1. Release lines

# Warden (Plate) Release line
1 Dorian (Blank) "Three hundred years of pageants, and this is the only true scene I ever staged. Exit, pursued by nothing. Lights down."
2 Tamsin (Insect) "Granny wove a whole village around this. I think she'd want me to finish the pattern. Cut the thread."
3 Marisol (Splash) "The Ebb ran both ways because of this. It'll run one way now, like any honest river. Go on, tides take you."
4 Rook (Zap) "First time I've ever held it. Kinda thought it'd be heavier. ...Stay charged, wherever you're going."
5 Sahar (Earth) "The desert keeps everything. I'm asking it, just this once, to give something back."
6 Corvin (Toxic) "Dose makes the cure. Three hundred years is rather over the dose. Off you go, dear."
7 Brann (Flame) "Forge it to break right, lad. Forge it to break right." (He's weeping.)
8 Kaito (Fist) "A fist is a promise. So is an open hand." (He opens it.)
9 Juno (Meadow) "Verdance has never had an autumn. I'd like to see one." (She is always the first to let go in her bar.)
10 Anja (Icicle) "We'll move south. We've hauled heavier things than a city. Take it before I count my grandchildren's toes again."
11 Odessa (Sky) "The wind doesn't care who owns it. Never did. Fly home."
12 Ilsa (Mind) "I've heard everyone's thoughts but yours. I'd like the quiet. Go." (If reconciled, she says it with one hand still on her father's shoulder.)
13 Bastian (Stone) "First time in three hundred years a Warden's had nothing in his keeping. Feels like setting down a sack of stone. Go on, then."
14 Ysolde (Spooky) "Go home. All of you. Go home." (The echoes in the stands fade as she says it. If Kestrel is beside her, he puts his hand over hers on the pylon.)
15 Magnus (Iron) "Tolerances exceeded. I'm releasing the part." (A beat.) "That was a joke. I'm told I should make them."
16 Nyx (Dread) "My family kept one secret for three hundred years. I'm keeping none. It's yours, sweetheart. Take the dark with you."
17 Celestine (Pixie) (sung) "Not chained, not broken, not bought, not crowned: given back, as a gift is found."
18 Sigrun (Draco) "Dragons don't let anything through they haven't weighed. I've weighed this. It's too heavy for anyone. Go."

2. Refusal lines (with the cause)

# Warden Condition that fails Refusal line
1 Dorian :ch5_lowlight_testimony = mourner (you told the official story on record) "You told them the pageant version, darling. So did I, for thirty years. I find I can't stop on cue."
2 Tamsin :ch2_tamsin = keep_secret (the pylon still drains Briarwick) "I can't. I can't. The contract's still running and there's nothing left in the village but this. I'm sorry — sorry —"
3 Marisol Teo not saved and Bond < 3 "My brother's in the river mud because of what this thing started. It owes Ebbmouth. It stays."
4 Rook neither ROOK_CUTS_GRID nor MARCHETTI_TURNED (he can't reach his Plate) "It's not mine to give! It never was! It's in their cradle, I can't even — chat, I can't reach it."
5 Sahar :ch6_drillsite = directorate "I buried the truth once because someone with a badge asked me to. You stood with the badge. I'll keep what the sand gave me."
6 Corvin not CORVIN_FREED (a Choir porter in his mask holds the Plate) Porter: "I — I'm not him. I don't know how. Nobody told me how."
7 Brann :ch8_lightstone = dominar "You gave my guild's Light away to a king, and now you'd have me give the fire too? No, lad. Not for you."
8 Kaito not KAITO_TESTIFIED "I never said it out loud. Marrowgate. A man who can't open his mouth can't open his hand."
9 Juno Bond < 0 "I let go of him. I let go of the dock we started on. I'm not letting go of the last thing that's mine because you asked."
10 Anja :ch11_anja ≠ let_confess "Rimeholt drowns without it. You threw me to the court for less. Ice remembers."
11 Odessa :ch12_letter = burn "Dead letters are the last thing some people ever said. You burned one. I don't hand things to people who burn them."
12 Ilsa not reconciled and Bond < 5 "He's dying on that Ring for a country that never thanked him. Someone in this family is going to keep something."
13 Bastian :ch14_telemetry = leave "You walked a Meridian beacon into my seams, child, and they came for my people by it. I'll keep my stone."
14 Ysolde KESTREL_FALLEN and not reached "She asked me to keep one boy safe and I couldn't. I won't lose the only place I can still hear them both."
15 Magnus not MAGNUS_KEPT_FAITH "I won't hand my city's future to a god. Gods have had three hundred years. Engineers have had ten."
16 Nyx no bargain and Bond < 4 "Everything has a price, sweetheart, and you never paid mine. The dark stays where it's useful."
17 Celestine Resonance < 2 "I cannot lie, so hear it plainly: you're singing in the wrong key, and I won't give the dusk to that song."
18 Sigrun :ch19_oath = keep or ruin "You swore over my fire you'd keep them, or end them. I believed you. So I'm keeping mine from you."

Forced-lock beat: when a refused lock is broken by force, the Warden is thrown back from the pylon and the Plate tears free with a crack of Bleed light. No line. The camera holds on their empty hands.

3. Homecoming, Unfinished slides (one per refusing Warden, gym order)

# City Last Shatter slide
1 Saltmere "The one city the Bleed never touched has a glass promenade. The Lantern Theatre plays to it."
2 Briarwick "The looms went still in one night. Tamsin weaves by hand now."
3 Ebbmouth "The Ebb stopped, then ran out to sea and didn't come back. The mills are museums."
4 Lumen City "The Lowlight's glass took three more streets before the dark came. Rook reads the names on air every year."
5 Duneholt "The well never refilled. The caravans left by the east gate, in order of age."
6 Mirefen "The mire went clear and killed everything that had learned to live in it. Corvin's Ward was empty by then."
7 Cindervault "The Cinderhorn went cold with its forges full. Brann's last blade is still in the stone."
8 Ironreach "The shafts fell in on the Pit. Kaito dug for nine days."
9 Verdance "Autumn came all at once, and winter the same week. Juno planted anyway."
10 Rimeholt "The lake let go. The Holdfast is an island now, and Anja lights its beacon for nobody."
11 Skyreach "The Stormfront fell on the masts. The Gale Post flies from Ebbmouth, when it flies."
12 Lucent "The city in the sky came down on the city below. The Athenaeum's books were found as far as Gloaming."
13 Cragholm "The crystal halls went dark and brittle. Pip carried her grandfather's lamp out."
14 Gravenmoor "Every echo spoke at once, and then none ever did again. Ysolde keeps the candles lit out of habit."
15 Cogsworth "The foundries seized mid-shift. The clock-towers stopped at eleven-forty, all of them."
16 Underveil "The long night ended at noon, and the towers couldn't bear the light. Nadir moved up the lifts, uninvited."
17 Gloaming "Dusk became midnight and stayed. The lantern-moths are the only stars."
18 Wyrmrest "The dragons left the Rift in one flight and didn't choose a new one."

Script: Prologue, Chapter 1, Chapter 2 (Saltmere, through Gym 1 and the Pageant)

Final playable script for the game's first hour (SPINE Revisions 8 and 14). It covers maps 109–110, 100–108, 520, 523, 522, 521 (Chapter 1), then the Strand Road 520 → 527 → 528 and Saltmere 140–147, the Pell Playhouse 150/154 (Gym 1) and the Lantern Theatre 145 (Chapter 2). Structure follows the built events in mapgen/specs; where this file adds an event, it is marked [NEW]. Maps 527 and 528 are new (cartographer, tools/worldmap/world_data.py), so all of their events are new. Chapter 3 (the Weavers' Road, Briarwick, Gym 2) moved to story/21_SCRIPT_CH3.md when Revision 14 swapped the first two gyms. Sources: 04_ACT_I (outline), 15_COMEDY (scenes Ch0–Ch2, inlined), NARRATIVE_KEYS (choice keys), FLAGS (switches), SYSTEMS (script calls), GYM_PUZZLES (Gym 1), BALANCE 4b (versions). Keys and switches keep their old names. :ch3_juno_talk, CH3_PAGEANT_DONE, CH3_J1_DONE and CH3_UNDERSTUDY_GOT are all Chapter 2 now; IDs never renumber (FLAGS.md).

Conventions

  • Portrait use (SPINE Rev 22; story/13_CUTSCENES.md): Name · expression = the cast's Desolation-style face window, tagged on a speaker's first line in a conversation and on expression changes. Their later lines are Name, and the face stays. Name · expression · emote = the rare speech bubble, for a marked comic or dramatic beat. Only Prismfall::Portrait::CAST gets either. Everyone else is X (generic NPCs, trainers, Coll). No tag = plain message box (narration, signs).
  • (italics) = staging. An emote only shows on a ... line (SPINE Rev 22). MOVE: = movement route. SE: / BGM: = audio. WAIT n = frames.
  • > option = a choice. → = what follows. PC = the player; [Player] = player name.
  • Script calls: pf_choose(:key, :value), pf_bond_add(:ID, n), pf_standing_add(:FACTION, n), pf_resonance_add(n), Prismfall.rival_battle(...), Prismfall.gym_battle(n), Prismfall.game_over(:GO_X), Prismfall.record_starter(...). Choice effects in NARRATIVE_KEYS §4.2 apply automatically on pf_choose; extra deltas are written out.
  • Gym numbers: events look a Warden's number up instead of hard-coding it (Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_DORIAN)), pfm_gym_won?(:LEADER_TAMSIN), from mapgen/ruby/008_GymOrder.rb). The script writes the number for readability: Dorian is 1, Tamsin is 2.
  • Switches/variables: names from design/FLAGS.md (S101 = PRO_FERRY_DONE, etc.).
  • Reactive lines: [after X] variants replace the default once switch X is on.

PROLOGUE — "The Last Ferry"

Set at start: V101 STORY_ACT = 0, V102 STORY_CHAPTER = 0.

Map 109 — The Dovetail, Deck (dusk; BGM: sea wind, low strings)

EV "Prologue intro" (autorun)

(Black screen.)
SE: ship's horn, long.
TEXT (center, white on black): Spring, AF 300.
TEXT: The Concert of Regions has sealed the borders of Velmora.
TEXT: This is the final civilian crossing.
(Fade in: the deck. The PC stands at the port rail, one bag at their feet. Gulls. On the horizon, a low line of eighteen colored glows.)
Deckhand Twenty minutes to the Landing! Mind your bags, mind your feet, mind the Captain!
MOVE: Deckhand walks aft.
(Control to player. The PC can walk the deck. The gangway aft is roped off until S101.)

Key Item (start inventory): Mum's Letter

ITEM DESCRIPTION: A letter in your mother's handwriting. The ink runs where the sea got at it.
USE →
"Go to Imelda Larch at Ferrow's Landing, before they close the strait.
Don't let anyone scan you. Don't go to Crownhaven.
I'm sorry I never told you why. I wanted one of us to have an ordinary life.
— Mum."

EV "Rail sign" (action)

SIGN: DO NOT LEAN ON RAIL. — Capt. E. Morrow
(If the PC is facing the rail tile next to it:) You are leaning on it.

EV "Captain Edda" (touch trigger at the rail; comedy scene Ch0, "Do Not Lean")

MOVE: Edda stomps in from the wheelhouse. *(anger vein)*
Edda · angry Oi! Sprog! Can you read?
> Yes.
  Edda · deadpan Then you're doing it on purpose. That's worse.
> No.
  Edda · shocked ...Oh. Oh, stars. Right. That's a D. That one's an O. *(sweat drop)*
> ...
  Edda · deadpan Strong silent type. Wonderful. I'll just talk to the rail, shall I?
  Edda · angry Rail! Tell the sprog to get off you!
(All branches continue:)
MOVE: Edda steps closer, then stops dead. *("..." bubble)* WAIT 40.
Edda · shocked Don't lean on my rail like that, you'll— huh.
Edda · neutral ...Never mind. You stand how you like.
Edda Mind the gap when we dock. And don't look down at the water after dark.
> Why not?
  Edda · deadpan Because I said, and it's my boat.
> ...
  Edda · sad ...Good. Somebody used to ask me that every crossing.
MOVE: Edda returns to the wheelhouse door and stays there, watching the PC.

Reactive (talk to Edda at the wheelhouse):

Edda · neutral Thirty-one years on this strait. Never thought I'd see them close it.
Edda · deadpan Don't touch the wheel. Don't touch the rail. Touch the horizon if you like, it's free.

Flavor passengers (deck)

Old Man See the colors on the skyline? Eighteen of 'em. That's Velmora.
Old Man When I was a lad you only saw the Imprints on a clear night. Now you see 'em through fog.

Woman With Crate I'm going home to Saltmere. My sister says don't. I said, where else would I go? I get ill anywhere else.
Woman With Crate Three weeks abroad and I was grey as dishwater. They call it wilting. You'll see.

Boy Mum says when we land a machine tells you what color you are! I want to be red.
Boy'S Mother You'll be green like the rest of us, love. We're Briarwick.
Boy ...Can I be green AND red?

Sailor Last crossing. After tonight the Concert's cutters turn back anything bigger than a gull.
Sailor Captain says she'll tie up at the Landing and learn to knit. She won't.

Seasick Man Don't talk to me. If I open my mouth, more than words come out.

EV "Horizon" (action at the bow)

Eighteen lights sit low over the sea, each a different color.
One of them, far to the north, flickers.
(Hidden item on the coiled rope beside the bow: POTION. "Someone's seasick remedy. It's just a Potion with a lemon drawn on it.")

EV "Aurelian Voss" (starts when the PC returns to the rail after talking to Edda)

MOVE: Voss walks up beside the PC and leans on the rail, right next to the sign. He holds a chipped white mug with a faded sunburst.
Voss · happy First crossing? Everyone goes quiet when they see the lights.
Edda · angry *(from the wheelhouse)* RAIL! *(anger vein)*
Voss I believe the rail has no objection, Captain.
Edda Nobody asked the passengers in the nice coats!
Voss · neutral She's been shouting at me since I was a linesman. It's how I know I'm home.
Voss I've spent a month in a marble room asking the Concert not to do this. They did it anyway. Politely.
Voss So. You're coming *in* on the day everyone else wishes they could get out. That takes nerve or bad luck.
> Nerve.
  Voss · happy Good. Velmora runs on it.
> Bad luck.
  Voss · happy Then you'll fit right in.
> ...
  Voss · neutral Or grief. Forgive me. I shouldn't guess.
Voss · neutral Are you challenging the gyms? You've got the look. Eighteen Wardens, eighteen badges. Nobody's done all eighteen in ten years.
Voss · happy Here. You'll want one of these.
(Received: BADGE CASE.)
ITEM DESCRIPTION: A slim brass case with eighteen empty settings. Stamped on the hinge: MERIDIAN CONCORD.
Voss · neutral We make them for the League anyway. Call it a welcome from a fellow traveler.
Voss And this, if you'll take it. A Meridian Fellowship. A little money each month, a discount at any Mart. We give them to young trainers with promise.

CHOICE :pro_fellowship

> Thank you. (accept)
  Script: pf_choose(:pro_fellowship, :accept)
  (Received: FELLOWSHIP CARD. ₽3000.)
  Voss · happy No, I insist. Somebody should be kind to you on a day like this.
> No, thank you. (decline)
  Script: pf_choose(:pro_fellowship, :decline)
  Voss · happy Independent. Good. Keep that. It's worth more than the card.
> ... (silent)
  Script: pf_choose(:pro_fellowship, :silent)
  Voss · neutral Think about it.
  (He sets the card on the rail. Received: FELLOWSHIP CARD. It is not activated; a Mart clerk can activate it later for the ₽3000.)

SE: ship's horn.
Voss · neutral That's the Landing. Aurelian Voss. If you ever need anything in Lumen City, ask for me by name. They'll laugh, and then they'll fetch me.
MOVE: Voss walks aft. At the gangway he looks back once.
Switch S101 PRO_FERRY_DONE = ON. (Gangway rope removed.)

If the PC inspects the mug mark he left on the rail: A ring of cold tea. He drank it black.

Map 110 — The Dovetail, Cabin (optional before docking)

BUNK: Your bunk. You didn't sleep in it.
PORTHOLE: Dark water. Far down, for a moment, something glows. Then it doesn't.
Cook Last bowl of chowder on the last ferry. Historic chowder. Eat it slow.
  (Received: OLD CHOWDER. "Restores 20 HP. Tastes like the end of an era.")
BOOKSHELF: "Passenger Notice: Persons of Velmoran birth are advised that prolonged absence from one's home Imprint may cause fatigue, pallor and low spirits. The line accepts no liability for wilting."
LOCKED TRUNK (Edda's): It's locked. Scratched into the lid, very small: I.A. + child, night crossing, 290. Paid in full.

(The trunk is the first Edda clue. No reaction is scripted.)

Map 100 — Ferrow's Landing, the dock (arrival; BGM: harbor morning, accordion)

Dorian · smug Dorian Pell. Warden of Saltmere, Pageant-Master to the Accord, and for thirty-one consecutive years, Saltmere's Most Eligible Something.
Dorian · neutral You saw the barge? The Queen sends it every week. Our charter says we answer to no crown. Every week we remind her, in the only language a crown understands.

Dorian · happy And the Pageant opens tonight at the Lantern Theatre. I wrote none of it and I'm in all of it.

Quill Free port means free. Meridian's ships pay the same dues as a fishing smack. Mr. Voss is very gracious about it.

[after S108] Quill The Queen's herald came by boat this morning. First time a Crown boat's tied up here in eighty years. Nobody booed. That's how frightened everyone is.

Flavor townsfolk (Saltmere promenade, harbour and Old Town)

Caramel Seller Salt-caramel! Fresh salt-caramel! Pageant tonight — the Loyal Three companion piece!
Caramel Seller (again) It's mostly salt. That's the secret. Don't tell anyone. Everyone knows.

Busker Saltmere's Plate makes everything ordinary — no Bleed, no miracles. So we make our own, on stage!
Busker (again) I've played this corner twenty years. Not one strange thing has happened to me. I find it very hard to write songs.

Lamplighter No Meridian lamps on the promenade. The Warden says these lamps are part of the set. Meridian can light the rest of Velmora; the set stays oil.

Stagehand On A Smoke Break Opening night's tonight. The Accord sends an inspector to make sure we say every line of the official text.
Stagehand On A Smoke Break (again) He sleeps through the second act. We've timed it. Eleven minutes in, every year.

Fisherman Ordinary fish. Ordinary sea. Fifty years and never seen a thing out of the way. I find that very restful.

Child With An Ogre Puppet The Ogre steals the Plates and the Three bite him! Then everyone claps! Then there's caramel!
Child With An Ogre Puppet (again) I like the Ogre. Don't tell anyone. He's got a nice face.

Retired Actor On A Bench I played a king once. In a play they closed before the dress. I'm not allowed to say which.
Retired Actor On A Bench (again) Better part than Ogre, I'll tell you that. The Ogre never gets a speech.

Hound Number Two I'm Hound Number Two! I bite on the beat! The beat is "GRR". I have to wait for Hound Number One's "GRR" and then I go "GRR".

Grey Pilgrim Lovely night for a play. Sit near the back, child. You'll see more from the back.

Rival Theatre Barker (again) Dorian's seen it nine times. He says it's "to gather evidence". He laughs at all the right parts.

Fishwife You've no tint at all? In Saltmere that's barely worth gossip. We're all Blank here. You're just Blanker.

Accord Inspector I have a copy of the official text. Every word approved. I will be following along. Closely. Until the second act.

Meridian Clerk We're not trying to light Saltmere. We're just asking. Every week. Politely.

Old Sailor Saltmere won't wilt you, they say. Born here, live anywhere. It's the one Plate that doesn't hold on. Kindest Plate there is.

Sidequest B — "The Inspector's Text"

(Accord Inspector, after S108, on the promenade with his copy of the official text open, staring at nothing:)
Accord Inspector Every word approved. I've followed every word for nineteen years. Last night a man said four sentences and none of them are in here.
Accord Inspector I've been asked to report what was said. Word for word. I didn't write it down. I was... I was listening.
> Tell him what the Mourner said.
  Accord Inspector *(writing)* "...ever rots." "...underwater." "...collars." Collars. Yes. Thank you.
  Accord Inspector I'm going to send this to Crownhaven, and then I am going to take a very long walk.
> Tell him you don't remember.
  Accord Inspector No. Nor do I. Nor does anyone. That's what I'll write. "Nobody remembers." It's the safest sentence in the language.

Script: Chapter 3 — "The Weaver's Debt" (the Weavers' Road, Briarwick, Gym 2 and its aftermath)

Final playable script for Chapter 3 (SPINE Revisions 8 and 14). It covers the Weavers' Road out of Saltmere's North Gate (541 the Grey Saltings, 544/545 Brinecut Mine, 552 the Dyers' Ford, 540 Thistledown Lea, 546/547 Thistledown Manor), the Gossamer Wood 524 and Woodward's Hut 526, Briarwick 120–125, the Loomhouse 130–131 (Gym 2), then the Gossamer Deepwood 525 and Cocoonfall Hollow 548. It follows story/20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md (Prologue, Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 in Saltmere) and uses its conventions. Structure follows the built events in mapgen/specs; where this file adds an event, it is marked [NEW]. Map 552 is new (cartographer, tools/worldmap/world_data.py), so all of its events are new. Sources: 04_ACT_I (outline), 15_COMEDY (scene Ch3, inlined), NARRATIVE_KEYS (choice keys), FLAGS (switches), GYM_PUZZLES (Gym 2), DUNGEON_PUZZLES (D4 Brinecut, D5 Thistledown), CAMEOS §1 (Shelly), BALANCE 4b (versions). Before Revision 14 this was Chapter 2. Keys and switches keep their old names: :ch2_tamsin, :ch2_matriarch, CH2_THISTLE_DONE, CH2_MATRIARCH_DONE are all Chapter 3 now. Events must test Tamsin's badge by Warden (pfm_gym_won?(:LEADER_TAMSIN)), never badge_count >= 1: the player arrives here already holding Dorian's badge.

Conventions

Same as 20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md: Portrait use per SPINE Rev 22 (story/13_CUTSCENES.md): Name · expression faces for the cast (first line and expression changes; later lines X keep the face), the rare Name · expression · emote, and X for everyone else (generic NPCs, trainers, the cameo Shelly), > option choices, MOVE:/SE:/WAIT n, [after X] reactive variants. Gym numbers are written for readability (Tamsin is 2); events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_TAMSIN)).

Juno travels with the PC for this whole chapter (placed events per map) until she leaves at the Cocoonfall Veil.

CHAPTER 3 — "The Weaver's Debt"

Chapter start: V102 = 3, set at Saltmere's North Gate (end of Chapter 2). The road inland is the one Briarwick's cloth comes down: salt marsh, the dyers' river, the dead House Thistledown's meadows, then silk.

Map 541 — The Grey Saltings (:BEACH; BGM: route theme, fuller)

ROAD SIGN: THE GREY SALTINGS — The Weavers' Road. ↓ Saltmere (North Gate) · ↑ The Dyers' Ford, Thistledown Lea & Briarwick. Mind the pans. The pans do not mind you.
(Salt pans to the horizon, white stacks, the smoke of the boiling-house, and a chalk cliff behind with a mine mouth in it.)
Juno · neutral This is where Saltmere's salt comes from. "Grey" is the salt before it's washed.
Juno ...And the weather. It's mostly the weather.

Route trainers and flavor:

Dyer Morwenna Red's my color! Red's everyone's color, eventually, if you work the madder vat. (Battle. After:) Look at my hands. They'll be red till Fallmorn.
Dyer Ash Woad blue. The Queen's Elowen green is woad and weld together. She's never paid for a yard of it. (Battle.) [after] Bill her. Somebody bill her.
Dye Foreman Step the stones in the order I hum. Red, blue, yellow. No — that's blue, red, yellow. I've been humming it wrong for thirty years and nobody's told me.
Smeargle Owner My Smeargle paints a mark on the boundary stone for every trainer who passes. Yours is... it's left yours blank. It's never done that.
Shearer Briarwick's dyers, Saltmere's salt, Ferrow's fish. Every town in Elowen's got a thing the Plate gives it. We've got colors. Lovely colors. You can't eat them.
HIDDEN ITEM (base of the third flag): ANTIDOTE. "A surveyor dropped it. He'll want it in about ten minutes."
BERRY TREE: Juno: "Pecha! Pick it gently. It bruises if you look at it wrong. Like Kestrel."
SHRINE OF THE FOURTH COLOR: A plain white ribbon tied to a stake at the edge of the undyed band. Dozens more are tied beside it. A card in a child's hand: "for the color nobody gets".

ROAD SIGN: THISTLEDOWN LEA — The lands of House Thistledown (extinct). ← The Dyers' Ford · → Gossamer Wood & Briarwick · ↑ Thistledown Manor (PRIVATE. DECEASED.)
Juno · happy Mum says the Thistledowns were actors. All of them. Even the dog. They played Saltmere for a hundred years and then they all died in the same winter.
Juno · neutral People say they're still up there. Rehearsing. I'd like to see that. From a distance. A long distance.
Drover Race you to the fence! (He wins. He always wins. He has a Ponyta.)

Guildmistress Hett (Weavers' Guildhall, map 123)

Hett Old Mother Loom ran this guild forty years and never once missed a moth-count. The girl's missed three.

Flavor townsfolk

Weaver At Loom Clack-clack. Sixty picks a minute. Don't talk to me on the downstroke.

Dyer Elowen green, that's my vat. The Queen's own shade. She's never paid for a yard of it. "The Crown's by right of soil," says the taxman. So's the mud, I said.

Apprentice I wove my first scarf! It's got eleven mistakes. Tamsin found a twelfth and then apologized for an hour.

Silk Merchant Briarwick silk never tangles and never rots. That's why nobody ever buys a second one. Terrible business. Wonderful product.

Meridian Linesman Pylon'll be humming by month's end. Free light for the looms! Folk here look at me like I'm selling plague.
Meridian Linesman (again) Truth is, I don't know what it does to the wood. I just bolt the brass.

Boy In Dog Mask And I'm a Loyal Hound and I bite you! ...Why does the Ogre mask look sad?

Egg-Seller Silk-moth eggs, a copper each. That loud girl in the flowers bought forty. FORTY. For her uncle, she says. In a hatbox.

Tax-Barge Deserter I rowed the Queen's tax-barge. Jumped off at Saltmere when they booed us. You've heard them? Then you know. Weaving's quieter. Nobody boos a scarf.

Accord Chaplain The chapel's open. The mural's older than the looms. Mind the Crown in it — people say it's painted wrong. It isn't. It's painted *before*.

Youngster The Warden cries in the gym at night. I heard her through the wall. Then she apologized to the wall.

Woman With Basket East wood rings like a bell now. My mother says a ringing wood means a wedding. I don't think this is a wedding.

Cutter'S Wife You'll want my husband if there's a tree in your way. He'll say no first. He always says no first. Wait for the second answer.

Bun-Seller A boy in a black coat came through yesterday asking about masks. Who carves them, who wears them, who doesn't take them off. Rude. Bought a bun. Went north.

[after gym, village-wide variants]

Signs and objects

TOWN SIGN: BRIARWICK — Where the Thread Never Tangles. (Carved under it, smaller: "Unlike the Guild Accounts.")
LOOMHOUSE SIGN: LOOMHOUSE GYM. WARDEN: Old Mother Loom (painted over) TAMSIN LOOM. "A thread holds because it's twisted with others."
FESTIVAL POSTER (square): The same poster as the Landing and Saltmere. Here the dark fleck in the Crown's stone has been circled in charcoal. Someone has written: "SEE CHAPEL."
PYLON (east edge): Half a brass pylon. A plate reads: MERIDIAN CONCORD — LATTICE 15 (BRIARWICK) — "Light for Everyone." It is faintly warm, and the grass around it is stiff, like spun sugar.
SURVEY FLAGS: Orange cloth on stakes. Four of the stakes have been neatly cut. The cuts are very clean. A weaver's shears. (You saw ropes cut like that in the Lantern Theatre.)
OGRE MASK STALL: Carved bark masks for Fallmorn, rows of them. Every one has the same sad face. "That's how the Ogre looks," says the carver. "Always has." You've seen that face before, stepping out of a painted sky in Saltmere.
SILK RACKS: The silk moves in no wind at all.
HIDDEN ITEM (under the rope bridge): X ATTACK. "It fell out of someone's pocket mid-bwoing."
HIDDEN ITEM (behind the dye vats): TINY MUSHROOM. "Dyed Elowen green. Still a mushroom."

(A stone shrine: three carved beasts, a dog, a monkey and a pheasant, standing over a broken ogre mask. An old woman in a grey shawl is sweeping it. She is barefoot.)
Old Woman Three loyal hounds and an ogre so bold...

  Old Woman Oh, I couldn't say. I could *sing* it, but I couldn't say.

  Old Woman Quiet. Good. You'll hear more that way. Most of it's under the floor.
Old Woman You've no color on you, child. Did you know? Like water in a glass.
Old Woman Walk carefully. Eighteen roads is a long way, and people will want to carry you.
(She goes back to sweeping. After Tamsin's badge she is gone; a single dusk-colored flower lies on the shrine. S170 OFF.)

Map 131 — Loomhouse Gym, the Canopy (the hollow of the elder; web trampolines; variables V305–307 CANOPY_WEB_A/B/C, the Loomhouse's IDs since before the swap)

(Layout and rules: GYM_PUZZLES Gym 2 §131. A taut web throws you three tiles the way you stepped on; a sticky web stops you; nothing under you means the net. The climb: the floor → ledge 1 → ledge 2 → the sticky turn → ledge 3 → the Joltik perch and back → Tamsin's ledge.)

(First entry. The stair comes up into the hollow of the elder. Inside it's as tall as a cathedral and full of webs: silver drum-tight ones, sagging yellow ones beaded with dew, and far overhead a ledge with a lantern on it. Moths drift across the drop. Something small and yellow crackles along a strand.)
CARD: WEBS (on a twig at the foot of the hollow): "Tight webs THROW you, three bounds, the way you step on. Mind which way you're facing. — T.L."
Pim Pim. I mind the nets. Want the Joltik calmed down, or a nudge?
  > A nudge. (one hint per ask)
    Pim A Joltik's spark runs the whole strand. Look at which webs hang on each one.
    Pim Up there you want to go up, stop, then go across. Taut throws, sticky stops.
    Pim Spark both Joltik, once each: the one on the third ledge and the one on the west perch. Then the bottom web throws you up, the middle one holds you, and the top one throws you across to Tamsin.
  > Calm the Joltik. (reset: V305–307 = 0, back to the foot of the hollow)
    Pim *(clicks his tongue; somewhere above, a Joltik yawns)* There. Every strand as Tamsin left it.
FALL (a web throws you onto nothing): ...and nothing there to land on. You drop into Tamsin's safety net, far below.
  The net lowers you, very gently, all the way back to the bottom of the hollow. A card is pinned to it: "Sorry! — T.L."
SPINARAK (floor): The Spinarak is spinning a very small web. It is very proud of it.
SWADLOON (by the stair): The Swadloon is wrapped in leaves for the night. It's the middle of the afternoon.

Juno (at the foot of the hollow, once the PC has beaten a trainer in here; she's holding a hatbox with great care)

Juno · happy Forty eggs! In a hatbox! Don't knock the hatbox! And don't fall on me!
Juno Go on, I'll be loud. Quietly. I learned that in Saltmere.
(again:) Juno · happy · exclaim *(a whisper you can hear from the top of the tree)* GO ON, [Player]!

Ledge 1 (one web, straight up from the floor)

Ledge 3 (up through the sticky turn; the two webs either side of the first sticky web, and the one beside the start, throw you into the drop)

CARD: JOLTIK: "The Joltik eat the current in the strands. Spark one and every web on its strand changes. Gold strand here, blue strand on the perch. Sorry about the zaps. — T.L."

(The obvious move is the trap: spark only the gold Joltik and the bottom two webs both go taut, so they throw you straight up the trunk and into the net. Spark both, once each: up, stop, across.) Tamsin's ledge

STAIR (behind Tamsin, before the badge): A silk rope across the stair, and a card: "Upper lofts: Gran's old practice rooms. After your badge. Sorry! — T.L."

Warden battle (double)

(Tamsin stands at the top of the hollow, among the webs. She has stopped fidgeting.)
Tamsin · neutral Gran wove the looms downstairs. She never came up here. She said the Bugs had better hands than hers, and she was right.
Tamsin · sad She held this village together for fifty years with thread and shouting. I've had it since spring. I can't shout.
Tamsin · neutral Dorian goes first because he makes people brave. I go second because by then you think you know what a gym is.
Tamsin · angry But I can hold a thread. So can they. We spun this whole hollow together, the Bugs and me. Don't you dare tear it.
Script: Prismfall.gym_battle(2)     # LEADER_TAMSIN, :SILKWOOD, cap 19, DOUBLE battle (GYMS double: true)
(When her ace enters:) Tamsin · neutral Twist with me. Hold.
(LOSE: standard whiteout to the Pokémon Center. Tamsin on retry: "Again? Good. I mean— sorry. I mean good.")
(WIN:)
Tamsin · shocked ...It held, and you still came through it.
Tamsin · happy That's allowed. Gran said a good web always leaves one way through, for the right one. I didn't think I'd ever meet one.
(Received: the WEFT BADGE.)
(The PC opens the Badge Case and sets the badge beside Dorian's. SE: the first note, then a second, higher, in tune with it. The two hang in the air together. *(music note)* over Juno.)

Tamsin · neutral I don't think they do that. ...Do they do that?

Tamsin · sad [Player]... could you come up to the loft? There's something I should say to someone, and you've an honest sort of silence.

Tamsin, after the confession (her ledge): Tamsin · neutral The Cutter in town owes me a favour. Tell him I sent you. And— thank you. Not sorry. Thank you. / Tamsin · neutral The stair behind me goes up to Gran's practice lofts. They're open to you now. Mind the brass wire. It isn't hers. (the brass wire is Meridian's, stamped with a sunburst: GYM_PUZZLES §132) If Granny's Knot is solved (S308): Tamsin · crying You finished Gran's row. ...She'd have shouted. Happily. Sorry — I'm crying, that's the Silkwood, it's very dusty.

Map 130/131 loft — EV "Tamsin's confession" → CHOICE :ch2_tamsin (the key keeps its old name; staged in the Warden's loft, high in the elder above the webs, where Hett says the ledger is kept; or in the Guildhall loft 123: guard whichever copy is built with pf_choice(:ch2_tamsin).nil? && pfm_gym_won?(:LEADER_TAMSIN))

(The Warden's loft, high in the elder above the webs: a ledger open on a table, a contract with a gold sunburst seal. Tamsin won't sit.)
Tamsin · sad That woman at the pylon. With the shears. She was right. I signed it.
Tamsin Briarwick's bankrupt. It has been for three years. Gran hid it. I found the accounts the week I buried her.
Tamsin Meridian offered four hundred thousand for "stewardship rights". One pylon. Free light. I signed it by myself, at night, so nobody would have to know how bad it was.
Tamsin · neutral And it WORKS. That's the thing. The looms ran till midnight for a week. Everyone was so happy. Nobody had been happy since the funeral.
Tamsin · crying And now the Glasswood's walking up the survey line like it was invited. Fourteen moths this week. I count them. I count them every morning.
Tamsin · sad The man in Saltmere told everyone to ask their Warden. Nobody's asked me yet. They're all too kind. The guild meets tonight.
Tamsin Tell me what to do. Please. I've run out of thread.
> Tell them the truth. I'll stand next to you. (help_confess)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch2_tamsin, :help_confess)
  Tamsin · shocked Next to me. Not in front?
  Tamsin · neutral ...A thread holds because it's twisted with others. I've had that on the SIGN.
  → Scene: the guild meeting. Tamsin speaks; her voice cracks twice; Hett stands up first: "Then we sign it WITH you, girl, and then we tear it up together." The contract is renegotiated: a smaller pylon, off the grove.
> They deserve to know. If you won't say it, I will. (expose)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch2_tamsin, :expose)
  Tamsin · panic No— wait— not like—
  → Scene: the guild meeting. The PC lays the contract on the table. Uproar. The looms stop. Tamsin stands very still, then tears the contract in half herself, in front of them: "I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. That's the last time I'll say it tonight."
  (Outcome flag TAMSIN_PUBLIC_CONFESSION is derived from this choice.)
> It's your secret. I won't tell. (keep_secret)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch2_tamsin, :keep_secret)
  Tamsin · sad ...Thank you. I think. I'll fix it quietly. I'll find the money somewhere.
  → No meeting. The pylon is finished within the week (map state). Hett's lines stay suspicious. (In Act V, Tamsin can't afford to let go of her Plate.)
(All branches:)
Tamsin · neutral Whatever's making the wood ring, it's in Cocoonfall Hollow, at the Glasswood's heart. I can't cross the Veil. Nobody can.
Juno · neutral *(from the stairs, hatbox in her arms)* ...They can.
Tamsin · shocked *(shock lines)* What?
Tamsin · neutral Then take this. It was Gran's shuttle. It's only wood. But she never dropped a thread while she held it.

(A dew-pond clearing. A pink-haired girl is crouched in front of a Caterpie, bowing to it.)

Shelly Oh! A person! Um. Hello. Is this— this isn't the Rhodochrine Jungle, is it. *(sweat drop)*
Shelly I looked into a pond at home and then I was looking OUT of this one. That was three days ago. The paths keep re-weaving.

BATTLE: FESTIVAL_SHELLY "Shelly", version 1 (double, `:SILKWOOD`; level per BALANCE §6, after Gym 2).

Shelly Your forest sounds like home used to, before the city got sick. Look after it?
(Received: SILVER POWDER and TM STRUGGLE BUG.)

Map 548 — Cocoonfall Hollow (:BLEED)

(The Veil at the Hollow's mouth. Inside: a crater of crystal trees, and silk that has turned to glass thread, strung between them like a harp. It rings.)
(Juno and Tamsin stop at the Veil. Juno: "Shout if— no. You can't hear through it, can you. Just come back.")
INSPECT, glass cocoons: Dozens, hanging. Inside each, a moth, wings spread, perfectly still. One of them twitches.

Boss: "The Glass Matriarch" (multi-bar; design/BOSSES.md)

(At the center, a Galvantula the size of a cart, half crystal, sits on a nest of glass silk wound around something that glows faintly green beneath the roots.)
It turns eight eyes on you. Four of them are glass.
BOSS BATTLE: Glass Matriarch (GALVANTULA, 2 bars, level per BOSSES.md for the segment after Gym 2; field `:BLEED`; at the bar break it "re-strings the nest": the field borrows `:SILKWOOD` for 3 turns).
(WIN:)
The Matriarch collapses onto the nest. The ringing drops by half. It thrashes, shedding slivers of crystal.

CHOICE :ch2_matriarch (the key keeps its old name)

> Stay with it. (soothe)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch2_matriarch, :soothe)
  You sit down in the glass. You hold Mother Loom's shuttle because you don't know what else to hold.
  (Fade. Night passes. Fade in: dawn through crystal.)
  The Matriarch is asleep against your knee. Around you, half the grove has gone to glass in the night. The other half hasn't.
  The ringing has stopped.
> Put your hand on it. Make it stop. (silence)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch2_matriarch, :silence)
  You press your palm to its crystal side.
  Something goes out of it, like water down a drain. Through you. To nowhere.
  The crystal falls away as dust. The grove stops ringing at once. Not one more tree turns.
  The Matriarch stands. It is whole. Its eyes are dull as buttons. It doesn't look at you. It doesn't look at anything.
Switch S107 CH2_MATRIARCH_DONE = ON. V105 BRIARWICK_GLASSWOOD = 1. (The Accord cordon on the forest road to Windfall Row lifts: the shortcut home is open.)

Script: Chapter 4 — "Both Ways" (the Hoar Road, Frostwick, Gullcry, Ebbmouth, Gym 3; K2)

Final playable script for Chapter 4. It covers the Hoar Road north out of Briarwick (566 Spinners' Rise, 577 Frostwick Pass, 570 Frostwick and its interiors 571–576, 578 Rimewood Path, 562 the Rimewood), 561 Gullcry Cliffs (K2) and 564 Gullcry Caves, then Ebbmouth (160 and 167 the Mill Quay, interiors 161–166 and 168 the Net Loft) and the Tidelock Gym 170–174 (Gym 3). It follows story/21_SCRIPT_CH3.md and uses the conventions of story/20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md. These maps are built (map builders 10–14). Their flavour events stand as built; this script adds the story events and the lines that change, and marks every event that isn't on the built map [NEW]. Where a built event's text changes, the new text is here and the event is marked [CHANGED]. The list at the end says exactly what to wire. Sources: 04_ACT_I Ch4, 03_CAST (Marisol, Teo, Kestrel, Larch, Hesper), 09_MYSTERIES (#2a, #3, #10, #14, #22, #29), 10_CHOICES_ENDINGS and NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch4_kestrel_mourner, :ch4_teo), 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING (the Ch4 seed), 15_COMEDY (Ch4 "He Followed You Here"; running gags 1–3), TRIALS / TRIALS_QUESTS (the Tally and Prize Exchange quests of Ch4), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 3 (the trim), BALANCE (K2, Marisol), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md (proposal A).

Conventions

As in 20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md: Name · expression faces for the story cast in Prismfall::Portrait::CAST (tagged on a speaker's first line in a conversation and where the expression changes; later lines X), the rare Name · expression · emote for a marked comic beat, and X for everyone else. > option choices, MOVE: / SE: / BGM: / WAIT n, [after X] and [if ...] variants. Gym numbers are for reading; events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_MARISOL), double: false) and pfm_gym_won?(:LEADER_MARISOL). In the cast list here: Kestrel, Marisol, Teo, Larch, Juno (letters only), Thistle (seen, not heard). Plain: Aria and the other Octave singers, Bersi, Pella, Mrs Reyes, every townsperson and trainer. Counter: V124 CH4_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 the Hoar Road · 1 K2 · 2 Marisol met · 3 the strike vote · 4 the night · 5 the morning after · 6 Gym 3 won · 7 Larch's confession (chapter closed).

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. The Night the Ebb Stopped. Meridian's night export draw kills the river for an hour (the cause); the masked cell blows the intake to stop the draw, and in doing it brings the river back all at once, recklessly, without looking at the water; the river comes back and drags a child's punt at the Guild mill-race, the same race that killed the Reyes siblings' father; the masked boy who helps haul the gate is Teo; the PC answers a Meridian guard with Marisol standing there (:ch4_teo). Build-up: Teo by day at the strike vote, and the river stuttering longer each time. Payoff: the morning after shows the choice on the quay. Consequence: Teo hunted or hidden in Ch5 and Ch9, Marisol's bond and Consent.
  2. Larch's confession. The tide tables prove the stutters, and the full stop, are Meridian's draw. "I lit up this whole region, you know. Eleven cities on my design." The first time the PC learns their mentor built the machine (the red herring "Larch works for Meridian" starts here; it resolves in Ch12). Nothing comic inside the night from the moment the river stops until the guard leaves, or in Larch's confession once the tide tables come out (15_COMEDY §1: jokes before, a full scene after).

"Dear [Player],
Forty eggs, forty caterpillars. One is a Spewpa already and very rude.
