(LOSE: standard whiteout to the Pokémon Center. Marisol on retry: "Back in the water! That's the spirit. That's the ONLY spirit.")
(WIN:)
Marisol · shocked ...
Marisol · happy HA! Tides take it, you rode it both ways!
(Received: the TIDETURN BADGE.)
(The PC opens the Badge Case and sets the badge beside the other two. SE: the first note, the second, and then a third, low, under both of them, like a floor laid under a room.)
Marisol · shocked ...Your box is singing.
Marisol · neutral My da had a harmonium. Played three notes like that and called it a hymn. Never went to chapel in his life.
(Received: TM03 WATER PULSE.)
Marisol · happy Water Pulse. Hits like a wave, leaves 'em seasick.
Marisol And that badge is the Guild's word, and the Accord's, that Pokémon up to level twenty-seven will heed you. Come up on the quay. I'm buying you an eel. I'm buying the whole quay an eel.
V124 = 6.

EV "Pick One" (160, the quay by the eel stall, after Gym 3; autorun once) [NEW]

(Evening. Marisol and the PC on the quay's edge with their feet over the water, eating smoked eel out of newspaper. The Ebb runs out to sea, steady. For now.)
Marisol · neutral Half this quay draws a Meridian wage. The other half fishes a river Meridian's drinking dry. Same families. Same kitchens.
Marisol · angry Meridian pays my people. Meridian's killing my river. Pick one, kid. I dare you.
> The river.
  Marisol · neutral Easy to say when it's not your people's wages.
> Your people.
  Marisol · neutral Easy to say when it's not your river.
> I can't.
  Marisol · sad No. Neither can I. That's the whole problem. That's why I swear so much.
[if :ch2_tamsin == :expose]
  Marisol · neutral Briarwick's Warden signed with them, I hear. Then tore it up in front of her whole guild. Poor lamb.
  Marisol I'm not signing anything. I'm going to stand on this quay and swear till one of them blinks.
[if :ch2_tamsin == :help_confess]
  Marisol · neutral Briarwick's Warden signed with them, I hear. Then walked into her guildhall, owned up to it, and made them rewrite the whole thing. Poor lamb.
  Marisol I'm not signing anything. I'm going to stand on this quay and swear till one of them blinks.
[if :ch4_teo == :confront]
  Marisol · sad And I'd tell my little brother where the guards walk again. Every night. Don't look at me like that. You'd do it too.
Marisol · happy Finish your eel. There's a woman at the Center with a box of papers asking for you, and she looks like she bites.

Map 161 — Ebbmouth Pokémon Center: EV "Larch's Tide Tables" [CHANGED: replaces the built Larch event] — key event 2

Plays on entering the Center after "Pick One" (V124 == 6). The built event's two lines become this scene.

(Larch is at the corner table in her oilskin, salt in her grey braid, surrounded by rolled charts. A Gale Post satchel is on the floor. A pot of something brown and terrible steams beside her.)
Larch · neutral There you are. Sit.
Larch · angry No. First. You dropped a mill-race gate. At night. In Isenmar. During a Hollow sabotage. Four days after I said, in writing, "wear a hat".
Larch · angry · anger This is LECTURE THREE. It has a DIAGRAM.
> You came all this way to tell me off?
  Larch · deadpan I came all this way because of the river. Telling you off is on the way.
> I wore a hat.
  Larch · deadpan You did not wear a hat.
> ...
  Larch · deadpan Silence. Lovely. Your mother did that. It never worked on me either.
Larch · neutral Drink this. It's disgusting.
(Received: a cup of kelp tea. You hold it. It holds you back.)
(She unrolls the first chart across the table and weighs the corners with sugar bowls.)
Larch · neutral Tide tables. Ebbmouth, six months. Every stutter the Guild's logged since winter, by the minute. I've been collecting them by post.
Larch And this, on top: the tidal Lattice's draw, hour by hour. Don't ask how I got it. I trained half the linemen in Isenmar. Some of them still answer my letters.
(She lays the second sheet over the first. The paper is thin enough to see through. Every stutter sits exactly on a spike.)
Larch · sad Every one. Every single stutter is a draw peak. On the hour, every hour they need the load.
Larch And last night. Midnight to five to one. That's the night export: Meridian runs the Lattice flat out while the Guild's asleep, fills the Prism Cells, and ships them south to the Concert of Regions on the night boats. The quarantine has an exemption for that. It always did.
Larch · neutral The Hollow blew the intake at eight minutes to one. The river came back at eight minutes to one.
Larch · sad They didn't stop your river, child. They started it.
Larch · neutral All at once, in the dark, with a child on the water, because nobody looked. Both of those are true. That's the trouble with being right in a hurry.
WAIT 40.
Larch · sad It's not the Hollow stopping the river. It's us.
Larch It's my design.
> Your design?
> You built it?
> ...
Larch · neutral I was Meridian's Chief Engineer. The Lattice is mine. Pylon, intake, the cells, the switching. I drew the first one on a napkin in a Lumen tea-shop.
Larch · sad I lit up this whole region, you know. Eleven cities on my design. And I think I'm killing it.
Larch I left them eight years ago. Don't ask me why yet. I'll tell you when I can say it without throwing something.
Larch · deadpan Drink your tea.
> (Drink it.)
  Larch · shocked ...You actually—
  Larch · deadpan Don't tell anyone. They'll expect it of themselves.
  (The tea is warm, and vile, and you finish it. Somehow that's the worst part.)
> (Save it for later.)
  Larch · deadpan That's what Kestrel says. He's had one "for later" since spring.
Larch · neutral I'm going back to the Landing on the morning post-boat. Tidewatch doesn't run itself, and I need to put these somewhere Meridian doesn't read my letters.
Larch You go on up the Lock Road to Lumen. Rook Calder's the next Warden. Pretty boy, very loud, always being filmed. Try not to be filmed.
V124 = 7.

(No portrait for Hesper: her letter is plain text.)

Chapter 4 close — 161 Gale Post desk, then 167 (V124 == 7) [NEW]

GALE POST DESK: A letter is waiting. No name on the envelope. The paper is cheap and heavy and smells of lamp-oil.
"Whoever you are —
stay away from my grandson.
Everyone who gets close to that boy's mother's ghost gets hurt."
(Unsigned.)
Larch · neutral *(reading over your shoulder, because of course she is)* That's Hesper Vane's paper. She buys it from the Landing chandler by the ream and writes to nobody.
Larch · sad ...Well. She wrote to you.
[if :ch4_kestrel_mourner == :kind]
  (A second note, folded small, pushed under the desk's blotter in a sharp hand:)
  "Ferry kid. Gone home. Gran wrote. Don't follow. — K.
   The eel was good. Don't tell anyone."
[else]
  Nurse Your friend in the black coat took the salt-sledge south at dawn. He left owing the eel stall for one eel. The eel stall's started a third page.
(Outside, 167 the Mill Quay: the towpath gate east is open. A gatekeeper leans on it.)
Towpath Gatekeeper The towpath east. The Reedholms, the Icecutters' Haul, the Locks, and up onto the Crownland. Lumen's four days on foot. Or one by airship, if you're rich. You're not rich.
SIGN: THE TOWPATH EAST — The Lock Road. The Reedholms · the Icecutters' Haul · Brassfall · the Icefall Locks · LUMEN CITY.
QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Earn the fourth badge in Lumen City, up the Lock Road.
V102 STORY_CHAPTER = 5.

(Kestrel goes home to the Ferrow Lighthouse because Hesper sent for him: that's where Interlude I finds him on the night of the Shatter, Ch5.)

Script: Chapter 5 — "Ten Years of Light" (the Lock Road, Lumen City, Gym 4, the Gala and the Lowlight Shatter)

Final playable script for Chapter 5, the end of Act I. It covers the Lock Road out of Ebbmouth (580 the Reedholms, 592 the Icecutters' Haul, 590 Brassfall, 581 the Icefall Locks, 595 Coppice Ride, 594 Wallshadow Row, 593 the Arc-Lamp Mile, 582 Lumen West Gate; optional 584/585 the Voltaic Sluiceworks and 588 Ebb Hollow), Lumen City (180 the Concourse, 181 the Lowlight, the Circuit Gym 190–193, Meridian Spire 185/186 and two new rooms below it), the Lowlight (Shattered) 608, and Interlude I at the Ferrow Lighthouse (105/106). None of these maps is built yet (map builder 15 is building them); the "Map events needed" list at the end is what to build from. Follows story/23_SCRIPT_CH4.md and uses the conventions of story/20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md. Sources: 04_ACT_I Ch5 and Interlude I, 05_ACT_II (the Act II opener), 03_CAST, 09_MYSTERIES (#2, #4, #8, #12–15, #17, #21, #23), 10_CHOICES_ENDINGS / NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch5_lowlight_testimony, GO_LIVE_WIRE), 13_CUTSCENES (portraits), 15_COMEDY (Ch5 "Chat Has Opinions"), 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING, GYM_PUZZLES Gym 4, TRIALS_QUESTS (ZE_OCTAVE_OFF_BEAT, ZE_CUSTOMER_SUPPORT, ZE_FIZZBOLT, ZE_ROTOM_RECALL), ROUTES.yaml (the Lock Road), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md. Key events (CHAPTER_BEATS): 1. the Lowlight Shatter (twelve named people Fixed in glass, Dex among them); 2. Valen sees the PC standing in the glass and grants Meridian the Mandate, and the PC testifies (:ch5_lowlight_testimony). Everything before the Gala is build-up for these: the twelve are met alive on 181 first, and the Plate's empty cradle is seen in Rook's gym. Nothing comic after the raid starts (15_COMEDY §1).

Conventions

As in 20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md and 23_SCRIPT_CH4.md. In the portrait cast here: Juno, Rook, Larch, Voss, Valen, Calla, Quent, Hollis, Renata (Councillor Sallow), Marchetti, Dex, Thistle, Sable, the Mourner, Teo, and in the interlude Kestrel and Hesper. Plain: Cadence and the other Octave singers, P-3NNY, the Lowlight's residents except Dex, every townsperson, guard and trainer. Gym numbers are for reading: events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_ROOK), double: false). Counter: V125 CH5_STEP (0–13; design/FLAGS.md and the map list below). Tone curve inside the chapter: the road is warm and funny; Lumen is a wow and then a question (the cold cradle, Juno's "How did he know which road you'd come up?"); the Gala is champagne with a crack running under it; from the moment the Gala's lights go grey, no jokes until the interlude, which is dry, not funny.

CHAPTER 5 — "Ten Years of Light"

Chapter start: V102 = 5 and V124 = 7 (Ebbmouth's towpath gate, Ch4 close). V125 = 0. The PC travels alone until Wallshadow Row.

Map 580 — The Reedholms (:SNOWY_MOUNTAIN; rain)

ROAD SIGN: THE REEDHOLMS — The Lock Road. ← Ebbmouth · → the Icecutters' Haul · ↑ the Sluiceworks dam. The boardwalks are re-laid every spring. This spring they weren't.
(Reed islets across the Ebb's delta, joined by boardwalks. Eel-weirs of woven willow across the channels. Rain hisses on the water.)
Eel-Weir Keeper Weirs catch eels when the river runs. When it stops, the eels just sit in them and look at you.
Eel-Weir Keeper (again) Since they blew the intake it's run like a clock. Meridian's still fixing it. I hope they take their time.

EV "A punt on the channel" (touch strip across the main boardwalk, once; only if pf_choice(:ch4_teo) != :report)

(A reed-cutter's punt slides out of the reeds. The punter has a cutter's hat pulled low, and a Carvanha noses along beside the hull.)
Teo · smug Don't wave. You'll make me look like I've got friends.
[if :ch4_teo == :confront]
  Teo · neutral Mari says you sat in the kitchen with her. Nobody sits in the kitchen with her when she's like that. Not even me. ...Thanks.
[if :ch4_teo == :keep_secret]
  Teo · neutral You told the Lattice man you didn't see my face. You were a foot from my face. I owe you. The Hollow pay their debts. Eventually. In eels.
Teo · sad Tell her I'm eating. Don't tell her where.
MOVE: the punt slides back into the reeds.

[if :ch4_teo == :report] WANTED POSTER (smoke hut): "TEO REYES — WANTED — SABOTAGE OF THE MERIDIAN TIDAL LATTICE." Someone has drawn him a moustache. Under it, smaller: "HE PULLED PELLA OUT." · Reed-Cutter Those went up on every hut from here to the Haul. They came down again on every hut, too. Wasn't me. Mostly.

BLEED VEIL (south bank): A shimmer over a sunken village. Through it, river water hangs in the air in slow round drops the size of houses, and fish swim through them.
Fisher At The Veil Holmsby. The Ebb took it in AF 296. Didn't flood it. Lifted the river clean off its bed and left it hanging. My sister's house is in there. Still dry, I'd bet.
Fisher At The Veil You'll go in? Nobody goes in.
SLUICEWORKS DOOR (sign): VOLTAIC SLUICEWORKS — MERIDIAN CONCORD — DECOMMISSIONED AF 291. DANGER: LIVE.
  Painted beside it in bright pink: "ROOK WAS HERE — EP. 112 'HAUNTED HYDRO' — STAY CHARGED!"

Maps 584/585 — Voltaic Sluiceworks (optional, :SCRAPYARD)

BUILDER'S PLATE (on the dead turbine): "VOLTAIC SLUICE No. 1 — FIRST LIGHT, AF 289 — DESIGN: I. LARCH, CHIEF ENGINEER."
  Scratched underneath, very small, in no particular hand: SORRY.
CLAPPERBOARD (on the floor): "ROOK CALDER LIVE — EP. 112 — TAKE 41." Forty takes are crossed out.

(The static Rotom on 585, the breaker doors and the Thunder Stone stay as maps.json has them.)

Map 588 — Ebb Hollow (optional, :BLEED)

FIELD NOTES pop-up (first entry): "EBB HOLLOW — BLEED. The Splash Plate's reach has lifted a river off its bed. Water hangs; fish swim in air; the field leans on water. (Larch, in the margin: 'If you're reading this inside it, I'm not speaking to you.')"
INSPECT, a kitchen: A table laid for four, perfectly dry. Above it, filling the room, a drop of river with a trout asleep in it.
INSPECT, a cradle: Empty. A single drop of water the size of a fist hangs over it, turning slowly, like a mobile.
INSPECT, a garden: The beans grew up toward the hanging water and into it. They're still growing, upside down, inside the drop.
INSPECT, a door: A house number, painted by hand: 9. Under it a child's chalk: "WE'LL BE BACK SATERDAY."

Map 592 — The Icecutters' Haul (:SNOWY_MOUNTAIN)

ROAD SIGN: THE ICECUTTERS' HAUL — The Lock Road. ← the Reedholms · → Brassfall & the Icefall Locks. Sled road: give way to ice.
Picket Captain Hulda Ice-cutters' union. No ice goes up the Locks to Lumen till Ebbmouth's wheel turns on its own.
Picket Captain Hulda Lumen puts Isenmar ice in its fancy drinks. Lumen can drink them warm for a week.
Striker We're on strike for Ebbmouth. Ebbmouth's not even on strike. That's solidarity. Look it up.
Mudsdale Driver The Mudsdale don't strike. They just refuse. It's different.
SAWYER'S CROSS (north gate): FROSTFANG PASS — CLOSED BY ORDER OF THE THANE.
SAWYER'S CROSS (south gate): SNOWBRIAR — CLOSED BY ORDER OF THE QUEEN.
  Chalked between them: "THEY AGREE ON ONE THING."
Meridian Recruiter Contract Seven! Heat for life! Ask me about Contract Seven!
DROPPED ICE BLOCK (action, once): A block of cut ice that slid off a sled. Something is frozen in the middle of it: a leather satchel with a Meridian sunburst on the flap.
  (Received: ICE-BOUND SATCHEL.) ITEM DESCRIPTION: "Frozen solid. You'd need a boiler."

Map 590 — Brassfall (lock-and-lift town) · 591 Pokémon Center · 596 Union Hall [NEW]

Arrival (autorun at the lower lock, once)

(A town built up the face of a frozen waterfall: lock after lock of brass and timber, each one a step higher than the last, with lift-cages on chains between them. Isenmar ice-cutters in fur, Zenith engineers in brass-buttoned coats, and everyone's breath smoking.)
Lockmaster Garrow The Locks lift the Ebb's boats onto the Crownland. Or they would, if the boats were moving.
Union Steward Gunnhild The Locks lift what we cut. Ice goes up, scrip comes down. Meridian pays us in scrip, and scrip's only good at Meridian's store.
Lockmaster Garrow It's perfectly good money!
Union Steward Gunnhild Try buying a pint with it in Ebbmouth.
Lockmaster Garrow ...I've never been to Ebbmouth.
Union Steward Gunnhild No. You haven't.

COMPANY STORE (sign): MERIDIAN COMPANY STORE — SCRIP ONLY.
Store Clerk Scrip only. ...You haven't got scrip. Nobody who isn't from here has scrip. I've sold one Potion this year, to myself.
Ice-Cutter Lumen's getting a gala and we're getting frostbite. That's the Lock Road for you. Everything goes uphill.

Optional: "The Ice Elevator" (the foot of the falls)

THE ICE ELEVATOR: A brass lift-cage frozen to its rail. A board: OUT OF ORDER SINCE THE STRIKE.
Lift-Boy It runs off a Cell, and Meridian took the Cells back when the union walked out. Give the motor a jolt and it'll go. Anything with a spark in it.
[if an Electric-type is in the party] > Let your Pokémon jolt it. → SE: Thunder1. The cage shakes off its ice and grinds upward. (The shortcut to the top of the Locks opens.)
[elif CELL BATTERY in the bag] > Use a Cell Battery. → (You lose one CELL BATTERY. The cage shudders and climbs.)
Lift-Boy (after) It goes all the way to the top of the Locks. Don't tell the union I fixed a Meridian lift. Don't tell Meridian the union let me.

591 — Brassfall Pokémon Center, Gale Post desk (V125 0 → 1)

GALE POST DESK: A letter is waiting, in green ink, with three exclamation marks on the envelope.
"[Player]!!!
Uncle Rowan was invited to Meridian's gala in Lumen (the TENTH YEAR OF LIGHT, with AIRSHIPS) and he's got Warden business, again, so he gave me his invitation and said, 'Go and eat their little cakes for me, Juno. All of them.'
He's never once missed a chance to tell Meridian what he thinks of them. I think he's being nice to me. He's been very nice to me lately. It's a bit worrying.
I'm coming down the Prism Falls road. Meet me at the Four Ways on the Crown Road? It's the inn with the signpost that points at four kingdoms. You can't miss it. FOUR KINGDOMS.
— Juno
P.S. The Spewpa evolved. It's a Vivillon now, and it's still rude."
QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Meet Juno at the Four Ways on Wallshadow Row, then go on to Lumen.
V125 = 1.

596 — Brassfall Union Hall [NEW]

(Benches, a stove, a notice board, and a boiler that heats the whole hall and most of the street.)
NOTICE BOARD: "SOLIDARITY WITH THE EBB GUILD." · "SCRIP IS NOT MONEY." · "LOST: one (1) Mudsdale. Answers to Mudsdale."
BOILER (action with ICE-BOUND SATCHEL): You prop the satchel against the boiler. It drips for a long time.

Union Steward Gunnhild (reading over your shoulder) Contract Seven. That's ours. That's what keeps Rimeholt's children warm.
Union Steward Gunnhild And this is the same contract. Word for word. For Ashkaar. They're selling the same fire to both of them.
Union Steward Gunnhild Keep that. Don't show it to an Isenmar man with a drink in him. Or an Ashkaar man with a sword. Or anybody, really.

Map 581 — The Icefall Locks (:SNOWY_MOUNTAIN)

ROAD SIGN: THE ICEFALL LOCKS — The Lock Road. ↓ Brassfall · ↑ Coppice Ride & the Crownland. Isenmar ends at the top. So does the ice.
(The Ebb comes off the Crownland downs here and falls into Isenmar in a staircase of frozen falls. Zenith's engineers cut locks into the ice and brass sluices into the rock. A Lattice pylon stands on every terrace, humming.)

Extraction Lattice No. 4 (the fenced terrace)

PLATE (sign): "MERIDIAN CONCORD — EXTRACTION LATTICE No. 4 (ICEFALL). COMMISSIONED AF 289. DESIGN: I. LARCH, CHIEF ENGINEER. LIGHT FOR EVERYONE."
Linesman Tolly Number Four. Eleven like her in the realm, and she was the second one built. The Professor's own drawing. Larch. Before she went soft.
Linesman Tolly Know her? ...Course you do. Everybody who comes up this road with that look on them knows her.

Notes for other teams

  • Mysteries seeded here (09): #2 (Rowan gives away his gala invitation; the Mourner's smoking right glove), #4 (Valen's crystal hand at the Veil; "Velmora endures", and nobody in the script remarks on the word), #8 (the Spire's plaque: the Aurelian sun tower), #9 (Lamp 47's draw spike, vague), #12 (Sable cheerful, gone before Security), #13 (Larch's fatigue lines; the Locks ledger's "draw x3"), #14 (Rook films the case glowing; Voss asks about it; Juno's "How did he know which road?"), #15 (the Prism Arena hoarding and model, "eighteen pylons"), #17 (Valen avoids the Lucent delegation), #23 (the black core that breathes), #29 (Contract 7-B). #5 and #6 are not touched: the Southgate prayer and window are hints only, and nobody says the Crown is cracked.
  • Comedy (15_COMEDY): Juno's pies, the scrip store, the tram stop, the vending and kiosk quests, Rook's blackout ("This is content"), "Chat Has Opinions", Larch's formal oilskin, Quent's bet. Script: Chapter 6 — "What the Sand Keeps" (the Brass Road, Duneholt, Gym 5, the Ossuary of Dunes; K3)

Final playable script for Chapter 6, the first chapter of Act II. It covers the Act II opener in the Lowlight (Shattered) 608, the Brass Road north out of Lumen (612 the Meridian Mainline, 602 Candle Down, 603 the Highwold, 600 the Brass Dunes with 610 Copperdune and 604/605 the Static Tunnels, 601 the Rib Road, 613 Sunbleach Flats), Duneholt (200–209, 214) and its gym (210–213, Gym 5), then the Marrow Road 620, the Ossuary of Dunes 624/625 (K3) and Sinkfield 628. None of these maps is built; the list at the end is what to build from. Follows story/24_SCRIPT_CH5.md; conventions of story/20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md. Sources: 05_ACT_II (the act opener and Ch6), 03_CAST (Sahar, Kestrel, Juno, Rook, Kassan), 09_MYSTERIES (#2, #2a, #7, #21, #24, #29), NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch6_drillsite, :ch6_kestrel_rumor, GO_SINKFIELD), 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING (the Ch6 seed), 15_COMEDY (Ch6 "Lecture, Archaeological", adapted; the Ossaria bits), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 5, TRIALS_QUESTS (the Rolls of Unearthing, Ch6), BALANCE (K3, Sahar), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md.

Conventions

As in the earlier scripts. Portrait cast here: Juno, Rook, Sahar, Kestrel, Marchetti (only if met in Ch5's testimony; otherwise her officers are plain). Plain: Sona and the Octave, Nadim, the Dig Lab interns, the caravan-mothers, Directorate officers, every townsperson and trainer. Events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_SAHAR), double: false). Counter: V126 CH6_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 leaving Lumen · 1 the Lowlight at dawn (Juno's goodbye) · 2 the Mandate checkpoint on the Mainline · 3 arrived in Duneholt · 4 the drill site and :ch6_drillsite · 5 Gym 5 won · 6 the Ossuary opened (Sahar's confession) · 7 the murals (S116) · 8 K3 (S117) · 9 Juno's letter (chapter closed).

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. The Ossuary murals and Sahar's confession. A dune-shift uncovers the door she sealed in AF 281 on Valen's order. Inside, the Gilded King, the two titans, the chain of eighteen locks and the city falling into the sea. Build-up: the warm ground, the "sleeping red giant", Sahar's three warnings, the drill site sinking the well. Payoff: the Duneholt Rubbing. Consequence: the Prismfall thread (Ch17), Sahar's Consent (by :ch6_drillsite), the war on the western dunes (her finger on the coastline).
  2. K3: Kestrel says the rumour out loud. With his mother's veil from the lighthouse trunk in his hand. :ch6_kestrel_rumor decides how Ironreach hits him. The Mandate's first arrests (the drill site) carry the chapter's middle: the Shatter's consequence, on screen, two weeks later.

CHAPTER 6 — "What the Sand Keeps"

Chapter start: V101 = 2, V102 = 6, V126 = 0 (Interlude I's end). The PC wakes in the Lumen Pokémon Center.

Map 608 — The Lowlight (Shattered), at dawn: the Act II opener (autorun on first entry, V126 == 0 → 1)

BGM: none. A wind-chime someone has hung on a glass washing line.
(Dawn in the Lowlight. Two weeks. The glass ring is still there under the Spire's foot, grey and silent. Round its edge, outside the Veil, a shrine has grown: soda cans, candles in jars, chalk on the stones. Twelve names, written over and over in twelve different hands.)
(At the Veil's edge, Mandate officers in white-and-gold stand by a new brass barrier. A sign on it: MERIDIAN SECURITY DIRECTORATE — BY MANDATE OF THE ACCORD — NO ENTRY.)
(Rook is sitting on the bottom step of the vault stair in a plain hooded jacket, no lights in it, no drone. He's holding a Fizzbolt he hasn't opened.)
Rook · sad I'm not filming. I'm just sitting.
Rook I come down every night. The guards let me. I think they think I'm doing a segment.
Rook · neutral Chat would say something. I don't know what chat would say. I haven't asked.

DEX (inspect his glass figure from inside the Veil; the PC can still walk in)

(You step through. The Directorate officers don't stop you. They don't know how to.)
(Dex is where he was: glass, mid-wave, his mouth open on a word. Someone outside the Veil has leaned a soda can against the shimmer as close to him as they could reach.)
(You stand with him. After a while you put your hand on his glass shoulder.)
SE: a single, very low note, from somewhere under your ribs.
(The glass is cold. And then, under your hand, it isn't. It's warm. Barely. Like a window with the sun on the other side.)
WAIT 60.
(You take your hand away. The warmth fades. Dex hasn't moved. Nothing has. But you felt it.)

(09 #21, the Harmony seed for the Homecoming waking. No text says what it means. The Trials quest ZE_LOWLIGHT_LAMPS (Dex's Pichu at the shrine) runs from here: S164 DEX_SHRINE.)

Marlo (lighting candles at the shrine, outside) You're the one who walks in. I saw you, that night.
Marlo Tell him— no. You can't tell him anything. ...Tell him anyway.

Juno's goodbye (at the top of the Lowlight stairs)

(Juno is waiting with her hatbox and a sack of seed packets. The curtain dress is gone; she's in her old flower-girl dress with the hem let down, and her eyes are red.)
Juno · sad I'm not going home.
Juno · neutral There's a doctor in Mirefen, down in Nadir. Dr Mott. He's got a whole ward of people turning to glass, slowly, and Uncle Rowan sends him seed stock every month for the medicine.
Juno I was going to send it by post this time. I'm not sending it by post. I'm taking it.
Juno · sad I couldn't do anything for Dex. I can't even walk in there. But I can carry a sack.
> I'll come with you.
  Juno · happy You can't, silly. You've got a badge to get. Duneholt's north, and Mirefen's down, and they're not letting anyone down the lifts any more.
  Juno · neutral I'll find a way down. Verdancers always find the way down. It's up we're bad at.
> Be careful.
  Juno · neutral I'm always careful. I'm careful about everything. It's very tiring.
> ...
  Juno · sad I know. Me too.
Juno · happy Write to me! Gale Post. "Juno, Mirefen, the one wearing a tree."
MOVE: Juno hugs you, hard and quick, and goes off along the Concourse toward the lift-shafts with the sack over her shoulder.
V126 = 1.
QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Earn the fifth badge in Duneholt, up the Brass Road north (the Meridian Mainline out of the Concourse).

Map 180 — Lumen City after the Shatter (state change; S115 on)

Office Worker They've put Mandate men on every lift down to Nadir. My cleaner lives down there. She hasn't been up in a week. The office is filthy and nobody's allowed to say why.
Old Man Gas lamps and smog. I said it was worse. I'd take it back now. I'd take it all back.
Pin-Seller Anniversary pins, half price. ...Quarter price. ...Take one. Please. I can't look at them.
LIFT-GRILLE (inspect): A brass barrier over it now, and a Directorate seal. Someone has chalked a grey ring on the seal.

Map 612 — The Meridian Mainline (:MOUNTAIN)

ROAD SIGN: THE MERIDIAN MAINLINE — The Brass Road. ↓ Lumen City · ↑ Candle Down & the Crown Road. Walk the service road. Do NOT walk the line.
(Zenith's first railway, running off the plateau's north lip on brass-and-iron trestles. Signal gantries clank. Trains go by full of crates stamped with the sunburst. You walk the service road beside the track.)

EV "The Checkpoint" (a Mandate barrier at the signal gantries; touch, V126 == 1 → 2)

(A brass barrier across the service road, a tent, a scanner plate on a post, and two officers in white-and-gold. A queue of drovers and pedlars waits with their hands out.)
Directorate Officer Mandate checkpoint. Papers and tint. Hand on the plate.
Drover Two weeks ago this was a road.
Directorate Officer It's still a road, sir. It's a road with a checkpoint on it.
MOVE: your turn. SE: chime... nothing. NULL.
Directorate Officer ...Hold on.
(She turns to a ledger on the tent pole and runs a finger down it. She stops.)
[if :ch5_lowlight_testimony == :someone_else]
  Directorate Officer You're flagged. By the Director herself. "Do not obstruct. Report movements." That's all it says.
  Directorate Officer So I'm not obstructing you. And I'm reporting that you went north. Have a nice trip.
[else]
  Directorate Officer You're on the Chair's guest list. Gala, Lumen. ...You were THERE?
  Directorate Officer Go on through. And — I'm sorry. About the Lowlight. My sister's on the Spire feeds. She was off that night. She's not been off since.
MOVE: the barrier swings up.
Drover (behind you) Oh, very nice. Very fair. Some of us have been here since six.
V126 = 2.

Trainers on 612 (trainer designer): rail workers and Directorate cadets.

Map 602 — Candle Down (:MEADOW; the Crown Road, east)

ROAD SIGN: CANDLE DOWN — The Crown Road. ↙ Wallshadow Row · ↘ the Meridian Mainline · ↑ the Highwold. Light one for whoever you've lost.
(Open downs round the Crownwall's east face. Cairns of white stones every few hundred yards, each with a niche for a candle. Pilgrims walk the cairns.)
CAIRN (any; inspect): Twelve candles in the niche. Twelve on the next one. And the next.
Pilgrim News travels round the Crown Road faster than the Gale Post. Every cairn from here to Kingsmead's got twelve on it.
Pilgrim I didn't know any of them. I light them anyway. Somebody should be counting.
CAIRN, the big one at the gap: From here the Crownwall has one gap in it, a notch in the white, and through it, very far off, something glitters on the inside of the wall like frost on a window. Old Pilgrim That's the Scar. Where the Glassfall came down, ten years back. Forty of them, in there. Nobody lights candles for those. The Accord says it's "not encouraged".
Coaching-Inn Keeper (the east junction's inn) Tea, bed, a horse if you've money. The road north's clear. The road east's full of Ashkaar envoys going to see the Sovereign about the Shatter. They've been very polite. It's frightening.

(The Glassfall Scar is seen properly in Ch13 from Kingsmead; here it's only a glitter through the gap.)

Map 603 — The Highwold (:MEADOW)

ROAD SIGN: THE HIGHWOLD — The Crown Road, north. ↓ Candle Down · → the Brass Dunes & Ossaria · ← Kingsmead (closed).
(Chalk downland north of the Crownwall, all skylarks and sheep. The Wold Stones stand in a ring on the top.)
WOLD STONES (inspect): Eighteen standing stones in a ring, and in the middle a flat one with nothing carved on it. The eighteen are worn smooth by three hundred years of hands. The middle one isn't. Nobody touches the middle one.
Shepherd Sheep won't graze inside the ring. Never have. Not even the stupid ones, and I've some very stupid ones.
Dew-Pond Girl The dew-pond fills itself every morning and nobody knows how. Grandad says the wold sweats. I say that's disgusting.

Map 600 — The Brass Dunes (borderland C) and Map 610 — Copperdune

ROAD SIGN: THE BRASS DUNES — ← the Highwold (Elowen) · → Copperdune & the Rib Road (Ossaria). The railway ends here. Ask the sand why.
(Where the downs give out, the sand starts. The Meridian railway runs out into it on a brass viaduct and simply stops, its last span hanging over a dune with nothing under it. Beyond, fossil ribs as big as houses stick up out of the sand.)
Rail Ganger They laid it to Duneholt. Three times. The sand moved the dunes over it three times. Meridian says they'll lay it a fourth. The sand says nothing. The sand doesn't have to.
COPPERDUNE (610): a rail-junction caravanserai round the broken viaduct; Ossarian bone-traders and a Zenith freight depot.
Bone-Trader Prices in bones, stranger. A Potion's two bones. A Super's five. A bone's a bone, don't ask me which.
Freight Clerk Meridian deep-drill crews come through here every week, north, with drill-heads the size of houses. They go out shiny and come back scraped.
Caravan Child My mum says the ground under Duneholt's warm. She says the sleeping red giant's turning over in his bed. I said, is he going to get up? She said not while I'm talking.

Trials on 610: The Riddle Trader (OS_RIDDLE_CARAVAN), Tomb Freight (OS_TOMB_FREIGHT). Copperdune's tablet rack (the Rolls of Unearthing).

Maps 604/605 — The Static Tunnels (:CAVE; dark: Flash)

(The old tram tunnels Meridian dug under the dunes before the sand ate the railway. Dead tram cars, live cables, Joltik in the dark.)
TRAM CAR No. 9 (inspect): Destination board: DUNEHOLT. Underneath someone has scratched: "EVENTUALLY."

Map 601 — The Rib Road (:DESERT; sandstorm) and Map 613 — Sunbleach Flats (:DESERT)

ROAD SIGN: THE RIB ROAD — Ossaria, the Bone Sands. ↓ the Static Tunnels · ↑ Sunbleach Flats & Duneholt. Keep to the ribs in a sandstorm.
(A red canyon road between the ribs of something that died before the Prismfall. Sandstorms come down it in walls.)
Caravan Guide Ribs on your left, ribs on your right. You can't get lost on the Rib Road. People do it every week.
ROAD SIGN (613): SUNBLEACH FLATS — ↓ the Rib Road · ↑ DUNEHOLT (the Sandgate). Linen, bones and everything else go white here in a season.
(White flats under a white sky. Frames of linen bleaching in rows, and Duneholt's Sandgate on the horizon, cut into the canyon mouth.)
Linen-Maker We bleach Briarwick's cloth for the Zenith market. It goes white in a week here. So do you, if you stand still.

Trials off 613: The Noon Bell (OS_OCTAVE_NOON_BELL), Sona of the Octave at the Temple of the Noon Sun (Octave 4 of 8; see the map list for its map ID).

Duneholt (200–209, 214; the Bone Sands)

Map 203 — the Sandgate: arrival (autorun, V126 == 2 → 3)

(A canyon mouth walled across in sandstone, with gate-towers carved straight out of the cliff. Through the gate: terraces of sandstone houses climbing the canyon's sides round an enormous round well, the width of a town square, going down and down.)
NOTICE (on the gate): "By license of His Excellency Idris Kassan, Prince-Elector of Ossaria, the Concord deep-works are a protected enterprise. Interference is an offence against the Elector."
NOTICE (pasted over a corner of it, newer): "BY MANDATE OF THE ACCORD: MERIDIAN SECURITY DIRECTORATE OPERATES IN DUNEHOLT FOR THE PROTECTION OF LATTICE ASSETS."
Caravan-Mother (spitting at the notices) Two notices. One from a man we elected for life and can't get rid of. One from a company we never elected at all.
Caravan-Mother And the western wells have changed hands twice this year. Both times the new owners had an accent.
Gate Guard Welcome to Duneholt. Water's a bone a cup. It was free last year.
QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Earn the fifth badge at the Dig, Duneholt's gym.
V126 = 3.

(09 #29 and 14_WAR's Ch6 seed: "the new owners had an accent".)

Map 200 — the Terrace Bazaar · 201 PC · 202 Mart

Spice-Seller The well drops a rung a week. My grandfather's name's on the third rung from the top, where he carved it as a boy. You need a rope to see it now.
Water-Seller A bone a cup! Two for a cold one! The cold ones come from the deep-works pipe, and don't ask what they did to get it cold.
Old Digger The desert keeps everything. My wife used to say that. She'd lose her keys and say "the desert's got them". It never gave them back.
Child The ground's warm. Put your hand on it. See? Mum says the red giant's dreaming. I think he's having a bad one.
201 GALE POST: "Duneholt: drink water. Not their water. Bottled. Lecture Six is being written in the dark because the Mandate has rationed my lamp-oil. — I.L." (Received: KELP TEA BAG. "Five.")

(Lecture numbers: Lecture Three was in Ebbmouth; Four and Five went by post in between. Larch's count is her own.)

Map 209 — Sahar's Dig Lab: Sahar (first meeting)

(A long room cut into the canyon wall, crowded with bones, crates, rubbings and three exhausted interns. At the back, a woman in a sand-coloured keffiyeh and wire spectacles is brushing dust off a skull the size of a cart, one stroke at a time.)
Sahar · neutral Don't come any closer. You'll breathe on it.
Sahar · neutral ...You're the challenger. The Lumen one. The one who walks in the glass. Everyone's heard.
Sahar Sahar Ostrand. I keep the Dig, and the Earth Plate, and a well that's falling into itself a rung a week while a man in a palace sells the water underneath it.
Sahar · deadpan You'll have read his notice. He has a lovely hand. He should have been a calligrapher. We'd all be happier.
Sahar · neutral One thing, before you go anywhere in Ossaria. Walk the bones, never the sand. Where there's a rib or a road of bone, walk on it. Where there's only sand, don't. The desert keeps everything.
Sahar It just doesn't keep it where you left it.

(Warning 1 of 3 for GO_SINKFIELD.) Trials in 209: Kevin (OS_KEVIN); the Hall of Unearthing board. The fossil revival service opens here (WORLD.md: "Fossil revival at Lumen Fossil Lab (Act II)" is the other site).

Map 204 — the Aquifer Quarter: EV "The Deep-works" → CHOICE :ch6_drillsite (autorun the first time the PC enters 204 after meeting Sahar; V126 == 3 → 4)

(The great well. Terraces of houses round it, caravanserai, washing, goats. On the far side, a Meridian deep-works: a brass derrick over a shaft beside the well, a fence, and a pipe running down into the dark.)
(As you come to the rail, the ground shakes. Under your feet, very deep, something shifts its weight. The water at the bottom of the well slops against the stone.)
SE: a heavy WHUMP from the deep-works. A gout of sand and steam from the shaft. The derrick leans.
(Out of the shaft come Pokémon: three Drilbur and an Excadrill, scrabbling up the shaft's side and out onto the terrace. Each one has a brass collar round its neck with a sunburst on it, and a cable trailing from the collar back down the shaft.)
Meridian Foreman The cores! The CORES are loose! Somebody's cut the collars—
(Grey cowls at the fence. Bark masks with sad faces. Hollow. They're cutting the cables, one by one, and the caravan children of the Quarter are running out to help them, laughing, herding the freed Drilbur away from the shaft toward the Sandgate and the open dunes.)
Bereaved Go on! Go on, you're free, GO!
Caravan Boy This way! This way, little one!
(And then the white-and-gold. A Directorate squad comes down the terrace steps at a run.)
Directorate Sergeant By Mandate of the Accord! Everyone STOP! Those are Meridian assets!
Directorate Sergeant Those children are aiding saboteurs. Take them.
(An officer grabs the caravan boy by the arm. The boy's mother screams from a terrace above. The Excadrill, collar still on, plants itself in front of the children and bares its claws.)
Bereaved (to you, across the terrace) You! The one from the Lowlight! Help us get them into the dunes!
Directorate Sergeant (to you) You! Guest of the Chair! Help us secure the site!

> Help the Hollow get the freed Pokémon into the dunes. (hollow)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch6_drillsite, :hollow)
  BATTLE: MERIDIAN_DIRECTORATE "Sergeant" (Duneholt version; the game's first Directorate battle; Lv per BALANCE for the segment before Gym 5). Field: Desert.
  (WIN:) Directorate Sergeant This is obstruction of the Mandate. You'll be in a report by tonight.
  (The Hollow and the children run the Drilbur out through the Sandgate. The Excadrill goes last, looks back once at the shaft, and digs.)
  Bereaved The red giant thanks you. So do we. ...So does Ochre, the big one. That was her name, before they put a number on her.
  (The sergeant lets the caravan boy go. Nobody's told her what else to do.)
> Help the Directorate secure the site. (directorate)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch6_drillsite, :directorate)
  BATTLE: HOLLOW_GRUNT_M "Bereaved" (Duneholt version). Field: Desert.
  (WIN:) (The Hollow scatter over the terrace walls. Meridian handlers loop new cables onto the Drilbur's collars and lead them back to the shaft. The Excadrill fights all the way down.)
  Directorate Sergeant Good work. Very good work. The Directorate remembers its friends.
  (Received: MANDATE PASS.) ITEM DESCRIPTION: "A brass card with the Directorate's seal. 'The bearer has assisted the Mandate. Extend every courtesy.' It's warm, as if somebody's still holding it."
  (They take the caravan boy anyway. His mother doesn't scream this time. She just watches you.)
> Shout for Sahar. (sanctuary)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch6_drillsite, :sanctuary)
  (You shout her name. It goes up the terraces and round the well and comes back to you three times.)
  MOVE: Sahar comes down the terrace stairs, not fast, with sand on her sleeves and her spectacles pushed up on her head. Everyone stops.
  Sahar · angry Sergeant. Let go of that child.
  Directorate Sergeant Warden, with respect, the Mandate—
  Sahar · neutral The Mandate is two weeks old. The Warden's right of sanctuary is two hundred and ninety-six years old. "Any child of the city who stands within sight of its Plate stands under its Warden." The Earth Plate is in that well. That child is in sight of it.
  Sahar Under the Concordance, Sergeant. Read it sometime. It's short. I'll lend you mine.
  (The sergeant looks at her squad. Her squad looks at the well. She lets go.)
  Directorate Sergeant This goes in my report.
  Sahar · deadpan Spell my name right. It has an H in it nobody hears.
  Sahar · sad *(lower)* That law covers children, Sergeant. It doesn't cover them. *(the Drilbur)* I can't stop you. I'm sorry.
  (The Hollow are gone. The sergeant's handlers loop cables onto the nearest collars before the rest can bolt: half the Drilbur go back down the shaft. The Excadrill, Ochre, fights all the way down and doesn't come back up. The rest scatter into the dunes. The children stay where they are, very close to Sahar.)
  Sahar · angry *(to no one, after)* Two hundred and ninety-six years, and the law still thinks a digger is a shovel.
(All:)
Sahar · sad *(looking down the well)* It dropped again. Did you feel it? A whole rung, just now.
Sahar They put collars on diggers and sent them down to drink my well for a man in Lumen. And now the Hollow have let them go, and the shaft's open, and the water will run down it like a drain.
Sahar · neutral Come to the Dig when you're ready. I'd like to hit something that's allowed to hit back.
V126 = 4.

(Long-term: :directorate costs Sahar's Consent in Act V; :hollow brings Directorate ambushes in Ch7; :sanctuary gives Accord Standing but costs the Drilbur: half go back down the shaft with Ochre, so it is no free third option (Gemini review 2026-11-21). The Mandate Pass opens checkpoints later.)

Map 214 — the Sinkwells (slum) and the Elector's Palace (205–207, closed)

Sinkwells Woman Our well went in last month. The whole street went down two feet in a night. We're the lucky ones; we're still above it.
Water-Carrier Something in the Sinkfield's been taking our Pokémon off the carrying-sledges. Something flat. It grins. (Trials, Ch7: OS_SINKFIELD.)
PALACE GATE (205): Palace Guard His Excellency is not receiving. His Excellency is in Lumen, receiving.
MURAL GALLERY DOOR (207): CLOSED FOR RESTORATION BY ORDER OF HIS EXCELLENCY. (The door is new. The lock is newer.)
NECROPOLIS OF THE ELECTORS (208): Rock-cut tombs in the canyon wall. The road through them goes out to the Marrow Road and the Ossuary. Tomb-Keeper The Electors are buried facing the dunes. So they can see who's coming. Lately they've seen a lot of drill-heads.

Maps 210–213 — the Dig (Gym 5; GYM_PUZZLES Gym 5)

Sahar'S Aide Everyone tries the door. The door's painted on. The way in is down.
Gym Guide The Dig: Ground-types on the Desert field. Water, Grass and Ice dig in. Electric doesn't, ever, at all.
Gym Guide Sun hardens and shade sinks. The mirrors pick which lanes are in the sun. Falling isn't failing in here. Sahar says falling's how you find the second floor.

213 — the Warden Arena: Sahar

(The arena at the bottom of the dig: a pit of sand under a shaft of sunlight, the walls lined with labelled bones. Sahar stands in the light with a Claydol drifting at her shoulder. She coughs, once, into her sleeve.)
[if :ch6_drillsite == :sanctuary]
  Sahar · neutral You shouted my name across the well. Nobody's shouted my name since I was a girl. It was very loud. Thank you.
[if :ch6_drillsite == :hollow]
  Sahar · neutral You let the Hollow take Meridian's diggers into my dunes. I've been told to be angry about it. I'm working on it.
[if :ch6_drillsite == :directorate]
  Sahar · neutral You helped them put the collars back on. I saw. I'm not going to say anything about it. The sand will.
(All:)
Sahar · neutral The desert keeps everything. It just doesn't keep it where you left it.
Sahar · deadpan Patience is a Ground-type's whole art. I'm fifty-eight and I have a cough. Let's see who runs out first.
Script: Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_SAHAR), double: false)     # LEADER_SAHAR, :DESERT, cap 31, single
(When her ace enters:) Sahar · neutral Effigy. We've dug up older things than this one.
(LOSE: whiteout. Sahar on retry: "Again. Good. The second dig always finds more.")
(WIN:)

(Received: the SANDGLASS BADGE.)

Map 620 — The Marrow Road: EV "The Door in the Skull" (autorun the first time past the dig terraces after Gym 5; V126 == 5 → 6)

ROAD SIGN: THE MARROW ROAD — Ossaria, the deep desert. ← Duneholt (the Necropolis) · → the Kneeling Stones. Walk the bones.
(Deep desert. Dig terraces cut into the dune faces. At the end of the terraces a skull lies half out of the sand, a skull the size of a house, and in the last night's dune-shift the sand has slid off its brow and uncovered a doorway carved into the bone: a square of dark with a lintel of glyphs.)
(Sahar is already there, with two diggers and a lamp. She's staring at the door. She has gone very pale.)
Sahar · shocked ...
Sahar · sad I know this door.
Sahar AF 281. I was thirty-nine. My team took four months and a Claydol to open it. Nine of us. I was so proud I couldn't sleep.
Sahar · neutral I made rubbings. I wrote a report. I sent it to the Sovereign, because that's what you do when you find something that changes the history of the world. You tell the Accord.
Sahar · sad He came himself. Valen. He walked through it with a lamp, all the way to the end, alone. And when he came out he said, "Seal it, Sahar. For the realm."
Sahar So we sealed it. I burned the rubbings. I told my team we'd found a collapsed granary. Two of them still don't speak to me.
Sahar · neutral I buried the truth once because I was told to. The sand has dug it up.
Sahar · deadpan I'd rather not argue with sand twice.
Sahar Walk the bones in there, the way I told you. The floor's older than the rules about floors. Come on.
V126 = 6.

(Warning 2 of 3: "Walk the bones".)

Maps 624/625 — The Ossuary of Dunes (Unown ruins; Strength boulders; puzzles per the puzzle engineer)

(Inside the skull: a hall cut into bone and sandstone, running down. Strength boulders choke the side passages. In the walls, Unown drift like fish in a tank, in and out of the stone.)
FIELD NOTES pop-up: "THE OSSUARY OF DUNES — CAVE. Unown in the walls. They aren't hiding. They're the words." (Larch, in the margin: "Copy everything. Twice.")
Sahar The Unown are the inscription. They move. That's why nobody could read it, before. You have to wait for the sentence to come round.

The four murals (one inspect event each, in the order the hall reaches them; Sahar comments on each)

MURAL 1: A king in gold, on a throne under a sun, with his arms raised. Below him, his city: towers and domes and a harbour full of ships. His face has been scratched out, very carefully, by someone with a chisel and a lot of time.
Sahar · neutral A golden king. There's only one golden king in the old songs. Nobody sings that verse any more.

MURAL 2: Two titans tearing at the land: one red, rising out of the earth with fire in its back; one blue, rising out of the sea with the tide in its arms. Between them, the king's armies, very small, holding chains.
Sahar · neutral The Year of Two Weathers. The song says the sky and the earth went to war. This says somebody started it.
(Sahar steps closer and traces the coastline behind the two titans with one finger, very slowly.)
Sahar · sad That's our western dunes. Before the Dry Tide was dry. The sea came that far once.

MURAL 3: A great beast with a ring of eighteen lights round its body, radiant, enormous, and round it a chain: eighteen golden locks, one on each light. The king's tiny figure holds the end of the chain.
Sahar · shocked ...Eighteen locks. One for each.
Sahar He didn't pray to it. He tried to lock it up.

MURAL 4: The beast breaking apart. The eighteen lights falling out of it like rain, each one a different colour. Under them, the golden city tipping into the sea, towers first.
Sahar · neutral And the lights fell. Eighteen of them. Onto all of us.
Sahar · sad And the city went into the sea, and three hundred years later we built Zenith on its roof and called it progress.

(Sahar takes a sheet of paper and a block of red wax from her satchel and rubs the third mural, the chain, very fast, with her mouth set.)
(Received: DUNEHOLT RUBBING.) ITEM DESCRIPTION: "A wax rubbing of a chain of eighteen locks round a beast of eighteen lights. Signed in the corner, small: S.O., AF 300. And under it, smaller: AF 281."
Sahar · neutral I made two. Keep yours. I burned the first one I ever made; I'm not burning a second.

Map 620 — the Ossuary's mouth: comedy scene Ch6, "Lecture, Archaeological" (adapted), then K3

15_COMEDY's version has Kestrel mention a pit bracket, which is Ch9; the lines below keep the beat (Sahar's deadpan, Kestrel's smug ambush) and fix the timeline.

(Outside, in the evening light. Sahar is looking at the inner seal-stone you came out past, now lying flat on the bone floor.)
Sahar · neutral The seal on that inner door was three hundred years old.
Sahar · neutral It took a team of nine and a Claydol four months to shift it in AF 281.
Sahar · deadpan You leaned on it.
> It was loose.
  Sahar · deadpan It was not loose. Things are not "loose" around you. Things give up.
> I was tired.
  Sahar · deadpan You were tired, and a three-hundred-year-old seal fell over. I'll put that in the report. "The challenger was tired."
> ...
  Sahar · deadpan Don't do the silence at me. I'm an archaeologist. I've been stared at by better skulls than you.
(A voice from the top of the skull.)
Kestrel · smug Told you. Things give up around them. Rivers. Plates. Me. Twice.
Sahar · shocked ...Twice?
Kestrel · deadpan Don't.

EV "Kestrel K3"

MOVE: Kestrel drops down off the skull's brow onto the sand in front of you. He's thinner. The black coat is dusty to the knee. Round his neck, under the coat, something black and lace.
Kestrel · neutral I saw them. Over your shoulder. The king and the chain. I was in there before you, in the dark. I couldn't read it till you brought the lamp.
Kestrel I left the lighthouse the night of the Lowlight and I've been on the Hollow's trail ever since. They've got a cell out here. They came through Duneholt last week asking about old doors.
Kestrel · angry And everywhere I go there's you. In front of me. Getting there first. Leaning on things.
Kestrel · neutral Fight me. I need to know if I'm getting closer.
Script: Prismfall.rival_battle(:RIVAL_KESTREL, "Kestrel", 3)     # K3; version 30 + starter slot; field :DESERT (620)
(When Honedge's line enters, now a Doublade:) Kestrel · neutral Both blades, Morwen. Both.
(LOSE: whiteout to the Duneholt Pokémon Center. Kestrel on retry: "Again. I'm not done being right.")
(WIN:)
Kestrel · shocked ...
Kestrel · sad No. Not closer.
(He sits down on a rib of bone with his back to the skull. After a while he takes the lace out from under his coat: a black veil, with a ghost-lantern stitched in silver at the hem.)
Kestrel · neutral Gran's trunk. It was hers. Her Warden's veil. Gran kept it in a trunk that wasn't even locked, for six years, and never said.
Kestrel · angry Everyone keeps telling me to let it go. My mother had a seat, and a Plate, and a city that loved her. Then one night she had nothing. Let WHAT go?
Kestrel They say she died in exile. Of the wilting. They sent a box. Nobody saw a body. Nobody in Gravenmoor will say where she's buried.
Kestrel · neutral And now there's a man in a mask who talks like her, and the whole realm's saying it. Every inn from here to Ebbmouth. The Mourner's Morwen Vane. She didn't die. She was made to disappear, and she came back.
Kestrel · sad She wasn't killed by the Bleed. She was made to disappear.

CHOICE :ch6_kestrel_rumor

Chapter 6 close — the Duneholt Pokémon Center (201) or the Marrow Road, after K3 (V126 == 8 → 9)

(A Gale Post courier in goggles, out of breath, sand to the eyebrows.)
Gale Post Courier [Player]? Thought so. You're the only one in Ossaria nobody can describe. Letter. It's been chasing you since Lumen.
(The letter, in green ink, a little smudged:)
"[Player],
I found a way down! There was a ferryman on the Leach and he knew Dr Mott, and now I'm in Mirefen and it's BLUE at night, the whole marsh glows, and the noodles are the best I've ever had and Dr Mott says they'll kill me.
I'm helping him with his seed-medicine. His ward is very quiet. I'll tell you about it when you come. I don't want to write it.
Uncle Rowan wrote. He burned his hand on the kettle, he says, the same night as the Lowlight. His right hand, all across the palm. He's made tea every morning for forty years.
He's been "away on Warden business" every time something happens. Every time. I counted.
I'm being silly. I know I'm being silly.
Come to Mirefen? Bring snacks.
— Juno"
QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Earn the sixth badge in Mirefen, down the Leach Road into Nadir.

Items owner: MANDATE PASS, DUNEHOLT RUBBING (Key Items). Badge name: the Sandglass Badge (creator, 2026-11-21).

Script: Chapter 7 — "The Quiet Ward" (the Leach Road, Mirefen, Gym 6; J2)

Final playable script for Chapter 7. It covers the Leach Road (620 the Marrow Road's east end, 632 the Kneeling Stones, 621 the Leach Canyons with 630 Charwell, 634 Wormwood Lea, 633 the Gutterfall) down into Nadir, then Mirefen (220–223; the Sweet Market), the Weeping Fen 648 (Wick), and the Infirmary gym (230–233, Gym 6). None of these maps is built; the list at the end is what to build from. Follows story/25_SCRIPT_CH6.md; conventions of story/20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md. Sources: 05_ACT_II Ch7, 03_CAST (Corvin, Wenlow, Juno, Wick, Sable), 09_MYSTERIES (#2, #19, #20, #21, #26), NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch7_ledger, GO_SWEET_TOOTH), 15_COMEDY (Ch7 "Invoice"; running gag 7; the Nadir bits), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 6, TRIALS_QUESTS (the Gutter Book, Ch7), CAMEOS (Venam), BALANCE (J2, Corvin), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md (proposal B, approved by the creator 2026-11-21). The Ward Night is canon (CHAPTER_BEATS proposal B, approved by the creator 2026-11-21). It replaces 05_ACT_II's old roof scene, where Sable's broadcast was only a cliffhanger.

Conventions

As in the earlier scripts. Portrait cast here: Juno, Corvin, Wenlow, Wick, Sable (on screen), Mother Gutter (GUTTER, one line). Plain: Noct and the Octave, Six-Fingers Ottoline, Venam (cameo), the Ward's patients, the Sweetrot vendors, every townsperson and trainer. Events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_CORVIN), double: true). Counter: V127 CH7_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 east on the Marrow Road · 1 down the Gutterfall (the first descent into Nadir) · 2 the Infirmary and the Ward (Corvin, Wenlow, the patients by name) · 3 J2 and the ledger (S118) · 4 Wick at the Weeping Fen (S119) · 5 Gym 6 won · 6 the Ward Night · 7 chapter closed (V102 = 8). Sweetrot counter: V128 SWEETROT_TAKEN (0–3). Every vendor offer adds 1 when accepted; the third acceptance is GO_SWEET_TOOTH.

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. J2 and the ledger. Juno, alphabetising Corvin's ledgers, finds "R.A. — Bleed-burn, right palm and fingers, lightning pattern" on the night of the Shatter. Build-up: her Ch6 letter (the right hand, the kettle, "every time"). :ch7_ledger decides how Ironreach hits her.
  2. The Ward Night. The night of Sable's broadcast, the Hammer cuts the Infirmary's current; the Quiet Ward's Bleed rises into a Veil; the PC carries out Ama, the salt-haired girl Wenlow introduced by name, and under the glass her eyes are moving. Corvin: "They're not dying. They're dreaming." The Hammer becomes the Hollow's enemy on screen, and Wick's "he wants to carry them home" lands as a split. No jokes inside the Ward Night from the moment the lights go out until the dampers are back on (15_COMEDY §1). Wenlow is cheerful all chapter: write every Wenlow line so it hurts on a replay after Ch16.

CHAPTER 7 — "The Quiet Ward"

Map 632 — The Kneeling Stones (Ossaria's crossroads)

ROAD SIGN (the crossroads post): ← DUNEHOLT · ↓ CHARWELL & THE LEACH · → VIGIL (closed: "BY ORDER OF THE EMBALMERS. WE'RE BUSY.").
(Nine standing stones bent forward in a ring, as if they'd all knelt at once to look at something on the ground.)
Caravan Guide They say they knelt when the Prismfall came over. Looked up, saw the sky breaking, and knelt. Stones aren't stupid.

Map 621 — The Leach Canyons (borderland D) and Map 630 — Charwell

ROAD SIGN: THE LEACH CANYONS — ↑ the Kneeling Stones · ↓ Charwell & Wormwood Lea. Don't drink the river. The river's had a drink already.
(Red canyon walls. Down the middle runs the River Leach, and into it, from pipes in the cliff, Lumen's foundry runoff: streaks of blue and silver in the brown water.)
Char-Burner Ossarian bone-char filters Nadir's poison. Burn the bones, pack the char, run the water through. Clean water. For now. The runoff's thicker every month.
CHARWELL (630): a cliff-cave town; Ossarian char-burners and Nadir sump-folk; filter carts on rails.
Sump-Folk Woman Up top they say Nadir's dirty. Up top's where the dirt comes FROM, love. We just live under the tap.

[if :ch6_drillsite == :hollow] EV "Escort" (621, touch strip at the canyon's narrows, once)

(Two Directorate officers step out from behind a filter cart.)
Directorate Officer By Mandate. You're the obstruction from Duneholt. You're to be escorted to the nearest checkpoint for questioning.
Directorate Officer That's not a request. It's not even an escort. It's an arrest with good manners.
BATTLE: MERIDIAN_DIRECTORATE "Officer" ×2 (double; Leach version). Field: per 621.
(WIN:) Directorate Officer ...You'll be in another report.
(They let you through. They don't know what else to do.)

Map 634 — Wormwood Lea (Elowen, east of the Crown)

ROAD SIGN: WORMWOOD LEA — ↑ Charwell · ↓ the Gutterfall (NADIR). The wormwood stills: bitters, tonics, and Mirefen's medicine.
(Water-meadows in strips along the Leach, grey-green with wormwood. Copper stills steam in a row by the ford.)
Still-Keeper Mirefen's doctor buys half our wormwood. The other half goes in drinks that make you forget Mirefen. Same plant. That's medicine.

Map 633 — The Gutterfall: "Down" (the first descent into Nadir; autorun at the lift-cage, V127 == 0 → 1)

(The edge of the Crownland. The Leach goes over it in a blue waterfall into a gulf of air, and beside the fall, from the cliffs above, Zenith's outfall pours in: grey, warm, steaming. A ladder-town of shacks clings to the rock beside the fall.)
Lift-Keeper Down's a copper. Up's a silver. Don't ask why. Everybody asks why.
(The lift-cage rattles down the cliff beside the fall. The light changes as you go. Then the sky goes: you're under the overhang, and above you, instead of sky, there's a ceiling of pipes and girders dripping slag, a city's underside, a city on a lid.)
(The air tastes of pennies.)
Lift-Keeper Welcome to Nadir. Mind the drips. Rebreathers at the bottom, two bones. Don't buy the cheap ones. The cheap ones are just masks.
V127 = 1.

(Stilt-houses over a marsh, joined by walkways. Grey cranes on the roofs. Hollow Ring graffiti on every wall, and beside it, over and over, a painted Ogre in a sad mask: Nadir's folk-saint. Under the walkways the water is brown, and at the edges of the lamplight it glows faintly blue.)
Noodle-Cart Cook Slag-fried noodles! You're new. You look it. Sit. I rate everyone out of ten. Nobody's scored over four.
Noodle-Cart Cook (again) Boy in a black coat came through two days back. Three out of ten. Ate like he was angry at the bowl. Asked about masks.

Child With A Grimer (an Alolan Grimer) Don't be scared of Gloop. Gloop eats the bad bits. That's his job. He's very good at his job.
GRAFFITI (a wall): A grey ring broken at the top, and an Ogre's sad face. Under it, chalked: "HE TALKED. HE DIDN'T STEAL."

Wenlow · neutral This is Mister Garrod. He hums. We don't know the tune. If you know it, tell us; he'd like that.

Map 223 — the Infirmary roof, then the Quiet Ward: EV "The Ward Night" — key event 2

(Autorun the first time the PC returns to the Infirmary after Gym 6; V127 == 5 → 6.)

(Night. The Infirmary roof, over the blue-glowing marsh. Corvin has two tin mugs of bog coffee and a lamp. He has taken the mask off. Without it he looks older and kinder and more tired than anyone you've met.)
Corvin · neutral Sit. It's bog coffee. It tastes exactly like it sounds.
Corvin I haven't slept properly since AF 288. You get used to it. You don't, actually. You get used to saying you've got used to it.
(Down on the walkway, every lamp-screen in Mirefen flickers at once. The picture on all of them: grey static, then a face. A woman, the top half masked, the bottom half smiling.)
Sable · happy *(on every screen in Nadir)* Evening, Nadir!
Sable The Mourner's gone soft. You can tell; he's stopped turning up. He wants to "carry them home". Bless.
Sable · happy The Hammer hasn't gone soft. The Hammer doesn't carry things. The Hammer breaks them, until somebody up there listens.
Sable Cindervault's next. Light for everyone, right? Let's start with you.
(And the Infirmary's lamps go out.)
(Not the screens. Every lamp in the Infirmary, at once. And then a sound from the top floor, from the Quiet Ward: a long, rising chime, like a wet finger on a glass, getting louder.)
Corvin · shocked The dampers.
Corvin · angry The ward's dampers run on Zenith current off the Gutterfall junction. Somebody's CUT the junction—
(Wenlow bursts up the roof ladder, white.)
Wenlow · panic Doctor! Doctor, the ward, the Bleed's coming up off the beds, it's — it's a Veil, Doctor, it's a Veil across the door, I can't get IN—

(The Quiet Ward's doorway. Across it, a shimmer like heat over a road. Behind it, the ward in grey, wrong light, the beds, the patients. The glass on Old Fen's arm is climbing toward his shoulder as you watch. Mister Garrod has stopped humming. The chime fills everything.)
(Corvin puts his hand to the Veil and snatches it back, burned. Juno arrives at a run with a lamp, sees it, and stops.)
Juno · shocked It's the same. It's the Lowlight. It's the—
Corvin · neutral The dampers hold the ward's Bleed down. Without them it goes up like this, and in an hour every patient on that floor is stage four.
Corvin · sad Stage four doesn't come back.
Corvin The stills. Juno. The seed-medicine stills run on peat, not current. If we can get the stills to the damper coils, the medicine might hold them — might—
Juno · neutral I'll do it. I know where the stills are. I've been sorting this building for a week.
MOVE: Juno runs down the stairs with Wenlow.
(Corvin stays at the Veil. He looks at you.)
Corvin · neutral I've heard about you. The Lowlight. You walked in.
Corvin · sad The child nearest the window. Ama. She's the furthest along and she's the smallest. If anyone goes past three tonight, it's her.
Corvin I'm a doctor. I can't ask you to walk into that. So I'm not asking.

(You walk in.)
(Inside, the chime is everywhere. The light is grey and comes from every direction. Your skin doesn't burn. Under your ribs something is very still.)
(Ama's bed by the window. The salt in her hair has spread down onto the pillow and onto her cheek, and it's turning clear, the way the Lowlight turned clear.)
(You lift her. She's too light for nine, except where the salt has taken hold: there she's heavy and cold as stone. Glass and salt crackle under your hands.)
(At the Veil's edge, with Ama in your arms, you look down.)
(Under the clear salt over her eyes, her eyes are moving. Side to side. Fast. The way eyes move when someone's dreaming.)
WAIT 60.
(You carry her out through the Veil.)
Corvin · shocked ...
(He takes her. He puts two fingers to her throat, then lifts the lamp to her face, and holds it there a long time.)
Corvin · sad You saw that. Tell me you saw that.
SE: from below, the clank of iron and a hiss of steam. The chime falters.
Juno · neutral *(from the stairwell, shouting)* The stills are on the coils! It's — it's taking! Is it taking?
(The Veil across the door thins, wavers, and sinks back into the beds like mist going down into grass. The chime stops. In the ward, Mister Garrod starts humming again, the same tune nobody knows.)
(Old Fen's glass has stopped climbing. It's at his shoulder.)
Wenlow · crying Old Fen? Old Fen, can you hear me? ...He winked. Doctor, he WINKED.

(Later. The roof. The coffee is cold. Ama is back in her bed under three blankets, and Wenlow is sitting with her, telling her about the weather up top. Some of it is made up.)
Corvin · neutral Do you know why nobody in my Ward is dead?
Corvin · sad They're not dying. They're dreaming.
Corvin I've watched their eyes move under the glass for twelve years, and I've never said it out loud, because a doctor who says "dreaming" about a stage-three Fixing gets laughed out of the Accord's medical college.
Corvin · neutral You saw it too. So now there's two of us. Two's a study.

Juno · sad *(sitting down on the roof's edge next to you, soot on her face, blossoms singed)* The Hammer did this. Sable did this. On purpose. To a ward full of people who can't run.
Juno · neutral The man in the mask, in Saltmere. He never hurt anyone. He said "let the land grieve". He sounded sad.
Juno · angry She doesn't sound sad. She sounds like she's enjoying it.
Corvin · deadpan That's how you tell them apart, in my experience. The ones who are enjoying it.

Script: Chapter 8 — "The Light Stone" (the Sulfur Road, Cindervault, Gym 7; the Caldera Crisis)

Final playable script for Chapter 8. It covers the Sulfur Road (640 Leechman's Walk, 641 Lake Sallow with 650/651 Scaldwater and the optional 658 Lantern Isle, 652 the Pyre Road), Cindervault (240–249, 254), the Foundry gym (250–253, Gym 7), the Caldera Crisis at the tap under the Slag Ward (new room 255), and the war drums in the caldera square. None of these maps is built yet; the list at the end is what to build. Replaces story/22_SCRIPT_CH8.md (the withdrawn Ring-Day; SPINE Revision 21 moved the ring to Ch14, Bastian, Cragholm). Nothing here gives a Mega Ring or a Mega Stone to the PC. What stays from the old plan is Brann's chestnut slip, the clue the Ring-Day pays off. Follows story/26_SCRIPT_CH7.md; story/27_SCRIPT_CH9.md follows this (its opening reads S120, S121, V110 and :ch8_caldera, :ch8_lightstone). Conventions of story/20_SCRIPT_CH0-2.md. Sources: 05_ACT_II Ch8, 03_CAST (Brann, Sigrun, Quent, Wick, Larch), 09_MYSTERIES (#4, #5, #6, #18), NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch8_caldera, :ch8_lightstone, GO_LET_THEM_LISTEN), 15_COMEDY (Ch8 "The Hug"; Ashkaar's honest shop signs; the afraid-of-heights recruit), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 7, TRIALS_QUESTS (Ashkaar board, Ch8), BALANCE and the trainer notes (Quent v0 at the taps), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md (Ch8), SPINE Revisions 21–25.

Conventions

As in the earlier scripts. Portrait cast here: Larch, Brann, Sigrun, Quent, Wick, Sable (on screen, one line). Plain: the Dominar's envoys (Envoy Haskar and two oath-guards), the Dominar's herald, the Hammer bomber, Hearthguild smiths, Scaldwater's bath-keepers, every townsperson and trainer. Events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_BRANN)). Counter: V129 CH8_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 down Leechman's Walk · 1 Lake Sallow and Scaldwater · 2 the Pyre Road oath · 3 Cindervault and "The Hug" · 4 Hearthguild Hall (the envoys, Sigrun) · 5 Gym 7 won · 6 the Caldera Crisis (S120, V110) · 7 the Light Stone (:ch8_lightstone) · 8 chestnuts (the slip) · 9 the herald (S121, V122 = 1) · 10 chapter closed (V102 = 9). State set here: V110 CINDERVAULT_STATE (0 normal, 1 ashen after :vent, 2 overdrawn after :dampers; :shutdown leaves it 0), S120 CH8_CALDERA_DONE, S121 CH8_WAR_DRUMS, V122 WAR_STATE = 1. Ashkaar's rule: lying to a Dominion guard is a crime. Oath-braziers stand at every gate; a guard asks a question and the PC can answer true or say nothing. There is never a lying option in Ashkaar. (Comedy rides on it: shop signs are painfully honest.)

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. The Caldera Crisis (:ch8_caldera). Meridian's tap under the Slag Ward is overdrawing the Flame Plate's Imprint; the Hammer plants a Splitter on it; Wick's Hollow want to vent it with lake water; Quent wants to fit dampers and keep it running. Three answers, three costs. Build-up: the forges too hot to touch, the honest sign "WATER (BOILING)", Sable's "Cindervault's next" (Ch7). Consequence: V110 for the whole game, Brann's line at the Conclave, the Ashmarch's ash.
  2. The Light Stone and the war drums (:ch8_lightstone). The Dominar's envoys try to take Reshiram's stone in the confusion; Sigrun stops them herself; the PC says who should keep it. Then the herald: Ashkaar closes the eastern passes to Zenith. Build-up: the envoys in Hearthguild Hall, Sigrun's "my father", the oath-braziers. Consequence: Sigrun's Bond, DOMINAR_SWAYED's seed, Brann's Act V Consent, the war's first step (V122). The slip (09 #5/#6): Brann, three cups of mulled cider in, "I reset the Crown's stone myself... it was smaller than it should've been." The shard answers. Larch sees the PC wince. Nobody explains anything. No jokes from the moment the tap alarm sounds until the pressure gauge drops back to the green (15_COMEDY §1). "The Hug" and the shop signs are on arrival, well before.

CHAPTER 8 — "The Light Stone"

Chapter start: V102 = 8, V129 = 0 (Ch7 close: Mirefen's chalked walls; Surf from the ferrymen). Larch travels with the PC this chapter (she left Lumen with the PC in Ch6 and has been "in the Infirmary library, being useful" through Ch7). Juno stays in Mirefen with Corvin until the Conclave.

Map 640 — Leechman's Walk (east out of Nadir, :SWAMP default)

ROAD SIGN: LEECHMAN'S WALK — ← Mirefen & the Sweet Market · → Lake Sallow & the Sulfur Road. Boards only. The boards know where the bottom is. You don't.
(Plank walks on stilts over a black peat-marsh. Lanterns on poles, every tenth one lit. The air smells of eggs and pennies.)
(Larch is waiting on the first platform with her carpet-bag, a fresh notebook and a thermos.)
Larch · neutral There you are. I've borrowed six books from Corvin's library and told him about four of them.
Larch Brann's expecting me. I wrote to say I'd come with you. He wrote back in capitals. That's how he writes. That's also how he talks.
Larch · deadpan He's going to hug you. I'm telling you now so you can make your peace with it.
V129 = 1.
Leech-Gatherer Leeches for the Infirmary. Sixpence a jar. The Doctor says they're medicine. I say they're the only things in Nadir that work for food.
Peat-Cutter (by a stack of black bricks) The Lattice runoff's in the peat now. Burns blue. Pretty. You wouldn't want to cook on it.

Trainers on 640 (trainer designer): leech-gatherers, a Fisher on the stilt-dock, a Hex Maniac who "reads the bubbles". Wild: BALANCE segment 6.

Map 641 — Lake Sallow (borderland E, Surf) and Map 650 — Scaldwater

ROAD SIGN: LAKE SALLOW — Elowen's last water. ↑ Scaldwater (the baths) · → the Pyre Road & Ashkaar. Warm water. Do not drink. Do not boil. It's already boiling.
(A wide green lake that steams. In the shallows, sulfur crusts like yellow lace. Out in the middle, Lantern Isle's one tower, unlit.)
(The first Surf crossing of the game that matters: the road east runs out at the water, and the ferry-stage has a sign: FERRY SUSPENDED (HOT).)
Larch · neutral Two years ago you could swim this in October. Now the fish come up cooked. Something's warming it from underneath.
Larch I'll take the Scaldwater barge round. You go across. Meet me at the bath-house, and don't fall in. You'll come out as soup.
SCALDWATER (650): terraced bath-houses on the north shore; Elowen hot-spring keepers; a Pokémon Center (651).
Bath-Keeper The springs run hotter every week. Used to be you sat in them. Now you lower yourself in on a rope and pray.
Bath-Keeper Cindervault's tap, they say. Up the mountain. Meridian put a pipe in the Flame and now the whole lake's a kettle.
Elowen Pilgrim There's a Hollow woman in the low bath, giving out cool cloths to anyone who walks in from the east. She won't say her name. She smells of the Fen.
(Low bath, V129 == 1: a woman in a grey cowl with the hood down, wringing cloths into a bucket of lake water and cooling them on a slate. One of Wick's faithful from the Weeping Fen.)
Hollow Faithful You're the one Brother Wick talks about. The one the Fen let through.
Hollow Faithful He's gone up to Cindervault. He says the mountain's got a fever, and you don't cure a fever by stoking it. ...He also says hello. He said to say it like that: "hello". He's not good at messages.
V129 = 2 (at the bath-house, with Larch).
Larch · sad Wick. Of course he's gone up. Everyone I ever liked is walking toward that mountain.

Trials hook: "Ashes Home" (Scaldwater, the Ashkaar board, Ch8). Optional: Lantern Isle (658, :BEACH) — the unlit lighthouse; the keeper's logbook (its last entry: "Lake warm. Lamp oil sweating. Will light tomorrow."); a Lapras in the cove that follows the PC's boat to the island and back. No story; atmosphere and items.

ROAD SIGN: THE PYRE ROAD — Ashkaar, the Dragonfire Dominion. ← Lake Sallow (Elowen) · ↑ Cindervault. At the gate, say true or say nothing.
(The land climbs out of the steam onto black basalt. Red lacquer banners on the cliffs. Overhead, too high to hear, a dragon-rider circles.)
(At the oath-gate: a brazier as tall as a door, two guards in red lacquer, and a stone plinth with a bronze hand on it.)
Oath-Guard Hand on the bronze. Say true or say nothing. Are you here to do harm in the Dominion?
> (Hand on the bronze.) No.
  (The bronze is warm. The brazier doesn't change. The guard nods.)

Map 243 — Cindervault, the Caldera Gate: "The Hug" (autorun at the gate, V129 == 3 → 4)

Terrace Smith I can't work. The quench-channels are running at a boil. You can't quench in boiling. A blade wants a shock, not a bath.

Map 244 — Hearthguild Hall: "My Father" (V129 == 4)

(A long hall with a forge at one end and a table made from a single slab of basalt down the middle. On the wall over the forge, behind a grille: a white stone the size of a fist, giving off a light like a cold morning. The Light Stone.)
(In Brann's chair at the head of the table: a lean man in red lacquer with a gold dragon on his collar. Two oath-guards behind him.)
Envoy Haskar Warden. The Dominar's patience is a coal. It glows a long while. It is not endless.
Brann · angry And my answer's a hammer, Haskar. It doesn't glow at all. The Light Stone is the Hearthguild's. It's been the Hearthguild's since before your Dominar's great-grandmother learned to ride.

Envoy Haskar ...No.
Brann · happy There! See! Honesty! Isn't it marvellous!
SE: wingbeats, close, like a sail cracking. Dust comes down from the rafters.

Sigrun · neutral Haskar. Get out of the Warden's chair.

Map 249 — the Slag Ward and Map 255 — the Tap Chamber [NEW]: "Three Doctors"

(The Slag Ward: shacks of slag-brick at the bottom of the caldera, where the city's poor live under the channels' run-off. Families coming up the stairs against you with bundles. A child carrying a Litwick in a jam jar like a lantern.)
(Down the tap's service stair. The Tap Chamber: a round iron room around a pipe the width of a well, going down into rock that glows. A ring of gauges. A heat that pushes on your face. Three groups, and nobody listening to anybody.)
(At the valves: Meridian engineers in scorched white coats around a crate of brass rings, and in the middle of them a man in round smoked spectacles, bouncing on his toes.)

(At the old lava-channel sluices on the far wall: Wick, in his grey cowl with the hood back, and six Hollow faithful hauling a canvas hose that runs up the stair and out toward the lake pipe.)
Wick · neutral Hello. *(It's exactly the way the woman in Scaldwater said it.)*
Wick · sad We open the old channels and run Lake Sallow down them, onto the Imprint. The fever breaks. The mountain sleeps. And the forges go cold for a season, and the ash comes down on the Ashmarch like snow.
Wick It isn't kind. It's only safe.
(And on the pipe itself, halfway up the iron ladder, a figure in a grey cowl and a bark mask with a painted hammer on it, strapping a brass-and-glass device to the pipe's collar. A Splitter. It's ticking.)
Hammer Bomber Stay back! All of you! The Hollow, the Meridian, the lot!
Hammer Bomber They'll cover up a fever. They'll cover up a crack. They can't cover up a mountain. When this goes, every screen in Velmora will show it, and THEN they'll listen.
Wick · angry There are families on the stairs, child.
Hammer Bomber There were families in the Lowlight!

(WIN:)

Hammer Bomber Do it. They'll finally listen.
> (Take the detonator and turn the key.)

  Script: pf_choose(:ch8_caldera, :vent)
