The Light Stone (autorun back at 244, V129 == 6): "Whose Is It"

(Hearthguild Hall, after midnight. The grille over the forge is open. Two oath-guards are lifting the Light Stone out of its cradle in a cloth, and Envoy Haskar is holding the yard door.)
Envoy Haskar The Warden was occupied. The city was in danger. The Stone was safest with—
SE: a Salamence's growl, very close, from the yard.
Sigrun · angry *(in the doorway behind him)* Say true, Haskar.
Envoy Haskar ...The Dominar told me to take it while everyone was looking at the mountain.
Sigrun · neutral Thank you. Put it down.
(The guards put it down on the basalt table. In the dark hall it lights everyone's faces from below, cold and white.)
(Brann comes in, sees it, and sits down heavily on the bench.)
Brann · sad Thirty years it's been on that wall. Nobody touched it. And tonight I'd have let them, if they'd asked nicely. I was carrying a woman's grandmother up four hundred steps.
Sigrun · neutral This won't stop. My father will send another envoy, and another, and one day he'll send a legion. *(to the PC)* You've stood in three kingdoms' business this year. You might as well stand in a fourth.
Sigrun · neutral Say it. Who should keep it?
CHOICE :ch8_lightstone
> The Hearthguild. It's Brann's to keep. (hearthguild)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch8_lightstone, :hearthguild)
  Brann · crying *(very quietly)* Thank you. *(He puts it back in the cradle and closes the grille himself.)*
  Sigrun · neutral Then my father's grudge gets heavier, and Brann carries it. He's strong. *(to Haskar)* Go home and say true.
> Wyrmrest. A Warden's neutral ground. (wyrmrest)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch8_lightstone, :wyrmrest)
  Sigrun · shocked ...Mine?
  Brann · neutral *(slowly)* Hers. Aye. Not the Dominar's. Not mine. A Warden's, with dragons round it. *(he nods)* That's the Concordance done properly. I'm too fond of the thing to have thought of it.
  Sigrun · neutral My father will hate it. He can't argue with it. *(to the PC; something like a smile)* You think like a rider.
  (The choice itself seeds the Ch19 petition: the Dominar respects his daughter's claim more than Brann's, so `:ch8_lightstone == :wyrmrest` makes `:ch19_dominar == :swayed` reachable.)
> The Dominar. It's his people's. (dominar)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch8_lightstone, :dominar)
  (Brann doesn't say anything. He looks at the PC for a long time, and then at the stone, and then at his hands.)
  Brann · sad ...Take it, then, Haskar. Tell him the ferry child said.
  Sigrun · angry *(to the PC, cold)* You've just told a man who wants a war that the war's right. Remember you did.
  Larch · sad *(later, on the steps)* He'll forgive you. He forgives everybody. He won't forget, though. Smiths don't.
(All:)

Map 244 — Hearthguild Hall, later: "Chestnuts" (V129 == 7 → 8; the slip)

(Two in the morning. The Hall's forge, the one that's still lit (or, on :vent, a brazier somebody's carried in). Brann roasting chestnuts in an iron pan. Larch with her boots off. Mulled cider in a jug that has been refilled more than once.)
Brann · happy *(peeling a chestnut with thumbs like spoons)* I'll tell you a thing about chestnuts, ferry child. You've to cut a cross in 'em first. Else they go off like a Voltorb.
Larch · deadpan He told me that in AF 271. And AF 280. And AF 288.
Brann · happy And it's still TRUE!
(He pours. He's three cups in. He looks at the forge for a while, the way people do at two in the morning.)
Brann · neutral Thirty years at this anvil. You know the best thing I ever made? Not a blade. A setting. A little gold setting for a little white stone.
Brann · sad I reset the Crown's stone myself, y'know. After the accident. Ten years back. It was smaller than it should've been.
(The PC's chest goes tight, all at once, as if something under the ribs has been flicked with a fingernail. A single note, too low to hear. Then nothing.)
Larch · neutral *(her eyes on the PC, not on Brann)* ...
Brann · shocked *(catching himself)* Ach. Ach, I'm an old fool. Forget it. Cider talking. Forget it.
Brann · neutral Have a chestnut. Cross on top. *(He doesn't look at either of them for a while.)*
Larch · neutral *(later, alone with the PC, at the door)* You flinched. Just then. When he said "smaller".
> It was nothing.
  Larch · deadpan It's always nothing. I've got a notebook full of nothings. They're starting to rhyme.
> I don't know what it was.
  Larch · sad No. Neither do I. That's the bit I don't like.
> ...
  Larch · neutral All right. Go to bed. I'm going to write something down and then pretend I didn't.
FIELD NOTES: "Brann reset the Crown's stone ten years ago. It was 'smaller than it should've been'. Something in me answered when he said it. I don't know what that means. I'm writing it down so I can't pretend I didn't hear it."

(09 #5 the reset, #6 the cracked Crown: one sentence, no explanation. The ring's payoff is Ch14 (Bastian); the Crown's is Ch15–17. Brann names neither the Legend Plate nor the reset's reason.)

Map 240 — the caldera square: "The Herald" (autorun next morning, V129 == 8 → 9; the cliffhanger)

(Morning. On :vent the square is grey with ash and the smiths are sweeping it into the cold channels. On :dampers and :shutdown it's busy and loud and the forges are going.)
SE: drums. Not the Hearthguild's bells: war-drums, big ones, coming up the Pyre Road.
(A column in red lacquer comes into the square: twelve oath-guards, a standard with the gold dragon of the Dominar, and a herald on a Rapidash who doesn't get off it.)
Dominar'S Herald By the Dominar of Ashkaar, the Dragonfire, Keeper of the Flame and the Oath. Say true, and hear true.
Dominar'S Herald Last night the Sovereign of Zenith put a pipe into the Flame of Ashkaar and near-burned a city of the Dominion to the rock.
[if :ch8_caldera == :shutdown] Dominar'S Herald It was shut by a child from Elowen with their own two hands, while Zenith's soldiers stood in front of the lever. The Dominar has marked it.
[if :ch8_caldera == :dampers] Dominar'S Herald Zenith's engineers have since bound the Flame with brass and call it mended. The Dominar does not.
[if :ch8_caldera == :vent] Dominar'S Herald The Flame was quenched by the Hollow's faithful to save the city, and Cindervault's forges are cold. The Dominar holds Zenith accountable for every one.
Dominar'S Herald Therefore. The Dominar holds Zenith responsible for this assault upon the Flame. From this hour the eastern passes of Ashkaar are closed to Meridian, to its rails, its taps and its soldiers.
Dominar'S Herald Say true: this is not war. *(a pause)* It is the door to it.
(The drums start again. The column turns and goes down toward the Ashmarch. The square is very quiet.)
(Sigrun is on the bell-tower's balcony above the square, in her riding leathers, watching her father's banner go. The PC can see her face from the square. She says nothing at all.)
Brann · sad *(beside the PC)* Well. There it is. I've seen that standard come up that road twice in my life. Both times it took ten years to go home.
Larch · neutral The Sovereign's called the Wardens to Ironreach. A Conclave. Every Warden in the realm in one room.
Brann · neutral Aye. I'll see you there. Sigrun will too, if her father lets her, and he won't, and she'll come anyway.

Script: Chapter 9 — "The Iron Conclave" (the Iron Road, Ironreach, Gym 8; K4; the Conclave; the Mourner unmasked; Interlude II)

Final playable script for Chapter 9, the end of Act II. It covers the Iron Road (660 the Ashmarch, 661 the Ironway, 602 Candle Down, 672 the Long Drop) down into Nadir, then Ironreach (260–263, two new rooms 264/265), the Ironreach Open and K4 in the Iron Pit (263), Kaito's gym (270–275, Gym 8), the Conclave and the attack (263/264/265), and Interlude II at the Heartgarden (294) as Rowan. None of these maps is built; the list at the end is what to build from. Follows story/26_SCRIPT_CH7.md. Chapter 8's script is story/29_SCRIPT_CH8.md (it replaced the withdrawn Ring-Day in 22_SCRIPT_CH8.md); this chapter reads its results for continuity: :ch8_caldera, :ch8_lightstone, V110, S120/S121, Brann's chestnut slip and the Dominar's herald. Sources: 05_ACT_II Ch9 and Interlude II, 03_CAST (Kaito, Kestrel, Juno, Rowan, the Wardens), 09_MYSTERIES (#2, #2a, #4, #12, #16, #17, #27, #29), NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch9_teo_sable, :ch9_rowan_words, GO_PULL_THE_NAIL), 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING (the Ch9 insert), 15_COMEDY (Ch9 "The Bracket"; running gag 3; the pit announcer), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 8, TRIALS_QUESTS (the Gutter Book, Ch9), CAMEOS (Garret), BALANCE and the trainer PBS (K4, Kaito, Sable + Brisk, the Mourner), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md.

Conventions

As in the earlier scripts. Portrait cast here: Larch, Kestrel, Juno, Kaito, Rowan, the Mourner, Sable, Teo, Marisol, Valen, Hollis, Marchetti, Voss, Calla, Brann, Corvin, Dorian, Tamsin, Rook, Sahar, Sigrun, Anja, Odessa, Ilsa, Bastian, Ysolde, Magnus, Nyx, Celestine. Plain: Nell the chalk-girl, the pit announcer, Captain Brisk, the envoys (the Dominar's, Kassan's), the Open's pit-fighters, Six-Fingers Ottoline, Garret (cameo), every townsperson, guard and trainer. Events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_KAITO), double: false): Gym 8 is a single battle (Core GYMS; BALANCE). Kestrel's tag battle is the Sable + Brisk fight, not the gym. Counter: V130 CH9_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 leaving Cindervault · 1 Larch's goodbye on the Ashmarch · 2 down the Long Drop into Ironreach · 3 the Conclave opens (the roll-call) · 4 the Open sign-up ("The Bracket") · 5 K4 won (S122) · 6 Gym 8 won (Fly) · 7 the vote and the attack (Sable + Brisk) · 8 the Mourner unmasked (S124) · 9 :ch9_teo_sable made · 10 the aftermath (Rowan led away; S123) · 11 Valen: "Come to Verdance" · 12 Interlude II done (V101 = 3, V102 = 10).

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. The Mourner unmasked. The Hammer rigs the Fist Plate's reliquary; the Mourner is there to disarm it; the charge goes off; his Trevenant's roots wall off the glass racing at Juno and the chalk-girl Nell, and his mask takes the burst. "...Uncle Rowan?" Build-up: Juno's ledger (Ch7), Rowan's bandaged right hand and bare ring finger at the roll-call, the Mourner's "get BACK". Payoff: the mask in two halves on the floor. Consequence: Rowan in Meridian custody (V113 = 1), Juno's seat (Ch10), Kestrel's "It's not her".
  2. :ch9_teo_sable. Teo pinned and Fixing under the scaffolding; Sable running for the lift with the comm-device. One life against one proof. Build-up: Teo glimpsed in the shafts, Marisol at the roll-call not knowing where he is. Consequence: Teo alive with glassed fingers, or dead reaching for his sister; Kroll's public exposure (Ch13). No jokes from the moment the galleries go dark until Valen leaves the Pit (15_COMEDY §1: Rowan's unmasking). The comedy scene "The Bracket" sits on the sign-up day, well before. Side content: the Open's undercard and the Gutter Book's board close at V130 == 6 (the gym won) until V130 >= 10, so nothing sends the player away between the gym and the vote.

CHAPTER 9 — "The Iron Conclave"

Chapter start: V102 = 9, V130 = 0 (Ch8 close: the Dominar's herald; S121 CH8_WAR_DRUMS on). The PC leaves Cindervault by the west gate.

Map 660 — The Ashmarch: "Eight Years Late" (autorun at the first mile-fort, V130 == 0 → 1)

ROAD SIGN: THE ASHMARCH — Ashkaar. ← the Ironway (to Elowen and Nadir) · → Cindervault. Sweep your boots at the mile-forts. The Legion will.
(The legions' marching road, grey with ash. At the mile-fort a recruiting table: a red banner, a brazier, and a queue of young men and women holding their own swords.)
Legion Recruiter Say true or say nothing. Do you want to fight for the Dominar?
Forge Apprentice ...I want to eat.
Legion Recruiter That's true. Sign here.
(Larch is sitting on the fort's mounting-block with her oilskin buttoned to the chin and a carpet-bag at her feet.)
Larch · neutral There you are. I've been sitting on this block for an hour being looked at by soldiers. I'm told it's an honour.
Larch I'm not coming to Ironreach.
Larch · neutral I've a report to finish. I started it in AF 292. It's eight years late, and every time I look at it there's a new chapter.
Larch Ebbmouth's river. The Lowlight. Brann's caldera. It's all the same chapter, really. I just keep having to write it again with more people in it.
> Where are you going?
  Larch · deadpan Somewhere with a transmitter and a Warden who doesn't do what she's told. I'll write.
> Is it about the Lattice?
  Larch · sad It's about the person who built it. Which is worse, because I can't blame her.
> ...
  Larch · deadpan Yes, I'll miss you too. Don't make it a whole thing.
Larch · neutral Kaito Ren keeps the gym at Ironreach. He was Wardguard. He doesn't talk. You'll get on.
Larch And the Sovereign's called a Conclave there. Every Warden in the realm in one hole in the ground, and a Hammer loose that's already broken one Plate.
Larch · angry So if anything in Ironreach starts to hum, or glow, or go quiet in the wrong way, you will walk AWAY from it. This is Lecture Eleven. I'm delivering it in advance to save postage.
(Received: KELP TEA BAG. "Six.")
Larch · sad Look after Juno. She's going to need somebody who doesn't need anything back.
MOVE: Larch picks up the carpet-bag and walks east toward Cindervault's coaching-yard, not looking back, which is how she does it.
V130 = 1.
QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Earn the eighth badge in Ironreach, down the Long Drop into Nadir.

(Larch's report is the Larch Papers, Ch12. "A transmitter and a Warden who doesn't do what she's told" is Odessa. V115 LARCH_STATUS stays 0 until Ch12.)

Sweeper (at the second mile-fort, with a broom taller than she is) Ash falls every day. We sweep it every night. The Dominar says it's discipline. I say it's ash.
Legion Veteran The passes are shut to Zenith. You'll be the last thing out of Ashkaar that isn't a soldier. Walk fast.

Map 661 — The Ironway (borderland E, :MOUNTAIN)

ROAD SIGN: THE IRONWAY — the Sulfur Reach. ← Candle Down & the Crown Road (Elowen) · → the Ashmarch (Ashkaar). Ore down, money up. Keep off the incline.
(The ore-pass out of the Dominion: rails laid by Nadir, paid for by Ashkaar, down through burnt woods to the Leach ford. At the top, a Truce Post: a stone with two carved hands on it, one Ashkaar's, one Elowen's. Someone has chalked a hammer between them.)

Pit Announcer (from a gantry, through a brass trumpet, to nobody in particular) AND HERE COMES A NEW ARRIVAL OFF THE LONG DROP, FOLKS. FIFTEEN, MAYBE SIXTEEN. GOOD SHOES. IT'S... THE NULL KID! THE NULL KID IS IN IRONREACH!

Chalk-Circle Woman Got an argument? Draw a circle. Settle it. Leave. That's Ironreach. Topside they have courts and it takes three years and nobody's happy.

(He drops the ring into the envelope with the folded testament. Seals it. Writes, under the address: "She's ready. She doesn't know it.")
SE: a Pidgey on the shed roof. The Gale Post's morning collection bell, down in the town.
(He takes the envelope out to the post-box by the Heartgarden gate and holds it over the slot a long time.)
(He posts it.)

THE STAIR (action, last):
(At the head of the stone stair, the sunken grove below: green, ordinary, the Meadow Plate lying in the Bride Tree's roots at the bottom, warm, humming. Anyone could see it from here. Anyone could walk down.)
(Rowan takes the mask out of his satchel. Ash-bark. One white lily, a carved one. He doesn't put it on. He looks at it. Then he folds it into his coat, lily-side in, next to the real one.)
Rowan · neutral One more.
Rowan Then I'll find the other way. I promise.
Rowan · sad *(to the tree)* I promise, love.
(He goes down the terraces toward the gate, and the road, and the Long Drop, and Ironreach.)
(Behind him, in the Bride Tree's branches, where the blossom came off, a new bud is already opening.)
V119 = 0. V130 = 12. V101 STORY_ACT = 3. V102 STORY_CHAPTER = 10.
TITLE CARD: END OF ACT II.
TITLE CARD: III — FAULT LINES

(05_ACT_II Interlude II. Changed from the outline: Rowan packs the mask instead of putting it on, because he walks into the Conclave unmasked as the Grass Warden. Spoilers ahead: this chapter covers late-game twists.

Script: Chapter 10 — "The Seat That Blooms" (the Root Road, Verdance, the Bride Grove, Gym 9; J3)

Final playable script for Chapter 10, the first chapter of Act III. It covers the Act III opener and the Root Road (692 the Tailings, 680 the Rootdeep and its Lift Road, 690 Lanternroot, 681 Prism Falls, 693 the Briarway; optional 684/685 Grudgestone Quarry, 688 Echo Coliseum), the Standing branch (698 the Hollow Sanctuary or 699 the Meridian Black Site), Verdance (280–289, 294–296), the Bride Grove 708 (Juno's trial, Ogerpon, the Loyal Three), the Heartgarden Gym (290–293, 297; Gym 9, J3) and the Royal Chase 682. None of these maps is built; the list at the end is what to build from. Follows story/27_SCRIPT_CH9.md. Sources: 06_ACT_III Ch10, 03_CAST (Juno, Rowan, Valen, Maelis, Caedmon, Tamsin, Wick, Quent, Calla), 09_MYSTERIES (#4, #14, #16, #19, #20, #21, #26), NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch10_null, :ch10_ogre, :ch10_succession_stance, GO_LOYAL), 15_COMEDY (Ch10 "The Royal We"; the Wardens' Circular; the Elowen bits), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 9, TRIALS_QUESTS (EL_GERALD, EL_ROOTWARD_WAKE, EL_EVER_BLOOM, EL_BRIDE_TREE_HEART), CAMEOS (Melia; Venam's Testimony), BALANCE (J3), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md.

Conventions

As in the earlier scripts. Portrait cast here: Juno, Valen, Maelis, Tamsin, Wick, Calla, Quent, Kestrel, Corvin (one line by letter), Celestine (one line). Plain: Prince Caedmon (not in Prismfall::Portrait::CAST), the Meridian delegate, the Thornguard, the press, Bram, the Lowmarsh weavers, Lanternroot's growers, the refugees, Melia (cameo), every townsperson and trainer. Ogerpon and the Loyal Three are Pokémon: staging only, no portraits. Events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_JUNO), double: false): J3 is a single battle (Core GYMS, BALANCE §5; GYM_PUZZLES 293 said double and is corrected). Counter: V131 CH10_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 the Act III opener · 1 the Lift Road branch · 2 Kestrel at the Lift's top station · 3 arrived in Verdance (the bloom) · 4 the testament (Juno named; the ring) · 5 the Bride Tree with Juno · 6 into the Bride Grove · 7 the Loyal Three done (S127) · 8 the Plate accepts Juno (S125; V106 = 2) · 9 Gym 9 won (J3) · 10 Juno's first act, and :ch10_succession_stance · 11 the Royal Chase opened (S126) and the Queen's garden · 12 "Dear Uncle Rowan" (chapter closed; V102 = 11).

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. Juno becomes Warden. Rowan's testament names her; Valen puts his ring in her hand; she walks the Bride Grove behind the PC to the Meadow Plate in the Bride Tree's roots, and the Plate accepts her. Build-up: Ironreach, Verdance drowning without a Warden, the three claimants, "I didn't want this seat". Payoff: the bloom goes quiet under her hand. Consequence: the Greenward, Juno's Act III–IV politics, J4.
  2. The Loyal Three and the truth about the Ogre (:ch10_ogre, GO_LOYAL). The pageant's heroes come for the Plate in Sweetrot-pink collars; the Ogre that has guarded Elin since AF 288 roars at the PC. Build-up: the Ch2 pageant, the Mourner's "poison on their collars", Celestine's Ch3 rhyme, Ch7's peach smell. Consequence: Ogerpon with Juno (Festival), Pecharunt (Ch18). Also: the first explicit "nobody" (:ch10_succession_stance). No jokes inside the Grove from the Veil to the Plate (the comedy scene is "The Royal We" in the Chase, after J3). No side content opens in Verdance between the testament (V131 == 4) and the Plate (V131 == 8): the Rootward and Chase boards wait.

CHAPTER 10 — "The Seat That Blooms"

Chapter start: V101 = 3, V102 = 10, V131 = 0 (Interlude II's end). The PC wakes in the Ironreach Pokémon Center.

Act III opener: every Pokémon Center door (from V101 >= 3)

(The Center's doors have a new frame round them: a brass arch with a scanner plate set into it, and a small screen.)
SE: a soft two-note chime as you walk through.
SCREEN: ◆ FELLOWSHIP PRIORITY GUEST ◆ Welcome back, [Player]. Meridian is glad you're safe.
[if :pro_fellowship != :accept] SCREEN: ◆ PRIORITY GUEST ◆ Welcome back, [Player]. Meridian is glad you're safe.
Nurse (the first time) They put them in every Center last week. Under the Mandate. It's very polite. It says hello to everyone by name. It says hello to me by name. I've never told it my name.

(06_ACT_III's act-opening state: even being watched is courteous. The screen changes in Ch12, V133 >= 7: "SUSPENDED".)

Map 261 — the Ironreach Pokémon Center: "Morning" (autorun on waking, V131 == 0)

(Morning. The Center is quiet. On the bench by the door, a small girl with chalk to the elbows is waiting with her knees pulled up.)
Nell You're awake. Mum said not to wake you. I didn't. I just waited very loudly.
Nell The lady with the flowers. Juno. She went up with the Sovereign's people in the night. In the Sovereign's own cage. She didn't want to go and she didn't want to stay.
Nell She left you this.
(A folded page, green ink, the handwriting going downhill at the end of every line.)
"[Player] — They're taking me to Verdance. The Sovereign says I have to be there when they open his letter. I don't know what letter. I don't know anything any more. Come the long way if you want. I'd understand. I'd come the long way. — J."
Nell (holding up her chalk) She saved me. The roots came up and she had her arms round me and I couldn't see anything but flowers. Tell her I've got the neatest S in Ironreach and she can have it.
V131 stays 0 until the Lift Road branch on 680 (0 → 1). QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Go to Verdance. Up the Root Road: the Tailings, the Rootdeep's Lift Road, then the Crown Road west.

Map 692 — The Tailings (:SCRAPYARD)

ROAD SIGN: THE TAILINGS — Nadir. ← Ironreach · → the Rootdeep & the Lift Road. Mind the cones. They move.
(Grey cones of mine-waste outside Ironreach. Kids sledge down them on shovels. A Directorate checkpoint has been put up at the bottom of the biggest cone, which the kids treat as a ramp.)
Sledging Boy They put a barrier at the bottom! It's the best jump in Nadir now!
Directorate Officer It is NOT a jump. ...It's quite a good jump.
NOTICE (on the barrier): "BY MANDATE OF THE ACCORD (CONCLAVE OF AF 300): THE DIRECTORATE OPERATES IN ALL LATTICE TERRITORIES." Under it, chalked: "NOT OURS. — the Hollow". Under that, a hammer, scrubbed half out.

Trials off 692: Grudgestone Quarry (684/685) by the waste cones; the Hollow Sanctuary branch below starts there. Echo Coliseum (688) is off the Tailings' east end.

Map 688 — Echo Coliseum (optional; :BLEED)

FIELD NOTES pop-up: "ECHO COLISEUM — BLEED. An old pit, out past the Tailings. The Fist Plate's burst came down the seams to it and it hasn't stopped ringing. It plays back. (Larch, in the margin, older ink: 'It isn't a recording. Don't argue with it.')"
(An empty fighting pit, rimmed with glass. In the Bleed light, nothing moves. But the air is full of sound: a crowd, very far away, breathing in.)
ECHO (centre of the pit; action):
  (A man's voice, doubled through something in a mask:) "Not now — you don't understand — get back."
  (A crack like a branch breaking.)
  (A girl's voice:) "...Uncle Rowan?"
  (Then it starts again, from the crowd breathing in.)
(At the pit's edge, a glass-flecked Timburr is sitting with its log across its knees, listening, the way a dog listens at a door.)
WILD BATTLE (once): TIMBURR, Bleed-touched, Lv 42 (catchable; the field is Bleed).

(06_ACT_III's Echo Coliseum. Fighting-type: Gym 8 is behind the player, so it's no counter to the next Warden (SPINE Rev 16). The distribution owner may change the species.)

Map 680 — The Rootdeep (borderland F, :CAVE) and the Rootdeep Lift Road

ROAD SIGN: THE ROOTDEEP — where Elowen's roots come through Nadir's roof. ← the Tailings · ↑ the Lift (to Lanternroot & the Crown Road).
(Mine shafts that turn, as you go, into a cathedral of roots: the Gossamer Wood's roots, as thick as towers, coming down through the rock overhead. Ore carts overgrown with moss. Fungus lamps.)
(At the far end, the great freight-lift: a cage the size of a house on four chains, hauling ore up the cliff to Elowen's downs.)
Lift-Hand Up's free today. Up's been free all week. Everybody wants to go up. Nobody wants to come down.

The Lift Road branch (autorun at the lift's foot, V131 == 0 → 1; one of three, by Standing, in this order)

A. [if standing(:MERIDIAN) >= 4] "A Fellowship Privilege" → Map 699, the Meridian Black Site (S172 BLACK_SITE_OPEN)

(A neat young woman in a charcoal suit is waiting by the lift with a clipboard and an umbrella she doesn't need underground.)
Calla · neutral [Player]. Calla Wren, from the Chairman's office. We met at the Landing. You won't remember. Nobody remembers the person holding the scanner.
Calla The Chairman asked me to offer you a tour. One of our research stations is just off the Lift Road. It's a Fellowship privilege. Very few people see it.
Calla · neutral *(a pause that's slightly too long)* You can say no.
> Go with her.
  (Through a maintenance door in the root-wall. Behind it, a steel corridor, white light, and a smell of disinfectant.)
> Not today.
  Calla · neutral Of course. *(She writes something down. She seems relieved.)*
  → the refugee scene (C) plays on the way up instead.

(699. A white room with a glass cradle in the middle, and in the cradle a Pokémon in a heavy iron helmet, bolted shut, its body like something made of three different animals by people who'd never met. Wires run from the cradle to a console. Behind the console, a giggling man in a white coat.)
Quent · smug Oh, it's YOU. The null reading! I've still only got one probe, you know. You broke the other one at the caldera.
Quent This is Project NULL. Well. The first one. It's a Type: Null. Look at the helmet. That's to keep its strength in.
Quent · happy And look what it does when you come in.
(In your bag, the badge case hums. Eight notes, low. The Type: Null's helmet turns toward the sound, slowly, and stays there.)
Quent · smug Just like that. Every time. It's modelled on something, you see. We're not allowed to say what.
Calla · sad *(very quietly, by the door)* Doctor.
Quent · happy Not allowed! I said not allowed. Calla, I'm a model of discretion.
Quent The Chairman says you can take it with you, if you like. A gift. It likes you. Or it likes something about you. It's very hard to tell with the helmet.

CHOICE :ch10_null

> Take the Type: Null. (take)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch10_null, :take)
  (Received: TYPE: NULL, Lv 45.) Switch S180 TYPE_NULL_GIFT = ON.
  (When you lift it out of the cradle, the badge case goes quiet. The Type: Null doesn't.)
  Quent · happy Do write and tell us how it gets on. In detail. We'd love the detail.
> Leave it. (leave)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch10_null, :leave)
  Quent · sad Oh. Well. It'll be here. It's always here.
  (As you go, the helmet turns to follow you, all the way to the door.)
Calla · neutral *(at the lift, alone)* I'm sorry. It isn't a zoo. I don't know what it is.
V131 = 1.

(09 #14: the Type: Null reacts the way the badge case does. Gated by NARRATIVE_KEYS §4.1; takes priority over B. Voss +2 on :take.)

B. [else, if standing(:HOLLOW) >= 4] "The Leaderless" → Grudgestone Quarry 684/685 → Map 698, the Hollow Sanctuary (S171 HOLLOW_SANCTUARY_OPEN)

(A boy in a grey cowl too big for him steps out from behind an ore cart. He has an Alolan Grimer in his arms and a bark mask pushed up on his head.)
Hollow Runner You're the one who walks in. Brother Wick wants you. Not for anything bad. He said to say "not for anything bad" twice. Not for anything bad.
(He leads you back down to the Tailings and into Grudgestone Quarry by a gap in the fence. At the bottom of the quarry's second level, behind a curtain of hanging roots: a cave full of lamps and people. The Hollow, leaderless. Bedrolls. A kettle. Children.)
Wick · sad Sit, child. You've seen the Gazette. Everyone has. He's in their cells, and they've written "terrorist" next to his name in letters a yard high.
Wick He was pulling her wires out. I know. You know. The roots know. The Gazette doesn't print roots.
Wick · neutral I was going to give you this at the end. There isn't going to be an end the way I thought, so you're having it now.
(He takes a fold of old paper out of his sleeve, soft as cloth.)
Wick · neutral The Hymn the Choir sings at every Festival is half a hymn. I was defrocked for reading the other half. This is the verse I could still remember after they took the book.
(Received: HYMN FRAGMENT.) ITEM DESCRIPTION: "...then one of no colour, the eighteen roads walked, / shall carry them home, as the old ones talked — / not chained, not broken, not bought, not crowned: / given back, as a gift is ________. (The last word is torn away.)"
Wick · sad I never found the last word. I used to think it was "kept". It isn't. It doesn't even rhyme. Kept things don't go home.
Wick And this. For whoever holds him. They'll read it before he does. That's all right. It's for them, too.
(Received: WICK'S LETTER.) ITEM DESCRIPTION: "Sealed with candle-wax. 'To the keepers of Rowan Ashby. Be kind to him; he's been kind to everything else.'"
Hollow Woman (at the kettle, a Lowmarsh weaver's shears on her belt) They took Mara at Lumen. Thistle. She'd want somebody to say thank you for the Ward, in Mirefen. So. Thank you.
V131 = 1.

(06_ACT_III's Hollow branch: Wick's verse early. Fixed: the outline had Thistle hand over the letter here, but she was captured at Lumen (Ch5, 24_SCRIPT_CH5.md); the letter is Wick's, and her people speak for her. WICK'S LETTER is delivered to Rowan's gaoler in Ch13. The verse completes in Ch18.)

C. [else] "Up" (the refugees; also plays for A's "Not today")

(The lift-cage comes down empty and goes up full. A family with a cart of furniture lashed down with rope. An old man carrying a birdcage with a Pidove in it. A woman with a baby and a pit-fighter's championship belt over her shoulder, because it's the most valuable thing she owns.)
Refugee Woman They put the scanners on the cage-foot the morning after the Conclave. Hand on the plate, every time. They said it's for our safety.
Refugee Woman My husband's tint came up "Hollow-adjacent". He's never been Hollow anything. He sells noodles.
Old Man With A Pidove Sixty years in Nadir. Never been up. Is it true the sky's blue? My granddaughter says it's blue. I think she's having me on.
V131 = 1.

The Lift's top station: "The Envelope" (touch on arrival at the top, V131 == 1 → 2)

(The top of the cliff. Elowen's downs, wide and green and windy after the Rootdeep, and a stone station-house where the ore is weighed.)
(On the station's bench, a boy in a black coat a size too big. He has an envelope in his hands: thick paper, a gold sunburst pressed into the wax. He's turning it over and over.)
(He sees you. He puts it inside his coat.)
Kestrel · neutral Don't.
Kestrel It's post. People get post.
Kestrel · angry I said don't.
MOVE: Kestrel gets up and walks away east along the edge of the downs, toward the Crown Road, the long way round to Zenith.
V131 = 2.

(The envelope is Voss's: "the full AF 290 file" (K5, Ch12). The PC isn't told. Kestrel's coat pocket has a gold corner showing in his sprite until Ch12, if the art allows.)

Map 690 — Lanternroot (border F's town)

(A town of mushroom farms on terraces at the Lift's top, lit by lamp-moss. Ore comes up, ale and lamp-moss go down.)
Fungus-Grower We grow on the roots. The miners dig past the roots. Every year we argue about it. Every year the roots win, because the roots don't come to the meeting.
Miner'S Wife There's a root in the low field that bleeds when you cut it. Red. Real blood, near as anyone can tell. Nobody's cut it in thirty years. Somebody cut it last week.

(The Rootdeep's secret, "The Root That Bleeds", is a local sidequest hook (WORLD.md, border F); the Trials owner may wire it.)

Map 681 — Prism Falls (:RAINBOW)

ROAD SIGN: PRISM FALLS — Elowen. ← the Crown Road · → the Briarway & Verdance. The rainbow is the Imprint. Do not try to stand at the end of it. People try.
(A waterfall coming off the Crownland edge into a gorge, and across the gorge, all day, every day, a rainbow so solid it casts a shadow. The Rainbow Stair climbs beside the falls.)
Painter Twenty years I've painted it. It's never the same rainbow twice. It's always the same colours.
Pilgrim They say Verdance is drowning in flowers. Roses through the cobbles. People wear masks for the pollen. You'd think, a city so sick it's blooming. You'd think that'd be the nice kind of sick.

Map 693 — The Briarway (:FAIRY_TALE)

ROAD SIGN: THE BRIARWAY — the Queen's road. ↓ Prism Falls · ↑ the Kingsgate & Verdance. Do not trim the briar. The briar belongs to Her Majesty.
(The royal road, hedged on both sides with briar clipped flat as walls by gardeners for three hundred years. But the briar's out of hand now: shoots as thick as a wrist across the road, roses the size of plates, the clippers' ladders abandoned in the verge.)
Royal Gardener I clipped this hedge for forty years. Since the Warden went, it grows a yard in a night. I clip it at dusk, and at dawn the yard's back and it's brought a friend.
Thornguard (at a royal milestone, in thorn-green armour) The Heartgarden's under the Queen's protection, traveller. Pending the succession. You'll want a pollen mask.

The gardeners' door in the hedge (WORLD.md's secret) opens onto the Royal Chase's back fence after S126.

Map 284 — the Kingsgate Barbican: arrival (autorun, V131 == 2 → 3)

Map 294 — the Heartgarden: "Three Claimants" → the testament (autorun at the head of the Heartgarden stair, V131 == 3 → 4)

(The Heartgarden: Verdance's walled garden on the hill's shoulder, under the castle. Five days ago it was ordinary-beautiful. Now it is a jungle of blossom, roses as tall as men, and in the centre, at the head of a stone stair going down into a sunken grove, the Bride Tree: a tree in the shape of a woman, arms raised, head back, in blossom from root to crown.)
(The sunken grove at the stair's foot is gone under bloom so thick it's black. Across the stairhead, a shimmer like heat over a road. A Veil.)
(On the steps of the Heartgarden's little chapel, a scene like a painting: in white, the Sovereign, with a sealed envelope. On his left, the Thornguard in a line, and at their head an ancient woman in a gown of thorn-green and a crown of briar, leaning on a cane topped with a silver rose. On his right, a smiling man in Elowen's colours, and beside him a woman in a Meridian sunburst pin. And in front of them all, on the bottom step, alone, Juno, in her wreath and veil, with her gardening gloves twisted in her hands.)
Maelis · neutral The Meadow Plate lies on Crown soil, Sovereign. It has done since my great-great-grandmother planted this garden. A Warden kept it for the Crown. There is no Warden. So the Crown will keep it.
Meridian Delegate With respect, Majesty, the Plate is overflowing. Meridian can offer temporary custody, for public safety. Our dampers held the Quiet Ward through worse. We'd ask nothing but the right to keep the city breathing.

Maelis · deadpan Caedmon, you've called everything Meridian offers generous since you were twelve. It's how I know what you're for.

The path (DUNGEON_PUZZLES: a "safe path" puzzle; the puzzle engineer owns the layout)

Intent: the bloom parts round the PC as they walk, and where they've walked, the petals lie flat and pale and the Veil thins to nothing: a corridor of quiet. It closes again behind them after a set number of steps unless it reaches a root-node (six of them, glowing faintly in the bloom), which pins it open. The PC has to walk a route from the stair to the Plate through all the root-nodes needed, then go back to the stair for Juno, who follows the quiet corridor step for step as a follower event. Bleed-maddened Grass Pokémon (Bramblin, Shiinotic, Bellossom) calm near the PC and wander off; a few that don't are wild battles. Verify a unique shortest route with the puzzle BFS.

ROOT-NODE (each, on reaching it): The root under your feet is warm. The bloom round it lies down, the way grass lies down for wind. It stays down.
(Halfway down, on the third node, the bloom ahead is torn, trampled, broken in a wide circle round the Bride Tree's deepest roots. In the middle of the circle, something is standing in the dark.)

"The Ogre" (the root-hollow under the Bride Tree; touch, once)

(A Pokémon, small and fierce, in a mask carved out of bark: a face with a scowl and two horns. It has a club made of a branch. It stands between you and the roots, where a warm green light pulses under the soil. The Meadow Plate.)
(Round it, the bloom is broken in a ring. Nothing grows inside the ring. It's been standing here so long it's worn a circle.)
(It sees you, and it roars.)
SE: Ogerpon's cry.
(It doesn't charge. It plants the club and stays exactly where it is.)
FIELD NOTES pop-up: "The Ogre in the Mask. I've seen that mask. On every Hollow cowl in Nadir. On the shrine at Briarwick. It's been here the whole time. It's been guarding her."
(You come no closer. After a long time, it lowers the club an inch.)

Meridian Delegate I'm sorry?
Juno · neutral I've been to Mirefen, where the Lattice runoff makes the marsh glow. I've been to Lumen, where it cracked the Plate. I've been to Briarwick, where it fed the Glasswood. I'm fifteen and I've seen three.
Juno · angry Verdance doesn't need a Lattice to stop it drowning. It needed a Warden. It's got one. No, thank you.
(The delegate closes the folder. Prince Caedmon smiles at her, and at the delegate, and at his mother, warmly, at all of them.)
Juno · neutral And Majesty. Your Thornguard are standing in my garden.
Maelis · neutral Our garden, child. The Heartgarden is on Crown soil.
Juno · neutral Then your soil's in my garden. Please take your men off it. They're standing on the tulips.
(A very long pause. The whole Heartgarden waits.)
Maelis · smug *(and the Queen laughs, a dry little sound like a seed-pod)* Thornguard. Off the tulips.
(The Thornguard file out of the gate.)
Maelis · neutral Little gardener. We'll see how long you bloom.
MOVE: the Queen goes down the hill on her cane, very slowly, with her son at her elbow. She doesn't lean on him.

CHOICE :ch10_succession_stance (the press, on the Heartgarden steps; they've been waiting for you)

Press Clerk You! You're the one from Ironreach. The one who walked into the glass. You were in the grove with her.
Press Clerk Everyone's asking. The Queen says the Plates are the Crown's. Meridian says they're everybody's, under Meridian. The Accord says they're the Wardens'. Who should own the Plates?
> The Wardens. The Accord. (accord)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch10_succession_stance, :accord)
  Press Clerk "Null Witness Backs Sovereign." Good. Solid. Boring. Thank you.
> The kingdoms. The land they're in. (kingdoms)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch10_succession_stance, :kingdoms)
  Press Clerk "Null Witness: Give Them to the Crowns." Oh, the Queen'll like that. The Thane'll like that. The Dominar'll LOVE that.
> Nobody. (nobody)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch10_succession_stance, :nobody)
  Press Clerk ...Nobody?
  Press Clerk You mean... nobody should HAVE them? Then who keeps them?
  (You don't answer. The clerk writes for a long time.)
  Press Clerk "Nobody," says the null. Well. That's a headline. I don't know what it means. I don't think I'm supposed to.
  (At the back of the crowd, an old woman in a moth-silk shawl with flowers in her hair is smiling at you as if you've said something she's been waiting a long time to hear. When you look again, she's gone.)
V131 = 10.

Map 682 — the Royal Chase (Safari-style reserve): "The Gates" and the Queen's garden (V131 == 10 → 11)

(The next morning, a royal herald on the Market Terraces, reading from a scroll with a lot of ribbon on it.)
Royal Herald Her Majesty Queen Maelis Thorne, in these troubled times, of Her great love for Her people, throws open to them the Royal Chase, Her Majesty's own hunting reserve, for their recreation and the catching of game. God save the Queen.

Chase Warden Thirty Chase Balls, five hundred steps. Don't feed the Scatterbug. Don't name the Scatterbug. They've all got names already. Every one. It's a whole thing.

The Queen's garden (a gate in the Chase's inner wall, the first time the PC passes it; touch, once)

(A small private garden in the Chase's heart: a sundial, a bench, an old woman alone on it with her crown off in her lap. No Thornguard. Nobody at all.)
Maelis · neutral Sit, child. I don't bite. I used to. My teeth aren't what they were.
Maelis You stood in that grove with her. The null child. Everyone in Velmora's heard of you, and everyone wants you to say something for them. I find I don't. I find I'd like to say something to you.
Maelis · neutral I've sat on the Thorn Throne sixty-one years. I've buried four Sovereigns. Did you know that? Wyndham, and the three before her. Every one of them died tired.
Maelis Every Sovereign since Maren has died tired. They come to the Festival young and strong, and ten years later they're old men at fifty, and nobody asks why, because the Accord says it's the weight of the office.
Maelis · smug It's a very heavy office, apparently. Heavier than mine. I'm eighty-two and I can still climb my own stairs.
Maelis · neutral So ask yourself, little colourless thing, why the Accord needs a new champion so badly this year. And why its Sovereign looks at you the way he did on my chapel steps.
Maelis Then come and tell me what you find out. I'll pay well. I always pay well. It's how I've outlived everyone who didn't.

(Night. The Heartgarden. The flowers closed for the night, the way flowers are supposed to. The Bride Tree in moonlight. In the potting shed, a lamp is lit.)
(Juno is at the shed bench, in her nightdress and her wreath, with a pen. The same bench, though she doesn't know it. A seed-tin on the shelf above her says NOT SEEDS.)

(Where each page lands in the garden, a flower comes up through it. Pale, white, small. By morning there will be a little path of them from the shed door into the dark.)

Script: Chapter 11 — "The Thaw" (the Hart Road, Rimeholt, Gym 10, the Thaw and Kyogre; the war; the Ebbmouth Strike; the Mast Road)

Final playable script for Chapter 11, the second chapter of Act III. It covers the Hart Road (700 the Hart's Run, 701 the Hoarwood, 710/711 Snowbriar, optional 703 the Gossamer Heartwood, 704/705 Frostfang Pass, 712 the Whalebone Road), Rimeholt (300–314: the Thane's Harbour, the Icewall Gate, the Sled Market, Whalebone Keep, Net Row and the Sinking Quarter), the Lake Hall (Gym 10, 310–313, 315–316), the Thaw and Kyogre, the court in the Thane's Seat (307), the detour south to Ebbmouth (160, 167; optional 723), and the Mast Road out (720 the Thane's Sled-Road, 721 the Mast Glacier, 730/731 Anchorhold; optional 728 Stillwater). None of these maps is built; the list at the end is what to build from. Follows story/28_SCRIPT_CH10.md; story/31_SCRIPT_CH12.md ("Dead Letters") follows this (its opening reads S128, V107, V122 = 2 and :ch11_anja). Sources: 06_ACT_III Ch11, 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING (the Ch11 insert; War 1 :war_warning), 03_CAST (Anja, Eirik, Juno, Marisol, Teo, Voss), 09_MYSTERIES (#21 the sleepers dream; #22 Kyogre and the Sleeping Whale), NARRATIVE_KEYS (:war_warning, :ch11_anja, :ch11_strike, GO_WEATHER, GO_THIN_ICE, JUNO_ESTRANGED, ANJA_EXPOSED), 15_COMEDY (Ch11 "Toes"; the Isenmar bits; the Wardens' Circular), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 10, DUNGEON_PUZZLES (the Ice Vault ties), BOSSES (:KYOGRE_ISENMAR, KYOGRE_WEATHER), TRIALS_QUESTS and WALKTHROUGH Ch11 (the Tally quests), CAMEOS #5 (Alexandra), design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md.

Conventions

As in the earlier scripts. Portrait cast here: Juno, Anja, Eirik, Marisol, Teo, Voss (on screens only), Valen (one line, by relay), Larch (the banner only, no portrait). Plain: the Meridian technician Pell, the Directorate officers, the strikebreakers and their foreman, the pass-warden Bryn, the Ashkaar rider, Old Torstein, Liv (Anja's granddaughter), the ice-climbers, the ice-fisher, the skalds, the net-menders, Alexandra (cameo), every townsperson and trainer. Kyogre is a Pokémon: staging only. Events call Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_ANJA), double: false): Gym 10 is a single battle. Counter: V132 CH11_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 leaving Verdance · 1 :war_warning made on Frostfang Pass · 2 through Rimeholt's Icewall Gate · 3 "Toes" (Anja meets Juno; the gym opens) · 4 Gym 10 won · 5 the Thaw (S128, V107 = 1; the partner battle) · 6 Kyogre (S129) · 7 :ch11_anja made in the Thane's Seat · 8 the third day: war declared (V122 = 2), the column leaves · 9 the Ebbmouth Strike (S130, V108 = 3) · 10 Anchorhold, "LARCH SPEAKS TONIGHT" (chapter closed; V102 = 12). State set here: S128 CH11_THAW, S129 CH11_KYOGRE_DONE, S130 CH11_EBB_STRIKE, V107 RIMEHOLT_STATE = 1, V108 EBB_STATE = 3, V122 WAR_STATE = 2, S174 DOCTORS_CELL_QUEST (the hook only). Keys: :war_warning, :ch11_anja, :ch11_strike.

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. The Thaw. Rimeholt's heat-towers overdraw (the passes are closed, so they run the local Lattice past its limit), the lake breaks under the lower town, a quarter of the city goes under, and Kyogre wakes. Build-up: the Ch8 manifest ("destination Rimeholt"), the grey ice under the towers, the fishers' holes that don't refreeze, the Sleeping Whale song sung too often, Anja's "When the lake breathes, you run", and Gym 10's cracking tiles. Payoff: the ice going out from under the lamps, the partner battle as the field gives way, the eye under the water. Consequence: V107 for the rest of the game (the Sinking Quarter, the refugees in Ch14, the Ice Vault's meltwater channels), Anja's Act V vote, :war_legend in Ch17–18.
  2. War is declared. Kyogre's Primal rain rolls east for three days and floods the Dominar's forward camps on Ossaria's western dunes. On the third morning every screen in Isenmar carries it: war. Build-up: Ch8's closed passes, Ch9's near-brawl at the Conclave, :war_warning from the top of Frostfang Pass. Payoff: the Thane's host leaving east along the Sled-Road while the evacuation column goes south. Consequence: V122 = 2, Isenmar's refugees in Elowen and Ossaria, the Siege of Skaldfast (Ch15), the war choices. Also: :ch11_anja (expose her, or let her confess), and :ch11_strike at the Ebbmouth picket. No jokes from the first red reading on Pell's console (V132 == 4, at night) to Anja on the hut roof (15_COMEDY §1: the Thaw is joke-free). No side content opens in Rimeholt between Gym 10 (V132 == 4) and the court (V132 == 7): the Tally board, the ice-climbers' wall and Torstein's hole all wait until the morning after.

CHAPTER 11 — "The Thaw"

Chapter start: V101 = 3, V102 = 11, V132 = 0 ("Dear Uncle Rowan" closed Ch10). The PC wakes in the Verdance Pokémon Center (281). Juno's two modes (NARRATIVE_KEYS JUNO_ESTRANGED = bond(:JUNO) <= -5): normally she travels with the PC as a follower (PrismfallMaps Juno follower, leg :hart_road) from 284 to Rimeholt. If estranged, she has gone ahead alone by sled; every Juno line on the road is cut, the "Toes" scene still plays (she is already in Rimeholt), and Anja is the PC's partner in the Thaw. Lines marked [estranged] replace the default.

Map 281 — the Verdance Pokémon Center: "Walking Papers" (autorun on waking, V132 == 0)

(Morning. The Center's window is full of white flowers: the little path from the potting shed reaches all the way across the Heartgarden now, and somebody has put a rope round it so the tourists don't step on it.)
(Juno is at the counter in a travelling coat over her Warden's sash, with a satchel so full it won't close. Her wreath is on top, in a hatbox. She is reading from a sheaf of paper under her breath.)
Juno · panic "—the Greenward bloc believes that sustainable Imprint stewardship is—" no. "—believes in—" no. Hi. Morning. Hi.
Juno · neutral I'm going north. The northern Wardens haven't answered a single letter, so I'm going to stand in their halls till they do. Anja Sorrel first. Rimeholt.
Juno · sad She signed the heat contract. Her whole city runs on Meridian. If the Greenward can't talk to her, it can't talk to anybody.
Juno · happy And your tenth badge is up there. So. Same road. If you want. You don't have to.
(She is already holding the door.)
[estranged] (Juno isn't here. On the counter there's a note in green ink, very short.)
[estranged] "Gone ahead to Rimeholt by the mail-sled. Don't wait for me. — J."
[estranged] Nurse She asked me if you'd slept well. Then she said not to tell you she asked.
V132 stays 0. QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — North up the Hart Road to Rimeholt, Isenmar's capital on the frozen lake.

(Ch10's close set up this exit. The Ogre, if S223, sees them off at the Kingsgate and goes back to the Bride Tree.)

Map 284 — the Kingsgate Barbican (touch, once, on leaving north)

(The Thornguard on the north gate are new: twice as many as yesterday, with a sergeant who checks every pass twice.)
Thornguard Sergeant Isenmar? Hm. Her Majesty's compliments, Warden, and the border's open. For now. The Thane's been asking about grazing rights on our side of the Hart's Run, if he has to "move people". Move what people, I said. He didn't say.
Juno · neutral (outside the gate, quietly) Move people. Why would you need to move people?

(The first seed of the evacuation and the Thornguard border crisis. Cut if estranged; the sergeant says it to the PC alone.)

Map 700 — The Hart's Run (:MEADOW)

Road sign: "THE HART'S RUN. North to the Hoarwood and Isenmar. The Crown's deer have the right of way."

(Wide downs going pale with frost toward the north. Juno walks backwards in front of your lead Pokémon, holding her papers up.)
Juno · happy Right. You're the Thane. Be the Thane. Look kingly.
(Your lead Pokémon looks at her.)
Juno · neutral "Your Majesty. The Greenward bloc proposes that no Plate should be drawn past the point where its land can—" Do you think "drawn" sounds rude? It sounds rude. "—tapped"? "Milked"?
(Your Pokémon sits down.)
Juno · sad That's what the Thane will do as well, isn't it.

(One running gag this chapter: Juno practises on the PC's Pokémon at three spots on the road (700, 710, 712), each speech a little better. Joke-light, before the blow; 15_COMEDY §1 allows it. Cut if estranged.) Trainers (Lv 45–48): a deer-herd (Stantler, Sawsbuck), a Crown huntsman, two hikers. Optional: the deer-herd: "The white stag's been seen up in the Hoarwood. Crown says it's the Queen's. Trappers say it's nobody's. Stag says nothing, which is the most sensible position." (IS_WHITE_STAG starts at 710.)

Map 701 — The Hoarwood (:SNOWY_MOUNTAIN, borderland A2) and Map 710/711 — Snowbriar

(The first snow. Juno stops in the middle of the road and holds her hand out.)
Juno · happy Oh. Oh, it's— I've never— Verdance doesn't— It's COLD. Why didn't anyone tell me it was this cold? You told me. You told me twice. I know.
(The blossoms in her hair close up against the cold, one by one, like hands.)

Snowbriar (the lodge-town in the Hoarwood):

  • The lodge-keeper: "Meridian's heaters? Not up here. We burn wood, like people. The wood doesn't send you a bill with a seal on it." (IS_WHITE_STAG giver.)
  • A sledge-driver back from Rimeholt: "Ice under the harbour's grey as a gull. You can see the fish through it. You shouldn't be able to see the fish through it."
  • The Wardens' Circular at the Center (281's board, here too): Odessa's post: "SKYREACH WEATHER: wind. FORECAST: wind. Mail's late because of the wind." Dorian replies: "(Enter WIND, stage left.)"
  • Juno's second speech (at the lodge fire, to the PC's second Pokémon): "—so the bloc asks only that Isenmar's heat be drawn at a rate the lake can bear." (Your Pokémon nods off.) "That's better, right? It's shorter. Shorter's better."

Map 703 — The Gossamer Heartwood (optional; :SILKWOOD; the Silkwood revisit)

As DUNGEON_PUZZLES "the forest is a loom" (7/10). Flavour only, no story beat. Juno, at the first silk curtain: "This is where you found the Matriarch's glass, isn't it. Everybody in Elowen tells that story wrong. I'd like to hear it right one day."

Map 704/705 — Frostfang Pass: "Those Aren't Caravans" → CHOICE :war_warning (War 1; autorun at the watch-cairn on 705's summit, V132 == 0 → 1)

(The top of the pass. A cairn of black stones with a frozen flag on a pole, and a stone hut beside it with smoke from the chimney. The air is so clear it hurts.)
(North-east, beyond the Mast Glacier's white tongue, the land goes the colour of old bone: the sands. And along the horizon, very small, a line of thin grey threads going straight up. Twenty. Fifty. Too many to count.)
(Over them, high up, a slow ring of black specks, turning and turning, like a wheel of ash.)
Juno · neutral Are those chimneys? There's no town out there. Larch's map says there's no town out there.
Juno · shocked Those aren't caravans, are they.
(The hut door opens. A woman in a pass-warden's furs with a long brass glass under her arm. Bryn, the watch.)
Bryn Cookfires. Four days now. Dragons over them since yesterday. I've counted a hundred and sixty in that ring before the light went.
Bryn That's Ossarian sand, that. Western dunes. Kassan's land. Ashkaar's got no business on it unless somebody let them.
Bryn I sent it down the mountain. They sent back: "Thank you for your diligence. The Thane is aware of all troop movements." He isn't. Nobody is. You're the only two who've looked.

The sprint (309 → 300, the tower platform; a scripted crack-run)

  • The player crosses about 30 tiles of breaking harbour ice from the harbour edge to the fourth tower's platform. It uses Gym 10's own rules: ice slides, and cracked tiles hold once. Here every tile the player leaves cracks behind them, so you can't go back.
  • The route has three choices. Each choice is a family or a Pokémon on a tilting slab: a net-mender with a child, an old man on a sled, and a Lapras calf caught in a net.
  • Reaching one costs a slide or two.
  • Every one reached is carried to the platform: they follow the player and lift up the ladder at the end.
  • Missing one is allowed and isn't punished in keys. Their slab just goes under. The Sinking Quarter quest later counts who made it.
  • There is no fail state: if the player slides into black water, they're pulled out at the last marker ("Roll to the marker!").
  • Puzzle engineer owns the layout. Keep it short: one screen, under a minute.
  • When the player reaches the platform, Juno is already at the top of the ladder, hauling people up. If she is estranged, Anja is there instead.
(The fourth tower's platform: steel, on piles that go down into the dark, into the bedrock. The only thing out here that doesn't move.)
(Everybody who can get here is here. Children in fur hoods lying flat, the way they were taught. Anja is at the ladder, hauling people up by their collars, one after another.)
Anja · neutral (not looking at you) Good. You ran. Now help from here.
(The water at the platform's edge rises again. And this time it doesn't sigh out. It comes up, and up, a hill of black water with the eye in it, and rain starts falling out of a clear sky: warm, heavy, tropical rain, on a frozen sea at midnight.)
(The boss follows at once.)

  (Then the eye closes. The hill of water goes down. The rain stops, here; you can see it going on, out east, a grey wall walking away across the ice.)

BANNER: LARCH SPEAKS TONIGHT.
Gale Post Loader All of it! Every sack! Captain wants us over Skyreach by dark! (He sees you.) You! You're the one with no colour. The Professor's lot. Captain Gale said if you turned up to put you on. She didn't say why. She never says why.

(East, the sands. Isenmar's host strung out along its white road toward Skaldfast, tiny, like ants. And beyond it, the smoke of the Dominar's camps, still rising, fewer than before.)
(The ship turns south. Over Ossaria's dunes. Over Elowen's forest, green going on forever, and somewhere in it, on the border, a column of families, and a girl in a borrowed fur with a sash on.)
(And then, rising over the horizon: the Crownwall. A white ring, miles across, with a city inside it.)

It covers the mail-ship's arrival and the Tetherline (732), the Cloudstair (724–726, Rock Climb), Skyreach (320–326: the Mast Ward, the Center and Mart, the Lower Gantries, the Skybridge Ward, the Gale Post Hall, the Smugglers' Gantry), the Gale Post gym (Gym 11, 330–334), Stormwatch Spire (744–746), Interlude III in Meridian Spire (Voss's office, Lumen), and the road out onto Conductors' Causeway (740). None of these maps is built; the list at the end is what to build from. Follows story/30_SCRIPT_CH11.md; story/32_SCRIPT_CH13.md follows this. Sources: 06_ACT_III Ch12 and Interlude III, 03_CAST (Odessa, Larch, Kestrel, Marchetti, Kroll, Voss, Calla, Morwen), 09_MYSTERIES (#8 the pin, #10 and #16 and #28 the letter to "I.", #12 Sable is Kroll, #14 the badge case, #15 the arena model, #23 the Stormfront Wyrm, #25 the reflection), NARRATIVE_KEYS (:ch12_letter, GO_FINE_PRINT, Odessa's Consent), 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING (the Ch12 insert), 15_COMEDY (Ch12 "Flight Safety"; the first mirror gag; the Wardens' Circular), GYM_PUZZLES Gym 11, MEGA_EVOLUTION §1.2 (Meridian's keystones), BALANCE (K5, Marchetti Ch12, Odessa), WALKTHROUGH Ch12, design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md.

Conventions

As in the earlier scripts. Portrait cast here: Larch, Odessa, Kestrel, Voss, Calla, Marchetti. Juno appears only by Circular. Sable/Kroll does not appear: she is exposed in Ch13, and nothing here may name Kroll on screen. Plain: Pip (the Gale Post courier boy, the gym's hint giver), the mail-ship's loader and captain's mate, the sky-river guides, the Directorate officers, the Mart clerk, the newsreader and the Meridian spokesman, every townsperson and trainer. Odessa's gym battle is a double: Prismfall.gym_battle(pfm_gym(:LEADER_ODESSA), double: true). K5 is Prismfall.rival_battle(:RIVAL_KESTREL, "Kestrel", 5, field: :STORMFRONT). Marchetti is TrainerBattle.start(:MERIDIAN_MARCHETTI, "Helene") (base version; her Ch12 team, Mega Manectric). Counter: V133 CH12_STEP (design/FLAGS.md): 0 aboard the mail-ship · 1 moored on the Tetherline · 2 up the Cloudstair into the Mast Ward (the curfew) · 3 the Gale Post Hall: Larch and Odessa · 4 "Flight Safety" (the skiff drill; the gym opens) · 5 Gym 11 won · 6 the Larch Papers broadcast (S131) · 7 the raid: the bomb, Marchetti, Larch away by skiff, the Fellowship SUSPENDED (S132) · 8 K5 and :ch12_letter (S133, V114 = 2) · 9 Interlude III done (V119 3 → 0) · 10 Conductors' Causeway, the late reflection (chapter closed; V102 = 13). State set here: S131 CH12_LARCH_PAPERS, S132 CH12_GALE_RAID, S133 CH12_K5_DONE, V114 KESTREL_STAGE = 2, V119 INTERLUDE_ACTIVE = 3 then 0. Key: :ch12_letter. Key Items: SPLITTER CASING; MORWEN'S LETTER (if :keep). The Mandate arch at every Pokémon Center reads SUSPENDED from V133 >= 7 (28_SCRIPT_CH10, the Act III opener).

The chapter's key events (design/CHAPTER_BEATS.md)

  1. The Larch Papers. At midnight Larch reads her own AF 292 report to every screen in Velmora: Lattice extraction accelerates the Bleed. "I designed the Lattice. I was wrong." Within the hour a bomb kills the broadcast mid-sentence, and by dawn Meridian's news has her as the bomber. Build-up: Larch's Ch4 confession ("It's my design"), her Ch8 goodbye, Rimeholt's ice, Cindervault's caldera, Lumen's cracked Plate, the "Larch works for Meridian" red herring (resolved here). Payoff: the broadcast, the realm hearing it, the bomb. Consequence: Larch a fugitive in Cragholm (Ch14), the SPLITTER CASING (Ch13's tribunal, Kroll), Odessa's Consent, the Fellowship SUSPENDED.
  2. K5 and the dead letters. Kestrel, in Meridian's sponsor jacket with a Resonance Gauntlet, robs Odessa's dead-letter archive for Voss in exchange for "the full AF 290 file". One letter falls: Morwen's, to "I.". :ch12_letter. Build-up: the envelope at the Lift (Ch10), K3's rumour (Ch6), K4's anger (Ch9). Payoff: the letter's text, the first time the PC reads Morwen's own words. Consequence: Interlude III, K6's opening line, Odessa's and Ysolde's lines, :ch21_reach_kestrel. No jokes from the first red line on Stormwatch's board (V133 == 5, at night) to Larch's skiff clearing the storm wall, and none in Interlude III after Voss steps out. "Flight Safety" plays in the afternoon, before (15_COMEDY §1: a joke before a blow). No side content opens between Gym 11 (V133 == 5) and the archive (V133 == 8).

CHAPTER 12 — "Dead Letters"

Chapter start: V101 = 3, V102 = 12, V133 = 0 (Anchorhold closed Ch11). The PC is aboard the Gale Post mail-ship over the Crownwall.

The mail-ship (a short deck map or cutscene; autorun, V133 == 0 → 1)

(The mail-ship's deck in the late afternoon. Sacks lashed everywhere. A Pelipper asleep on every rail. Ahead, out of the plain north of the Crownwall, a thing like a needle: a spire of masts and gantries a mile high, going straight up into a wall of cloud that never moves. Lightning walks along the inside of the cloud like veins.)
Captain'S Mate Skyreach. And the Stormfront on top of it, the Sky Plate's own weather. Been there since before the Accord. Never rained a drop on the city. Just sits there and thinks.
Captain'S Mate We'll not moor at the top. Directorate's searching every sack at the upper docks since the Thaw. Everything from Isenmar gets opened. Captain says we go in low, on the Tetherline, and you climb.
(Something moves in the storm wall. Very big, very dark, along the lightning, and gone.)
Captain'S Mate (not looking) Don't. Crews have a word for that. The Stormfront Wyrm. You see it, you don't say you saw it, and you buy the next round.
SE: the mooring horn. The ship drops into the shadow of the spire.
V133 = 1.

(09 #23: the Wyrm is Zekrom, the Spire's Dark Stone, wired into Stormwatch's core; Larch's line in the Gale Post Hall is the seed's second half. Freed in Ch16.)

Map 732 — The Tetherline (:STORMFRONT)

(A walkway of iron grating slung under Skyreach's mooring cables, a hundred feet above the plain, swaying. The cables go up into the dark of the spire overhead, thick as trees.)
Loader (handing your bag down) Up the Cloudstair. It's the porters' way. Nobody official's climbed it in years. They'll be looking at the lifts.

Road sign: "THE TETHERLINE. Cable crews only. Do not lean." Trainers (Lv 52–54): cable-crew riggers, a Gale Post courier on a break. The Tetherline's far end is the Cloudstair's foot.

Maps 724–726 — the Cloudstair (:MOUNTAIN; Rock Climb)

The porters' stair up the outside of the spire's rock core: climbing walls (Rock Climb, from Rimeholt), wind-scoured ledges, a cave section (725) through the core, and the summit (726) at the Mast Ward's back door.

  • A porter resting with a sack of mail on his back: "Lifts are for people with nothing to hide. That's nobody, these days."
  • At the summit, a Directorate searchlight sweeps the ledge every few seconds (a timed event; walking into the beam isn't a fail, it sends you back to the last ledge with "A searchlight finds you. You duck back down."). Trainers (Lv 52–55): climbers, a birdkeeper, a porter.

Skyreach (320–326; Zenith's airship spire, :STORMFRONT)

Map 320 — the Mast Ward: arrival (autorun at the Cloudstair's top gate, V133 == 1 → 2)

(Skyreach. A city built up the outside of a needle: platforms bolted to the masts, skybridges strung between them, airships nosed into docking cradles like bees into a comb. Everything creaks. Everything is lit.)
(At dusk, from the highest mast, a searchlight comes on. Then another. Then a dozen, sweeping the bridges.)
SE: a bell, nine strokes.
SCREEN (on every mast): ◆ MANDATE CURFEW IN EFFECT 21:00–06:00 ◆ Remain indoors. The Directorate thanks you for your patience.
(On the nearest bridge, two Directorate officers walk past. Each has a steel band on the wrist, with a bead of cloudy glass set in it.)
V133 = 2. QUEST LOG: "Eighteen Roads" — Find the Gale Post Hall. Odessa Gale's gym is the Post itself.

Townsfolk (320, 321 PC, 322 Mart, 323 Lower Gantries, 324 Skybridge Ward):

  • A dock-hand: "Gale Post flies war mail for both sides now. Isenmar's letters and Ashkaar's, same sack. Captain says mail's mail." (14_WAR_AND_BLESSING, the Ch12 insert.)
  • A Directorate clerk at the lift: "Prism munitions crates for the front? The Post refused them. Refused! The Warden said she doesn't carry things that go bang. We'll see about that."
  • A child on the Skybridge Ward, pointing up at the storm: "My dad says there's a dragon in it. My mum says there's a dragon in everything if you're drunk enough."
  • The Center (321), the Mandate arch: SCREEN: ◆ PRIORITY GUEST ◆ Welcome to Skyreach, [Player]. Curfew begins at 21:00. (From V133 >= 7: ◆ FELLOWSHIP STATUS: SUSPENDED ◆ Please present yourself to a Directorate officer.)
  • The Wardens' Circular at 321: Juno's post, from the Elowen border: "THORNGUARD COUNTED FOUR THOUSAND AND TWELVE. THEY COUNTED THE BABIES TWICE. I MADE THEM. — J.H., WARDEN OF VERDANCE." Dorian replies: "(Applause.)" Anja doesn't reply. (If :ch11_anja == :let_confess, Anja replies: "Twice is right. They're heavy.")

Map 325 — the Gale Post Hall: "Guest of the Post" (autorun on entering, V133 == 2 → 3)

(A hangar-sized sorting hall inside the spire. Pigeonholes up to the roof, rope ladders, letter sacks sliding on overhead rails, Pelipper and Corvisquire coming and going through round doors in the walls like a dovecote. It smells of paper, rain and engine oil.)
(At a sorting table at the far end, in a borrowed Gale Post coat with the sleeves rolled up, a grey-haired woman is sorting letters very fast and very badly.)
Larch · happy [Player]! You found it. Of course you found it. Did you come up the Cloudstair? Don't tell me. I know you did. You've got that look. The rock-dust look.
(A young woman drops down a rope from a pigeonhole twenty feet up and lands on the table. Goggles, a scarf that goes round three times, a scar through one eyebrow.)
Odessa · happy So this is the famous one. No colour on the scanners. You'd make a great smuggler.
Odessa · smug Odessa Gale. I run the Post and the Post runs me. Skyreach's got one law: the wind doesn't care. Everything else is negotiable.
Larch · neutral Odessa's been kind enough to hide me. In plain sight. Nobody looks at a woman sorting mail.
Odessa · neutral She's terrible at it. Three letters to Lumen in the Isenmar hole this morning.

Larch · neutral (lower) Did you see the officers on the bridges? The bands on their wrists?
Larch · neutral Lattice-glass. Meridian can't buy a Warden's ring off the Hearthguild, so it grows its own keystones. A Warden's ring asks a heartstone to open. Theirs pry it open.
Larch · sad If they come for me tonight and Marchetti's dog changes shape on you, don't stand there gawping.
Larch · neutral And the dragon. The crews' dragon in the storm. I've seen the drawings they make of it.
Larch · shocked (very softly) That's impossible. That's the shape of the Spire's core. I signed off on that core. It was a battery.

Larch · neutral I'm going to say something tonight, [Player]. On every screen. Odessa's relays reach every Center in Velmora, and every Center has a screen now, thanks to the Mandate. Meridian built me an audience.
Larch · sad Everything I wrote in AF 292. The report they buried. Rimeholt's in it. Cindervault's in it. The Ebb's in it. Lumen's Plate. I predicted all of it, and then I took their money and I let them bury it.
Larch · neutral And a Lattice technician in Rimeholt sent me something on the ship you came in on. The last hour of Tower Three. Signed "Pell". I don't know who Pell is. I'd like to buy him a drink.
Odessa · neutral Midnight. Stormwatch Spire. The relay crown's at the top of the storm. Get your badge first. If tonight goes how I think it'll go, there won't be a gym tomorrow.
V133 = 3.

(The Ch4 red herring ("Larch works for Meridian") is resolved here: she did, and she's about to say so. Pell's cache is the Ch11 GO_THIN_ICE beat's consequence.)

Map 326 — the Smugglers' Gantry: comedy scene Ch12, "Flight Safety" (touch, the skiff on the gantry, V133 == 3 → 4)

(A narrow gantry sticking out of the spire into empty air. Moored to it, a Gale Post skiff: a wing, a basket and a rope.)
(Odessa is in the basket. Larch is on the gantry, holding the rope with both hands.)
Odessa · happy Drill! If it goes wrong tonight, this is your door. Safety briefing! There's one rope. Hold it.
Larch · panic Where is the rest of the briefing?
Odessa · smug That was the long version.
Larch · angry I have a DOCTORATE in things that should not be airborne and this is all of them!
Odessa · happy Professor, you invented the thing that's eating the country. You don't get to be scared of a kite.
Larch · neutral ...That's fair. I hate that that's fair.
> (Let go of the rope)
Larch · crying LECTURE FOURTEEN STARTS NOW—
(The skiff drops six feet on its tether, bobs, and comes back up. Larch is still holding on. Odessa is laughing so hard she has to sit down in the basket.)
Odessa · happy Six feet! She did six feet! (to you) You heard her. Lecture fourteen. Don't let me forget.
V133 = 4. The Gale Post gym opens.

(15_COMEDY Ch12 "Flight Safety", staged as a drill so the real escape at midnight lands: the joke goes before the blow. The "(Let go of the rope)" option is the PC's only line; it's always offered, and always taken.) Also here: the first mirror gag (15_COMEDY): on the way back in, a puddle on the gantry. The PC's reflection is caught mid-yawn and snaps to attention. Pip, the courier boy, sees it: "Do it again!" (It won't.) (15_COMEDY gives the line to Juno; she's at the Elowen border this chapter, so Pip has it.)

(An open deck on the outside of the spire, in the wind, with the storm wall close enough overhead to hear it hum. Odessa on the far rail with her goggles down.)

Odessa · neutral I've flown letters through three storms and a Bleed. People write things in letters they'd never say. Love. Sorry. Goodbye. I carry them. I don't read them. I don't hand them to a clerk because he said please.

  • A maintenance board on 745: "RELAY CROWN: ALL CHANNELS. CORE: DO NOT OPEN." Underneath, chalked: "IT HUMS WHEN THE STORM DOES."

Map 746 — the Roof: the broadcast (autorun at the relay crown, V133 == 5 → 6)

(The top of the spire. A ring of relay dishes round a little glass booth, and above it, close enough to touch, the underside of the storm: slow, purple, full of light.)
(Inside the booth, Larch at a microphone, in her own coat again, with a stack of paper and her reading glasses on a cord. Odessa at the switchboard.)
Odessa · neutral Every Center. Every mast. Every screen in Velmora. You're live in three. Two.
(She points.)
SCREEN (every screen in the realm; shown here on the booth's monitor and, in quick cuts, on screens the player has seen: the Ebbmouth quay, Rimeholt's Keep gate, Ironreach's Pit, the Verdance Heartgarden where Juno is sleeping on a bench under it, Cindervault's forge hall):
Larch · neutral Good evening. My name is Imelda Larch. Most of you have never heard of me, and every one of you has a light on because of me.
Larch · neutral Twenty-one years ago I designed the Prism Lattice. Eleven cities. I was very proud. In AF 292 I wrote a report for the Fellowship's board. This is it.
(She holds it up. It has a stamp across the front: SUPPRESSED.)
Larch · neutral Page four. Lattice extraction accelerates the Bleed. Every Plate we draw on thins the world around it. I gave them the rate. I gave them the cities that would go first.
Larch · sad Ebbmouth's river. Lumen's Plate. Cindervault's caldera. Rimeholt's lake. In that order. It's in my handwriting. I was right about all of it, and nobody stopped, and I took the money and I let them put this in a drawer.
Larch · neutral (a smaller sheet) This came to me on a mail-ship today, from a technician named Pell. It's the last hour of Rimeholt's Tower Three. The draw at a hundred and fifty-five percent. An override signed in Lumen, not in Rimeholt.
Larch · neutral (another) And these are the heat contracts. Isenmar's and Ashkaar's. Side by side. Same price per—
Larch · sad (she stops herself, looks into the camera) No. You won't read that page. Nobody will. Here's the only line that matters.
Larch · neutral I designed the Lattice. I was wrong. I'm telling you now because nobody else will.

Larch · neutral Section two. The Unimprinted. In AF 290, at Crownhaven, during the—
(A sound under the floor. Not loud. A cough of the building.)
(Then the relay mast below the booth bends like a reed, and the dishes on the north side go up in white light.)

(The monitor shows: ◆ SIGNAL LOST ◆)
(Smoke. Larch on the floor of the booth with her papers everywhere. Odessa already up, dragging her by the coat.)

The raid (autorun, the stair down 746 → 745 → 325)

(Down the stair in the smoke. Below, on every landing, boots. Torches. Directorate grey, coming up.)
(At the 745 landing, in the wreckage of the relay mast's base, something glints in the debris by your foot: a curved shard of dark casing with a blinking dead light on it.)
RECEIVE: SPLITTER CASING. "A fragment of a Splitter's housing. The same make as the one at Lumen's Shatter."
Larch · shocked That's— that's what cracked Lumen's Plate. That's the Hammer's. That's Sable's—
Odessa · neutral Then it's the same hand that did Lumen. Pocket it. Run.

(09 #12: the casing matches Lumen's because the same hand set both: Sable, who is Sabine Kroll of Meridian's Special Accounts. Tonight it makes the bombing look like the Hollow's. At the Ch13 tribunal, with the COMM-DEVICE (IRONREACH_EVIDENCE), it does the opposite. Key Item for Ch13 and Ch14.)

(The Gale Post Hall, 325. Sacks spilled across the floor, Pelipper screaming in the rafters, couriers with their hands up. Directorate officers everywhere. On the sorting-hall catwalk above, a woman in a long grey coat with a steel band at her wrist and a Manectric at her heel.)
Marchetti · neutral Professor Larch. Warden Gale. And our Fellowship guest. Good. Everyone I wanted, in one room.
Marchetti · neutral Nobody is under arrest. You're all under protection. A Hollow bomb has just destroyed public infrastructure, and the Directorate's first duty is your safety.
Larch · angry A Hollow— You did that. Your people did that.
Marchetti · neutral Professor. You'll want to be careful what you say in front of witnesses. It's all being written down.
Odessa · neutral (to the PC, not moving her lips) Skiff. Gantry. Two minutes. Keep her busy.
Marchetti · neutral (coming down the catwalk stair) You're not under arrest. You're under protection. Learn the difference before it's taught to you.

(WIN:)

(Behind her, through the hall's round doors, a skiff drops off the Smugglers' Gantry into the dark: a wing, a basket, a rope, two figures.)
(Larch's voice comes back on the wind, very faint.)
LARCH (off): —LECTURE FOURTEEN—
(The skiff goes up into the storm wall, into the lightning, and doesn't come out.)
Marchetti · angry (for the first time) Get me an airship. Any airship.
(An officer, apologetic.) Director, nothing flies into the Stormfront. Only the Post.

  (You fold it along its old folds and put it in your bag, next to the badge case. The case hums, once, as if it noticed.)
  RECEIVE: MORWEN'S LETTER.
> Send it to Kestrel by Gale Post. (send)
  Script: pf_choose(:ch12_letter, :send)
  (Pip, at the archive door with his eyes very wide, takes it from you in both hands.)
  Pip Kestrel Vane, Meridian Spire, Lumen. That's easy. That's a real address. (He looks at it.) It's been undeliverable for twelve years. Not any more.
  (He puts a Postmark on it himself, carefully, in the corner, and runs.)
> Burn it. (burn)
  > It's the last thing someone wrote. Burn it?
    > Burn it.
      Script: pf_choose(:ch12_letter, :burn)
      (There's a lamp on the archive desk. The paper takes quickly, the way old paper does. The little drawing of three leaves goes last.)
      (Behind you, at the door, Odessa, back from the storm, wet through, with her goggles round her neck. She looks at the ashes.)
      Odessa · sad Dead letters are the last thing some people ever said.

    > No.

(NARRATIVE_KEYS §4.2 :ch12_letter: :send KESTREL+3 YSOLDE+1, and K6 opens "You sent me a letter. Hers."; :burn RES−2 YSOLDE−2, Ysolde's "So you chose not to know. That's a choice too.", and Odessa won't release the Sky Plate in Act V (WARDEN_CONSENT entry 11); :keep leverage or a gift in Ch15. :ch21_reach_kestrel checks != :burn. 09 #10, #16, #28: "I." is Ines, the PC's mother; "the child" is the PC; "keep wilting" means stay abroad and sicken rather than come home. The PC isn't told: a player who remembers Ines's letter from the prologue ("I wanted one of us to have an ordinary life") can put it together. The Ch15 echo confirms it.)

[if :ch12_letter != :burn]
  (Odessa comes in from the roof door, back from the storm, wet through, with her goggles round her neck.)
  Odessa · neutral She's out. Cragholm by now, under a mountain with a lot of miners who owe me favours. She was sick twice over the Mast Glacier and lectured me the whole way. Lecture fourteen. It's about wind shear. It's actually very good.
