Gym 17 — the Storybook Gym (Celestine Aubade) (design only)

  • Puzzle (10/10, about 40 minutes): "she cannot lie, but she can phrase." Everyone in the storybook is truth-bound; every statement is literally true, and the puzzles are about what the statements don't say.
    • 450 Prologue Page: the sign says at least one door leads on; the left door's plaque says the right door leads on. If the plaque were false the sign would be false too, so take the right door.
    • 451 The Red Path (stepping off the path calls the wolf): right, right, then the stone that isn't painted. "The left way is shorter" is true, and it ends at the wolf's den.
    • 452 Midnight Ballroom: reach a stair within 40 steps (60 on Casual) past six looping dancers (touching one costs 3 steps). Only the silver (west) stair leads on, though nobody has ever been seen leaving by it; the intended route is 32 steps. (To be verified by the builder.)
    • 453 The Eight Princesses: beat the eight princess trainers (one Eeveelution each) in any order; their eight true statements locate the Sylveon key in the Glaceon alcove (cold, lit, east).
  • Badge: Badge 17. TM21 Dazzling Gleam. Level cap after: 85.
  • Mastery (optional): the Ninth Door (455): ask the Courtier "Which door would the Knight tell me is the right one?" Reward: Magical Seed ×2, Fairy Feather and a page of the Hymn in Celestine's hand.
  • Gym trainers: 8 princesses, a Lady and a Beauty, Lv 76–79. (Not in PBS yet.)

Chapter 19 — "The Last Gate"

The Truce Road: the Gloamwood (860, :FAIRY_TALE), the Thornwar Marches (861) with Thornwatch (870), the Wyrmspine (872) to Wyrmrest (460–475, Ashkaar), the Wyrmscar Rift (864 :CAVE / 865 :DRAGONS_DEN). The war theatre on Ossaria's western dunes (built): the Rimed Sands (920), the Ashkaar Siege Camp (924) and its Command Pavilion (928), the Steamline (925), the Glass Dunes (926), the Observers' Mesa (929) and the bone-carters' camp (930). Then the Rainbow Scar (868) and the Pilgrim Road: Dominar's Toll (892), the Pilgrim Pass (880), Pilgrim's Rest (890), the Coronation Road (893), the Sovereign's Ascent (884–886) or the Glassfall Scar (888). Gym 18.

Key events

  • Sigrun's trial and oath. She won't let you challenge her until you walk the Wyrmscar Rift to the Draco Plate with her and say aloud what you mean to do at the Festival (⚑ :ch19_oath). On the walk, her confession: "He told me I'd never survive the Crown, and I was relieved. ... For two years I knew, and I let it happen, because it meant it wasn't me."
  • The Battle of the Glass Dunes (WAR-1, ⚑ :war_climax): Kyogre drags a flood-sea across the desert, Reshiram wakes in the Dominar's hand, and their beams meet over the flooded dunes.

Order of events

  1. The Gloamwood, the Thornwar Marches and the Wyrmspine to Wyrmrest. The Dominar is at the front; he has ordered the pass closed to everything Zenith-tainted (your Fellowship, your badge case). Sigrun Ashfall keeps it open anyway, standing on the gate with her Salamence: "I do the weighing, Father. Not you."
  2. Sigrun's trial in the Wyrmscar Rift, and her confession (above).
  3. ⚑ :ch19_oath at the brazier over the Draco Plate (an authored PC line): "I'm going to give them back." (Return) / "I'm going to keep them safe. Whatever it costs me." (Keep) / "I don't know yet. I'm going to find out with my eyes open." (Open) / (only at Resonance ≤ −2) "I'm going to end it. All of it." ☠ GO_LIARS_PYRE "Liar's Pyre": the fifth option, "Whatever you want to hear." Comedy scene "Weighed" (the night before the oath; the only joke in the chapter).
  4. To the front: word comes that Kyogre has risen and the Dominar has carried the Light Stone to the dunes. Sigrun flies you there overnight and sets you down at dawn on the Dry Tide by the bone-carters' camp (930).
  5. The lines (the side you didn't choose; both, by way of the Steamline, if you stand between): Isenmar's trench-lines on the Rimed Sands (920) or the Siege Camp's earthworks (924), and the Steamline (925).
  6. ⚑ :war_climax (MAJOR) on the Glass Dunes (926): stand between (switch 607) / back Ashkaar (605) / back Isenmar (606).
  7. Partner battle on the crest of the Glass Dunes (by your choice; see Key battles).
  8. The legend: you fight whichever legendary is about to fire on the other army: Reshiram by default, Kyogre if you back Ashkaar. Then the cutscene WAR-1 "The Beam Clash on the Glass Dunes". If :war_legend was neither, no legend comes (the clash is between the Wardens' aces) and Reshiram's fight happens at Wyrmrest after the truce, as below.
  9. The outcome: WAR_STOPPED (stood between with War Trust ≥ 4: the beams part over you) / WAR_BOTH_BROKEN (stood between without that trust: both front lines are glassed, both kingdoms lose a Festival seat) / WAR_ASHKAAR_WON or WAR_ISENMAR_WON (the loser forfeits a seat). Meridian observers on the Observers' Mesa (929) pack up before the steam clears; Larch by radio: "That wasn't a battle to them. That was a reading." The Glass Dunes stay glass: Ossaria's newest necropolis.
  10. ⚑ :war_terms (only if one side won), at the armistice table in Skaldfast's great hall with Kassan uninvited at the end of it: mercy / reparations / occupation (occupation poisons the Good ending).
  11. Optional: the Dominar's petition in the Command Pavilion (928; lies are a capital crime, the oath-brazier is lit). ⚑ :ch19_dominar: he flies for Crownhaven (DOMINAR_SWAYED) if you sent the Light Stone to Wyrmrest in Ch8 and bring proof (the Arbiter Blueprints or the Larch Papers), or if Sigrun's Bond is ≥ 4 and she speaks for you. Not possible if Isenmar won without mercy terms.
  12. Reshiram (when the fight happens at Wyrmrest): any true oath wakes the Light Stone in the Rift-shrine (or a Hearthguild runner brings it). Its fire is the truth of your oath: Return and Open lean Harmony, Keep is neutral, Ruin makes the fight savage. It bows to Sigrun, not to you, and flies to Crownhaven ahead of you.
  13. Gym 18, the Weighing Hall: Sigrun at her absolute best ("If you can't beat me, you can't survive him."). The 18th badge, TM59 Dragon Pulse, and the badge case sings all eighteen tones together. With the telemetry intact a Meridian airship turns toward Crownhaven within the minute; sabotaged, Larch on the radio: "He bought it. God help us, he bought it."
  14. The Rainbow Scar (868, :RAINBOW; all eighteen Imprints bleeding together into light) and the Pilgrim Road. At high Accord Standing or with the Royal Writ the Wardguard escort takes you up the Sovereign's Ascent; otherwise Edda's smugglers take you through the Glassfall Scar (888), among the forty Fixed of AF 290, to the place where you stood at five.

Key battles

Partner battle on the Glass Dunes (double; your partner by :war_climax):

  • Stand between (S607): you + Sigrun vs an Isenmar Captain and an Ashkaar Captain ("Both captains are coming. Back to back.").
  • Back Ashkaar (S605): you + Sigrun vs an Isenmar Captain and Soldier ("The Isenmar line breaks here or nowhere.").

  • Partners: Sigrun Flygon 83 @Soft Sand, Dragonite 84 @Lum Berry, Salamence 85 @Sitrus Berry; Marisol Pelipper 83 @Damp Rock, Lanturn 84 @Sitrus Berry, Gyarados 85 @Sitrus Berry.

Boss — Reshiram (RESHIRAM_GLASS_DUNES, Prismfall Bosses; map 926 on its default Desert field)

  • Lv 85 Calm; bars Casual 2 / Standard 3 / Hard 3. Bar 1: Flamethrower, Dragon Pulse, Earth Power, Extrasensory.
  • Break 1: Kyogre's flood-sea pours in (:FLOODED_DUNES, rain) and it learns Blue Flare, which glasses the flood in one (:GLASS_DUNES). Break 2: Fusion Flare, Sp. Def +1.
  • Last bar: it turns back (result :turned_back): no faint, no catch.
  • Tip: Ground, Rock and Dragon. On the Flooded Dunes its Flamethrower is hissed down to ×0.5 but Blue Flare and Fusion Flare are not, and Blue Flare turns the flood to glass, where Fire is ×1.2: switch to Water-resistant, Fire-resistant Pokémon once it learns Blue Flare.

Boss — Kyogre (KYOGRE_GLASS_DUNES, if you back Ashkaar)

  • Lv 85 Calm, Drizzle (the dunes bloom); Surf, Ice Beam, Thunder, Aqua Ring; bars Casual 2 / Standard 3 / Hard 3.
  • Break 1: the flood-sea (:FLOODED_DUNES); the rain passes (so rain and flood don't stack); Origin Pulse and Calm Mind. Break 2: Def and Sp. Def +1 (Hard: Sp. Atk +1 too). No Primal Reversion in this fight.
  • Last bar: it turns back (:turned_back).
  • Tip: Electric (×1.3 against grounded targets in the flood) and Grass; Blue Flare or Fusion Flare (or two other searing moves) fuse the flood into the Glass Dunes.

Boss — Reshiram at Wyrmrest (:DRAGONS_DEN; only when :war_legend is neither) (planned; only the Glass Dunes version is registered).

Field note: "the den's heat rises each turn, and the dragons grow stronger the longer you hesitate." Dragon ×1.5, Fire ×1.3, Water and Ice ×0.7; Dragon types take ×0.83 (lair armour); nothing can be frozen. Four Dragon attacks wake Wyrmfire (Dragon ×2, Fire ×1.5, Water and Ice ×0.5); three Water or Ice attacks cool it to a Cave; three Fairy attacks tame it into a Fairy Tale. Mega Salamence "Dreamwing". Tip: Fairy is the plan twice over: it hits her whole team and three Fairy moves take the den away from her.

Gym 18 — the Weighing Hall (Sigrun Ashfall) (design only)

  • Puzzle (10/10, about 45 minutes): "nothing passes unweighed." Scales lower bridges when balanced; statues turn on chains, and each chain drags its two neighbours; the magma tide rises and falls every 10 steps, and crust paths exist only at low tide.
    • 470 Gate: push both hoard piles (2 and 3) onto the pan that needs 5.
    • 471 Wyrm's Spine (recall): Rock Smash, one Strength push, Rock Climb and Waterfall, timing the tide (a brazier flares at steps 7, 8, 9); two dragon-tamer battles.
    • 472 Statue Court: follow the chains, not the compass. 9 turns: S1 ×2, S3 ×2, S4 ×2, S5 ×3 (S2 needs no turn of its own).
    • 473 Hoard Scales (A needs 9, B needs 10; piles 1, 2, 3, 5, 8): the 8 can only reach B, so A = 1 + 3 + 5, B = 2 + 8. Push the 2 and the 8 to B over two low tides (the 8 needs both windows), then ferry 1, 3 and 5 to A across the short crust.
  • Badge: Badge 18. TM59 Dragon Pulse. Level cap after: 90 (the Festival cap).
  • Mastery (optional): the Weighing of the Heir (475): push the 3-pile onto the great pan and stand on it yourself (the scale reads you as 5), with the three chained statues facing the pan, all within one low tide. Reward: Elemental Seed ×2 and Dragon Fang ("It weighed you and let you pass. It never let me.").
  • Gym trainers: 6 (Cool Trainer ×4, Ace Trainer ×2), Lv 81–84. (Not in PBS yet.)

Chapter 20 — "The Festival of Champions"

Crownhaven (480–499) in its caldera: Lower Crownhaven and its Market Ring and Pilgrims' Quarter, the Eighteen Gates, Upper Crownhaven's Basilica Close, the Basilica of First Light and its crypts, the Accord Palace (Court of Wardens, Throne Room, Gallery of Plates), the Glassfall Memorial Garden (489), the Festival Grounds' Court of Eight Pavilions (499), the Concordance Spire (493/494/498, a teaser), and the Temple-Arena of the Blessing, the Meridian Prism Arena (490/491/495, :PRISM_ARENA). Design only. Festival week, Days 0–6. Caps: R16 90, QF 92, SF 94.

Key events

  • The opening ceremony. Eighteen Wardens carry their Plates down the Sovereign's Stair into the Concordance Ring; Valen performs the Tuning with his crystal arm bare; and your shard sees Arceus: "...Little light. You have carried me far."
  • Valen's audience (⚑ :ch20_audience): "I chose a country over a woman's name. I'd do it again. I hate that I'd do it again." Then the Night of Masques and K8.

How the Festival works

  • Sixteen stand in the arena: you and fifteen kingdom delegates, two per kingdom and the Sovereign; every possible opponent is someone you have met at least twice. A kingdom that lost the war (or both, if the clash broke both armies) forfeits its second seat, and the Accord lends it to a seatless Warden (Dorian first, then Tamsin, Rook, Odessa, Ilsa, Nyx, Corvin).
Kingdom Seat A Seat B (what decides it)
Elowen Juno Celestine (Juno gives her seat to "the Gardener" if you earned it)
Antumbra Ysolde Kestrel if Gravenmoor names him (Redeemed, and the ring given or Ysolde's Bond ≥ 4), else Ilsa
Zenith Rook if he held the footage and is still Meridian's face, else Odessa Kestrel under Meridian's sunburst if Gravenmoor didn't claim him; else Magnus unless exposed; else Odessa or Rook
Nadir Kaito Nyx, or Corvin if you freed him and refused Nyx's bargain
Ossaria Sahar Bastian, unless the raid came in on your beacon (telemetry left)
Isenmar Marisol (or Anja) Anja, or forfeit (the war)
Ashkaar Sigrun Brann, or forfeit (the war)
The Accord Valen —
  • Your opponent at each stage is the first matching name (the last line is the fallback). The bowl is honest; the Accord's customs (the Right of Grievance, yielded invitations) bend it on screen.

Valen fallback
  • Your colours (⚑ :ch20_colors, Day 0): Queen Maelis, the Zenith Council and Nyx each offer theirs; Larch offers none (the old clause for "the Unsworn").
  • Matches between other entrants resolve by rule, and you can watch the notable ones as highlight cutscenes (e.g. Kestrel beats Kaito: "That isn't him fighting.").

Order of events

  1. Day 0, arrival: white stone and bells; Tamsin's eighteen banners in Upper Crownhaven, hanging white (that Warden would let go of their Plate) or grey (won't) by Day 1: the Consent count, made visible. Meridian runs security; the Lantern Hollow are disguised as Choir porters; the kings are in the observers' gallery; Envoy Delphine Okoro of the Concert is deciding on Severance. Dask refuses to reopen the Veil Gate: "I won't open a door in a wall that's falling down." In the Glassfall Memorial Garden you meet Carol, the Octave's Crownhaven singer. The Draw at the Basilica steps.
  2. Day 1, the opening ceremony (above), in gym order to the Choir's counting rhyme (Rook's cracked Zap Plate in a cradle, or carried by a Meridian officer if he was fired; Corvin's by a porter unless freed; Magnus under guard if exposed; Bastian leaning on Pip). The whole arena sees Valen's crystal arm. You collapse in the stands; Ilsa takes off her earmuffs and flinches. Rook's leak if he held the footage (:ch16_rook = hold): Kroll with a Meridian keycard on the arena's own screens; Voss doesn't blink.
  3. Day 2, Round of 16 ("someone from your past"; see the draw). After the match, the garden court: if Rowan lives, Juno and Rowan on the same bench; Teo (if he lived) or Venam's Testimony: "I could hear everything while it had me." Rowan cries, and Juno takes his good hand.
  4. Day 3, exhibitions and the Festival Grounds: the Eevee Octave gauntlet (once all eight singers are helped), the Pageant Bout (Dorian and Rook, "a duet for the cameras"), Juno's Garden Match (if she wasn't your R16), the Ebb Guild match with Marisol (Teo saved and close). The Concordance Spire teaser, street food from every kingdom, Dorian rehearsing in secret with Celestine.
  5. ⚑ :ch20_envoy: proof needs two of three, the Larch Papers, the Arbiter Blueprints, and testimony that the Fixed still dream (Teo's, Corvin's Quiet Ward records, or Venam's Testimony): Okoro recommends against Severance (ENVOY_PERSUADED). A plea alone: she drafts Severance "with regret".
  6. Day 4, Quarterfinal ("the honest view"). Default: Celestine confirms the Return as an oath: "Give them back. I've waited forty years to say that to someone who could."
  7. Day 5: Corvin, after treating Valen: "He's holding the Plates quiet right now, with his body." The Night of Masques: Dorian stages Ansel Crewe's banned play The Gilded King for the first time in 248 years, Celestine voices Maren's lament, the Wardguard won't push past Kaito, and when the King says "If heaven will not kneel, we'll build a chain" every head turns to the Meridian box. Voss stands and applauds, alone: "Bravo. They finally cast the king correctly." Comedy scene "The Good Tea" (before the audience).
  8. ⚑ :ch20_calla (only if someone inside is already moving: Rook holding the footage, or MAGNUS_KEPT_FAITH): Calla Wren, shaking in her lanyard ("I scanned you on the dock."). Shelter her on Edda's boat (one crack in the Engine; she lives) / send her back for the full schematics (two cracks; Kroll finds her in the Spire stairwell) / turn her away.
  9. Valen's audience in the Sovereign's Sanctum. ⚑ :ch20_audience (authored PC line): "There's another door. The Hymn. We give them back." (Return; answer with the Hymn if you hold it complete: "...Maren wrote that. I thought it was a poem.") / "Then I'll wear it. Somebody has to." (Keep) / "You don't get to decide that for me. Nobody does." (Refuse; with a cold Bond, no Little Owl and live telemetry this sets VALEN_COLLAPSED). ☠ GO_EARLY_CROWN "Early Crown": accept his desperate offer to crown you tonight (Ilsa warned you: "Don't let him hand you anything tonight.").
  10. Little Owl (:sq_little_owl, Ilsa's quest culmination): if you carried her messages through Acts III–V, she comes to the Sanctum: "Then save the country, Father. Don't make a child pay for it." "...Little owl." (ILSA_RECONCILED.)
  11. Morwen's Echo (exhibition: Kestrel and Ysolde reconciled and the K6 line was Resolve): after midnight Ysolde lights the Cathedral's lantern in a Crownhaven chapel, and Morwen fights you once, gently, "to see what I bought".
  12. Interlude V, "The Last Night" (play as Valen): three letters (to Ilsa, to Morwen's son, to "whoever wears it next"), and a question to a single Zygarde Cell on the sill: "Order, not justice. I chose order. Was I wrong?"
  13. Day 6, Semifinal: K8. Redeemed (fallback): at the first field cycle he tears the Gauntlet off ("If I beat you, I beat you."); with Morwen's Ring his Scizor Mega Evolves ("Mum. Just this once. Answer me."). Fallen: he keeps the Gauntlet on, it burns his hand, and Voss's men carry him off. Afterwards Ysolde gives him Morwen's sealed letter on the arena floor ("I didn't fail. I chose."). Other semifinal: Valen beats Sigrun to protect her.

Chapter 21 — "Sovereign"

Day 7 in the Prism Arena (491, :PRISM_ARENA). Design only. Caps: Final 96, hijack 100, Arceus 100.

Key events

  • The hijack. As Valen raises the Crown over you, the Meridian Prism Arena wakes: it is the Arbiter Engine. The keystone cradle rises in a golden hand, the Concordance Ring sprouts eighteen golden locks, the Crown is torn into the cradle, and Voss descends in an Engine-harness: "You carried my key through eighteen doors. Let me show you what it opens."
  • Arceus, Valen's death and the final choice (⚑ :ch21_final).

Order of events

  1. The Final: Valen Corrigan ("Come on, then. Show me there's another door."). His crystal spreads from shoulder to throat each time the field cycles. If VALEN_COLLAPSED, you fight his successor instead: Sigrun (Bond ≥ 5) or Brann, in tears ("He asked me to. Last thing he asked."). "Velmora has a new champion."
  2. The Coronation. ⚑ :ch21_crown: kneel / stand / step back (flavour the endings may read). The eighteen Plates scream.
  3. The hijack (above). The hijacker is Voss, or Dr Quent if Voss was discredited (MAGNUS_EXPOSED + Rook's leak + the Night of Masques), or Theodric on the Ruin Route.
  4. His hand (Larch warned you that morning: "Don't let him make you a part."). ⚑ :ch21_hand with VOSS_ACCEPTED: take it (Concord Dawn begins here; Arceus is never fought) / refuse ("You promised."). Without it, ☠ GO_HIS_HAND "His Hand": take his hand.
  5. The allies move (one line each, only if earned: Larch's eleven lamps): Rook cuts Lumen's grid (ROOK_CUTS_GRID); Nyx blacks out Meridian's comms (surgical with her bargain); Magnus disables the governor (MAGNUS_KEPT_FAITH); Marchetti stands the Directorate down (MARCHETTI_TURNED); Larch reads the miscalibration (TELEMETRY_SABOTAGED); Calla's schematics (one lamp or two); Sigrun and Reshiram hold the sky (with the Ashkaar legions if DOMINAR_SWAYED); Marisol's fleet and Edda evacuate Lower Crownhaven; Tamsin's silk nets catch the debris; the Lantern Hollow guard the pylons (LANTERN_HOLDS); Kaito holds the gate.
  6. Tag battle on the cracking arena floor: you + Kestrel (Redeemed) or Juno (J7) vs two of Marchetti, Quent and Kroll (whichever aren't turned, dead or hijacking).
  7. Voss (multi-bar for his ace, Silvally "Project NULL", whose type follows the active field). "I'm the only adult in this arena who'll say the true thing out loud: we don't need it." Between bars 2 and 3, if KESTREL_FALLEN, Kestrel is revealed harnessed into the Engine: ⚑ :ch21_reach_kestrel: reach him (needs Morwen's Ring or her words from a kept letter: "Be the kind that's nearest when it matters.") / burn the Gauntlet off (he lives, scarred; Ruin −3) / let go (KESTREL_LOST: the road to The Empty Lighthouse). On defeat Voss drives his harness-spike into the cradle: "Then I'll hold it."
  8. Arceus descends, dragged into the golden chains; the arena turns to :BLEED across the caldera. Its Judgment strikes the harness: ⚑ :ch21_spare_voss: shield him with the shard (PC_SPARED_VOSS) / let it judge.
  9. Valen holds the Ring: he puts the cracked Crown back on and holds the surge with his bare hands on two pylons (Ilsa at his back if reconciled: "Little owl's got you."). "Go. Free it. I'll hold the door — I've had thirty years of practice."
  10. The True Finale: Arceus (below). Between bars the three Wardens of that bar's gyms kneel at their pylons and release their Plate or refuse (every refusal makes the next lock forced: +1 to all Arceus's stats for that bar). All 36 lines are in story/11_FINALE_LINES.md. Celestine sings the Hymn's last verse as her lock breaks, and the arena picks it up.
  11. Valen's death (every main-route path except Gilded): as the last lock breaks his crystal burns through to light; he says your name (or "Little owl").
  12. Arceus speaks (through Ilsa if reconciled): "I will not take what is not given. I learned that here." ⚑ :ch21_final: Return "Go home. Take them with you." (always) / Keep "I'll keep them. I'll keep everyone safe." (always) / Borrowed (Kestrel Redeemed and devoted, or Sigrun's Bond ≥ 6: they take the Crown instead: "Not you. Let me be nearest.") / Concord (VOSS_ACCEPTED, or the governor never switched off) / Unmake (Resonance ≤ −6, or Hollow Standing ≥ 4 with Rowan radicalised or Kroll never publicly exposed). Comedy scene "Lecture Forty" belongs to the epilogue only.

The Ruin Route

With all 23 game overs in the Ledger (ruin_unlocked), the black pane in Giratina's Reverse Depths (Ch15) offers Look back? once more, and Yes walks you into the Ruin Route ("Every Type and None", story/12_RUIN_ROUTE.md): it replaces the rest of Ch15 through Ch21, with the Ferrymen's Mile, Archseer Dask in the quarterfinal, Valen's Last Tuning in the final, Theodric the Gilded Reflection as the hijacker, and Arceus's Judgment variant. This walkthrough doesn't cover it chapter by chapter yet.

Spoilers ahead: this chapter covers late-game twists.

CHAPTER BEATS — the one or two key events every chapter must land

User (2026-11-21): "try not to make each chapter thin please... we want every chapter to be significant to some extent with either 1 or 2 key events happening each chapter." Owner: story editor. Sources: story/04_ACT_I.md – 08_ACT_V.md, 09_MYSTERIES_FORESHADOWING.md, 10_CHOICES_ENDINGS.md, 14_WAR_AND_BLESSING.md. This file adds no keys; it says which beats carry each chapter so scripts, side quests and maps give them room. A key event is a story turn the player will remember: a reveal, a betrayal, a disaster, a choice with consequences, a big boss or legendary encounter, a character arc landing. A gym or a routine rival fight never counts on its own. How to use it. Script writers: each key event needs build-up on screen before it, a payoff you can see, and a consequence that shows up later (an NPC line, a map state, a choice key). Side-quest and map builders: don't put a sidequest, joke or optional zone inside a key event (15_COMEDY §1), and keep the maps it happens on free of clutter at that spot.

Status: ● strong (two real key events in the outline, or a strengthening the creator approved) · ◐ thin in the outline, strengthened here (the script must deliver the proposal) · ○ thin, proposal needs the creator's yes. After the creator's decisions of 2026-11-21 every chapter is ●.

Proposals for the thin chapters

A. Chapter 4, "Both Ways" — make the night one event, and give Larch's confession a scene (approved)

What the outline had: K2, a Hollow cell spiking the Lattice, a child's boat, Teo running, a three-way choice, and Larch's "It's my design" as a line after the gym. All the pieces, but spread thin, and Larch's line read as a status update. The strengthening (no new keys, no new characters):

  1. Build-up. Teo is met by day first, as Marisol's charming, furious little brother at the strike vote on the Mill Quay, heckling his sister. The river stutters three times during the day, each time longer. Kestrel is hunting "Thistle's people" and swears the cell is in Ebbmouth.
  2. The night. At midnight Meridian's tidal Lattice runs its night export draw, and the Ebb stops dead for an hour (V108 = 2), longer than it ever has. A girl takes a punt out on the dead-still river to fetch her toy boat. The masked cell blows the Lattice intake to shut the draw, and the river comes back all at once, recklessly, because nobody looked at the water: the punt is dragged at the Guild mill-race, the race that killed the Reyes father in AF 297. Battle-and-chase on the towpath (the cell, then the masked leader), then the PC, Marisol and the masked boy haul the race gate down together. In the lamplight his mask is pushed up: it's Teo. Marisol lets him run.
  3. The choice in public. A Meridian guard arrives and asks the PC who it was, with Marisol standing right there (:ch4_teo: report / keep_secret / confront her privately afterwards).
  4. The morning after. The consequence is on the quay before the gym: wanted posters for Teo (report), or Marisol's mother's door open (keep_secret / confront).
  5. Larch's confession as its own scene (after the gym): she lays the tide tables on the Pokémon Center counter. The stutters line up with Meridian's draw, and the full stop lines up with the night export. Meridian's draw is the cause; the Hollow's sabotage brought the river back, recklessly, with a child on the water. Both are true, and that is what gives :ch4_teo its weight. "It's not the Hollow stopping the river. It's us. It's my design. I lit up this whole region, you know. Eleven cities on my design." It's the first time the PC learns their mentor built the machine, and it seeds the red herring that she works for Meridian (resolved Ch12). Why it doesn't break later beats: Teo is still only an Ebbmouth cell leader, so his Ch9 fate is the same choice with more weight. The Hollow being partly right is the Act I thesis. Larch's secret was always revealed here; only the staging grows.

B. Chapter 7, "The Quiet Ward" — turn Sable's broadcast into the night the Ward nearly falls (approved)

What the outline had: J2 and the ledger (strong), Wick (good), Sweetrot (texture), and Sable's broadcast as a cliffhanger. The chapter has one key event and a lot of mood. The strengthening (uses existing cast and threads; no new keys):

  1. The night of Sable's broadcast, the Hammer cuts the Infirmary's power from the Gutterfall junction (the Ward's dampers run on Zenith current). The broadcast plays on the Ward's own screen as the lights die: "The Mourner's gone soft. The Hammer hasn't."
  2. Without the dampers, the Quiet Ward's Bleed rises into a Veil. Corvin and Wenlow can't go in. The PC can. They carry out the salt-haired child (the patient Wenlow introduced by name earlier in the chapter), and under the glass the child's eyes are moving. Corvin, on the roof afterwards: "They're not dying. They're dreaming." (09 #21, now seen, not just told.)
  3. Juno helps restart the dampers with her seed-medicine stills; it's the last time in Act II she's luminous with purpose before Ironreach.
  4. Consequence: the Hammer is now a named enemy of the Hollow's own people, and Wick's "he wants to carry them home" lands as a schism, not a sermon. The Ward is the place the Purge goes for in Ch16, so the player already knows every bed. Doesn't break: no one dies (Wenlow's death stays in Ch16), the child stays Fixed (the Homecoming waking is unchanged), and the PC's immunity is something everyone has already seen at the Lowlight. Staging: a scripted Bleed set piece to Mirefen, staged on the Infirmary's own Quiet Ward (map 223's top floor; maps.json "Quiet Ward on the highest stilts"), not the gym's Mastery room 234. Approved 2026-11-21: it's canon in story/26_SCRIPT_CH7.md and 05_ACT_II.md; the old roof-only version is retired.

Notes for the other workstreams

  • Side quests: a chapter's optional content should sit around its key events, never in the hour between the build-up and the payoff (e.g. nothing posted on the Ebbmouth board that sends the player away between the strike vote and the night; nothing new in the Lowlight after the Gala starts).
  • Map builders: every key event above needs room on its map: the Guild mill-race and towpath on 160 (Ch4), the Lowlight 181 → 608 swap with twelve figures at the positions of twelve living NPCs (Ch5). Those lists are in each script's "Map events needed".
  • Densest chapters (13, 14, 20): keep their gyms and side content short so the key events breathe.

Creator decisions (2026-11-21)

  1. Proposal B is approved: the Ward Night is Ch7's second key event, canon in 26_SCRIPT_CH7.md and 05_ACT_II.md. The roof-only fallback is removed.
  2. Proposal A: the Hollow are partly right. Meridian's night export draw is the cause of the Ebb stopping; the Hollow's sabotage restarts the river recklessly, with a child on the water. Kept morally grey so :ch4_teo has weight (23_SCRIPT_CH4.md, 04_ACT_I.md).
  3. Keep the Reyes father's death in the Guild Mill race, AF 297.
  4. Rook's "Turn it off. Rotom. Turn it off." stays in the Lowlight after the Shatter (03_CAST). At the Circuit Gym's cold cradle his PA line is "Rotom. Cut the feed. ...That bit's not for chat, buddy. Cut it." (GYM_PUZZLES Gym 4 updated).
  5. Keep Rowan giving Juno his Gala invitation as a fair clue (09 #2).
  6. Keep Lamp 47's tag as the vague hint at mystery #9.
  7. Badge names: Gym 3 the Tideturn Badge, Gym 4 the Arclight Badge, Gym 5 the Sandglass Badge, Gym 6 the Remedy Badge. Badges aren't defined in PBS or BADGE_TIERS; the names live in the story docs (04/05 and scripts 23–26) and GYM_PUZZLES.

Field logic audit (SPINE Revision 24)

The creator (2026-11-21): "I just want to make sure our field effects make sense and their transitions are relevant" and "I'm also perfectly fine with certain field effects not having any transition effects."

Every rule of the 35 fields was checked against two questions:

  1. Rules: could a player guess why this happens here? Each needs a physical or lore reason. Rules that were arbitrary, contradicted another rule, or were pure number noise were reworked or cut.

  2. Transitions: is the trigger plausible (fire burns a meadow, a flood fills a desert), is the destination what that place would really become, and does it matter in a real fight (does a trainer play it, or is it a fair player answer)? Implausible or pointless ones were reworked or cut. Fields with no transitions are fine.

Two fights are locked and were not touched: Brann's Gym 7 (every Volcanic and Cinderglass rule his fight uses stays exactly as it is) and the Gym 1 Grand Stage crowd rules. Rows are at the grain of the Field Notes bullets: one row can cover several numbers that share one reason.

The Glass Dunes rework (approved concept)

Real glass forms from sand only at extreme heat (lightning, a blast site's trinitite, a meteor's impact glass), stays hot a long time, flashes water to steam, bends and reflects light, is brittle (thermal shock, impacts), doesn't conduct and cools. So the field has two stages:

CAMEOS — Sister-Game Sidequests (Story lead; SPINE Revision 4)

The Reborn / Rejuvenation / Desolation cameos are optional sidequests, the way Rejuvenation features Reborn's Aya and Adrienn: a small quest somewhere in the world, usually ending in one tough optional fight. They are never in the Festival, never required, never in the finale. The Festival uses original entrants (03_CAST "Festival Outsiders"; 10_CHOICES_ENDINGS §3). The old Festival default draw in earlier drafts of this file is obsolete. Trainer type IDs keep the SPINE cameo convention FESTIVAL_<NAME>. Versions: 1 = the sidequest fight, 2 = post-game rematch at level 100 (unless noted). SPINE difficulty offsets (+100 Hard, +200 Casual) apply. Facts marked ✔ were checked against web sources (bottom). The rest is our own invention, in the spirit of the source game. Rulings: Lin's Togekiss keeps Oblivion Wing; Amaria's Lapras is "Deliverer".

Why they're in Velmora (in-universe)

Antumbra, the Kingdom Behind the Glass, is the reverse side of the world. Its Glass faces outward too, onto other worlds that already brush against each other:

  • ✔ Desolation's Shiv appears in Reborn's post-game.
  • ✔ Reborn's Adrienn and Aya help rebuild Aevium.

The Festival once invited champions through Antumbra's Veil Gate, but the Synod sealed it in AF 230. Since the Bleed accelerated (AF 289) and above all since the Fault (end of Act III), the Glass has been leaking. Travelers from Reborn, Aevium and Ayrith slip through mirrors, puddles, sewer-grates and dreams, and wake up somewhere in Velmora. Each one needs a way home, and the PC, who can walk through Bleed Veils, is the one who can find the right mirror. Rule of the Glass: a traveler can bring only what is theirs. Anything bound to their home world's gods stays behind.

1. "Lost in the Gossamer" — Shelly (Reborn)

  • Source ✔: Reborn's pink-haired Bug Gym Leader, who loves throwing bugs at you in double battles. ✔ In Reborn's post-game she becomes Champion, and insists she isn't the region's Professor "until her credentials arrive next year".
  • Where/when: Act I, Ch3, Gossamer Deepwood (:SILKWOOD), after Gym 2 (Tamsin's badge and Cut). It's the first cameo and teaches players that the Glass leaks.
  • Premise:
  • Silk-moth weavers report "a girl who keeps apologizing to the Bugs" deep in the wood.
  • Shelly fell through a dew-pond's reflection and has spent three days lost, because the Silkwood keeps re-weaving the paths.
  • She's terrified of crowds, so Briarwick's busy looms scare her more than the wood does.
  • The PC finds her, walks her through a small Bleed Veil to the dew-pond she came through, and helps her calm a Bleed-glassed Masquerain guarding it.
  • Before she steps back through, she asks for "one practice battle, so I'm not rusty when I get home".
  • Fight: double battle, lv ~21 (after Gym 2 since SPINE Rev 14 swapped Saltmere and Briarwick; trainer data [FESTIVAL_SHELLY,Shelly,1]), on :SILKWOOD. Bug core with a partner, so it's tough for its placement.
  • Reward: Silver Powder and a TM (Struggle Bug). Lore: "Your forest sounds like home used to, before the city got sick."
  • Post-game (v2): she comes back through the same pond, at lv 100 in doubles.

2. "Sewer Royalty" — Venam (Rejuvenation)

  • Source ✔: Veronica "Venam" Vasile, 17, a Punk Girl and Aevium's Poison Gym Leader (Poison Heart Badge).
  • ✔ She leads East Gearen's teen trainers out of the Abandoned Sewers.
  • ✔ Ace: Seviper, and ✔ her signature move is Venam's Kiss (a Poison move super-effective against Steel).
  • ✔ She was petrified and restored by the Spring of Rejuvenation.
  • Where/when: Act II, Ch7, the Miasma Caverns runoff tunnels under Mirefen (:CORROSIVE_MIRE), after Gym 6 and J2.
  • Premise:
  • Wenlow mentions "a loud girl with a snake" helping drag Sweetrot addicts to the Infirmary from the deep tunnels. She fell through a sewer-grate's reflection.
  • Venam loves Nadir within five minutes ("better graffiti than mine, worse air") and hates the Sweet Market vendors on sight.
  • The quest is a tunnel crawl with her as a temporary partner: a partner battle against Mother Gutter's vendors.
  • At the Quiet Ward, she sits with the half-Fixed patients and goes quiet. Then she tells Corvin and the PC about being stone: "I could hear everything. Everyone who sat with me." Corvin asks if he can record it.
  • Fight: the farewell fight at the grate she came through, lv ~38, on :CORROSIVE_MIRE. Ace Seviper with a custom Venam's Kiss (if the move team adds it; otherwise a strong Poison move).
  • Reward: Venam's Testimony (Key Item, Corvin's recording).
  • It can be played for Juno at the Bride Tree (Ch10) or in Ch20.
  • It is one of the three proofs for Envoy Okoro (:ch20_envoy).
  • Also Black Sludge.
  • Post-game (v2): lv 100.

3. "Two Lucarios" — Garret (Desolation)

  • Source ✔: Ayrith's Fighting Gym Leader (Cellia South). Gruff, blunt and loyal, and ✔ searching for his kidnapped sister Eden. ✔ Mega Lucario.
  • Where/when: Act II, Ch9, Ironreach's lower shafts below the Iron Pit, after the Conclave.
  • Premise:
  • During the Ironreach Open's undercard, a stranger with a Lucario asks every pit-fighter about a girl named Eden. He walked out of a puddle in the shafts during the Conclave's Bleed burst.
  • Kaito recognizes something in him and lends him a cot.
  • The PC helps him search the old Aurel shafts, where his Lucario senses people sleeping behind the walls. This is a tiny foreshadow of the Quiet Towns and Marrowgate.
  • She isn't here. He wants to fight the PC "to see if this world's worth searching".
  • Fight: lv ~46 on :COLOSSEUM, with Mega Lucario (if Megas are enabled; otherwise Lucario with an item build). Kaito watches.
  • Reward: Lucarionite if Megas are enabled, otherwise a Riolu egg. Also Black Belt. Lore: "Talk less. Fight more. Then we'll talk."
  • Post-game (v2): lv 100, plus the Marrowgate rumor: a girl matching Eden's description seen near the Quiet Towns. It's a deliberate dead end and a kindness. We never resolve another game's plot.

4. "What Are You For?" — Melia (Rejuvenation)

  • Source ✔: The heart of Rejuvenation. Adoptive daughter of Professor Jenner and a reserve Normal Gym Leader. ✔ Hapi (a Togekiss raised from her treasured Togepi), Zoroark, Mimikyu, Snorlax. ✔ She is Venam's close friend and ex.
  • Where/when: Act III, Ch10, the Royal Chase (Safari-style reserve) outside Verdance, after J3.
  • Premise:
  • A blonde girl with a Togekiss is searching the reserve for "a friend who fell through a sewer". If the Venam quest is done, the PC can tell her Venam got home safely.
  • The Queen's huntsmen think she's a poacher. The PC vouches for her.
  • She watched Juno's confirmation from the crowd and asks the PC the question nobody else does: "Everyone keeps telling you what you're for. Have you decided yet?"
  • Her way home is the reflection in the Chase's royal fishpond.
  • Fight: lv ~50, with Hapi (Togekiss) as ace.
  • Reward: a Togepi egg and a Soothe Bell.
  • Bonus if Venam's quest is done: a Gale Post letter from Venam, routed through the Glass ("u owe me a rematch, null kid").
  • Post-game (v2): lv 100.

5. "Crystal Sleep" — Alexandra (Rejuvenation)

  • Source ✔: Elite 8 member and Acting Champion of Aevium. ✔ Her known Pokémon lean Dragon/Psychic: Latias, Dragonite, Altaria, Starmie, Lapras, Sigilyph, Garchomp. ✔ Her mother Celine, Aevium's Champion, sleeps encased in crystal, recovering from wounds inflicted by Madame X.
  • Where/when: Act III, Ch11, Rimeholt's sunken lower town after the Thaw and Gym 10.
  • Premise:
  • Among the half-Fixed fishers on the broken ice sits a tall woman with a Latias, asking each one whether they can hear her. She came through the Thaw's black water.
  • Velmora's Fixing looks horribly like her mother's crystal. She has questions for Anja (blunt) and Corvin (by Gale Post).
  • The PC helps her move three Fixing fishers to the heat-tower shelters before the next freeze. She is quietly devastated by how many there are.
  • She leaves through a frozen mirror in the Thane's hall: "My mother has been asleep in crystal for a long time. I'd like to know if yours wake up."
  • Fight: lv ~56, on a Dragon/Psychic champion team. Ace: Latias.
  • Reward: a Draco Meteor tutor and Celine's Notes (lore Key Item: an otherworld physician's notes on crystal stasis). Field Notes then adds a line: "the sleepers may be dreaming".
  • Post-game (v2): lv 100.

6. "Deliverer" — Amaria and Titania (Reborn)

  • Source ✔: Amaria, Reborn's late-game Water Gym Leader, famous for her nicknamed team, including Lapras "Deliverer" (ace, per ruling), Starmie "Twinkle", Ludicolo "Indiana" and Kingdra "Atlantica". ✔ Her gym is an underwater maze. Titania, Reborn's Steel Gym Leader: ✔ her battle is on the Fairy Tale field in a sky castle, and her chapter is paired with Amaria's (badges 15–16). Her team concept is knightly (Aegislash, Mawile).
  • Where/when: Act IV, Ch17, drowned Aurelia's lower galleries (Seabed / Aurelia maps, Dive), after Gym 16, before the PC leaves Underveil.
  • Premise:
  • Edda's divers report a woman swimming without a suit in the drowned galleries, singing to a Lapras, and an armored knight pacing the drained shallows above who refuses to leave.
  • Amaria followed "a city under a city" through the Glass. Drowned places call to her, and Aurelia is calling hard.
  • Titania followed Amaria.
  • The PC dives a short underwater maze to reach Amaria, who is sitting in a flooded Gilder hall. She says the drowned city "isn't dead, it's waiting". This is a Ruin Route hint about Theodric's reflection.
  • Titania won't let Amaria go home until "someone who can walk through walls" proves the way back is safe.
  • Fight: double battle vs Amaria and Titania, lv ~78, on :WATER_SURFACE (Amaria's side; Titania's Steel suffers). Aces: Lapras "Deliverer" and Aegislash.
  • Reward: a Liquidation TM, an Assault Vest from Titania ("a knight's spare"), and a Lapras of the PC's own: Deliverer's calf. "She'll carry you out of a flood someday." This echoes Valen's Lapras.
  • Post-game (v2): both at lv 100.

7. "Dreamwalker" — Shiv (Desolation)

  • Source ✔: The Champion of Ayrith. Mysterious and initially shady, ✔ later revealed to be working under Darkrai. ✔ Signature Aipom → Ambipom with absurd HP. ✔ He's a trickster, and ✔ he has already crossed worlds, as "Dreamer Shiv" in Reborn's post-game.
  • Where/when: Act V, Ch18, Gloaming's dusk-chapels, after Gym 17.
  • Premise:
  • Gloaming's townsfolk keep dreaming the same grinning stranger. He walks dreams, and Gloaming's endless dusk makes the dream-road easy.
  • He greets the PC: "Met you already. You were standing on a ferry, glowing like a lighthouse."
  • The quest is three dream-errands for the townsfolk: return a lost name, finish a dead man's sentence, find a child's Pokémon in a dream that isn't hers.
  • He finally admits he's lost: "Dreams leak through your Glass like water through a roof. I followed one too far."
  • Fight: lv ~84. Trickster tech (Fake Out, Trick, Taunt, odd abilities). Ace: Ambipom with absurd HP (custom stats, balance-approved).
  • Reward: a Dusk Stone and Dream Mist (Key Item: re-watch any completed interlude).
  • Ruin hint: only if the Ledger holds any game over: "You've done this before, haven't you. I can smell the other nights on you."
  • Post-game (v2): lv 100.

8. "the meteor champion" — Lin (Reborn) — post-game superboss

  • Source ✔: Lin (Lindsey Paraeah), Reborn's hidden Big Bad. She usurped Team Meteor and is fought as Reborn's Champion.
  • ✔ Signature: a Togekiss with Oblivion Wing, a move it can't legally learn (signature beats legality, per ruling).
  • ✔ She caught Arceus.
  • ✔ Cynical, blunt, mean-spirited, Jekyll-and-Hyde. Her honest lines are written in lowercase, as an homage.
  • Where/when: post-game, any ending with a post-game. Hesper Vane reports "a woman who talks without capital letters" haunting the Ferrow's Landing lighthouse at night. Found there; fought at the Distortion Core antechamber (Antumbra).
  • Premise:
  • She came through the Glass the night Arceus came down, because she felt it from her world. Per the Rule of the Glass, her own Arceus wouldn't follow.
  • Her lines depend on the ending:
    • Homecoming: "you gave it back. good. i couldn't."
    • Long Vigil: "you kept it. i kept mine too. look at us."
    • Concord Dawn: "it's quiet, isn't it. for a while."
  • With any game over in the Ledger: "you've done this before, haven't you."
  • Fight: superboss, lv 100, the hardest optional fight in the game. Ace: Togekiss (Oblivion Wing). The rest are Reborn-endgame heavy hitters, chosen by balance (no Arceus).
  • Reward: the Ledger Lens (Key Item: turns Ledger hints on for this save, the in-game equivalent of the 'ledgerhints' password), plus a lowercase letter left in the lighthouse: "see you in the next one."

9. Nova (Desolation) — Ruin Route only

  • Source ✔: Leader of Team Crescent. An anti-villain who wants a dream world where everyone is happy, manipulative but sincere. ✔ Signature: Gothitelle.
  • Where/when: Ruin Route, R5, on the Mirrorwalk dream-road between Gloaming and Wyrmrest (story/12_RUIN_ROUTE.md).
  • Premise: drawn to a PC whose Resonance has locked at Ruin, she offers a gentler unmaking: everyone asleep and happy forever. Accepting is GO_R_SWEET_DREAMS. Refusing leads to a fight.
  • Fight: lv ~90. Ace: Gothitelle.
  • Reward: the Crescent Charm (Ruin Key Item; Nova's last kindness). In R7 it lets the Reflection speak one extra line.
